why should I wish to kill them, even though they might otherwise kill me?
translationHindi: हमें जिनके लिए राज्य, भोग और सुखादि अभीष्ट हैं, वे ही ये सब धन और प्राणों की आशा त्यागकर युद्ध में खड़े हैं।
translationGujarati: અમારે જેના માટે રાજ્ય, ભોગ અને સુખ વગેરે જોઈએ છે, તેઓ જ આ બધા ધન અને પ્રાણની આશા છોડીને યુદ્ધમાં ઉભા છે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna points out that the very people for whom one seeks worldly pleasures—teachers, fathers, sons, and relatives—are standing here ready to give up their lives and wealth in war.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि जिन लोगों के लिए हम सांसारिक सुखों की चाह रखते हैं—गुरुजन, पिता, पुत्र और संबंधी—वे ही यहाँ अपने प्राण और धन का मोह छोड़कर युद्ध के लिए खड़े हैं।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કહે છે કે જે લોકો માટે અમે સાંસારિક સુખોની ઈચ્છા રાખીએ છીએ—ગુરુજનો, પિતા, પુત્ર અને સંબંધીઓ—તેઓ જ અહીં પોતાના પ્રાણ અને ધનનો મોહ છોડીને યુદ્ધ માટે ઉભા છે.
tweetEnglish: Those for whom we desire wealth and happiness are standing here, ready to give up their lives.
threadsEnglish: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, and other relatives are standing before me, ready to give up their lives.
englishTransliteration:
ta ime ’vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṁs tyaktvā dhanāni ca
ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrās tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ
englishWBW: te (they) — ime (all these) — avasthitāḥ (situated) — yuddhe (in the battle) — prāṇān (lives) — tyaktvā (giving up) — dhanāni (wealth) — ca (also) — ācāryāḥ (teachers) — pitaraḥ (fathers) — putrāḥ (sons) — tathā (as well) — eva (certainly) — ca (also) — pitāmahāḥ (grandfathers)
englishExplain:
Arjuna points out the tragedy of the situation: the very people for whom one seeks wealth and happiness are standing here ready to sacrifice their lives. He lists his teachers, fathers, and sons, and grandfathers.

By naming these specific relationships, he emphasizes the heinous nature of the act. These are the people who should be respected and protected. To kill them for the sake of ‘earthly riches’ seems barbaric to him. He is overwhelmed by the irony that both sides are staking everything for a material prize.

Arjuna feels a deep sense of guilt being the potential executioner of his own mentors and elders. He views the war as a collision of greed that will result only in the destruction of the family unit, which he considers the foundation of society.

sanskrit:
आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः।
मातुलाः श्चशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा।।
translationEnglish:
Teachers, fathers, sons, and also grandfathers,
maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other relatives...
translationHindi: गुरुजन, ताऊ-चाचे, लड़के और उसी प्रकार दादे, मामे, ससुर, पौत्र, साले तथा और भी सम्बन्धी लोग हैं...
translationGujarati: ગુરુજનો, કાકાઓ, પુત્રો અને તે જ રીતે દાદાઓ, મામાઓ, સસરાઓ, પૌત્રો, શાળા અને બીજા સંબંધીઓ છે...
simpleEnglish: Arjuna lists the specific relationships of the people facing him: teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, in-laws, and other relatives.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन अपने सामने खड़े लोगों के साथ अपने संबंधों को गिनाते हैं: गुरुजन, पिता-तुल्य बुजुर्ग, पुत्र, दादा, मामा, ससुर और अन्य रिश्तेदार।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન પોતાની સામે ઉભેલા લોકો સાથેના પોતાના સંબંધો ગણાવે છે: ગુરુજનો, પિતા-તુલ્ય વડીલો, પુત્રો, દાદા, મામા, સસરા અને અન્ય સંબંધીઓ.
tweetEnglish: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, in-laws, and relatives are all here.
threadsEnglish: Although they may wish to kill me, I do not wish to kill them, even in exchange for the three worlds, let alone this earth.
englishTransliteration:
mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ sambandhinas tathā
etān na hantum icchāmi ghnato ’pi madhusūdana
englishWBW: mātulāḥ (maternal uncles) — śvaśurāḥ (fathers-in-law) — pautrāḥ (grandsons) — śyālāḥ (brothers-in-law) — sambandhinaḥ (relatives) — tathā (as well) — etān (all these) — na (not) — hantum (to kill) — icchāmi (do I wish) — ghnataḥ (being killed) — api (even) — madhusūdana (O killer of the demon Madhu)
englishExplain:
Arjuna continues listing his relatives: maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, and brothers-in-law. He declares his final resolve: “Even if they kill me, I do not wish to kill them.” He is adopting a stance of non-resistance and total non-violence.

He addresses Kṛṣṇa as ‘Madhusūdana’, the killer of the demon Madhu. This is subtle; he is saying, “You kill demons, but You are asking me to kill my relatives. How is that fair?” He is attempting to prove that his refusal to fight is a superior moral position.

Arjuna is choosing what he perceives as saintly behavior over his duty as a warrior. However, his non-violence is born of material attachment and a fear of guilt, not of spiritual enlightenment. He is putting his personal feelings above the divine plan Kṛṣṇa has for the world.

sanskrit:
एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते।।
translationEnglish:
O maintainer of all living entities, I am not prepared to fight with them even in exchange for the three worlds, let alone this earth.
What pleasure will we derive from killing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra?
translationHindi: हे मधुसूदन! मुझे मारने पर भी अथवा तीनों लोकों के राज्य के लिए भी मैं इन सबको मारना नहीं चाहता; फिर पृथ्वी के लिए तो कहना ही क्या है?
translationGujarati: હે મધુસુદન! મને મારવા છતાં પણ અથવા ત્રણેય લોકના રાજ્ય માટે પણ હું આ બધાને મારવા નથી ઈચ્છતો; તો પછી પૃથ્વી માટે તો કહેવું જ શું?
simpleEnglish: Arjuna declares that even if these people kill him, he does not wish to kill them, not even for the sovereignty of the three worlds, let alone for this earth.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन घोषणा करते हैं कि भले ही वे लोग उन्हें मार डालें, फिर भी वे उन्हें नहीं मारना चाहते, तीनों लोकों के राज्य के लिए भी नहीं, तो फिर इस पृथ्वी की तो बात ही क्या है।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન ઘોષણા કરે છે કે ભલે તે લોકો તેમને મારી નાખે, તો પણ તેઓ તેમને મારવા નથી ઈચ્છતા, ત્રણેય લોકના રાજ્ય માટે પણ નહીં, તો પછી આ પૃથ્વીની તો વાત જ શું છે.
tweetEnglish: I do not wish to kill them, even for the three worlds, let alone for this earth.
threadsEnglish: What pleasure will we derive from killing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Kṛṣṇa? Sin will overcome us if we slay such aggressors.
englishTransliteration:
api trailokya-rājyasya hetoḥ kiṁ nu mahī-kṛte
nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana
englishWBW: api (even) — trailokya (of the three worlds) — rājyasya (of the kingdom) — hetoḥ (for the sake of) — kim nu (what to speak of) — mahī-kṛte (for the sake of the earth) — nihatya (after killing) — dhārtarāṣṭrān (the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra) — naḥ (to us) — kā (what) — prītiḥ (pleasure) — syāt (will there be) — janārdana (O maintainer of all beings)
englishExplain:
Arjuna raises the stakes to a cosmic level. He says he wouldn’t kill them even for the sovereignty of the three worlds, let alone for this small earth. He asks Kṛṣṇa what satisfaction they could possibly derive from killing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

He addresses Kṛṣṇa as ‘Janārdana’, the maintainer of all living entities, implying that Kṛṣṇa should be maintaining these people rather than ordering their destruction. Arjuna believes that the act of killing his cousins will only bring misery and regret, not happiness.

He is projecting his future emotional state—one of haunted guilt—and finding it unacceptable. He fails to see that the satisfaction of a warrior comes from the performance of duty and the protection of Dharma, not from the personal outcome or the spoils of the battle.

sanskrit:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन।
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः।।
translationEnglish:
Sin will overcome us if we slay such aggressors.
Therefore it is not proper for us to kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and our friends.
What should we gain, O Kṛṣṇa, husband of the goddess of fortune, and how could we be happy by killing our own kinsmen?
translationHindi: हे जनार्दन! धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को मारकर हमें क्या प्रसन्नता होगी? इन आततायियों को मारकर तो हमें पाप ही लगेगा।
translationGujarati: હે જનાર્દન! ધૃતરાષ્ટ્રના પુત્રોને મારીને અમને શું આનંદ થશે? આ આતતાયીઓને મારીને તો અમને પાપ જ લાગશે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna argues that killing these aggressors will only bring sin upon them, and questions what happiness they could possibly find in killing their own cousins, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन तर्क देते हैं कि इन हमलावरों को मारने से उन्हें केवल पाप ही लगेगा, और पूछते हैं कि अपने ही चचेरे भाइयों, धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों, को मारकर उन्हें क्या खुशी मिल सकती है।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન તર્ક આપે છે કે આ હુમલાખોરોને મારવાથી તેમને માત્ર પાપ જ લાગશે, અને પૂછે છે કે પોતાના જ પિતરાઈ ભાઈઓ, ધૃતરાષ્ટ્રના પુત્રોને મારીને તેમને શું ખુશી મળી શકે છે.
tweetEnglish: What pleasure is there in killing Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s sons? Only sin will cling to us.
threadsEnglish: Therefore it is not proper for us to kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and our friends. What should we gain, and how could we be happy?
englishTransliteration:
pāpam evāśrayed asmān hatvaitān ātatāyinaḥ
tasmān nārhā vayaṁ hantuṁ dhārtarāṣṭrān sa-bāndhavān
sva-janaṁ hi kathaṁ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
englishWBW: pāpam (sin) — eva (certainly) — āśrayet (must come upon) — asmān (us) — hatvā (after killing) — etān (all these) — ātatāyinaḥ (aggressors) — tasmāt (therefore) — na (not) — arhāḥ (deserving) — vayam (we) — hantum (to kill) — dhārtarāṣṭrān (the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra) — sa-bāndhavān (along with relatives) — sva-janam (own kinsmen) — hi (certainly) — katham (how) — hatvā (after killing) — sukhinaḥ (happy) — syāma (will we become) — mādhava (O Kṛṣṇa, husband of the goddess of fortune)
englishExplain:
Arjuna introduces a legalistic argument. He acknowledges that the Kauravas are ‘ātatāyinaḥ’, or aggressors. In Vedic law, an aggressor—one who poisons, sets fire, or steals land—can be killed without incurring sin. The Kauravas had done all of this to the Pāṇḍavas.

However, Arjuna argues that because they are relatives, the general law for killing aggressors is superseded by the specific duty to protect family. He believes that sin will overcome them if they kill these men, regardless of their crimes.

He asks, “How can we be happy by killing our own people?” addressing Kṛṣṇa as ‘Mādhava’. He is arguing that the means—killing family—is so evil that it will destroy the end—happiness. He is prioritizing social bonds over the cosmic necessity of justice.

sanskrit:
तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान्।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव।।
translationEnglish:
Therefore, it is not befitting for us to kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and our kinsmen.
O Kṛṣṇa, how can we be happy by killing our own people?
translationHindi: अतएव अपने बान्धव धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को मारने के लिए हम योग्य नहीं हैं। हे माधव! अपने ही कुटुम्बियों को मारकर हम कैसे सुखी होंगे?
translationGujarati: તેથી પોતાના બાંધવ એવા ધૃતરાષ્ટ્રના પુત્રોને મારવા માટે અમે યોગ્ય નથી. હે માધવ! પોતાના જ કુટુંબીજનોને મારીને અમે કેવી રીતે સુખી થઈશું?
simpleEnglish: Arjuna concludes that it is not right to kill his own kinsmen, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, asking Kṛṣṇa how they could ever be happy after destroying their own relatives.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन निष्कर्ष निकालते हैं कि अपने ही बंधुओं, धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों, को मारना उचित नहीं है, और कृष्ण से पूछते हैं कि अपने ही रिश्तेदारों का विनाश करके वे कभी सुखी कैसे हो सकते हैं।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન નિષ્કર્ષ કાઢે છે કે પોતાના જ બાંધવો, ધૃતરાષ્ટ્રના પુત્રોને મારવા યોગ્ય નથી, અને કૃષ્ણને પૂછે છે કે પોતાના જ સંબંધીઓનો વિનાશ કરીને તેઓ ક્યારેય સુખી કેવી રીતે થઈ શકે છે.
tweetEnglish: It is not proper to kill our own kinsmen. How can we be happy after destroying our family?
threadsEnglish: O Janārdana, although these men, their hearts overtaken by greed, see no fault in killing one’s family or quarreling with friends...
englishTransliteration:
yady apy ete na paśyanti lobhopahata-cetasaḥ
kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṁ doṣaṁ mitra-drohe ca pātakam
englishWBW: yadi (if) — api (even) — ete (they) — na (not) — paśyanti (do see) — lobha (by greed) — upahata (overpowered) — cetasaḥ (their hearts) — kula-kṣaya (destruction of family) — kṛtam (done) — doṣam (the fault) — mitra-drohe (in quarreling with friends) — ca (also) — pātakam (sin)
englishExplain:
Arjuna acknowledges the motivation of his enemies: their hearts are overpowered by greed. He admits that Duryodhana and his party are blind to the sin of destroying the family and the crime of betraying friends. Greed acts as a blinder to their moral judgment.

However, Arjuna uses this very fact to argue for his own inaction. He posits that since he and the Pāṇḍavas are not blinded by greed—since they can clearly see the fault—they have a higher moral responsibility to stop the war.

This is a subtle ego trap. He thinks, “They are fools, but I am wise.” He believes that his wisdom should lead to renunciation, not realizing that true wisdom involves performing one’s duty even when it is painful. He is trying to take the moral high ground to avoid a difficult conflict.

sanskrit:
यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम्।।
translationEnglish:
O Janārdana, although these men, their hearts overtaken by greed,
see no fault in killing one’s family or quarreling with friends...
translationHindi: यद्यपि लोभ से भ्रष्टचित्त हुए ये लोग कुल के नाश से उत्पन्न दोष को और मित्रों से विरोध करने में पाप को नहीं देखते...
translationGujarati: જોકે લોભથી ભ્રષ્ટ બુદ્ધિવાળા આ લોકો કુળના નાશથી થતા દોષને અને મિત્રો સાથે દ્રોહ કરવાના પાપને જોતા નથી...
simpleEnglish: Arjuna observes that the Kauravas, blinded by greed, do not see the sin in destroying their family or betraying their friends.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि भले ही कौरव लोभ में अंधे होकर कुल का नाश करने और मित्रों से द्रोह करने में कोई पाप नहीं देखते...
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કહે છે કે ભલે કૌરવો લોભમાં આંધળા થઈને કુળનો નાશ કરવામાં અને મિત્રો સાથે દ્રોહ કરવામાં કોઈ પાપ જોતા નથી...
tweetEnglish: Although their hearts are overtaken by greed and they see no fault in killing the family...
threadsEnglish: ...why should we, who can see the crime in destroying a family, not refrain from these sins?
englishTransliteration:
kathaṁ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum
kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṁ doṣaṁ prapaśyadbhir janārdana
englishWBW: katham (why) — na (not) — jñeyam (should be known) — asmābhiḥ (by us) — pāpāt (from sin) — asmāt (this) — nivartitum (to turn away) — kula-kṣaya (destruction of family) — kṛtam (done) — doṣam (the fault) — prapaśyadbhiḥ (by those who can see) — janārdana (O Kṛṣṇa)
englishExplain:
Continuing his reasoning, Arjuna asks Kṛṣṇa why they should not turn away from this sin. He emphasizes that they ‘clearly see’ the crime in destroying the family. This highlights the difference between ignorance and willful sin.

Arjuna feels that if he fights, he is committing a greater sin than the Kauravas because he is doing it with full knowledge of the consequences. He presents himself as a man of foresight, predicting the chain reaction of social collapse that starts with war.

He is appealing to Kṛṣṇa’s sense of justice, essentially saying, “You cannot ask a man who knows the consequences to commit the same mistake as the ignorant.” He is deeply convinced that avoidance is the only ethical choice for someone with his level of understanding.

sanskrit:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम्।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन।।
translationEnglish: ...why should we, who can see the crime in destroying a family, engage in these acts of sin?
translationHindi: ...तो भी हे जनार्दन! कुल के नाश से होने वाले दोष को जानने वाले हम लोगों को इस पाप से हटने के लिए क्यों नहीं विचार करना चाहिए?
translationGujarati: ...તો પણ હે જનાર્દન! કુળના નાશથી થતા દોષને જાણનારા અમારે આ પાપમાંથી નિવૃત્ત થવા માટે કેમ વિચાર ન કરવો જોઈએ?
simpleEnglish: Arjuna asks Kṛṣṇa why they, who clearly see the crime in destroying a family, should engage in such sinful acts instead of turning away from them.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कृष्ण से पूछते हैं कि हम, जो कुल के नाश में होने वाले पाप को स्पष्ट रूप से देख सकते हैं, क्यों इस पाप में शामिल हों और इससे दूर हटने का विचार क्यों न करें।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કૃષ્ણને પૂછે છે કે અમે, જે કુળના નાશમાં થનારા પાપને સ્પષ્ટપણે જોઈ શકીએ છીએ, શા માટે આ પાપમાં જોડાઈએ અને તેનાથી દૂર હટવાનો વિચાર કેમ ન કરીએ.
tweetEnglish: Why should we, who can see the crime in destroying a family, engage in these acts of sin?
threadsEnglish: With the destruction of a dynasty, the eternal family tradition is vanquished, and thus the rest of the family becomes involved in irreligion.
englishTransliteration:
kula-kṣaye praṇaśyanti kula-dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ
dharme naṣṭe kulaṁ kṛtsnam adharmo ’bhibhavaty uta
englishWBW: kula-kṣaye (in the destruction of the family) — praṇaśyanti (become vanquished) — kula-dharmāḥ (family traditions) — sanātanāḥ (eternal) — dharme (religion) — naṣṭe (being destroyed) — kulam (family) — kṛtsnam (entire) — adharmaḥ (irreligion) — abhibhavati (overcomes) — uta (certainly)
englishExplain:
Arjuna now outlines the sociological consequences of the war. He argues that with the destruction of the family, the eternal family traditions, or ‘kula-dharmāḥ’, are vanquished. In Vedic culture, the elders are the custodians of Dharma, rituals, and ethical values.

If the male elders are killed in the war, there will be no one left to guide the younger generation. Arjuna fears that when these traditions are lost, the entire remaining family will be overwhelmed by ‘adharma’, or irreligion. He views the war as an act that kills the very soul of the culture.

He believes that the victory on the battlefield will come at the cost of the moral integrity of the entire dynasty. To him, the preservation of these family traditions is far more important than the political administration of the kingdom.

sanskrit:
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः।
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत।।
translationEnglish:
With the destruction of the dynasty, the eternal family tradition is vanquished,
and thus the rest of the family becomes involved in irreligion.
translationHindi: कुल के नाश से सनातन कुल-धर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं; धर्म के नाश हो जाने पर सम्पूर्ण कुल में पाप भी बहुत फैल जाता है।
translationGujarati: કુળના નાશથી સનાતન કુળ ધર્મો નાશ પામે છે; ધર્મનો નાશ થવાથી સમગ્ર કુળમાં પાપ પણ ફેલાઈ જાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna explains that when a dynasty is destroyed, its eternal family traditions vanish, and with the loss of tradition, the entire remaining family becomes involved in irreligion.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन समझाते हैं कि जब कुल का नाश होता है, तो उसकी सनातन परंपराएं खत्म हो जाती हैं, और धर्म के नष्ट होने पर पूरा परिवार अधर्म और पाप में डूब जाता है।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન સમજાવે છે કે જ્યારે કુળનો નાશ થાય છે, ત્યારે તેની સનાતન પરંપરાઓ સમાપ્ત થઈ જાય છે, અને ધર્મના નાશ થવા પર આખું કુટુંબ અધર્મ અને પાપમાં ડૂબી જાય છે.
tweetEnglish: With the destruction of the dynasty, eternal traditions vanish, and the family falls to irreligion.
threadsEnglish: When irreligion is prominent in the family, O Kṛṣṇa, the women of the family become polluted, and from the degradation of womanhood comes unwanted progeny.
englishTransliteration:
adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kula-striyaḥ
strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇa-saṅkaraḥ
englishWBW: adharma (irreligion) — abhibhavāt (from the predominance of) — kṛṣṇa (O Kṛṣṇa) — praduṣyanti (become polluted) — kula-striyaḥ (family women) — strīṣu (in womanhood) — duṣṭāsu (being polluted) — vārṣṇeya (O descendant of Vṛṣṇi) — jāyate (is born) — varṇa-saṅkaraḥ (unwanted progeny)
englishExplain:
This verse deals with the sensitive topic of ‘varṇa-saṅkara’, or unwanted population. Arjuna argues that when irreligion predominates, the women of the family become polluted. In the Vedic social structure, the protection of women was considered paramount for maintaining the purity of the lineage.

Arjuna fears that without the protection and guidance of the elders, the women of the family will stray from traditions, leading to the birth of children who are not raised according to sacred rituals. Such a population, lacking spiritual culture, would lead to a chaotic society.

He sees war not just as a military event, but as the catalyst for total societal degradation. His concern is for the long-term purity and stability of the human race, which he believes is at risk if the current generation of leaders is wiped out.

sanskrit:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः।
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः।।
translationEnglish:
When irreligion is prominent in the family, O Kṛṣṇa, the women of the family become polluted,
and from the degradation of womanhood, O descendant of Vrishni, comes unwanted progeny.
translationHindi: हे कृष्ण! पाप के अधिक बढ़ जाने से कुल की स्त्रियाँ दूषित हो जाती हैं और हे वार्ष्णेय! स्त्रियों के दूषित होने पर वर्णशंकर सन्तान पैदा होती है।
translationGujarati: હે કૃષ્ણ! પાપ વધી જવાને કારણે કુળની સ્ત્રીઓ દૂષિત થઈ જાય છે અને હે વાર્ષ્ણેય! સ્ત્રીઓ દૂષિત થવાથી વર્ણસંકર સંતાન પેદા થાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna argues that when irreligion prevails, the women of the family become corrupted, and this corruption leads to the birth of unwanted progeny.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि जब कुल में अधर्म फैल जाता है, तो स्त्रियाँ दूषित हो जाती हैं, और स्त्रियों के दूषित होने से अवांछित संतान (वर्णसंकर) पैदा होती है।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કહે છે કે જ્યારે કુળમાં અધર્મ ફેલાઈ જાય છે, ત્યારે સ્ત્રીઓ દૂષિત થઈ જાય છે, અને સ્ત્રીઓના દૂષિત થવાથી અનિચ્છનીય સંતાન (વર્ણસંકર) પેદા થાય છે.
tweetEnglish: When irreligion prevails, women become polluted, and from that degradation comes unwanted progeny.
threadsEnglish: An increase of unwanted population certainly causes hellish life both for the family and for those who destroy the family tradition.
englishTransliteration:
saṅkaro narakāyaiva kula-ghnānāṁ kulasya ca
patanti pitaro hy eṣāṁ lupta-piṇḍodaka-kriyāḥ
englishWBW: saṅkaraḥ (such unwanted children) — narakāya (for hellish life) — eva (certainly) — kula-ghnānām (for those who destroy the family) — kulasya (for the family) — ca (and) — patanti (fall down) — pitaraḥ (forefathers) — hi (certainly) — eṣām (of them) — lupta (stopped) — piṇḍa (offerings of food) — udaka (and water) — kriyāḥ (performances)
englishExplain:
Arjuna describes the spiritual consequences of unwanted population. He says it creates a hellish situation for both the family and its destroyers. Specifically, he mentions the cessation of ‘piṇḍa-odaka-kriyā’, the offerings of food and water to ancestors.

In Vedic tradition, male descendants offer these ceremonies to satisfy the souls of their forefathers. If the lineage is polluted or the progeny are irreligious, these offerings will stop. Consequently, the ancestors are said to ‘fall down’ from their heavenly abodes because they are no longer supported by these rituals.

Arjuna is terrified that his action will not only destroy the living but also damn the dead. He feels the weight of past and future generations resting on his decision, and he cannot bear the thought of being the cause of such widespread spiritual ruin.

sanskrit:
सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च।
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः।।
translationEnglish:
An increase of unwanted population certainly causes hellish life both for the family and for those who destroy the family tradition.
The ancestors of such corrupt families fall down, because the performances for offering them food and water are entirely stopped.
translationHindi: वह वर्णशंकर कुलघातियों को और कुल को नरक में ले जाने के लिए ही होता है। लुप्त हुई पिण्ड और जल की क्रिया वाले इनके पितर लोग भी गिर जाते हैं।
translationGujarati: તે વર્ણસંકર કુળઘાતીઓને અને કુળને નરકમાં લઈ જવા માટે જ હોય છે. પિંડ અને જળની ક્રિયા લુપ્ત થવાથી તેમના પિતૃઓ પણ અધોગતિ પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna warns that unwanted population leads to hell for the family and its destroyers, as the ancestors fall from their positions because the rituals of offering food and water stop.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन चेतावनी देते हैं कि वर्णसंकर संतान कुल और कुलघातियों को नरक में ले जाती है, क्योंकि पिंडदान और तर्पण की क्रिया बंद होने से उनके पितरों का पतन हो जाता है।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન ચેતવણી આપે છે કે વર્ણસંકર સંતાન કુળ અને કુળઘાતીઓને નરકમાં લઈ જાય છે, કારણ કે પિંડદાન અને તર્પણની ક્રિયા બંધ થવાથી તેમના પિતૃઓનું પતન થઈ જાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Unwanted progeny leads the family to hell; ancestors fall as offerings of food and water stop.
threadsEnglish: By the evil deeds of those who destroy the family tradition and thus give rise to unwanted children, all kinds of community projects are devastated.
englishTransliteration:
doṣair etaiḥ kula-ghnānāṁ varṇa-saṅkara-kārakaiḥ
utsādyante jāti-dharmāḥ kula-dharmāś ca śāśvatāḥ
englishWBW: doṣaiḥ (by the faults) — etaiḥ (all these) — kula-ghnānām (of the destroyers of the family) — varṇa-saṅkara (unwanted children) — kārakaiḥ (which cause) — utsādyante (are devastated) — jāti-dharmāḥ (community projects) — kula-dharmāḥ (family traditions) — ca (and) — śāśvatāḥ (eternal)
englishExplain:
Arjuna summarizes the devastation. He claims that the evil deeds of those who destroy the family lead to the ruin of two types of Dharma: ‘jāti-dharmāḥ’, or community duties, and ‘kula-dharmāḥ’, or family traditions.

He argues that war rips apart the social fabric entirely. Community welfare activities and specific family customs are lost in the chaos of social breakdown. He paints a picture of a world where structure and tradition have collapsed, leaving only anarchy.

By categorizing the war as an ‘evil deed’, he has firmly convinced himself that fighting is unrighteous. He ignores the fact that the war is actually sanctioned by Kṛṣṇa to establish real Dharma. He is looking at the surface-level social impact rather than the deeper cosmic necessity of the battle.

sanskrit:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः।।
translationEnglish:
By the evil deeds of those who destroy the family tradition and thus give rise to unwanted children,
all kinds of community projects and family welfare activities are devastated.
translationHindi: इन वर्णशंकरकारक दोषों से कुलघातियों के सनातन कुल-धर्म और जाति-धर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं।
translationGujarati: આ વર્ણસંકર કારક દોષોથી કુળઘાતીઓના સનાતન કુળધર્મ અને જાતિધર્મ નાશ પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna asserts that the evil deeds causing unwanted progeny destroy the eternal family and community traditions.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि इन दोषों के कारण, जो वर्णसंकर पैदा करते हैं, कुलघातियों के सनातन कुल-धर्म और जाति-धर्म पूरी तरह नष्ट हो जाते हैं।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કહે છે કે આ દોષોને કારણે, જે વર્ણસંકર પેદા કરે છે, કુળઘાતીઓના સનાતન કુળધર્મ અને જાતિધર્મ પૂરેપૂરા નાશ પામે છે.
tweetEnglish: By these evil deeds, community projects and eternal family welfare activities are devastated.
threadsEnglish: O Kṛṣṇa, maintainer of the people, I have heard by disciplic succession that those who destroy family traditions dwell always in hell.
englishTransliteration:
utsanna-kula-dharmāṇāṁ manuṣyāṇāṁ janārdana
narake ’niyataṁ vāso bhavatīty anuśuśruma
englishWBW: utsanna (destroyed) — kula-dharmāṇām (of those who have the family traditions) — manuṣyāṇām (of such men) — janārdana (O Kṛṣṇa) — narake (in hell) — aniyatam (indefinite) — vāsaḥ (residence) — bhavati (becomes) — iti (thus) — anuśuśruma (I have heard by disciplic succession)
englishExplain:
Arjuna seeks to validate his fears by citing authority. He says, “I have heard by disciplic succession” that those whose family traditions are destroyed dwell always in hell. He is no longer just giving his opinion; he is quoting what he believes to be scriptural truth.

This is the irony of his illusion. He is quoting scripture to Kṛṣṇa, the original author of the scriptures, to prove that his refusal to fight is the correct position. He is clinging to general moral codes while ignoring the direct order of the Divine present before him.

He believes that his residence in hell is guaranteed if he proceeds with the war. His fear is not of death, but of the eternal consequences of his actions. This belief has completely paralyzed his ability to act as a warrior.

sanskrit:
उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन।
नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम।।
translationEnglish:
O Kṛṣṇa, maintainer of the people, I have heard by disciplic succession
that those whose family traditions are destroyed dwell always in hell.
translationHindi: हे जनार्दन! जिनका कुल-धर्म नष्ट हो गया है, ऐसे मनुष्यों का अनिश्चित काल तक नरक में वास होता है, ऐसा हम सुनते आये हैं।
translationGujarati: હે જનાર્દન! જેમના કુળધર્મ નાશ પામ્યા છે, તેવા મનુષ્યોનો અનિશ્ચિત કાળ સુધી નરકમાં વાસ થાય છે, એવું અમે સાંભળતા આવ્યા છીએ.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna says he has heard that those whose family traditions are destroyed are condemned to dwell in hell indefinitely.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि उन्होंने सुना है कि जिनके कुल-धर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं, उन मनुष्यों को अनिश्चित काल तक नरक में रहना पड़ता है।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કહે છે કે તેમણે સાંભળ્યું છે કે જેમના કુળધર્મ નાશ પામે છે, તેવા મનુષ્યોને અનિશ્ચિત કાળ સુધી નરકમાં રહેવું પડે છે.
tweetEnglish: O Kṛṣṇa, I have heard that those whose family traditions are destroyed dwell always in hell.
threadsEnglish: Alas, how strange it is that we are preparing to commit greatly sinful acts. Driven by the desire to enjoy royal happiness, we are intent on killing our own kinsmen.
englishTransliteration:
aho bata mahat pāpaṁ kartuṁ vyavasitā vayam
yad rājya-sukha-lobhena hantuṁ sva-janam udyatāḥ
englishWBW: aho (alas) — bata (how strange) — mahat (great) — pāpam (sin) — kartum (to perform) — vyavasitāḥ (decided) — vayam (we) — yat (because) — rājya-sukha (royal happiness) — lobhena (driven by greed) — hantum (to kill) — sva-janam (own kinsmen) — udyatāḥ (prepared)
englishExplain:
Arjuna expresses deep regret and amazement at the situation. He laments that they are resolved to commit a great sin, driven solely by the greed for royal happiness. He simplifies the complex political and dharmic struggle into a simple narrative of selfish greed.

He equates the righteous struggle of the Pāṇḍavas with the selfish greed of the Kauravas. By labeling the war as a ‘great sin’, he psychologically distances himself from his duty. He is judging his own potential actions and finding them morally repugnant.

This verse shows the height of his confusion. He sees the execution of justice as a crime because the criminals are his relatives. His values are entirely centered on bodily relationships rather than on the higher principles of truth and justice that Kṛṣṇa is advocating.

sanskrit:
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्।
यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः।।
translationEnglish:
Alas, how strange it is that we are preparing to commit greatly sinful acts.
Driven by the desire to enjoy royal happiness, we are intent on killing our own kinsmen.
translationHindi: हाय! शोक है कि हम लोग बुद्धिमान होकर भी महान पाप करने को तैयार हो गये हैं, जो राज्य और सुख के लोभ से स्वजनों को मारने के लिए उद्यत हुए हैं।
translationGujarati: અરે! શોક છે કે અમે બુદ્ધિમાન હોવા છતાં મહાન પાપ કરવા તૈયાર થયા છીએ, જે રાજ્ય અને સુખના લોભથી સ્વજનોને મારવા તૈયાર થયા છીએ.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna laments that despite their wisdom, they are about to commit a great sin by killing their own kinsmen out of greed for royal happiness.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन शोक प्रकट करते हैं कि हम लोग बुद्धिमान होकर भी कितना बड़ा पाप करने जा रहे हैं, जो राज्य और सुख के लालच में अपने ही स्वजनों को मारने के लिए तैयार हैं।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન શોક વ્યક્ત કરે છે કે અમે લોકો બુદ્ધિમાન હોવા છતાં કેટલું મોટું પાપ કરવા જઈ રહ્યા છીએ, જે રાજ્ય અને સુખના લોભમાં પોતાના જ સ્વજનોને મારવા માટે તૈયાર છીએ.
tweetEnglish: Alas! Driven by greed for royal happiness, we are ready to commit the sin of killing our own kin.
threadsEnglish: Better for me if the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, weapons in hand, were to kill me unarmed and unresisting on the battlefield.
englishTransliteration:
yadi mām apratīkāram aśastraṁ śastra-pāṇayaḥ
dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣemataraṁ bhavet
englishWBW: yadi (if) — mām (me) — apratīkāram (unresisting) — aśastram (unarmed) — śastra-pāṇayaḥ (those with weapons in hand) — dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ (the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra) — raṇe (on the battlefield) — hanyuḥ (should kill) — tat (that) — me (for me) — kṣema-taram (better) — bhavet (would be)
englishExplain:
Arjuna reaches the final conclusion of his despondency. He decides that non-resistance is better than committing the sin of killing. He states that if the armed sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra were to kill him while he was unarmed and unresisting, that would be better for him.

This is an extreme emotional overreaction. A warrior preferring to die unarmed rather than fight is unheard of in the kṣatriya code. It reflects his complete loss of the will to live. He believes that by sacrificing his own life, he might save the family and avoid the sin.

He is adopting a martyr complex born of attachment, not spiritual enlightenment. He would rather be a victim than a victor if victory requires him to hurt those he loves. He has completely abandoned his identity as a protector of Dharma.

sanskrit:
यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः।
धार्तराष्ट्रान रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत्।।
translationEnglish:
Better for me if the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, weapons in hand,
were to kill me unarmed and unresisting on the battlefield.
translationHindi: यदि मुझे शस्त्ररहित और सामना न करने वाले को शस्त्र हाथ में लिये हुए धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्र रण में मार डालें, तो वह मरना भी मेरे लिए अधिक कल्याणकारक होगा।
translationGujarati: જો મને શસ્ત્ર વગરના અને સામનો ન કરનારને શસ્ત્ર હાથમાં લીધેલા ધૃતરાષ્ટ્રના પુત્રો રણમાં મારી નાખે, તો તે મરવું પણ મારા માટે વધુ કલ્યાણકારક હશે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna states that it would be better for him if the armed sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra killed him on the battlefield while he was unarmed and not fighting back.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि यदि शस्त्रधारी कौरव मुझे युद्धभूमि में मार भी डालें, जब मैं निहत्था हूँ और सामना नहीं कर रहा हूँ, तो वह भी मेरे लिए बेहतर होगा।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કહે છે કે જો શસ્ત્રધારી કૌરવો મને યુદ્ધભૂમિમાં મારી પણ નાખે, જ્યારે હું નિઃશસ્ત્ર છું અને સામનો નથી કરી રહ્યો, તો તે પણ મારા માટે વધુ સારું રહેશે.
tweetEnglish: Better for me if the armed sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra kill me unarmed and unresisting on the battlefield.
threadsEnglish: Sañjaya said: Arjuna, having thus spoken on the battlefield, cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
englishTransliteration:
sañjaya uvāca
evam uktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopastha upāviśat
visṛjya sa-śaraṁ cāpaṁ śoka-saṁvigna-mānasaḥ
englishWBW: sañjayaḥ (Sañjaya) — uvāca (said) — evam (thus) — uktvā (speaking) — arjunaḥ (Arjuna) — saṅkhye (in the battlefield) — ratha-upasthe (on the seat of the chariot) — upāviśat (sat down) — visṛjya (putting aside) — sa-śaram (along with arrows) — cāpam (the bow) — śoka (by grief) — saṁvigna (distressed) — mānasaḥ (within the mind)
englishExplain:
Sañjaya concludes the first chapter by describing Arjuna’s physical collapse. Having spoken his mind, Arjuna puts aside his bow and arrows and sits down on the chariot seat, his mind overwhelmed with grief and distress.

The image of the greatest archer in the world dropping his weapon and sitting down in the middle of a battlefield is the ultimate cliffhanger. It signifies the total defeat of the human spirit when faced with the conflict between affection and duty.

The first chapter ends not with a war, but with a breakdown. It sets the perfect stage for Kṛṣṇa to begin His instructions. Arjuna has stated his case and reached his limit; he is now ready to receive a higher wisdom that transcends his material logic.

sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्।
विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः।।
translationEnglish:
Sañjaya said:
Arjuna, having thus spoken on the battlefield, cast aside his bow and arrows
and sat down on the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
translationHindi: संजय बोले: रणभूमि में शोक से उद्विग्न मन वाले अर्जुन इस प्रकार कहकर, बाणसहित धनुष को त्यागकर रथ के पिछले भाग में बैठ गये।
translationGujarati: સંજય બોલ્યા: રણભૂમિમાં શોકથી વ્યાકુળ મનવાળા અર્જુન આમ કહીને, બાણ સહિત ધનુષ્યનો ત્યાગ કરીને રથના પાછલા ભાગમાં બેસી ગયા.
simpleEnglish: Sañjaya concludes that after speaking these words on the battlefield, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the chariot, overwhelmed with grief.
simpleHindi: संजय बताते हैं कि युद्धभूमि में ऐसा कहकर, शोक से व्याकुल मन वाले अर्जुन ने अपना धनुष-बाण त्याग दिया और रथ के पिछले हिस्से में बैठ गए।
simpleGujarati: સંજય જણાવે છે કે રણભૂમિમાં આવું કહીને, શોકથી વ્યાકુળ મનવાળા અર્જુને પોતાનું ધનુષ્ય-બાણ ત્યાગી દીધું અને રથના પાછલા ભાગમાં બેસી ગયા.
tweetEnglish: Sañjaya said: Saying this, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down, overwhelmed with grief.
threadsEnglish: Having thus spoken, Arjuna sat down in the chariot, casting aside his bow and arrows, his heart heavy with sorrow.
englishTransliteration:
sañjaya uvāca
evam uktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopastha upāviśat
vīsṛjya sa-śaraṁ cāpaṁ śoka-saṁvigna-mānasaḥ
englishWBW: sañjayaḥ uvāca (Sañjaya said) — evam (thus) — uktvā (speaking) — arjunaḥ (Arjuna) — saṅkhye (in the battlefield) — ratha-upasthe (on the seat of the chariot) — upāviśat (sat down again) — visṛjya (putting aside) — sa-śaram (along with arrows) — cāpam (the bow) — śoka (by lamentation) — saṁvigna (distressed) — mānasaḥ (within the mind).
englishExplain:
Sañjaya describes the final moment of Arjuna’s collapse before the Gītā dialogue begins. Arjuna, the greatest warrior of his time, is so overwhelmed by grief that he physically cannot stand. He sets aside his famous bow, Gāṇḍīva, and his arrows, collapsing onto the seat of his chariot. His mind is not just sad; it is ‘saṁvigna’, or deeply agitated and trembling with despair.

This verse marks the absolute low point for Arjuna. It shows that even the most powerful individuals can be paralyzed by emotional and moral crises. Arjuna’s physical surrender of his weapons symbolizes his mental surrender to illusion. He feels that no victory could possibly justify the pain of the upcoming conflict.

This setting is crucial because it establishes the need for the Gītā. Kṛṣṇa does not speak until Arjuna is completely broken and recognizes that his own logic has failed him. The silence on the battlefield at this moment is heavy with Arjuna’s silent cry for help, setting the stage for the transcendental wisdom that is about to be revealed.

sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच
तं तथा कृपयाऽविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम्।
विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः।।
translationEnglish:
Sañjaya said:
Seeing Arjuna full of compassion, his mind depressed, his eyes full of tears,
Madhusūdana, Kṛṣṇa, spoke the following words.
translationHindi: संजय बोले: उस प्रकार करुणा से व्याप्त और आंसुओं से पूर्ण तथा व्याकुल नेत्रों वाले शोकयुक्त उस अर्जुन को देखकर मधुसूदन कृष्ण ने यह वचन कहा।
translationGujarati: સંજય બોલ્યા: તે રીતે કરુણાથી વ્યાપ્ત અને આંસુઓથી ભરેલી તથા વ્યાકુળ આંખોવાળા શોકગ્રસ્ત અર્જુનને જોઈને મધુસૂદન કૃષ્ણે આ વચન કહ્યું.
simpleEnglish: Sañjaya describes to Dhṛtarāṣṭra how Lord Kṛṣṇa spoke to Arjuna, who was overwhelmed with compassion and whose eyes were full of tears due to grief.
simpleHindi: संजय धृतराष्ट्र को बताते हैं कि भगवान कृष्ण ने अर्जुन से बात की, जो करुणा से भरे हुए थे और दुःख के कारण जिनकी आँखों में आँसू थे।
simpleGujarati: સંજય ધૃતરાષ્ટ્રને વર્ણવે છે કે ભગવાન કૃષ્ણ અર્જુન સાથે વાત કરે છે, જે કરુણાથી ભરેલા હતા અને દુઃખના કારણે જેમની આંખોમાં આંસુ હતા.
tweetEnglish: Sañjaya said: Seeing Arjuna overwhelmed with compassion and eyes full of tears, Kṛṣṇa spoke these words.
threadsEnglish: Sañjaya said: Seeing Arjuna full of compassion, his mind depressed and his eyes full of tears, Kṛṣṇa spoke these words.
englishTransliteration:
sañjaya uvāca
taṁ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśru-pūrṇākulekṣaṇam
viṣīdantam idaṁ vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ
englishWBW: sañjayaḥ (Sañjaya) — uvāca (said) — tam (unto Arjuna) — tathā (thus) — kṛpayā (by compassion) — āviṣṭam (overwhelmed) — aśru-pūrṇa (full of tears) — ākula (distressed) — īkṣaṇam (eyes) — viṣīdantam (lamenting) — idam (these) — vākyam (words) — uvāca (said) — madhusūdanaḥ (Kṛṣṇa, the killer of Madhu)
englishExplain:
The second chapter begins with Sañjaya describing Arjuna’s condition to the blind king. Arjuna is overwhelmed with compassion, and his eyes are full of brimming tears as he laments on the battlefield. He is in a state of complete emotional and physical collapse.

The use of the word ‘Madhusūdana’ for Kṛṣṇa is significant here. It reminds the reader that Kṛṣṇa is the killer of the demon Madhu. The implication is that just as Kṛṣṇa killed the external demon, He is now about to kill the internal demon of misunderstanding that has taken over Arjuna.

Arjuna’s compassion, though seemingly noble, is misplaced. It is born of material attachment to the temporary body, not spiritual clarity. This emotional weakness is preventing him from performing his higher duty. The stage is set for the Lord to remove this ignorance with divine knowledge.

sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम्।
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन।।
translationEnglish:
The Supreme Personality of Godhead said:
My dear Arjuna, how have these impurities come upon you?
They are not at all befitting a man who knows the value of life.
They lead not to higher planets but to infamy.
translationHindi: श्री भगवान बोले: हे अर्जुन! तुझे इस असमय में यह मोह (अज्ञान) किस हेतु से प्राप्त हुआ? क्योंकि न तो यह श्रेष्ठ पुरुषों द्वारा आचरित है, न स्वर्ग को देने वाला है और न कीर्ति को करने वाला ही है।
translationGujarati: શ્રી ભગવાન બોલ્યા: હે અર્જુન! તને આ કસમયે આવો મોહ (અજ્ઞાન) કયા કારણથી પ્રાપ્ત થયો? કારણ કે આ ન તો શ્રેષ્ઠ પુરુષો દ્વારા આચરવામાં આવેલું છે, ન સ્વર્ગ આપનારું છે કે ન કીર્તિ વધારનારું છે.
simpleEnglish: Lord Kṛṣṇa asks Arjuna where this impurity of mind has come from at such a critical moment, warning him that it does not befit a noble man and leads to disgrace.
simpleHindi: भगवान कृष्ण अर्जुन से पूछते हैं कि ऐसे संकट के समय में उनके मन में यह मोह कहाँ से आ गया, और चेतावनी देते हैं કે यह श्रेष्ठ पुरुषों को शोभा नहीं देता और अपयश का कारण बनता है।
simpleGujarati: ભગવાન કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને પૂછે છે કે આવા કટોકટીના સમયે તેમના મનમાં આ મોહ ક્યાંથી આવ્યો, અને ચેતવણી આપે છે કે આ શ્રેષ્ઠ પુરુષોને શોભતું નથી અને અપયશનું કારણ બને છે.
tweetEnglish: Sri Bhagavan said: My dear Arjuna, how has this impurity come upon you? It leads to infamy, not heaven.
threadsEnglish: The Lord said: My dear Arjuna, how have these impurities come upon you? They are not at all befitting a man who knows the value of life. They lead to infamy, not heaven.
englishTransliteration:
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṁ mohayasīva me
tad ekaṁ vada niścitya yena śreyo ’ham āpnuyām
englishWBW: vyāmiśreṇa (by equivocal) — iva (as if) — vākyena (by words) — buddhim (intelligence) — mohayasi (You are bewildering) — iva (as if) — me (my) — tat (that) — ekam (only one) — vada (please tell) — niścitya (ascertaining) — yena (by which) — śreyaḥ (the ultimate good) — aham (I) — āpnuyām (may achieve)
englishExplain:
Arjuna expresses his frustration with what he perceives as contradictory advice. He says, “Your instructions seem ambiguous, and they are bewildering my intelligence.” He feels like Kṛṣṇa is telling him to be a monk and a soldier at the same time.

Arjuna wants a simple, direct answer. He says, “Tell me decisively which one path is best for me.” He is looking for a ‘yes or no’ solution to his dilemma. He wants the ‘śreyaḥ’, or the highest benefit, but he wants it delivered in a way that doesn’t require him to juggle complex ideas.

This verse reflects the typical struggle of a seeker who wants a quick fix. Kṛṣṇa, however, will not give a simple answer, because life is not simple. He will instead teach Arjuna how to integrate his spiritual understanding with his worldly duties, leading to a much deeper and more stable form of realization.

sanskrit:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप।।
translationEnglish:
O son of Prith, do not yield to this degrading impotence.
It does not become you.
Give up such petty weakness of heart and arise, O chastiser of the enemy.
translationHindi: हे पार्थ! नपुंसकता को मत प्राप्त हो, तुझमें यह उचित नहीं जान पड़ती। हे परन्तप! हृदय की तुच्छ दुर्बलता को त्यागकर युद्ध के लिए खड़ा हो जा।
translationGujarati: હે પાર્થ! નપુિસંકતાને વશ ન થા, તારામાં આ શોભતું નથી. હે પરંતપ! હૃદયની તુચ્છ નિર્બળતા છોડીને યુદ્ધ માટે ઊભો થા.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa urges Arjuna not to give in to this degrading weakness, telling him to abandon such petty faint-heartedness and stand up to fight.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को इस अपमानजनक दुर्बलતા के वश में न होने के लिए कहते हैं और उन्हें हृदय की इस तुच्छ कमजोरी को त्यागकर युद्ध के लिए खड़े होने का आग्रह करते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને આ અપમાનજનક નિર્બળતાને વશ ન થવા કહે છે અને તેમને હૃદયની આ તુચ્છ નબળાઈ છોડીને યુદ્ધ માટે ઊભા થવાનો આગ્રહ કરે છે.
tweetEnglish: Do not yield to this impotence. Give up petty weakness of heart and arise, O chastiser of the enemy!
threadsEnglish: O son of Pritha, do not yield to this degrading impotence. Give up such petty weakness of heart and arise, O chastiser of the enemy!
englishTransliteration:
klaibyaṁ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate
kṣudraṁ hṛdaya-daurbalyaṁ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa
englishWBW: klaibyam (impotence) — mā sma (do not) — gamaḥ (yield to) — pārtha (O son of Pṛthā) — na (never) — etat (this) — tvayi (unto you) — upapadyate (is befitting) — kṣudram (petty) — hṛdaya (of the heart) — daurbalyam (weakness) — tyaktvā (giving up) — uttiṣṭha (get up) — parantapa (O chastiser of the enemies)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa continues His rebuke with strong words. He tells Arjuna, “Do not yield to this degrading impotence.” For a mighty warrior like Arjuna, being called impotent or weak is the ultimate insult. Kṛṣṇa insists that this behavior is not befitting his character.

He commands Arjuna to give up this ‘petty weakness of heart’ and arise. Kṛṣṇa identifies Arjuna’s non-violence not as a spiritual virtue, but as a temporary failure of courage. He urges him to be a ‘Parantapa’, or a chastiser of enemies, rather than being chastised by his own emotions.

This verse is a clarion call to rise above mental weakness and perform one’s duty with strength. It establishes that true spirituality is not about escaping one’s responsibilities, but about having the inner fortitude to face them, no matter how difficult they appear.

sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच
कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन।
इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन।।
translationEnglish:
Arjuna said:
O killer of enemies, O Madhusūdana, how can I counterattack with arrows in battle men like Bhīma and Droṇa, who are worthy of my worship?
translationHindi: अर्जुन बोले: हे मधुसूदन! मैं रणभूमि में किस प्रकार बाणों से भीष्म पितामह और द्रोणाचार्य के विरुद्ध लड़ूँगा? हे अरिसूदन! वे दोनों ही पूजनीय हैं।
translationGujarati: અર્જુન બોલ્યા: હે મધુસૂદન! હું રણભૂમિમાં કેવી રીતે ભીષ્મ પિતામહ અને દ્રોણાચાર્ય સામે બાણોથી લડીશ? હે અરિસૂદન! તેઓ બંને પૂજનીય છે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna asks Kṛṣṇa how he can possibly fight with arrows against Bhīma and Droṇa, who are worthy of his worship and respect.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कृष्ण से पूछते हैं कि वे भीष्म और द्रोण जैसे पूजनीय जनों के विरुद्ध युद्धभूमि में बाणों से कैसे लड़ सकते हैं।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કૃષ્ણને પૂછે છે કે તેઓ ભીષ્મ અને દ્રોણ જેવા પૂજનીય લોકો સામે રણભૂમિમાં બાણોથી કેવી રીતે લડી શકે.
tweetEnglish: Arjuna said: O Madhusūdana, how can I fight with arrows against Bhīma and Droṇa, who are worthy of my worship?
threadsEnglish: Arjuna said: O Madhusūdana, how can I counterattack with arrows in battle men like Bhīṣma and Droṇa, who are worthy of my worship?
englishTransliteration:
Arjuna uvāca
kathaṁ bhīṣmam ahaṁ saṅkhye droṇaṁ ca madhusūdana
iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāv ari-sūdana
englishWBW: arjunaḥ (Arjuna) — uvāca (said) — katham (how) — bhīṣmam (Bhīṣma) — aham (I) — saṅkhye (in the fight) — droṇam (Droṇa) — ca (also) — madhusūdana (O killer of Madhu) — iṣubhiḥ (with arrows) — pratiyotsyāmi (shall counterattack) — pūjā-arhau (those who are worthy of worship) — ari-sūdana (O killer of enemies)
englishExplain:
Arjuna defends his hesitation. He is stung by Kṛṣṇa’s words but tries to explain his moral dilemma. He asks, “How can I counterattack Bhīṣma and Droṇa with arrows when they are worthy of my worship?” In Vedic culture, one offers flowers to the feet of a guru, not arrows.

Arjuna feels that fighting them would be a sacrilege. He addresses Kṛṣṇa as ‘Ari-sūdana’, the killer of enemies, implying that while Kṛṣṇa kills actual enemies, these men are Arjuna’s beloved elders. He feels he is being asked to do something fundamentally wrong.

Arjuna is still viewing the situation through the lens of worldly morality. He believes that respect for elders is an absolute rule that overrides all other duties. He is struggling to reconcile his role as a soldier with his identity as a devoted student and grandson.

sanskrit:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्
श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव
भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान्।।
translationEnglish:
It would be better to live in this world by begging than to live at the cost of the lives of great souls who are my teachers.
Even though desiring worldly gain, they are superiors.
If they are killed, everything we enjoy will be tainted with blood.
translationHindi: महानुभाव गुरुजनों को न मारकर मैं इस लोक में भिक्षा का अन्न भी खाना कल्याणकारक समझता हूँ। क्योंकि गुरुजनों को मारकर भी इस लोक में रुधिर से सने हुए अर्थ और कामरूप भोगों को ही तो भोगूँगा।
translationGujarati: મહાનુભાવ ગુરુજનોને ન મારીને હું આ લોકમાં ભિક્ષાનું અન્ન ખાવું પણ કલ્યાણકારી માનું છું. કારણ કે ગુરુજનોને મારીને પણ આ લોકમાં હું લોહીથી ખરડાયેલા અર્થ અને કામરૂપ ભોગોને જ ભોગવીશ.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna states that he would rather live by begging than kill his noble teachers, arguing that any wealth or pleasure gained by killing them would be tainted with their blood.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि अपने महान गुरुओं को मारने की बजाय वे भीख मांगकर जीना बेहतर समझते हैं, क्योंकि उन्हें मारने से मिलने वाला हर भोग उनके खून से सना होगा।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કહે છે કે પોતાના મહાન ગુરુઓને મારવા કરતા તેઓ ભિક્ષા માંગીને જીવવું વધુ સારું માને છે, કારણ કે તેમને મારવાથી મળનારો દરેક ભોગ તેમના લોહીથી ખરડાયેલો હશે.
tweetEnglish: It is better to live by begging than to kill my teachers. Any gain would be tainted with their blood.
threadsEnglish: It is better to live by begging than to live at the cost of the lives of my great teachers. Tainted with blood, their deaths would turn any gain into sorrow.
englishTransliteration:
gurūn ahatvā hi mahānubhāvān
śreyo bhoktuṁ bhaikṣyam apīha loke
hatvārtha-kāmāṁs tu gurūn ihaiva
bhuñjīya bhogān rudhira-pradigdhān
englishWBW: gurūn (the teachers) — ahatvā (not killing) — hi (certainly) — mahā-anubhāvān (great souls) — śreyaḥ (better) — bhoktum (to enjoy) — bhaikṣyam (by begging) — api (even) — iha (in this) — loke (world) — hatvā (killing) — artha (gain) — kāmān (desiring) — tu (but) — gurūn (superiors) — iha (in this world) — eva (certainly) — bhuñjīya (has to enjoy) — bhogān (enjoyable things) — rudhira (blood) — pradigdhān (tainted with)
englishExplain:
Arjuna presents a radical alternative. He says it would be better to live in this world by begging than to live at the cost of the lives of his great teachers. For a kṣatriya, begging is considered a great disgrace, yet Arjuna prefers it over the guilt of killing his gurus.

He argues that even though his teachers might be desiring worldly gain by siding with the Kauravas, they are still his superiors. He claims that any kingdom or pleasure he obtains after killing them would be tainted with their blood. To him, victory would feel like a crime.

Arjuna’s logic is driven by a deep sense of personal consequence. He feels that the ‘wealth’ he would win would be forever haunted by the memory of the massacre. He is willing to accept social shame (begging) to avoid what he perceives as a spiritual and emotional catastrophe.

sanskrit:
न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो
यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः।
यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषाम
स्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः।।
translationEnglish:
Nor do we know which is better—conquering them or being conquered by them.
If we killed the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, we should not care to live.
Yet they are now standing before us on the battlefield.
translationHindi: हम यह भी नहीं जानते कि हमारे लिए युद्ध करना और न करना - इन दोनों में से कौन-सा श्रेष्ठ है, अथवा यह भी नहीं जानते कि उन्हें हम जीतेंगे या वे हमको जीतेंगे। जिनको मारकर हम जीना भी नहीं चाहते, वे ही धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्र हमारे सामने खड़े हैं।
translationGujarati: અમે એ પણ નથી જાણતા કે અમારા માટે યુદ્ધ કરવું કે ન કરવું - આ બંનેમાંથી કયું શ્રેષ્ઠ છે, અથવા એ પણ નથી જાણતા કે અમે તેમને જીતીશું કે તેઓ અમને જીતશે. જેમને મારીને અમે જીવવા પણ નથી ઈચ્છતા, તે જ ધૃતરાષ્ટ્રના પુત્રો અમારી સામે ઉભા છે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna is confused and does not know whether it is better to conquer them or be conquered, as killing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra would make life meaningless.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन उलझन में हैं और नहीं जानते कि उन्हें जीतना चाहिए या हारना, क्योंकि धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को मारने के बाद जीवन का कोई अर्थ नहीं रह जाएगा।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન મૂંઝવણમાં છે અને નથી જાણતા કે તેમને જીતવું જોઈએ કે હારવું, કારણ કે ધૃતરાષ્ટ્રના પુત્રોને માર્યા પછી જીવનનો કોઈ અર્થ રહેશે નહીં.
tweetEnglish: We know not what is better: conquering them or being conquered. If we kill them, we won’t want to live.
threadsEnglish: We know not which is better—conquering them or being conquered. If we kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, we should not care to live.
englishTransliteration:
na caitad vidmaḥ kataran no garīyo
yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ
yān eva hatvā na jijīviṣāmas
te ’vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
englishWBW: na (neither) — ca (also) — etat (this) — vidmaḥ (do we know) — katarat (which) — naḥ (for us) — garīyaḥ (better) — yat vā (whether) — jayema (we may conquer) — yadi (if) — vā (or) — naḥ (us) — jayeyuḥ (they may conquer) — yān (those whom) — eva (certainly) — hatvā (by killing) — na (never) — jijīviṣāmaḥ (we would want to live) — te (all of them) — avasthitāḥ (are situated) — pramukhe (in the front) — dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ (the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra)
englishExplain:
Arjuna admits his complete confusion about the outcome of the war. He says he doesn’t know which is better: conquering them or being conquered by them. He has reached a point where even victory seems like a defeat because he wouldn’t care to live after killing his cousins.

He sees the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra standing before him, and he feels that his life is tied to theirs in a way that makes their destruction synonymous with his own misery. He is caught in a double-bind where every possible choice feels like a loss.

Arjuna acknowledges that his own intelligence is no longer sufficient to discern the right path. He is paralyzed by the paradox of his situation. This admission of helplessness is the final step before his total surrender to Kṛṣṇa as a student.

sanskrit:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः
पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः।
यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मे
शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम्।।
translationEnglish:
Now I am confused about my duty and have lost all composure because of miserly weakness.
In this condition I am asking You to tell me for certain what is best for me.
I am Your disciple, and a soul surrendered unto You. Please instruct me.
translationHindi: कायरता-रूप दोष से उपहत हुए स्वभाव वाला और धर्म के विषय में मोहित-चित्त हुआ मैं आपसे पूछता हूँ कि जो साधन निश्चित कल्याणकारक हो, वह मेरे लिए कहिये। मैं आपका शिष्य हूँ, इसलिए आपके शरण हुए मुझको शिक्षा दीजिये।
translationGujarati: કાયરતા રૂપી દોષથી હણાયેલા સ્વભાવવાળો અને ધર્મના વિષયમાં મોહિત થયેલા ચિત્તવાળો હું આપને પૂછું છું કે જે સાધન નિશ્ચિત કલ્યાણકારી હોય તે મને કહો. હું આપનો શિષ્ય છું, તેથી આપના શરણે આવેલા મને ઉપદેશ આપો.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna admits he is confused about his duty due to weakness and surrenders to Kṛṣṇa as a disciple, asking Him to say definitively what is best for him.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन स्वीकार करते हैं कि वे अपनी कमजोरी के कारण धर्म के विषय में भ्रमित हैं और कृष्ण की शरण लेते हुए शिष्य के रूप में पूछते हैं कि उनके लिए निश्चित रूप से क्या श्रेयस्कर है।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન સ્વીકારે છે કે તેઓ પોતાની નબળાઈના કારણે ધર્મના વિષયમાં ભ્રમિત છે અને કૃષ્ણના શરણે જઈને શિષ્ય તરીકે પૂછે છે કે તેમના માટે નિશ્ચિતપણે શું શ્રેયસ્કર છે.
tweetEnglish: I am confused about my duty. I am Your disciple surrendered to You. Tell me decisively what is best.
threadsEnglish: I am confused about my duty and have lost composure. I am Your disciple, a soul surrendered unto You. Please instruct me definitively on what is best.
englishTransliteration:
kārpaṇya-doṣopahata-svabhāvaḥ
pṛcchāmi tvāṁ Dharma-sammūḍha-cetāḥ
yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṁ brūhi tan me
śiṣyas te ’haṁ śādhi māṁ tvāṁ prapannam
englishWBW: kārpaṇya (of miserliness) — doṣa (by the weakness) — upahata (being affected) — svabhāvaḥ (characteristics) — pṛcchāmi (I am asking) — tvām (unto You) — Dharma (religion) — sammūḍha (bewildered) — cetāḥ (in heart) — yat (what) — śreyaḥ (all-good) — syāt (may be) — niścitam (confidently) — brūhi (tell) — tat (that) — me (unto me) — śiṣyaḥ (disciple) — te (Your) — aham (I am) — śādhi (instruct) — mām (me) — tvām (unto You) — prapannam (surrendered)
englishExplain:
This is a pivotal verse in the Gītā. Arjuna finally admits defeat—not to the enemy, but to his own confusion. He says he is afflicted by the ‘weakness of miserliness’ and is bewildered about his duty. He asks Kṛṣṇa to tell him for certain what is best for him.

Arjuna formally declares, “I am Your disciple and a soul surrendered unto You. Please instruct me.” This shift in the relationship is essential. As long as they were just friends, Kṛṣṇa’s advice was casual. Now that Arjuna has surrendered, Kṛṣṇa takes on the role of the Guru.

This surrender is the prerequisite for receiving transcendental knowledge. Arjuna has emptied his cup of material logic and is now ready to be filled with divine wisdom. He realizes that only a higher authority can solve his existential crisis and guide him toward the ultimate good.

sanskrit:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्या
द्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम्।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्
राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम्।।
translationEnglish:
I can find no means to drive away this grief which is drying up my senses.
I will not be able to dispel it even if I win a prosperous, unrivaled kingdom on earth with sovereignty like the demigods in heaven.
translationHindi: क्योंकि भूमि में निष्कण्टक, धन-धान्य सम्पन्न राज्य को और देवताओं के स्वामीपने को प्राप्त होकर भी मैं उस उपाय को नहीं देखता हूँ, जो मेरी इन्द्रियों को सुखाने वाले इस शोक को दूर कर सके।
translationGujarati: કારણ કે પૃથ્વી પર નિષ્કંટક, ધન-ધાન્ય સમૃદ્ધ રાજ્ય અને દેવતાઓનું સ્વામિત્વ પામીને પણ હું એવો કોઈ ઉપાય જોતો નથી, જે મારી ઇન્દ્રિયોને સુકવનારા આ શોકને દૂર કરી શકે.
simpleEnglish: Arjuna says that obtaining an unrivaled kingdom on earth or even sovereignty over the demigods would not drive away the grief that is drying up his senses.
simpleHindi: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि पृथ्वी पर निष्कंटक राज्य या देवताओं का स्वामित्व भी उस शोक को दूर नहीं कर सकता जो उनकी इंद्रियों को सुखा रहा है।
simpleGujarati: અર્જુન કહે છે કે પૃથ્વી પર નિષ્કંટક રાજ્ય કે દેવતાઓનું સ્વામિત્વ પણ તે શોકને દૂર કરી શકતું નથી જે તેમની ઇન્દ્રિયોને સુકવી રહ્યો છે.
tweetEnglish: Even an unrivaled kingdom on earth or sovereignty like the gods cannot drive away this grief.
threadsEnglish: I find no means to drive away this grief drying up my senses, even if I win an unrivaled kingdom on earth or sovereignty like the gods.
englishTransliteration:
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād
yac chokam ucchoṣaṇam indriyāṇām
avāpya bhūmāv asapatnam ṛddhaṁ
rājyaṁ surāṇām api cādhipatyam
englishWBW: na (not) — hi (certainly) — prapaśyāmi (do I see) — mama (my) — apanudyāt (can drive away) — yat (which) — śokam (lamentation) — ucchoṣaṇam (drying up) — indriyāṇām (of the senses) — avāpya (after achieving) — bhūmau (on the earth) — asapatnam (without a rival) — ṛddham (prosperous) — rājyam (kingdom) — surāṇām (of the demigods) — api (even) — ca (also) — ādhipatyam (supremacy)
englishExplain:
Arjuna explains why he has surrendered. He says he can find no means to drive away the grief that is drying up his senses. He confesses that even if he were to win a prosperous, unrivaled kingdom on earth or even sovereignty over the gods, his sorrow would remain.

This is a profound realization. Arjuna understands that material solutions—wealth, power, and status—cannot solve spiritual problems like existential grief and confusion about duty. He realizes that an earthly or heavenly throne cannot fill the hole in his heart.

He needs a solution that transcends the material plane. By rejecting the ultimate material rewards as insufficient, he shows that he is ready for the highest spiritual truth. He knows that only Kṛṣṇa’s instructions can provide the peace that the world cannot give.

sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह।।
translationEnglish:
Sañjaya said:
Having spoken thus, Arjuna, chastiser of enemies, told Kṛṣṇa, “Govinda, I shall not fight,” and fell silent.
translationHindi: संजय बोले: हे राजन्! निद्राजयी अर्जुन अन्तर्यामी श्री कृष्ण महाराज से ‘गोविन्द! मैं युद्ध नहीं करूँगा’ - यह साफ कहकर चुप हो गये।
translationGujarati: સંજય બોલ્યા: હે રાજન! નિદ્રાજયી અર્જુન અંતર્યામી શ્રી કૃષ્ણ ભગવાનને ‘ગોવિંદ! હું યુદ્ધ નહીં કરું’ - એમ સ્પષ્ટ કહીને મૌન થઈ ગયા.
simpleEnglish: Sañjaya narrates that after speaking to Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna declared “I shall not fight” and then fell silent.
simpleHindi: संजय बताते हैं कि कृष्ण से बात करने के बाद, अर्जुन ने साफ कह दिया “मैं युद्ध नहीं करूँगा” और फिर चुप हो गए।
simpleGujarati: સંજય વર્ણવે છે કે કૃષ્ણ સાથે વાત કર્યા પછી, અર્જુને સ્પષ્ટ કહી દીધું “હું યુદ્ધ નહીં કરું” અને પછી મૌન થઈ ગયા.
tweetEnglish: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus, Arjuna told Kṛṣṇa, ‘Govinda, I shall not fight,’ and fell silent.
threadsEnglish: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus, Arjuna told Kṛṣṇa, ‘Govinda, I shall not fight,’ and fell silent.
englishTransliteration:
sañjaya uvāca
evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaṁ guḍākeśaḥ parantapa
na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṁ babhūva ha
englishWBW: sañjayaḥ (Sañjaya) — uvāca (said) — evam (thus) — uktvā (speaking) — hṛṣīkeśam (unto Kṛṣṇa) — guḍākeśaḥ (Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep) — parantapa (the chastiser of enemies) — na yotsye (I shall not fight) — iti (thus) — govindam (unto Kṛṣṇa) — uktvā (saying) — tūṣṇīm (silent) — babhūva (became) — ha (certainly)
englishExplain:
Sañjaya narrates Arjuna’s final stance before the teaching begins. Addressing Kṛṣṇa as ‘Govinda’, Arjuna makes his definitive refusal: “I shall not fight.” After speaking his mind and surrendering as a disciple, he falls completely silent.

This silence is significant. It is the silence of a student waiting for the teacher. Arjuna has exhausted his arguments, admitted his helplessness, and is now ready to receive. He has ‘stopped’ his own mental machinery to allow Kṛṣṇa’s words to enter.

Sañjaya addresses Arjuna as ‘Guḍākeśa’, the conqueror of sleep and ignorance, implying that he is now moving toward enlightenment. The tension on the battlefield is at its peak as the greatest warrior sits in silence, waiting for the Supreme Lord to speak.

sanskrit:
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः।।
translationEnglish: O descendant of Bhārata, at that time Kṛṣṇa, smiling, in the midst of both the armies, spoke the following words to the grief-stricken Arjuna.
translationHindi: हे भरतवंशी धृतराष्ट्र! अन्तर्यामी श्री कृष्ण महाराज ने दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में उस विषादयुक्त अर्जुन को हँसते हुए से यह वचन कहे।
translationGujarati: હે ભારતવંશી ધૃતરાષ્ટ્ર! અંતર્યામી શ્રી કૃષ્ણ ભગવાને બંને સેનાઓની વચ્ચે તે વિષાદગ્રસ્ત અર્જુનને હસતા હોય તેમ આ વચન કહ્યા.
simpleEnglish: Sañjaya says that Lord Kṛṣṇa, standing between the two armies, smiled and spoke these words to the grief-stricken Arjuna.
simpleHindi: संजय कहते हैं कि दोनों सेनाओं के बीच खड़े भगवान कृष्ण ने मुस्कुराते हुए शोकग्रस्त अर्जुन से ये वचन कहे।
simpleGujarati: સંજય કહે છે કે બંને સેનાઓની વચ્ચે ઉભેલા ભગવાન કૃષ્ણે હસતા હસતા શોકગ્રસ્ત અર્જુનને આ વચન કહ્યા.
tweetEnglish: O Bhārata, standing between the armies, Kṛṣṇa smiled and spoke these words to the grief-stricken Arjuna.
threadsEnglish: O descendant of Bhārata, at that time Kṛṣṇa, smiling in the midst of both armies, spoke these words to the grief-stricken Arjuna.
englishTransliteration:
tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata
senayor ubhayor madhye viṣīdantam idaṁ vacaḥ
englishWBW: tam (unto him) — uvāca (said) — hṛṣīkeśaḥ (Lord Kṛṣṇa) — prahasan (smiling) — iva (as if) — bhārata (O descendant of Bharata) — senayoḥ (of the armies) — ubhayoḥ (of both) — madhye (in the midst) — viṣīdantam (unto the lamenting one) — idam (these) — vacaḥ (words)
englishExplain:
Sañjaya sets the scene for the divine instruction. He says that Lord Kṛṣṇa, standing between the two armies, spoke to the grieving Arjuna ‘prahasann iva’, or as if smiling. This smile is iconic and carries deep meaning.

Kṛṣṇa’s smile indicates that He is not disturbed by the crisis; He sees it as a delusion that can be easily removed by knowledge. While Arjuna is crying, Kṛṣṇa is calm and cheerful, showing the difference between the bound soul and the liberated Lord.

Kṛṣṇa is about to take on the role of the Universal Teacher. The casual friendship is suspended, and the serious philosophical discourse begins. This moment marks the transition from the narrative setup to the spiritual heart of the Bhagavad-gītā, where the eternal truths of the soul are revealed.

sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः।।
translationEnglish:
The Supreme Personality of Godhead said:
While speaking learned words, you are mourning for what is not worthy of grief.
Those who are wise lament neither for the living nor for the dead.
translationHindi: श्री भगवान बोले: हे अर्जुन! तू न शोक करने योग्य मनुष्यों के लिए शोक करता है और पण्डितों के से वचनों को कहता है; परन्तु जिनके प्राण चले गये हैं, उनके लिए और जिनके प्राण नहीं गये हैं उनके लिए भी पण्डितजन शोक नहीं करते।
translationGujarati: શ્રી ભગવાન બોલ્યા: હે અર્જુન! તું શોક ન કરવા યોગ્ય મનુષ્યો માટે શોક કરે છે અને પંડિતો જેવા વચનો બોલે છે; પરંતુ જેમના પ્રાણ ચાલ્યા ગયા છે તેમના માટે અને જેમના પ્રાણ નથી ગયા તેમના માટે પણ જ્ઞાનીઓ શોક કરતા નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna that while he speaks like a learned man, he is grieving for things not worthy of grief, as the wise mourn neither for the living nor the dead.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि तुम ज्ञानियों जैसी बातें तो करते हो, लेकिन उन चीजों के लिए शोक कर रहे हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, क्योंकि बुद्धिमान लोग न तो जीवित के लिए और न ही मृत के लिए शोक करते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને કહે છે કે તું જ્ઞાનીઓ જેવી વાતો તો કરે છે, પરંતુ એ વસ્તુઓ માટે શોક કરી રહ્યો છે જે શોક કરવા યોગ્ય નથી, કારણ કે બુદ્ધિમાન લોકો ન તો જીવિત માટે કે ન તો મૃત માટે શોક કરે છે.
tweetEnglish: You speak learned words but mourn for what is not worthy. The wise lament neither for the living nor dead.
threadsEnglish: The Lord said: While speaking learned words, you mourn for what is not worthy of grief. Those who are wise lament neither for the living nor for the dead.
englishTransliteration:
śrī-bhagavān uvāca
aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṁ prajñā-vādāṁś ca bhāṣase
gatāsūn agatāsūṁś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
englishWBW: śrī-bhagavān (the Supreme Personality of Godhead) — uvāca (said) — aśocyān (not worthy of grief) — anvaśocaḥ (you are lamenting) — tvam (you) — prajñā-vādān (learned talks) — ca (also) — bhāṣase (you are speaking) — gata (lost) — asūn (life) — agata (not lost) — asūn (life) — ca (also) — na (never) — anuśocanti (lament) — paṇḍitāḥ (the learned)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa begins His instruction by exposing the contradiction in Arjuna’s behavior. He says, “While speaking learned words, you are mourning for what is not worthy of grief.” Arjuna had been quoting scriptures to justify his refusal to fight, but Kṛṣṇa points out that a truly wise person does not lament for the body.

The learned, or ‘paṇḍitāḥ’, understand that the body is temporary and destined to perish. Therefore, they do not grieve for the living or the dead. They focus on the eternal soul, which cannot be destroyed. Kṛṣṇa is essentially saying that Arjuna’s ‘philosophy’ is just a cover for his emotional confusion.

This verse establishes the first principle of the Gītā: the distinction between the body and the soul. Grieving for the inevitable destruction of the material shell is a sign of ignorance, not wisdom. Kṛṣṇa invites Arjuna to shift his perspective from the temporary to the eternal.

sanskrit:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्।।
translationEnglish:
Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings;
nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.
translationHindi: न तो ऐसा ही है कि मैं किसी काल में नहीं था, या तू नहीं था, अथवा ये राजा लोग नहीं थे और न ऐसा ही है कि इससे आगे हम सब नहीं रहेंगे।
translationGujarati: એવું નથી કે હું કોઈ કાળે નહોતો, કે તું નહોતો, અથવા આ રાજાઓ નહોતા અને એવું પણ નથી કે ભવિષ્યમાં આપણે બધા નહીં હોઈએ.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains the eternity of the soul, stating that there was never a time when He, Arjuna, or these kings did not exist, nor will they ever cease to exist.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण आत्मा की नित्यता को समझाते हुए कहते हैं कि ऐसा कोई समय नहीं था जब मैं, तुम या ये राजा नहीं थे, और न ही ऐसा होगा कि हम भविष्य में नहीं रहेंगे।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ આત્માની નિત્યતા સમજાવતા કહે છે કે એવો કોઈ સમય નહોતો જ્યારે હું, તું કે આ રાજાઓ નહોતા, અને એવું પણ નથી કે આપણે ભવિષ્યમાં નહીં હોઈએ.
tweetEnglish: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings; nor in the future shall we cease to be.
threadsEnglish: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.
englishTransliteration:
na tv evāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ
na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param
englishWBW: na (never) — tu (but) — eva (certainly) — aham (I) — jātu (at any time) — na (did not) — āsam (exist) — na (not) — tvam (you) — na (not) — ime (all these) — janā-adhipāḥ (kings) — na (never) — ca (also) — eva (certainly) — na (not) — bhaviṣyāmaḥ (shall exist) — sarve (all of us) — vayam (we) — ataḥ param (hereafter)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa begins the instruction on the immortality of the soul. He states that there was never a time when He did not exist, nor Arjuna, nor all the kings present on the battlefield. Furthermore, He says that none of them will ever cease to exist in the future.

This verse establishes the eternal individuality of the soul. Kṛṣṇa confirms that our existence is not a temporary fluke of matter, but a permanent spiritual reality. This crushes Arjuna’s fear of ‘killing’ the kings, for if the soul never dies, their existence is not being terminated, only their physical covering is being removed.

Kṛṣṇa uses the plural ‘vayam’ (we), showing that both God and the individual souls are eternally distinct individuals. This is the foundation of spiritual understanding: we are eternal beings who have existed in the past and will continue to exist forever, regardless of the fate of our bodies.

sanskrit:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति।।
translationEnglish:
As the embodied soul continuously passes, in this body, from boyhood to youth to old age,
the soul similarly passes into another body at death.
A sober person is not bewildered by such a change.
translationHindi: जैसे जीवात्मा की इस देह में बालकपन, जवानी और वृद्धावस्था होती है, वैसे ही अन्य शरीर की प्राप्ति होती है; उस विषय में धीर पुरुष मोहित नहीं होता।
translationGujarati: જેમ જીવાત્માને આ શરીરમાં બાળપણ, યુવાની અને વૃદ્ધાવસ્થા આવે છે, તેવી જ રીતે અન્ય શરીરની પ્રાપ્તિ થાય છે; તે બાબતમાં ધીર પુરુષ મોહિત થતો નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa uses an analogy to explain that just as the soul passes from childhood to youth to old age in this body, it similarly passes into a new body at death, which does not bewilder the wise.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि जैसे आत्मा इस शरीर में बचपन से जवानी और फिर बुढ़ापे में जाती है, वैसे ही मृत्यु के बाद वह दूसरे शरीर में जाती है, जिससे धीर पुरुष मोहित नहीं होते।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે જેમ આત્મા આ શરીરમાં બાળપણથી યુવાની અને પછી વૃદ્ધાવસ્થામાં જાય છે, તેવી જ રીતે મૃત્યુ પછી તે બીજા શરીરમાં જાય છે, જેનાથી ધીર પુરુષો મોહિત થતા નથી.
tweetEnglish: As the soul passes from childhood to youth to old age, it similarly passes to a new body. Wise are not baffled.
threadsEnglish: As the soul passes from childhood to youth to old age in this body, it similarly passes into another body at death. A sober person is not bewildered by this.
englishTransliteration:
dehino ’smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā
tathā dehāntara-prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati
englishWBW: dehinaḥ (of the embodied) — asmin (in this) — yathā (as) — dehe (in the body) — kaumāram (boyhood) — yauvanam (youth) — jarā (old age) — tathā (similarly) — deha-antara (of another body) — prāptiḥ (achievement) — dhīraḥ (the sober) — tatra (thereupon) — na (never) — muhyati (is deluded)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa uses a simple analogy to explain the migration of the soul. Just as the embodied soul passes through boyhood, youth, and old age within a single lifetime, it similarly passes into another body at the moment of death. The ‘I’ remains the same even as the body changes.

We do not cry when a child becomes an adult, even though the ‘child’ body has technically disappeared. We know the person is the same. Kṛṣṇa says a ‘dhīraḥ’, or a sober and wise person, is not deluded by this final change called death. They see it as just another transition in a long journey.

Arjuna is worried about the loss of his relatives, but Kṛṣṇa assures him that they are simply changing their ‘dress’. The grandfather Bhīṣma he sees now is an eternal soul in an old body. If he dies, he will simply accept a new body. This perspective removes the sting of death and turns it into a natural evolutionary process.

sanskrit:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत।।
translationEnglish:
O son of Kunti, the nonpermanent appearance of happiness and distress, and their disappearance in due course, are like the appearance and disappearance of winter and summer seasons.
They arise from sense perception, O scion of Bhārata, and one must learn to tolerate them without being disturbed.
translationHindi: हे कुन्तीपुत्र! सर्दी-गर्मी और सुख-दुःख को देने वाले इन्द्रिय और विषयों के संयोग तो उत्पत्ति-विनाशशील और अनित्य हैं; इसलिए हे भारत! उनको तू सहन कर।
translationGujarati: હે કુંતીપુત્ર! ઠંડી-ગરમી અને સુખ-દુઃખ આપનારા ઇન્દ્રિયો અને વિષયોના સંયોગ તો ઉત્પત્તિ-વિનાશશીલ અને અનિત્ય છે; તેથી હે ભારત! તું તેને સહન કર.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa advises Arjuna to tolerate happiness and distress, explaining that they are temporary like the changing seasons and arise from sense perception.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को सुख और दुःख सहन करने की सलाह देते हैं और समझाते हैं कि ये बदलते मौसम की तरह अस्थायी हैं और इंद्रियों के संयोग से उत्पन्न होते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને સુખ અને દુઃખ સહન કરવાની સલાહ આપે છે અને સમજાવે છે કે આ બદલાતી ઋતુઓની જેમ અસ્થાયી છે અને ઇન્દ્રિયોના સંયોગથી ઉત્પન્ન થાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Happiness and distress come and go like seasons. They are temporary; learn to tolerate them, O Arjuna.
threadsEnglish: O son of Kunti, the temporary appearance of happiness and distress is like the changing seasons. They arise from sense perception; learn to tolerate them.
englishTransliteration:
mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ
āgamāpāyino ’nityās tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata
englishWBW: mātrā-sparśāḥ (sensory perception) — tu (only) — kaunteya (O son of Kuntī) — śīta (cold) — uṣṇa (heat) — sukha (happiness) — duḥkha (distress) — dāḥ (giving) — āgama-apāyinaḥ (appearing and disappearing) — anityāḥ (nonpermanent) — tān (all of them) — titikṣasva (just try to tolerate) — bhārata (O descendant of Bharata)
englishExplain:
Arjuna might argue that even if the soul is eternal, the pain of separation is real. Kṛṣṇa addresses this by advising tolerance. He explains that happiness and distress arise from sense perception, much like the changing seasons of winter and summer.

These feelings are ‘āgamāpāyino’, meaning they come and go. They are temporary and nonpermanent. Just as one tolerates the freezing cold to do their work, or the scorching heat to perform a task, one must learn to tolerate the emotional highs and lows of life without being derailed from one’s duty.

Kṛṣṇa commands, “Just try to tolerate them.” He doesn’t say the pain isn’t there; He says it is fleeting. A warrior cannot abandon the field because the sun is too hot. Similarly, Arjuna cannot abandon his Dharma because his mind is currently distressed. Emotional resilience is the key to spiritual stability.

sanskrit:
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते।।
translationEnglish: O best among men (Arjuna), the person who is not disturbed by happiness and distress and is steady in both is certainly eligible for liberation.
translationHindi: हे पुरुषश्रेष्ठ! दुःख-सुख को समान समझने वाले जिस धीर पुरुष को ये इन्द्रिय और विषयों के संयोग व्याकुल नहीं करते, वह मोक्ष के योग्य होता है।
translationGujarati: હે પુરુષશ્રેષ્ઠ! સુખ-દુઃખને સમાન માનનારા જે ધીર પુરુષને આ ઇન્દ્રિયો અને વિષયોના સંયોગ વ્યાકુળ નથી કરતા, તે મોક્ષને યોગ્ય બને છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa states that the person who remains calm and undisturbed by both happiness and distress is fit for liberation.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जो व्यक्ति सुख और दुःख दोनों में समान भाव रखता है और विचलित नहीं होता, वही मोक्ष का पात्र है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે જે વ્યક્તિ સુખ અને દુઃખ બંનેમાં સમાન ભાવ રાખે છે અને વિચલિત થતો નથી, તે જ મોક્ષને પાત્ર છે.
tweetEnglish: O Arjuna, the person undisturbed by happiness and distress, steady in both, is eligible for liberation.
threadsEnglish: O best among men, the person who is not disturbed by happiness and distress, remaining steady in both, is eligible for liberation.
englishTransliteration:
yaṁ hi na vyathayanty ete puruṣaṁ puruṣarṣabha
sama-duḥkha-sukhaṁ dhīraṁ so ’mṛtatvāya kalpate
englishWBW: yam (whom) — hi (certainly) — na (never) — vyathayanti (disturb) — ete (all these) — puruṣam (unto a person) — puruṣa-ṛṣabha (O best among men) — sama (equal) — duḥkha (in distress) — sukham (and happiness) — dhīram (patient/sober) — saḥ (he) — amṛtatvāya (for liberation) — kalpate (is considered eligible)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa defines the qualification for liberation. He says the person who is not disturbed by the waves of happiness and distress, and who remains steady in both, is eligible for immortality. Most people are emotional puppets, elated by success and crushed by failure.

However, a spiritualist understands that these dualities belong to the body and mind, not to the self. By remaining an observer of these changes without getting entangled, one develops the inner strength necessary to break the cycle of birth and death. This is the stage of a ‘dhīra’, or a sober person.

Kṛṣṇa is challenging Arjuna to rise to this level. If Arjuna fights only when he feels happy and quits when he feels sad, he is a slave to his emotions. To achieve ‘amṛtatvāya’, or immortality, he must perform his duty regardless of his internal weather. Equanimity is the gateway to freedom.

sanskrit:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः।
उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः।।
translationEnglish:
Those who are seers of the truth have concluded that of the nonexistent [the material body] there is no endurance and of the eternal [the soul] there is no change.
This they have concluded by studying the nature of both.
translationHindi: असत् (शरीर) का तो भाव (सत्ता) विद्यमान नहीं है और सत् (आत्मा) का अभाव विद्यमान नहीं है। तत्त्वदर्शी पुरुषों ने इन दोनों का ही तत्त्व देखा है।
