translationGujarati: અસત્ (શરીર) નું કોઈ અસ્તિત્વ નથી અને સત્ (આત્મા) નો ક્યારેય અભાવ નથી. તત્વદર્શી પુરુષોએ આ બંનેનું તત્વ જોયું છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that the temporary (body) has no true existence, and the eternal (soul) never ceases to exist; seers of truth know the nature of both.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि असत्य (शरीर) का कोई स्थायी अस्तित्व नहीं है और सत्य (आत्मा) का कभी नाश नहीं होता; तत्वदर्शी इन दोनों के सत्य को जानते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે અસત્ય (શરીર) નું કોઈ કાયમી અસ્તિત્વ નથી અને સત્ય (આત્મા) નો ક્યારેય નાશ થતો નથી; તત્વદર્શીઓ આ બંનેના સત્યને જાણે છે.
tweetEnglish: The unreal (body) has no duration; the real (soul) has no cessation. Seers have studied the nature of both.
threadsEnglish: Those who are seers of the truth have concluded that the unreal body has no endurance and the eternal soul has no change.
englishTransliteration:
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ
ubhayor api dṛṣṭo ’ntas tv anayos tattva-darśibhiḥ
englishWBW: na (never) — asataḥ (of the nonexistent/temporary) — vidyate (there is) — bhāvaḥ (endurance) — na (never) — abhāvaḥ (changing/cessation) — vidyate (there is) — sataḥ (of the eternal) — ubhayoḥ (of both) — api (also) — dṛṣṭaḥ (observed) — antaḥ (conclusion) — tu (indeed) — anayoḥ (of them) — tattva-darśibhiḥ (by the seers of the truth)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa introduces a fundamental metaphysical distinction between the ‘Sat’ (Real) and the ‘Asat’ (Unreal). He states that the nonexistent has no endurance, and the eternal has no cessation. The seers of truth have concluded this by studying the nature of both.

In this context, the body is ‘Asat’—it is a temporary assembly of matter that is constantly changing and eventually disappears. The soul is ‘Sat’—it is the eternal reality that remains unchanged. The grief Arjuna feels is for the ‘Asat’, which is illogical because the body was never meant to last.

By focusing on the ‘Sat’, or the eternal essence, one finds stability. Arjuna is crying for the passing shadow while ignoring the solid reality. Kṛṣṇa urges him to align his vision with that of the ‘tattva-darśibhiḥ’, those who see the truth, and stop lamenting for the perishable.

sanskrit:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित् कर्तुमर्हति।।
translationEnglish:
That which pervades the entire body you should know to be indestructible.
No one is able to destroy that imperishable soul.
translationHindi: नाशरहित तो तू उसको जान, जिससे यह सम्पूर्ण जगत व्याप्त है। इस अविनाशी का विनाश करने में कोई भी समर्थ नहीं है।
translationGujarati: નાશરહિત તો તું તેને જાણ, જેનાથી આ સમગ્ર જગત વ્યાપ્ત છે. આ અવિનાશીનો વિનાશ કરવામાં કોઈ પણ સમર્થ નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa affirms that the soul which pervades the entire body is indestructible and no one can destroy it.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण पुष्टि करते हैं कि जो आत्मा पूरे शरीर में व्याप्त है वह अविनाशी है और उसका विनाश कोई नहीं कर सकता।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ પુષ્ટિ કરે છે કે જે આત્મા આખા શરીરમાં વ્યાપ્ત છે તે અવિનાશી છે અને તેનો વિનાશ કોઈ કરી શકતું નથી.
tweetEnglish: Know that which pervades the entire body is indestructible. No one can destroy the imperishable soul.
threadsEnglish: Know that which pervades the entire body is indestructible. No one is able to destroy that imperishable soul.
englishTransliteration:
avināśi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaṁ tatam
vināśam avyayasyāsya na kaścit kartum arhati
englishWBW: avināśi (indestructible) — tu (but) — tat (that) — viddhi (know) — yena (by which) — sarvam (entire) — idam (this) — tatam (pervaded) — vināśam (destruction) — avyayasya (of the imperishable) — asya (of this) — na kaścit (no one) — kartum (to do) — arhati (is able)
englishExplain:
Expanding on the nature of the soul, Kṛṣṇa says, “Know that which pervades the entire body to be indestructible.” What pervades the body? It is consciousness. If you pinch any part of your body, you feel it. This spread of awareness is the symptom of the soul’s presence.

Kṛṣṇa declares that no one can destroy this imperishable soul. Not even the most powerful weapons on the battlefield can touch it. The soul is of a completely different energy than the material body. It is an ‘avyaya’, or an inexhaustible reality.

Arjuna is afraid of being a killer, but Kṛṣṇa assures him that on the deepest level, killing the self is a metaphysical impossibility. He can dismantle the body, but he cannot touch the person. This knowledge is intended to remove the fear of causing harm while performing one’s necessary duty.

sanskrit:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत।।
translationEnglish: The material body of the indestructible, immeasurable and eternal living entity is sure to come to an end; therefore, fight, O descendant of Bhārata.
translationHindi: इस नाशरहित, अप्रमेय, नित्यस्वरूप जीवात्मा के ये सब शरीर नाशवान कहे गये हैं, इसलिए हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन! तू युद्ध कर।
translationGujarati: આ નાશરહિત, અપ્રમેય, નિત્યસ્વરૂપ જીવાત્માના આ બધા શરીર નાશવંત કહેવાયા છે, તેથી હે ભારતવંશી અર્જુન! તું યુદ્ધ કર.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna that while the body is destined to end, the indwelling soul is eternal and immeasurable, so he should fight without hesitation.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि शरीर का अंत निश्चित है, लेकिन आत्मा अमर और अप्रमेय है, इसलिए उन्हें बिना हिचकिचाहट के युद्ध करना चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને કહે છે કે શરીરનો અંત નિશ્ચિત છે, પરંતુ આત્મા અમર અને અપ્રમેય છે, તેથી તેમણે ખચકાયા વિના યુદ્ધ કરવું જોઈએ.
tweetEnglish: The body ends, but the soul is eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable. Therefore, fight, O Bhārata.
threadsEnglish: The material body is sure to come to an end, but the indwelling soul is eternal and immeasurable. Therefore, fight, O descendant of Bhārata!
englishTransliteration:
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ
anāśino ’prameyasya tasmād yudhyasva bhārata
englishWBW: antavantaḥ (perishable) — ime (all these) — dehāḥ (material bodies) — nityasya (of the eternal) — uktāḥ (are said) — śarīriṇaḥ (of the embodied soul) — anāśinaḥ (never to be destroyed) — aprameyasya (immeasurable) — tasmāt (therefore) — yudhyasva (fight) — bhārata (O descendant of Bharata)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa draws a practical conclusion for Arjuna. He states that while these material bodies are sure to come to an end, the embodied soul is eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable. Therefore, He gives the direct command: “Fight, O descendant of Bharata!”

The logic is ruthless but liberating. The body is a perishable machine that is already doomed to decay. You cannot save it forever. The soul, however, is perfectly safe and can never be harmed. Since death is inevitable for the body and impossible for the soul, there is no reason to shrink from duty.

Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that avoiding the battle won’t save his relatives’ bodies in the long run, but it will certainly damage his own soul’s progress by neglecting his Dharma. He encourages Arjuna to fight based on this absolute understanding of reality.

sanskrit:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते।।
translationEnglish:
Neither he who thinks the living entity the slayer nor he who thinks it slain is in knowledge,
for the self slays not nor is slain.
translationHindi: जो इस आत्मा को मारने वाला समझता है तथा जो इसको मरा मानता है, वे दोनों ही नहीं जानते; क्योंकि यह आत्मा वास्तव में न तो किसी को मारता है और न किसी द्वारा मारा जाता है।
translationGujarati: જે આ આત્માને મારનાર માને છે અને જે આને મરેલો માને છે, તે બંને જાણતા નથી; કારણ કે આ આત્મા ખરેખર ન તો કોઈને મારે છે અને ન તો કોઈના દ્વારા મરાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa corrects the misconception that the soul kills or is killed, stating that the soul neither slays nor is slain.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण इस गलतफहमी को दूर करते हैं कि आत्मा मारती है या मरती है, और बताते हैं कि आत्मा न तो किसी को मारती है और न ही मारी जाती है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ એ ગેરસમજને દૂર કરે છે કે આત્મા મારે છે અથવા મરે છે, અને જણાવે છે કે આત્મા ન તો કોઈને મારે છે અને ન તો કોઈના દ્વારા મરાય છે.
tweetEnglish: He who thinks the soul kills or is killed does not understand. The soul neither kills nor is killed.
threadsEnglish: Neither he who thinks the soul a slayer nor he who thinks it slain is in knowledge, for the self slays not nor is it slain.
englishTransliteration:
ya enaṁ vetti hantāraṁ yaś cainaṁ manyate hatam
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṁ hanti na hanyate
englishWBW: yaḥ (anyone who) — enam (this) — vetti (knows) — hantāram (the killer) — yaḥ (anyone who) — ca (also) — enam (this) — manyate (thinks) — hatam (killed) — ubhau (both) — tau (they) — na (never) — vijānītaḥ (are in knowledge) — na (never) — ayam (this) — hanti (kills) — na (never) — hanyate (is killed)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa addresses the common misconception about death and agency. He says that anyone who thinks the soul is the slayer or that the soul is slain is in ignorance. Neither of them understands the truth, for the self neither kills nor is it ever killed.

The soul is the passenger, and the body is the vehicle. If a car is crushed, the driver may still be alive. On the battlefield of Kurukṣetra, arrows will pierce flesh and chariots will be destroyed, but the essence of the person—the soul—remains untouched. The act of ‘killing’ applies only to the material covering.

This verse clears Arjuna of the spiritual guilt of murder, provided he fights as a matter of duty without personal malice. It helps him understand that he is not actually taking a life, but merely participating in a physical transition that has already been ordained by the laws of nature.

sanskrit:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचि
न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे।।
translationEnglish:
For the soul there is neither birth nor death at any time. He has not come into being, does not come into being, and will not come into being.
He is unborn, eternal, ever-existing and primeval. He is not slain when the body is slain.
translationHindi: यह आत्मा किसी काल में भी न तो जन्मता है और न मरता है और न यह एक बार होकर फिर अभावरूप होने वाला है। यह आत्मा अजन्मा, नित्य, शाश्वत और पुरातन है; शरीर के मारे जाने पर भी यह नहीं मारा जाता।
translationGujarati: આ આત્મા કોઈ કાળે પણ જન્મતો નથી અને મરતો નથી, તથા એક વાર થઈને ફરી મટી જવાનો નથી. આ આત્મા અજન્મા, નિત્ય, શાશ્વત અને પુરાતન છે; શરીર મરાઈ જવા છતાં તે મરાતો નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa declares that the soul is never born and never dies; it is unborn, eternal, and primeval, and does not die when the body is killed.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण घोषणा करते हैं कि आत्मा न कभी जन्म लेती है और न कभी मरती है; यह अजन्मा, नित्य और शाश्वत है, और शरीर के नष्ट होने पर भी इसका नाश नहीं होता।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ઘોષણા કરે છે કે આત્મા ક્યારેય જન્મતો નથી અને ક્યારેય મરતો નથી; તે અજન્મા, નિત્ય અને શાશ્વત છે, અને શરીરનો નાશ થવા છતાં તેનો નાશ થતો નથી.
tweetEnglish: The soul is never born and never dies. Unborn and eternal, it is not killed when the body is killed.
threadsEnglish: The soul is never born nor does it die at any time. It is unborn, eternal, and primeval. It is not slain when the body is slain.
englishTransliteration:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin
nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato ’yaṁ purāṇo
na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
englishWBW: na (never) — jāyate (takes birth) — mriyate (dies) — vā (or) — kadācit (at any time) — na (never) — ayam (this) — bhūtvā (having come into being) — bhavitā (will come into being) — vā (or) — na (not) — bhūyaḥ (again) — ajaḥ (unborn) — nityaḥ (eternal) — śāśvataḥ (ever-existing) — ayam (this) — purāṇaḥ (the oldest) — na (never) — hanyate (is killed) — hanyamāne (being killed) — śarīre (the body)
englishExplain:
This is one of the most famous verses in the Gītā, summarizing the nature of the soul. Kṛṣṇa declares that the soul never takes birth and never dies at any time. It has not come into being, does not come into being, and will not come into being. It is unborn, eternal, and primeval.

While the body goes through changes—birth, growth, old age, and death—the soul remains constant. It is ‘purāṇaḥ’, the oldest, yet it always remains fresh and new. It is not slain when the body is slain. This knowledge is the ultimate antidote to fear and grief.

If Arjuna truly realizes this, his hands will stop shaking. He will see the war not as a slaughterhouse, but as a divinely orchestrated transition for the eternal souls involved. The soul’s existence is independent of the biological frame it currently occupies.

sanskrit:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम्।
कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्।।
translationEnglish: O Pārtha, how can a person who knows that the soul is indestructible, eternal, unborn and immutable kill anyone or cause anyone to kill?
translationHindi: हे पार्थ! जो पुरुष इस आत्मा को नाशरहित, नित्य, अजन्मा और अव्यय जानता है, वह पुरुष कैसे किसी को मरवाता है और कैसे किसी को मारता है?
translationGujarati: હે પાર્થ! જે પુરુષ આ આત્માને નાશરહિત, નિત્ય, અજન્મા અને અવ્યય જાણે છે, તે પુરુષ કેવી રીતે કોઈને મરાવે છે અને કેવી રીતે કોઈને મારે છે?
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa asks how a person who knows the soul is indestructible and eternal can possibly kill anyone or cause anyone to be killed.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण पूछते हैं कि जो व्यक्ति यह जानता है कि आत्मा अविनाशी और नित्य है, वह भला कैसे किसी को मार सकता है या मरवा सकता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ પૂછે છે કે જે વ્યક્તિ એ જાણે છે કે આત્મા અવિનાશી અને નિત્ય છે, તે કેવી રીતે કોઈને મારી શકે અથવા મરાવી શકે.
tweetEnglish: O Pārtha, how can a person who knows the soul is indestructible and eternal kill anyone or cause anyone to kill?
threadsEnglish: O Pārtha, how can a person who knows that the soul is indestructible and eternal kill anyone or cause anyone to kill?
englishTransliteration:
yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate
englishWBW: yat yat (whatever) — ācarati (does) — śreṣṭhaḥ (a respectable leader) — tat tat (that) — eva (certainly) — itaraḥ (common) — janaḥ (person) — saḥ (he) — yat (whatever) — pramāṇam (example) — kurute (does) — lokaḥ (all the world) — tat (that) — anuvartate (follows in the footsteps)
englishExplain:
This is one of the most important verses on leadership. Kṛṣṇa explains that whatever a great man does, common people follow. Whatever standard he sets by his actions, the rest of the world pursues. People are naturally inclined to imitate those they admire.

If a leader is lazy, the people become lazy. If a leader is corrupt, the society becomes corrupt. If Arjuna, the greatest hero of his time, walks away from his duty on the battlefield, the common man will use him as an excuse to avoid their own responsibilities. They will call it ‘saintliness’ when it is really just cowardice.

Arjuna has a massive social responsibility. His actions serve as a template for millions of people. Kṛṣṇa is telling him that he cannot afford to be private in his morality. A leader’s first duty is to set a perfect example of integrity and commitment to Dharma, even when it is difficult.

sanskrit:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय
नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा
न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही।।
translationEnglish: As a person puts on new garments, giving up old ones, the soul similarly accepts new material bodies, giving up the old and useless ones.
translationHindi: जैसे मनुष्य पुराने वस्त्रों को त्यागकर दूसरे नये वस्त्रों को ग्रहण करता है, वैसे ही जीवात्मा पुराने शरीरों को त्यागकर दूसरे नये शरीरों को प्राप्त होता है।
translationGujarati: જેમ મનુષ્ય જૂના વસ્ત્રો છોડીને બીજા નવા વસ્ત્રો ધારણ કરે છે, તેમ જીવાત્મા જૂના શરીરો છોડીને બીજા નવા શરીરો પ્રાપ્ત કરે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa uses the metaphor of changing clothes to explain that the soul discards old bodies and accepts new ones, just as a person changes old garments for new ones.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कपड़े बदलने का उदाहरण देते हुए समझाते हैं कि जैसे मनुष्य पुराने कपड़े त्यागकर नए पहनता है, वैसे ही आत्मा पुराने शरीर को छोड़कर नया शरीर धारण करती है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કપડાં બદલવાનું ઉદાહરણ આપીને સમજાવે છે કે જેમ મનુષ્ય જૂના કપડાં છોડીને નવા પહેરે છે, તેમ આત્મા જૂના શરીરને છોડીને નવું શરીર ધારણ કરે છે.
tweetEnglish: As one gives up old clothes for new ones, the soul accepts new bodies, giving up the old and useless ones.
threadsEnglish: As a person puts on new garments, giving up old ones, the soul similarly accepts new material bodies, giving up the old and useless ones.
englishTransliteration:
vāsāṁsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya
navāni gṛhṇāti naro ’parāṇi
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny
anyāni saṁyāti navāni dehī
englishWBW: vāsāṁsi (garments) — jīrṇāni (old and worn out) — yathā (just as) — vihāya (giving up) — navāni (new) — gṛhṇāti (accepts) — naraḥ (a man) — aparāṇi (others) — tathā (similarly) — śarīrāṇi (bodies) — vihāya (giving up) — jīrṇāni (old and useless) — anyāni (different) — saṁyāti (verily accepts) — navāni (new) — dehī (the embodied soul)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa gives the classic analogy of changing clothes to explain the process of reincarnation. Just as a person discards old, worn-out garments and puts on new ones, the soul similarly discards old and useless bodies and accepts new material ones.

This metaphor is deeply comforting. We do not mourn when we throw away a torn shirt; we simply get a new one. Similarly, death is merely the soul discarding a biological suit that no longer functions properly. The identity and consciousness of the ‘wearer’ remain completely unchanged.

This verse implies that individual identity survives the death of the body. Arjuna is worried about the loss of his grandfather, but Kṛṣṇa assures him that Bhīṣma will simply upgrade his ‘garment’ and continue his existence elsewhere. It normalizes the phenomenon of death and removes its terrifying mystery.

sanskrit:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः।।
translationEnglish: The soul can never be cut to pieces by any weapon, nor burned by fire, nor moistened by water, nor withered by the wind.
translationHindi: इस आत्मा को शस्त्र नहीं काट सकते, इसको आग नहीं जला सकती, इसको जल नहीं गला सकता और वायु नहीं सुखा सकता।
translationGujarati: આ આત્માને શસ્ત્રો કાપી શકતા નથી, અગ્નિ બાળી શકતો નથી, પાણી ભીંજવી શકતું નથી અને વાયુ સૂકવી શકતો નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa asserts that the soul is impervious to all physical damage: weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि आत्मा को कोई भौतिक नुकसान नहीं पहुँचा सकता: न शस्त्र उसे काट सकते हैं, न आग जला सकती है, न पानी गला सकता है और न हवा सुखा सकती है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે આત્માને કોઈ ભૌતિક નુકસાન પહોંચાડી શકતું નથી: ન શસ્ત્રો તેને કાપી શકે છે, ન આગ બાળી શકે છે, ન પાણી પલાળી શકે છે અને ન પવન સૂકવી શકે છે.
tweetEnglish: The soul cannot be cut by weapons, burned by fire, moistened by water, or withered by the wind.
threadsEnglish: The soul can never be cut to pieces by any weapon, nor burned by fire, nor moistened by water, nor withered by the wind.
englishTransliteration:
nainaṁ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ
na cainaṁ kledayanty āpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
englishWBW: na (never) — enam (this soul) — chindanti (can cut) — śastrāṇi (weapons) — na (never) — enam (this soul) — dahati (burns) — pāvakaḥ (fire) — na (never) — ca (also) — enam (this soul) — kledayanti (moistens) — āpaḥ (water) — na (never) — śoṣayati (dries) — mārutaḥ (wind)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa scientifically analyzes the soul’s immunity to the material elements. He states that weapons cannot cut the soul, fire cannot burn it, water cannot moisten it, and wind cannot dry it. In the material world, every object is subject to destruction by one of these forces.

By stating that the soul is immune to all of them, Kṛṣṇa establishes that the soul belongs to a completely different dimension of energy. It is anti-material and transcendental. No matter how many arrows Arjuna shoots, they can only affect the physical elements, never the spiritual essence.

The war creates havoc only on the material level. The souls on the battlefield remain pristine, untouched, and unchangeable. Kṛṣṇa uses this absolute security of the soul to convince Arjuna that he should not fear the physical consequences of the battle.

sanskrit:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः।।
translationEnglish:
This individual soul is unbreakable and insoluble, and can be neither burned nor dried.
He is everlasting, present everywhere, unchangeable, immovable and eternally the same.
translationHindi: यह आत्मा अच्छेद्य है, यह आत्मा अदाह्य, अक्लेद्य और अशोष्य है। तथा यह आत्मा नित्य, सर्वव्यापी, अचल, स्थिर रहने वाला और सनातन है।
translationGujarati: આ આત્મા છેદાય નહીં તેવો, બળે નહીં તેવો, પલળે નહીં તેવો અને સુકાય નહીં તેવો છે. તથા આ આત્મા નિત્ય, સર્વવ્યાપી, અચળ, સ્થિર રહેવાવાળો અને સનાતન છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa describes the soul as unbreakable, immune to burning or drying, eternal, all-pervading, unchangeable, immovable, and everlasting.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण आत्मा का वर्णन करते हुए कहते हैं कि यह अटूट है, इसे जलाया या सुखाया नहीं जा सकता; यह नित्य, सर्वव्यापी, अचल और सनातन है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ આત્માનું વર્ણન કરતા કહે છે કે તે અતૂટ છે, તેને બાળી કે સૂકવી શકાતો નથી; તે નિત્ય, સર્વવ્યાપી, અચળ અને સનાતન છે.
tweetEnglish: The soul is unbreakable, insoluble, and cannot be burned. It is everlasting, all-pervading and eternal.
threadsEnglish: This individual soul is unbreakable, insoluble, and can be neither burned nor dried. He is everlasting, all-pervading, and eternally the same.
englishTransliteration:
acchedyo ’yam adāhyo ’yam akledyo ’śoṣya eva ca
nityaḥ sarva-gataḥ sthāṇur acalo ’yaṁ sanātanaḥ
englishWBW: acchedyaḥ (unbreakable) — ayam (this soul) — adāhyaḥ (unable to be burned) — ayam (this soul) — akledyaḥ (insoluble) — aśoṣyaḥ (unable to be dried) — eva (certainly) — ca (and) — nityaḥ (everlasting) — sarva-gataḥ (all-pervading) — sthāṇuḥ (unchangeable) — acalaḥ (immovable) — ayam (this soul) — sanātanaḥ (eternally the same)
englishExplain:
Continuing the description of the soul’s qualities, Kṛṣṇa uses powerful adjectives: unbreakable, insoluble, and immune to fire or wind. He adds that the soul is everlasting, all-pervading, unchangeable, and eternally the same.

The word ‘sarva-gataḥ’ is significant; it implies that spirit souls are present everywhere—in the earth, water, fire, and air—and in all species of life. There is no vacuum in creation. The soul is not a byproduct of chemical evolution, but a fundamental and eternal truth of existence.

This solidifies the argument that the ‘destruction’ Arjuna fears is a myth. The soul is a permanent part of the cosmic fabric. By understanding these eight qualities, Arjuna can see that his relatives are safe in their spiritual nature, and his duty to fight becomes a matter of managing temporary matter rather than destroying eternal life.

sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि।।
translationEnglish:
It is said that the soul is invisible, inconceivable and immutable.
Knowing this, you should not grieve for the body.
translationHindi: यह आत्मा अव्यक्त, अचिन्त्य और विकाररहित कहा जाता है। इससे हे अर्जुन! इस आत्मा को उपर्युक्त प्रकार से जानकर तू शोक करने के योग्य नहीं है।
translationGujarati: આ આત્મા અવ્યક્ત, અચિંત્ય અને વિકારરહિત કહેવાય છે. તેથી હે અર્જુન! આ આત્માને આ પ્રમાણે જાણીને તું શોક કરવા યોગ્ય નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa concludes that since the soul is invisible, inconceivable, and unchangeable, knowing this truth, Arjuna should not grieve.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि चूँकि आत्मा अव्यक्त, अकल्पनीय और विकाररहित है, इसलिए इस सत्य को जानकर अर्जुन को शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે આત્મા અવ્યક્ત, અકલ્પનીય અને વિકારરહિત હોવાથી, આ સત્ય જાણીને અર્જુને શોક કરવો જોઈએ નહીં.
tweetEnglish: The soul is invisible, inconceivable, and immutable. Knowing this, you should not grieve for the body.
threadsEnglish: It is said that the soul is invisible, inconceivable, and immutable. Knowing this, you should not grieve for the body.
englishTransliteration:
avyakto ’yam acintyo ’yam avikāryo ’yam ucyate
tasmād evaṁ viditvainaṁ nānuśocitum arhasi
englishWBW: avyaktaḥ (invisible) — ayam (this soul) — acintyaḥ (inconceivable) — ayam (this soul) — avikāryaḥ (unchangeable) — ayam (this soul) — ucyate (is said) — tasmāt (therefore) — evam (like this) — viditvā (knowing) — enam (this soul) — na (not) — anuśocitum (to lament) — arhasi (you deserve)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa concludes this section on the soul by calling it invisible, inconceivable, and immutable. It is invisible to material eyes and inconceivable to the limited material brain. We cannot detect the soul with instruments because it is spiritual, not physical.

Therefore, knowledge of the soul must be accepted from the authority of the scriptures rather than from experimental observation. Kṛṣṇa says, “Knowing the soul to be such, you should not grieve.” If the soul is beyond the range of physical destruction and mental perception, then material grief is logically misplaced.

Arjuna’s sorrow is based on what he can see—the bodies of his kinsmen. Kṛṣṇa’s instruction is based on what is true but invisible—the eternal nature of the self. He asks Arjuna to upgrade his vision from the sensory to the transcendental.

sanskrit:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि।।
translationEnglish: If, however, you think that the soul [or the symptoms of life] is always born and dies forever, you still have no reason to lament, O mighty-armed Arjuna.
translationHindi: किन्तु यदि तू इस आत्मा को सदा जन्मने वाला तथा सदा मरने वाला मानता हो, तो भी हे महाबाहो! तू इस प्रकार शोक करने योग्य नहीं है।
translationGujarati: પરંતુ જો તું આ આત્માને સદાય જન્મવાવાળો તથા સદાય મરવાવાળો માનતો હોય, તો પણ હે મહાબાહુ! તું આ પ્રકારે શોક કરવા યોગ્ય નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa argues that even if Arjuna believes the soul is constantly born and dies with the body, there is still no reason to grieve.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण तर्क देते हैं कि यदि अर्जुन यह भी मानते हैं कि आत्मा का बार-बार जन्म और मृत्यु होती है, तो भी शोक करने का कोई कारण नहीं है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ તર્ક આપે છે કે જો અર્જુન એમ પણ માને કે આત્માનો વારંવાર જન્મ અને મૃત્યુ થાય છે, તો પણ શોક કરવાનું કોઈ કારણ નથી.
tweetEnglish: Even if you think the soul is constantly born and dies, O mighty-armed one, you still have no reason to grieve.
threadsEnglish: If, however, you think that the soul is always born and dies forever, you still have no reason to lament, O mighty-armed Arjuna.
englishTransliteration:
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇy anye saṁyamāgniṣu juhvati
śabdādīn viṣayān anya indriyāgniṣu juhvati
englishWBW: śrotra-ādīni (hearing process and others) — indriyāṇi (senses) — anye (others) — saṁyama (of restraint) — agniṣu (in the fires) — juhvati (offer/sacrifice) — śabda-ādīn (sound and others) — viṣayān (sense objects) — anye (others) — indriya (of the senses) — agniṣu (in the fires) — juhvati (offer)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes two types of sensory sacrifice. The first is practiced by students (‘brahmacārīs’) who sacrifice the senses themselves in the fire of mental control. They simply shut the doors of perception to avoid distraction, focusing entirely on their spiritual studies.

The second is practiced by regulated householders. They don’t shut their senses, but they sacrifice the sense *objects* into the fire of the senses. This means they hear, see, and eat, but only according to religious principles. They use their senses for duty and service rather than for whimsical pleasure.

Both are forms of yoga. One is the path of total withdrawal, and the other is the path of regulated engagement. Kṛṣṇa is showing Arjuna that there are different ways to manage the human machine. The goal in both cases is to ensure that the senses do not become the masters of the soul, but remain its disciplined servants.

sanskrit:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।
translationEnglish:
One who has taken his birth is sure to die, and after death one is sure to take birth again.
Therefore, in the unavoidable discharge of your duty, you should not lament.
translationHindi: क्योंकि जन्मे हुए की मृत्यु निश्चित है और मरे हुए का जन्म निश्चित है। इससे इस बिना उपाय वाले विषय में तू शोक करने के योग्य नहीं है।
translationGujarati: કારણ કે જન્મેલાનું મૃત્યુ નિશ્ચિત છે અને મરેલાનો જન્મ નિશ્ચિત છે. તેથી આ અનિવાર્ય વિષયમાં તું શોક કરવા યોગ્ય નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that for whatever is born death is certain, and for the dead birth is certain; therefore, one should not grieve over the inevitable.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि जिसका जन्म हुआ है उसकी मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत का पुनर्जन्म निश्चित है; इसलिए अपरिहार्य के लिए शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે જેનો જન્મ થયો છે તેનું મૃત્યુ નિશ્ચિત છે, અને મૃતનો પુનર્જન્મ નિશ્ચિત છે; તેથી અનિવાર્ય બાબત માટે શોક કરવો જોઈએ નહીં.
tweetEnglish: For one born, death is certain; for one who dies, birth is certain. Do not grieve over the inevitable.
threadsEnglish: One who has taken his birth is sure to die, and after death, one is sure to take birth again. Do not grieve over the inevitable.
englishTransliteration:
sarvāṇīndriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi cāpare
ātma-saṁyama-yogāgnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite
englishWBW: sarvāṇi (all) — indriya (of the senses) — karmāṇi (functions) — prāṇa-karmāṇi (functions of the life breath) — ca (also) — apare (others) — ātma-saṁyama (of self-control) — yoga (of yoga) — agnau (in the fire) — juhvati (sacrifice) — jñāna-dīpite (illuminated by knowledge)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes a more technical, internal form of sacrifice practiced by the ‘mystic yogīs’. They offer the functions of all their senses and even their life-breath (‘prāṇa’) into the fire of self-control. This fire is not physical; it is ‘jñāna-dīpite’, fueled and illuminated by spiritual knowledge.

This refers to the practice of deep meditation and ‘Prāṇāyāma’, where the practitioner stops all external activity to focus on the inner self. By withdrawing their energy from the outside world and the body’s automatic functions, they seek to burn up their material identity and find the pure soul within.

This is a rigorous path of ‘Aṣṭāṅga-yoga’. Kṛṣṇa mentions it to show the intensity of the spiritual search. It highlights that the body is not just a biological object, but a complex energy system that can be harnessed for liberation. However, such a path is very difficult, contrasting with the more accessible path of service He is teaching Arjuna.

sanskrit:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना।।
translationEnglish:
All created beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in their interim state, and unmanifest again when annihilated.
So what need is there for lamentation?
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! सम्पूर्ण प्राणी जन्म से पहले अप्रकट थे और मरने के बाद भी अप्रकट हो जाने वाले हैं, केवल बीच में ही प्रकट हैं; फिर ऐसी स्थिति में क्या शोक करना?
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! તમામ પ્રાણીઓ જન્મ પહેલાં અપ્રગટ હતા અને મર્યા પછી પણ અપ્રગટ થઈ જવાના છે, માત્ર વચ્ચેના સમયમાં જ પ્રગટ છે; તો પછી આવી સ્થિતિમાં શોક શો?
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa points out that beings are unmanifest before birth and after death, visible only in between, so there is no cause for grief.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि प्राणी जन्म से पहले और मृत्यु के बाद अदृश्य होते हैं, केवल बीच में ही दिखाई देते हैं, तो फिर शोक का क्या कारण है?
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે પ્રાણીઓ જન્મ પહેલા અને મૃત્યુ પછી અદ્રશ્ય હોય છે, માત્ર વચગાળામાં જ દેખાય છે, તો પછી શોકનું શું કારણ છે?
tweetEnglish: Beings are unmanifest in the beginning, manifest in the middle, and unmanifest again at the end. Why grieve?
threadsEnglish: All created beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in their interim state, and unmanifest again when annihilated. Why lament?
englishTransliteration:
dravya-yajñās tapo-yajñā yoga-yajñās tathāpare
svādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāś ca yatayaḥ saṁśita-vratāḥ
englishWBW: dravya-yajñāḥ (sacrifice of possessions) — tapaḥ-yajñāḥ (sacrifice in austerities) — yoga-yajñāḥ (sacrifice in eightfold mysticism) — tathā (as well as) — apare (others) — svādhyāya (study of the Vedas) — jñāna-yajñāḥ (sacrifice in real knowledge) — ca (also) — yatayaḥ (enlightened persons) — saṁśita (taken) — vratāḥ (vows)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa lists more varieties of sacrifice, showing that everyone can contribute according to their assets. Some perform ‘dravya-yajñā’—charity and the sacrifice of wealth. Others perform ‘tapaḥ-yajñā’—austerities and fasts. Some practice the eight-fold path of yoga, while others dedicate themselves to ‘svādhyāya’, the intense study of scriptures.

All these seekers are ‘saṁśita-vratāḥ’, meaning they take their vows seriously. They are not casual hobbyists; they are committed to their discipline. Kṛṣṇa is showing that spiritual life is diverse and accommodates different strengths. Some give money, some give their time, some give their physical comfort, and some give their intellectual energy.

The common thread is the voluntary acceptance of inconvenience for a higher purpose. Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that every human being has something to offer to the Divine. There is no excuse for a life without sacrifice; one must simply find the ‘yajña’ that matches their capacity and nature.

sanskrit:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन
माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः।
आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोति
श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित्।।
translationEnglish:
Some look on the soul as amazing, some describe him as amazing, and some hear of him as amazing,
while others, even after hearing about him, cannot understand him at all.
translationHindi: कोई एक महापुरुष ही इस आत्मा को आश्चर्य की भाँति देखता है और वैसे ही दूसरा कोई महापुरुष ही इसके तत्त्व का आश्चर्य की भाँति वर्णन करता है तथा दूसरा कोई अधिकारी पुरुष ही इसे आश्चर्य की भाँति सुनता है और कोई-कोई तो सुनकर भी इसको नहीं जानता।
translationGujarati: કોઈ એક મહાપુરુષ જ આ આત્માને આશ્ચર્યની જેમ જુએ છે અને તેવી જ રીતે બીજો કોઈ મહાપુરુષ જ આના તત્વનું આશ્ચર્યની જેમ વર્ણન કરે છે તથા બીજો કોઈ અધિકારી પુરુષ જ આને આશ્ચર્યની જેમ સાંભળે છે અને કોઈ કોઈ તો સાંભળીને પણ આને જાણતો નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa remarks that the soul is a wonder; some see it as amazing, some describe it as amazing, and some hear of it as amazing, while others still don’t understand it.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि आत्मा अद्भुत है; कोई इसे आश्चर्य से देखता है, कोई इसका वर्णन आश्चर्य से करता है, और कोई इसे आश्चर्य से सुनता है, फिर भी कई इसे समझ नहीं पाते।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે આત્મા અદ્ભુત છે; કોઈ તેને આશ્ચર્યથી જુએ છે, કોઈ તેનું વર્ણન આશ્ચર્યથી કરે છે, અને કોઈ તેને આશ્ચર્યથી સાંભળે છે, છતાં ઘણા તેને સમજી શકતા નથી.
tweetEnglish: Some see the soul as amazing, some describe it as amazing, others hear of it, yet many still don’t understand.
threadsEnglish: Some look on the soul as amazing, some describe him as amazing, and some hear of him as amazing, while others cannot understand him at all.
englishTransliteration:
apāne juhvati prāṇaṁ prāṇe ’pānaṁ tathāpare
prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ
englishWBW: apāne (in the outgoing air) — juhvati (sacrifice) — prāṇam (the incoming air) — prāṇe (in the incoming air) — apānam (the outgoing air) — tathā (also) — apare (others) — prāṇa-apāna (of the incoming and outgoing air) — gatī (the movements) — ruddhvā (checking) — prāṇāyāma (trance induced by breath control) — parāyaṇāḥ (fully absorbed)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the technical sacrifice of breath control, or ‘Prāṇāyāma’. Some yogīs practice by offering the movement of the incoming breath into the outgoing, or vice versa. Eventually, they learn to suspend all breathing entirely to enter a state of deep trance, or ‘samādhi’.

This process is intended to still the mind by controlling the body’s life force. When the breathing becomes rhythmic and then stops, the constant ‘flickering’ of thoughts also ceases. It is a biological way to reach a state of pure consciousness. The breath is used as a tool to tame the mind.

While impressive, Kṛṣṇa includes this in the list of sacrifices to show that even our very breath can be offered to the Supreme. It emphasizes that every function of the human body has a potential spiritual use. Arjuna, as a man of action, is being shown the spectrum of yoga, from the physical to the mystical, as part of his complete education.

sanskrit:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।
translationEnglish:
O descendant of Bhārata, he who dwells in the body can never be slain.
Therefore you need not grieve for any living being.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! यह आत्मा सबके शरीरों में सदा ही अवध्य (जिसका वध न किया जा सके) है। इस कारण सम्पूर्ण प्राणियों के लिए तू शोक करने के योग्य नहीं है।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! આ આત્મા બધાના શરીરમાં હંમેશા અવધ્ય (જેનો વધ ન થઈ શકે તેવો) છે. આ કારણે તમામ પ્રાણીઓ માટે તું શોક કરવા યોગ્ય નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa concludes that the soul dwelling within the body is eternal and can never be killed, so Arjuna should not grieve for any living being.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण निष्कर्ष निकालते हैं कि शरीर के भीतर रहने वाली आत्मा अमर है और उसे कभी मारा नहीं जा सकता, इसलिए अर्जुन को किसी भी प्राणी के लिए शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ નિષ્કર્ષ કાઢે છે કે શરીરની અંદર રહેલો આત્મા અમર છે અને તેને ક્યારેય મારી શકાતો નથી, તેથી અર્જુને કોઈપણ પ્રાણી માટે શોક કરવો જોઈએ નહીં.
tweetEnglish: O Arjuna, the soul in the body can never be slain. Therefore, do not grieve for any living being.
threadsEnglish: O descendant of Bhārata, he who dwells in the body can never be slain. Therefore, you need not grieve for any living being.
englishTransliteration:
dehī nityam avadhyo ’yaṁ dehe sarvasya bhārata
tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṁ śocitum arhasi
englishWBW: dehī (the owner of the material body) — nityam (eternally) — avadhyaḥ (cannot be killed) — ayam (this soul) — dehe (in the body) — sarvasya (of everyone) — bhārata (O descendant of Bharata) — tasmāt (therefore) — sarvāṇi (all) — bhūtāni (living entities) — na (never) — tvam (you) — śocitum (to lament) — arhasi (deserve)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa gives the final verdict on the analytical section of His teaching. He declares that the indweller of the body is eternal and can never be killed. This applies to everyone’s body, whether friend or foe. Therefore, He says, “You need not grieve for any living being.”

This includes the relatives Arjuna is so afraid of losing. Kṛṣṇa has proven that the person Arjuna wants to save cannot be killed, and the body he wants to save cannot be preserved. Thus, the logical ground for his grief has been completely removed.

With this, Kṛṣṇa closes the chapter on the metaphysics of the soul. He has established the eternal reality that stands behind the temporary drama of the battlefield. Now, He will shift His argument to the social and moral responsibilities of a warrior, showing why action is necessary even in a world of temporary forms.

sanskrit:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाछ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते।।
translationEnglish:
Considering your specific duty as a kṣatriya, you should know that there is no better engagement for you than fighting on religious principles;
and so there is no need for hesitation.
translationHindi: तथा अपने धर्म को देखकर भी तू भय करने योग्य नहीं है, क्योंकि क्षत्रिय के लिए धर्मयुक्त युद्ध से बढ़कर दूसरा कोई कल्याणकारी कर्तव्य नहीं है।
translationGujarati: તથા પોતાના ધર્મને જોઈને પણ તારે ભય ન રાખવો જોઈએ, કારણ કે ક્ષત્રિય માટે ધર્મયુક્ત યુદ્ધથી વિશેષ બીજું કોઈ કલ્યાણકારી કર્તવ્ય નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa reminds Arjuna of his duty as a warrior (Kṣatriya), stating that fighting for righteousness is the highest duty and he should not hesitate.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को एक क्षत्रिय के रूप में उनके कर्तव्य की याद दिलाते हैं और कहते हैं कि धर्म के लिए युद्ध करना सबसे बड़ा कर्तव्य है और उन्हें हिचकिचाना नहीं चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને એક ક્ષત્રિય તરીકેના તેમના કર્તવ્યની યાદ અપાવે છે અને કહે છે કે ધર્મ માટે યુદ્ધ કરવું એ સર્વોચ્ચ કર્તવ્ય છે અને તેમણે ખચકાવું જોઈએ નહીં.
tweetEnglish: Considering your duty as a warrior, know there is no better engagement than fighting for righteousness.
threadsEnglish: Considering your specific duty as a warrior, know there is no better engagement for you than fighting for righteousness; do not hesitate.
englishTransliteration:
sva-dharmam api cāvekṣya na vikampitum arhasi
dharmyād dhi yuddhāc chreyo ’nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate
englishWBW: sva-dharmam (one’s own religious duty) — api (also) — ca (and) — avekṣya (considering) — na (not) — vikampitum (to hesitate) — arhasi (you deserve) — dharmyāt (for religious principles) — hi (certainly) — yuddhāt (than fighting) — śreyaḥ (better engagement) — anyat (any other) — kṣatriyasya (for the kṣatriya) — na (does not) — vidyate (exist)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa switches from philosophy to social duty. He reminds Arjuna of his specific role as a kṣatriya, or warrior. Even if Arjuna doesn’t fully grasp the eternal soul, he must consider his social obligation. For a warrior, there is no better engagement than fighting for religious principles.

Violence is not considered bad in itself in the Vedic tradition; it is bad when used for aggression, but it is glorious and necessary when used to protect justice. For a king or a soldier, avoiding a righteous war is a sin and a failure of character. Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that he is wrong to hesitate.

He is tightening the screws of his argument: “Spiritually you are wrong to cry, and socially you are wrong to quit.” By following his ‘sva-Dharma’, or personal duty, Arjuna will actually be performing his highest service to society and himself.

sanskrit:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम्।।
translationEnglish:
O Pārtha, happy are the kshatriyas to whom such fighting opportunities come unsought,
opening for them the doors of the heavenly planets.
translationHindi: हे पार्थ! अपने-आप प्राप्त हुए और खुले हुए स्वर्ग के द्वार रूप इस प्रकार के युद्ध को भाग्यवान क्षत्रिय लोग ही पाते हैं।
translationGujarati: હે પાર્થ! આપોઆપ પ્રાપ્ત થયેલા અને ખુલ્લા થયેલા સ્વર્ગના દ્વાર રૂપ આવા યુદ્ધને ભાગ્યશાળી ક્ષત્રિયો જ પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna that he is lucky, as such an unsolicited opportunity for battle opens the doors to heaven for a warrior.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि वे भाग्यशाली हैं, क्योंकि युद्ध का ऐसा अनचाहा अवसर एक योद्धा के लिए स्वर्ग के द्वार खोल देता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને કહે છે કે તેઓ ભાગ્યશાળી છે, કારણ કે યુદ્ધની આવી અચાનક મળેલી તક યોદ્ધા માટે સ્વર્ગના દ્વાર ખોલી દે છે.
tweetEnglish: Happy are the warriors to whom such fighting opportunities come unsought, opening the doors of heaven.
threadsEnglish: O Pārtha, happy are the warriors to whom such fighting opportunities come unsought, opening for them the doors of heaven.
englishTransliteration:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṁ svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛśam
englishWBW: yadṛcchayā (by its own accord) — ca (also) — upapannam (arrived at) — svarga (of the heavenly planets) — dvāram (door) — apāvṛtam (wide open) — sukhinaḥ (very happy) — kṣatriyāḥ (the warriors) — pārtha (O son of Pṛthā) — labhante (achieve) — yuddham (war) — īdṛśam (like this)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa points out that Arjuna is actually fortunate. This fighting opportunity has come to him ‘yadṛcchayā’, or of its own accord. Arjuna didn’t go looking for this war; it was forced upon him by the unrighteousness of the Kauravas. Such a war is like a wide-open door to the heavenly planets.

In Vedic culture, a warrior who dies in a righteous battle is said to go straight to ‘vīra-svarga’, or the hero’s heaven. It is considered a ‘win-win’ situation. If he wins, he rules the earth; if he dies, he attains celestial glory. Kṛṣṇa says that only happy and fortunate warriors get such a chance.

He is trying to change Arjuna’s perspective from one of victimhood to one of privilege. Instead of seeing the war as a tragedy, Arjuna is encouraged to see it as a rare opportunity to prove his valor and secure a glorious future, either in this world or the next.

sanskrit:
अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि।।
translationEnglish:
If, however, you do not perform your religious duty of fighting,
then you will certainly incur sins for neglecting your duties and thus lose your reputation as a fighter.
translationHindi: किन्तु यदि तू इस धर्मयुक्त युद्ध को नहीं करेगा, तो स्वधर्म और कीर्ति को खोकर पाप को प्राप्त होगा।
translationGujarati: પરંતુ જો તું આ ધર્મયુક્ત યુદ્ધ નહીં કરે, તો સ્વધર્મ અને કીર્તિ ગુમાવીને પાપને પામીશ.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa warns that if Arjuna refuses to fight this righteous war, he will neglect his duty, lose his reputation, and incur sin.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण चेतावनी देते हैं कि यदि अर्जुन इस धर्मयुद्ध को लड़ने से मना करते हैं, तो वे अपने कर्तव्य की अवहेलना करेंगे, अपनी प्रतिष्ठा खो देंगे और पाप के भागी बनेंगे।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ચેતવણી આપે છે કે જો અર્જુન આ ધર્મયુદ્ધ લડવાનો ઇનકાર કરશે, તો તેઓ તેમના કર્તવ્યની અવગણના કરશે, તેમની પ્રતિષ્ઠા ગુમાવશે અને પાપના ભાગીદાર બનશે.
tweetEnglish: If you do not fight this righteous war, you will neglect your duty, lose your reputation, and incur sin.
threadsEnglish: If, however, you do not perform your religious duty of fighting, you will certainly incur sin for neglecting your duty and lose your reputation.
englishTransliteration:
atha cet tvam imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṅgrāmaṁ na kariṣyasi
tataḥ sva-dharmaṁ kīrtiṁ ca hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi
englishWBW: atha (if) — cet (however) — tvam (you) — imam (this) — dharmyam (religious) — saṅgrāmam (fighting) — na (not) — kariṣyasi (will do) — tataḥ (then) — sva-dharmam (your religious duty) — kīrtim (reputation) — ca (also) — hitvā (losing) — pāpam (sin) — avāpsyasi (will gain)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa warns of the consequences of inaction. If Arjuna refuses to perform his religious duty of fighting this righteous war, he will lose both his ‘sva-Dharma’ (duty) and his ‘kīrtim’ (reputation). More importantly, he will incur sin for neglecting his responsibilities.

Arjuna thought that by not fighting he was being pious and saintly, but Kṛṣṇa corrects him: by abandoning the field, he is actually being sinful. Neglecting one’s appointed duty, especially when the innocent need protection, is a serious crime against the social and cosmic order.

Kṛṣṇa is showing that renunciation is not about running away from difficulty. Real renunciation is performing one’s duty despite the difficulty. If Arjuna quits now, he won’t be remembered as a saint, but as a man who failed his people at their greatest hour of need.

sanskrit:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्।
संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते।।
translationEnglish:
People will always speak of your infamy, and for a respectable person,
dishonor is worse than death.
translationHindi: तथा सब लोग तेरी बहुत काल तक रहने वाली अपकीर्ति का भी कथन करेंगे; और माननीय पुरुष के लिए अपकीर्ति मरण से भी बढ़कर है।
translationGujarati: તથા બધા લોકો તારી લાંબા સમય સુધી રહેનારી અપકીર્તિનું પણ કથન કરશે; અને સન્માનનીય પુરુષ માટે અપકીર્તિ મૃત્યુ કરતા પણ વધારે ખરાબ છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa says that people will speak of his infamy forever, and for a person of standing, dishonor is worse than death.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि लोग हमेशा आपकी बदनामी की बातें करेंगे, और एक सम्मानित व्यक्ति के लिए अपमान मृत्यु से भी बदतर होता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે લોકો હંમેશા તમારી બદનામીની વાતો કરશે, અને એક સન્માનિત વ્યક્તિ માટે અપમાન મૃત્યુ કરતા પણ ખરાબ હોય છે.
tweetEnglish: People will speak of your infamy forever. For a respectable person, dishonor is worse than death.
threadsEnglish: People will always speak of your infamy, and for a respectable person, dishonor is worse than death.
englishTransliteration:
akīrtiṁ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te ’vyayām
sambhāvitasya cākīrtir maraṇād atiricyate
englishWBW: akīrtim (infamy) — ca (also) — api (also) — bhūtāni (all people) — kathayiṣyanti (will speak) — te (of you) — avyayām (forever) — sambhāvitasya (for a respectable man) — ca (also) — akīrtiḥ (ill fame) — maraṇāt (than death) — atiricyate (is worse)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa hits Arjuna where it hurts most: his pride and his honor. He says that people will speak of his infamy forever. For a respectable man, dishonor is considered worse than death itself. Arjuna is a legendary hero whose fame spans the world.

If he leaves the battlefield now, history will not record his misplaced compassion; it will record that the great Arjuna fled in fear. Kṛṣṇa warns him that living with such a stain on his character will be far more painful than any wound he might receive in battle.

He is appealing to Arjuna’s warrior ego to snap him out of his despondency. He wants Arjuna to realize that the ‘saintly’ path he is trying to take will lead only to permanent social disgrace, which a man of his stature should find intolerable.

sanskrit:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्।।
translationEnglish:
The great generals who have highly esteemed your name and fame will think that you have left the battlefield out of fear only,
and thus they will consider you insignificant.
translationHindi: और जिनकी दृष्टि में तू पहले बहुत सम्मानित होकर अब लघुता को प्राप्त होगा, वे महारथी लोग तुझे भय के कारण युद्ध से हटा हुआ मानेंगे।
translationGujarati: અને જેની દ્રષ્ટિમાં તું પહેલા ખૂબ સન્માનિત થઈને હવે લઘુતાને પામીશ, તે મહારથીઓ તને ભયના કારણે યુદ્ધમાંથી ભાગેલો માનશે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that the great generals will think Arjuna left the battlefield out of fear, and those who respected him will now look down upon him.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि महान सेनापति सोचेंगे कि अर्जुन डर के मारे युद्धभूमि से भाग गए, और जो लोग उनका सम्मान करते थे, वे अब उन्हें तुच्छ समझेंगे।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે મહાન સેનાપતિઓ વિચારશે કે અર્જુન ડરના કારણે રણભૂમિ છોડી ગયા, અને જે લોકો તેમનું સન્માન કરતા હતા, તેઓ હવે તેમને તુચ્છ ગણશે.
tweetEnglish: Generals will think you left out of fear, and those who respected you will now despise you.
threadsEnglish: The great generals will think that you have left the battlefield out of fear only, and they will consider you insignificant.
englishTransliteration:
bhayād raṇād uparataṁ maṁsyante tvāṁ mahā-rathāḥ
yeṣāṁ ca tvaṁ bahu-mato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
englishWBW: bhayāt (out of fear) — raṇāt (from the battlefield) — uparatam (ceased) — maṁsyante (will consider) — tvām (you) — mahā-rathāḥ (the great generals) — yeṣām (for whom) — ca (also) — tvam (you) — bahu-mataḥ (in great estimation) — bhūtvā (having been) — yāsyasi (you will go) — lāghavam (to insignificance)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa dismantles Arjuna’s hope that his withdrawal will be seen as a moral gesture. The great generals like Duryodhana and Karṇa will not believe that Arjuna suddenly became a non-violent saint. They will assume he panicked upon seeing the size of their army.

Those who currently hold Arjuna in high regard will see him as insignificant and ‘light’. He will lose his status as a formidable leader. Kṛṣṇa warns him that his attempts at appearing compassionate will be interpreted as simple cowardice by his enemies and peers alike.

In the world of warriors, reputation is everything. Kṛṣṇa is showing Arjuna that by quitting, he is committing social suicide. He won’t be saving his family’s honor; he will be destroying his own and making himself a laughingstock in the eyes of the other great generals.

sanskrit:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्।।
translationEnglish:
Your enemies will describe you in many unkind words and scorn your ability.
What could be more painful for you?
translationHindi: तेरे वैरी लोग तेरे सामर्थ्य की निन्दा करते हुए तुझे बहुत से न कहने योग्य वचन भी कहेंगे; उससे अधिक दुःख की बात क्या होगी?
translationGujarati: તારા શત્રુઓ તારા સામર્થ્યની નિંદા કરતા તને ઘણા ન કહેવા યોગ્ય વચનો પણ કહેશે; તેનાથી વધુ દુઃખની વાત શું હશે?
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa points out that his enemies will use harsh words to criticize his ability, asking what could be more painful than that.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि उनके दुश्मन उनकी क्षमता की आलोचना करते हुए कठोर शब्दों का प्रयोग करेंगे, और पूछते हैं कि इससे अधिक दुखदाई क्या हो सकता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે તેમના શત્રુઓ તેમની ક્ષમતાની ટીકા કરતા કઠોર શબ્દોનો પ્રયોગ કરશે, અને પૂછે છે કે તેનાથી વધુ દુઃખદાયક શું હોઈ શકે.
tweetEnglish: Your enemies will use harsh words to scorn your ability. What could be more painful than that?
threadsEnglish: Your enemies will describe you in many unkind words and scorn your ability. What could be more painful for you?
englishTransliteration:
avācya-vādāṁś ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ
nindantas tava sāmarthyaṁ tato duḥkhataraṁ nu kim
englishWBW: avācya (unkind) — vādān (words) — ca (also) — bahūn (many) — vadiṣyanti (will say) — tava (your) — ahitāḥ (enemies) — nindantaḥ (while vilifying) — tava (your) — sāmarthyam (ability) — tataḥ (than that) — duḥkha-taram (more painful) — nu (certainly) — kim (what is there)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa continues to emphasize the social pain of cowardice. He says that Arjuna’s enemies will speak many unkind and unspeakable words, vilifying his ability and his strength. He asks, “What could be more painful for you than that?”

For a warrior, physical pain is part of the job, but insults to his prowess are intolerable. Kṛṣṇa is using reverse psychology, inciting Arjuna’s anger and pride to counteract his misplaced compassion. He knows that for a kṣatriya, the fear of ridicule is often a stronger motivator than the fear of death.

He is painting a vivid picture of the humiliation that awaits Arjuna if he drops his bow. By highlighting the harsh reality of how his enemies will treat his ‘saintliness’, Kṛṣṇa is trying to provoke Arjuna back into his warrior mindset, where honor is valued above bodily comfort.

sanskrit:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः।।
translationEnglish:
O son of Kunti, either you will be killed on the battlefield and attain the heavenly planets,
or you will conquer and enjoy the earthly kingdom.
Therefore, get up with determination and fight.
translationHindi: या तो तू युद्ध में मारा जाकर स्वर्ग को प्राप्त होगा, अथवा संग्राम में जीतकर पृथ्वी का राज्य भोगेगा। इस कारण हे अर्जुन! तू युद्ध के लिए निश्चय करके खड़ा हो जा।
translationGujarati: કાં તો તું યુદ્ધમાં મરાઈને સ્વર્ગ પામીશ, અથવા યુદ્ધ જીતીને પૃથ્વીનું રાજ્ય ભોગવીશ. આ કારણે હે અર્જુન! તું યુદ્ધ માટે નિશ્ચય કરીને ઊભો થા.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa encourages Arjuna to fight, saying that if he dies he gains heaven, and if he wins he rules the earth, so he should arise with determination.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को युद्ध के लिए प्रोत्साहित करते हैं, यह कहते हुए कि यदि वे मरते हैं तो स्वर्ग प्राप्त करेंगे और यदि जीतते हैं तो पृथ्वी का राज्य भोगेंगे, इसलिए उन्हें दृढ़ निश्चय के साथ उठना चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને યુદ્ધ માટે પ્રોત્સાહિત કરે છે, એમ કહીને કે જો તેઓ મૃત્યુ પામશે તો સ્વર્ગ પામશે અને જો જીતશે તો પૃથ્વીનું રાજ્ય ભોગવશે, તેથી તેમણે દ્રઢ નિશ્ચય સાથે ઊભા થવું જોઈએ.
tweetEnglish: If killed, you attain heaven; if you win, you enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise and fight with determination!
threadsEnglish: O son of Kunti, either you will be killed and attain heaven, or you will conquer and enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise and fight with determination.
englishTransliteration:
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṁ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm
tasmād uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛta-niścayaḥ
englishWBW: hataḥ (being killed) — vā (or) — prāpsyasi (you will attain) — svargam (the heavenly kingdom) — jitvā (by conquering) — vā (or) — bhokṣyase (you will enjoy) — mahīm (the world) — tasmāt (therefore) — uttiṣṭha (get up) — kaunteya (O son of Kuntī) — yuddhāya (for fighting) — kṛta (determined) — niścayaḥ (decided)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa summarizes the ‘Win-Win’ logic for a warrior. If Arjuna is killed in this righteous battle, he will attain the heavenly planets. If he conquers, he will enjoy a flourishing kingdom on earth. There is no losing outcome for him if he fights.

Therefore, He commands: “Stand up, O son of Kuntī, with determination to fight!” The word ‘uttiṣṭha’ is a call for physical and mental mobilization. Arjuna must replace his doubt with ‘kṛta-niścayaḥ’, or firm resolve.

By addressing him as ‘Kaunteya’, Kṛṣṇa reminds him of his noble lineage and his mother’s expectations. He is showing Arjuna that the path of duty is the only path that leads to a positive result, whether in this life or the next. Hesitation is the only true failure.

sanskrit:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि।।
translationEnglish:
Do thou fight for the sake of fighting, without considering happiness or distress, loss or gain, victory or defeat—
and by so doing you shall never incur sin.
translationHindi: जय-पराजय, लाभ-हानि और सुख-दुःख को समान समझकर, उसके बाद युद्ध के लिए तैयार हो जा; इस प्रकार युद्ध करने से तू पाप को नहीं प्राप्त होगा।
translationGujarati: જય-પરાજય, લાભ-હાનિ અને સુખ-દુઃખને સમાન સમજીને, ત્યાર પછી યુદ્ધ માટે તૈયાર થા; આ રીતે યુદ્ધ કરવાથી તને પાપ નહીં લાગે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa advises Arjuna to fight for the sake of duty, treating happiness and distress, victory and defeat as the same, to avoid incurring sin.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को सलाह देते हैं कि वे सुख-दुःख, लाभ-हानि और जय-पराजय को समान मानकर केवल कर्तव्य के लिए युद्ध करें, ताकि उन्हें पाप न लगे।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને સલાહ આપે છે કે તેઓ સુખ-દુઃખ, લાભ-હાનિ અને જય-પરાજયને સમાન માનીને માત્ર કર્તવ્ય માટે યુદ્ધ કરે, જેથી તેમને પાપ ન લાગે.
tweetEnglish: Fight for the sake of duty, treating happiness and distress, loss and gain, victory and defeat as the same.
threadsEnglish: Do thou fight for the sake of fighting, without considering happiness or distress, loss or gain, victory or defeat—thus you shall never incur sin.
englishTransliteration:
sukha-duḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṁ pāpam avāpsyasi
englishWBW: sukha (happiness) — duḥkhe (in distress) — same (equal) — kṛtvā (making) — lābha-alābhau (loss and profit) — jaya-ajayau (victory and defeat) — tataḥ (thereafter) — yuddhāya (for the sake of fighting) — yujyasva (engage in battle) — na (never) — evam (in this way) — pāpam (sin) — avāpsyasi (you will gain)
englishExplain:
Having exhausted the social and worldly arguments, Kṛṣṇa introduces the secret of Yoga—how to act without being entangled. He tells Arjuna to treat happiness and distress, loss and gain, and victory and defeat as the same.

If Arjuna fights with this consciousness—fighting simply because it is his duty, without any personal desire for the result—he will never incur sin. This is the foundation of Karma-yoga. Sin lies not in the act of fighting, but in the attachment to the selfish outcome.

Kṛṣṇa is teaching Arjuna how to remain pure while performing a violent task. By neutralizing his mind toward the dualities of life, Arjuna can become an instrument of the divine will. This internal detachment transforms a mundane struggle into a spiritual sacrifice.

sanskrit:
एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु।
बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि।।
translationEnglish:
Thus far I have described this knowledge to you through analytical study.
Now listen as I explain it in terms of working without fruitive results.
O son of Prith, when you act in such knowledge you can free yourself from the bondage of works.
translationHindi: हे पार्थ! यह बुद्धि तेरे लिए ज्ञानयोग (सांख्य) के विषय में कही गयी और अब तू इसको कर्मयोग (बुद्धियोग) के विषय में सुन, जिस बुद्धि से युक्त होकर तू कर्मों के बन्धन को भली-भांति त्याग देगा।
translationGujarati: હે પાર્થ! આ બુદ્ધિ તારા માટે જ્ઞાનયોગ (સાંખ્ય) ના વિષયમાં કહેવામાં આવી અને હવે તું તેને કર્મયોગ (બુદ્ધિયોગ) ના વિષયમાં સાંભળ, જે બુદ્ધિથી યુક્ત થઈને તું કર્મોના બંધનને સારી રીતે છોડી દઈશ.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa says he has explained the analytical knowledge (Sankhya) and will now explain the yoga of selfless action (Buddhi-yoga), which frees one from karma.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि उन्होंने ज्ञानयोग (सांख्य) समझाया है और अब वे निष्काम कर्मयोग (बुद्धियोग) समझाएंगे, जो मनुष्य को कर्मों के बंधन से मुक्त कर देता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે તેમણે જ્ઞાનયોગ (સાંખ્ય) સમજાવ્યો છે અને હવે તેઓ નિષ્કામ કર્મયોગ (બુદ્ધિયોગ) સમજાવશે, જે મનુષ્યને કર્મોના બંધનમાંથી મુક્ત કરી દે છે.
tweetEnglish: I have explained analytical knowledge. Now listen to the yoga of selfless action, which frees you from bondage.
threadsEnglish: I have explained analytical knowledge. Now listen to the yoga of selfless action; when you act in such knowledge, you can free yourself from bondage.
englishTransliteration:
eṣā te ’bhihitā sāṅkhye buddhir yoge tv imāṁ śṛṇu
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karma-bandhaṁ prahāsyasi
englishWBW: eṣā (all this) — te (unto you) — abhihitā (described) — sāṅkhye (by analytical study) — buddhiḥ (intelligence) — yoge (in work without fruitive results) — tu (but) — imām (this) — śṛṇu (listen) — buddhyā (by intelligence) — yuktaḥ (dovetailed) — yayā (by which) — pārtha (O Arjuna) — karma-bandham (bondage of reaction) — prahāsyasi (you can be released from)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa marks a transition in His teaching. He says that so far He has described this knowledge through analytical study, or Sāṅkhya. Now, He wants Arjuna to listen as He explains it in terms of ‘Yoga’, or working without desiring results.

Sāṅkhya is the intellectual understanding that the soul is distinct from the body. Yoga is the practical application of that knowledge in the world. Kṛṣṇa promises that when Arjuna acts with this specific intelligence, he will be released from the bondage of karma.

He is showing that spiritual life doesn’t require one to stop acting; it requires one to change the ‘consciousness’ behind the action. This is the key to freedom: using one’s intelligence to work in a way that doesn’t create new knots of entanglement in the material world.

sanskrit:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्।।
translationEnglish: In this endeavor there is no loss or diminution, and a little advancement on this path can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear.
translationHindi: इस कर्मयोग में आरम्भ का नाश नहीं है और उलटा फल रूप दोष भी नहीं है, बल्कि इस कर्मयोग रूप धर्म का थोड़ा-सा भी साधन महान भय से रक्षा कर लेता है।
translationGujarati: આ કર્મયોગમાં આરંભનો નાશ નથી અને વિપરીત ફળ રૂપ દોષ પણ નથી, પરંતુ આ કર્મયોગ રૂપ ધર્મનું થોડું પણ સાધન મહાન ભયથી રક્ષા કરે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa assures that on this path of selfless action, no effort is wasted, and even a little progress protects one from great fear.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण आश्वासन देते हैं कि निष्काम कर्म के मार्ग पर कोई भी प्रयास व्यर्थ नहीं जाता, और थोड़ी सी भी प्रगति मनुष्य को बड़े भय से बचा लेती है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ આશ્વાસન આપે છે કે નિષ્કામ કર્મના માર્ગ પર કોઈ પણ પ્રયાસ વ્યર્થ જતો નથી, અને થોડી પણ પ્રગતિ મનુષ્યને મોટા ભયથી બચાવી લે છે.
tweetEnglish: In this path, no effort is wasted, and even a little advancement protects one from the greatest fear.
threadsEnglish: In this endeavor, there is no loss, and a little advancement on this path can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear.
englishTransliteration:
nehābhikrama-nāśo ’sti pratyavāyo na vidyate
svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
englishWBW: na (there is not) — iha (in this) — abhikrama (endeavor) — nāśaḥ (loss) — asti (there is) — pratyavāyaḥ (diminution) — na (not) — vidyate (exists) — su-alpam (a little) — api (even) — asya (of this) — dharmasya (occupation) — trāyate (releases) — mahataḥ (from very great) — bhayāt (danger)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa glorifies the path of selfless action. He says that in this endeavor, there is no loss or diminution. Material efforts are often wasted if they are not completed, but in spiritual life, every step counts and is permanently recorded.

Even a little advancement on this path of Dharma can protect a person from the most dangerous type of fear—the fear of degrading into a lower species in the next life. Spiritual assets are the only ones that survive the death of the body.

Kṛṣṇa is giving Arjuna immense confidence. He is saying that even if he fails to achieve perfect detachment immediately, his effort will not be in vain. It is a risk-free investment in one’s eternal future, offering protection that no worldly kingdom could ever provide.

sanskrit:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्।।
translationEnglish:
Those who are on this path are resolute in purpose, and their aim is one.
O beloved child of the Kurus, the intelligence of those who are irresolute is many-branched.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! इस कर्मयोग में निश्चयात्मिका बुद्धि एक ही होती है; किन्तु अस्थिर विचार वाले विवेकहीन सकाम मनुष्यों की बुद्धियाँ निश्चय ही बहुत भेदों वाली और अनन्त होती हैं।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! આ કર્મયોગમાં નિશ્ચયાત્મક બુદ્ધિ એક જ હોય છે; પરંતુ અસ્થિર વિચારવાળા વિવેકહીન સકામ મનુષ્યોની બુદ્ધિઓ નિશ્ચય જ ઘણા ભેદોવાળી અને અનંત હોય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that those on this spiritual path have a single, resolute focus, whereas the intelligence of the irresolute is scattered and many-branched.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि इस आध्यात्मिक मार्ग पर चलने वालों का लक्ष्य एक और दृढ़ होता है, जबकि अस्थिर मन वाले लोगों की बुद्धि बिखरी हुई और अनेक शाखाओं वाली होती है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે આ આધ્યાત્મિક માર્ગ પર ચાલનારાઓનું લક્ષ્ય એક અને દ્રઢ હોય છે, જ્યારે અસ્થિર મનવાળા લોકોની બુદ્ધિ વિખરાયેલી અને અનેક શાખાઓવાળી હોય છે.
tweetEnglish: Those on this path are resolute with one aim. The intelligence of the irresolute is many-branched.
threadsEnglish: Those on this path are resolute in purpose, and their aim is one. O beloved child of the Kurus, the intelligence of the irresolute is many-branched.
englishTransliteration:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana
bahu-śākhā hy anantāś ca buddhayo ’vyavasāyinām
englishWBW: vyavasāya-ātmikā (resolute) — buddhiḥ (intelligence) — ekā (only one) — iha (in this world) — kuru-nandana (O beloved child of the Kurus) — bahu-śākhāḥ (having many branches) — hi (certainly) — anantāḥ (unlimited) — ca (and) — buddhayaḥ (intelligence) — avyavasāyinām (of those who are not resolute)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa distinguishes between the focused and the scattered mind. He says that those on the spiritual path are resolute in purpose, and their aim is one. They have a single-pointed determination to serve the Supreme.

In contrast, the intelligence of the irresolute is many-branched and unlimited. People without a clear spiritual goal are pulled in a thousand directions by their various desires, whims, and social pressures. They are constantly distracted by new ideas and temporary rewards.

Kṛṣṇa urges Arjuna to have a focused intellect. By having one clear objective—satisfying the Divine through his duty—his life becomes simple and powerful. A scattered mind is a weak mind, but a resolute mind can conquer any obstacle on the path to liberation.

sanskrit:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः।
वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः।।
translationEnglish:
Men of small knowledge are very much attached to the flowery words of the Vedas,
which recommend various fruitive activities for elevation to heavenly planets,
resultant good birth, power, and so forth.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! जो भोगों में तन्मय हो रहे हैं, जो कर्मफल के प्रशंसक वेदवाक्यों में ही प्रीति रखते हैं, जिनकी बुद्धि में स्वर्ग ही परम प्राप्य वस्तु है और जो ‘स्वर्ग से बढ़कर दूसरी कोई वस्तु ही नहीं है’ - ऐसा कहने वाले हैं...
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! જેઓ ભોગોમાં તન્મય થઈ રહ્યા છે, જેઓ કર્મફળના પ્રશંસક વેદવાક્યોમાં જ પ્રીતિ રાખે છે, જેમની બુદ્ધિમાં સ્વર્ગ જ પરમ પ્રાપ્ય વસ્તુ છે અને જેઓ ‘સ્વર્ગથી વિશેષ બીજી કોઈ વસ્તુ જ નથી’ - એવું કહેનારા છે...
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa criticizes those with limited knowledge who are attracted to the flowery language of the Vedas offering worldly pleasures and power.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण उन अल्पज्ञानी लोगों की आलोचना करते हैं जो वेदों की उन लुभावनी बातों से आकर्षित होते हैं जो सांसारिक सुख और शक्ति का वादा करती हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ તે અલ્પજ્ઞાની લોકોની ટીકા કરે છે જે વેદોની તે લોભામણી વાતોથી આકર્ષિત થાય છે જે સાંસારિક સુખ અને શક્તિનું વચન આપે છે.
tweetEnglish: Men of small knowledge are attached to the flowery words of the Vedas that promise power and heaven.
threadsEnglish: Men of small knowledge are attached to the flowery words of the Vedas, which recommend activities for elevation to heaven and power.
englishTransliteration:
yām imāṁ puṣpitāṁ vācaṁ pravadanty avipaścitaḥ
Veda-vāda-ratāḥ pārtha nānyad astīti vādinaḥ
englishWBW: yām (which) — imām (this) — puṣpitām (flowery) — vācam (words) — pravadanti (say) — avipaścitaḥ (men with small knowledge) — Veda-vāda-ratāḥ (attached to the flowery words of the Vedas) — pārtha (O Arjuna) — na (never) — anyat (anything else) — asti (there is) — iti (thus) — vādinaḥ (advocates)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa critques those with limited knowledge who are overly attached to the ‘flowery words’ of the Vedas. These people are interested only in the sections of the scriptures that recommend rituals for material prosperity, good birth, and power.

They argue that there is nothing beyond these material rewards. They use the Vedas as a manual for successful material living rather than a guide for spiritual liberation. Kṛṣṇa calls them ‘avipaścitaḥ’, or men of small knowledge, because they mistake the means for the end.

He warns Arjuna not to be seduced by such superficial religious talk. True knowledge is not about getting a better life in this world or in heaven; it is about knowing the Self and the Supreme. Kṛṣṇa wants Arjuna to aim for the essence of the scriptures, not just their decorative rituals.

sanskrit:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति।।
translationEnglish: Being desirous of sense gratification and opulent life, they say that there is nothing more than this.
translationHindi: वे अविवेकीजन जन्म-मृत्यु रूप कर्मफल को देने वाली, भोग तथा ऐश्वर्य की प्राप्ति के लिए नाना प्रकार की बहुत-सी क्रियाओं का वर्णन करने वाली, इस प्रकार की जिस पुष्पित वाणी को कहते हैं...
translationGujarati: તે અવિવેકી લોકો જન્મ-મૃત્યુ રૂપ કર્મફળ આપનારી, ભોગ તથા ઐશ્વર્યની પ્રાપ્તિ માટે વિવિધ પ્રકારની ઘણી ક્રિયાઓનું વર્ણન કરનારી, આ પ્રકારની જે પુષ્પિત વાણી બોલે છે...
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa continues describing such people as desirous of sense gratification and opulence, performing many rituals that only lead to rebirth.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण आगे कहते हैं कि ऐसे लोग भोग और ऐश्वर्य की कामना करते हैं और ऐसे कई अनुष्ठान करते हैं जो केवल पुनर्जन्म की ओर ले जाते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ આગળ કહે છે કે એવા લોકો ભોગ અને ઐશ્વર્યની કામના કરે છે અને એવા ઘણા અનુષ્ઠાન કરે છે જે માત્ર પુનર્જન્મ તરફ લઈ જાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Desiring sense gratification and opulence, they perform rituals that only lead to rebirth.
threadsEnglish: Being desirous of sense gratification and opulent life, they perform many rituals that only lead to good birth and rebirth.
englishTransliteration:
kāmātmānaḥ svarga-parā janma-karma-phala-pradām
kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṁ bhogaiśvarya-gatiṁ prati
englishWBW: kāma-ātmānaḥ (desirous of sense gratification) — svarga-parāḥ (aiming for heaven) — janma-karma-phala (rebirth as the result of work) — pradām (yielding) — kriyā-viśeṣa (pompous ceremonies) — bahulām (various) — bhoga (enjoyment) — aiśvarya (opulence) — gatim (progress) — prati (towards)
englishExplain:
Expanding on the previous verse, Kṛṣṇa describes the mindset of the materialistically religious. Their hearts are full of desire, and their ultimate goal is reaching the heavenly planets for sense gratification. They perform various pompous ceremonies to achieve opulence and a good birth.

However, these activities only lead to more karma and repeated birth and death. Even the ‘heavenly’ rewards are temporary; once the merit is exhausted, the soul must return to earth. Their entire focus is on ‘bhoga’ (enjoyment) and ‘aiśvarya’ (power).

Kṛṣṇa is showing Arjuna that this type of religion is just another form of material entanglement. It keeps the soul busy with rituals while leaving it spiritually empty. He encourages Arjuna to transcend this transactional relationship with the Divine and seek something eternal and unchanging.

sanskrit:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते।।
translationEnglish:
In the minds of those who are too attached to sense enjoyment and material opulence, and who are bewildered by such things,
the resolute determination for devotional service to the Supreme Lord does not take place.
translationHindi: उस पुष्पित वाणी से जिनका चित्त हर लिया गया है, जो भोग और ऐश्वर्य में अत्यन्त आसक्त हैं, उन पुरुषों की परमात्मा में निश्चयात्मिका बुद्धि नहीं होती।
translationGujarati: તે પુષ્પિત વાણીથી જેમનું ચિત્ત હરાઈ ગયું છે, જેઓ ભોગ અને ઐશ્વર્યમાં અત્યંત આસક્ત છે, તે પુરુષોની પરમાત્મામાં નિશ્ચયાત્મક બુદ્ધિ નથી હોતી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa states that those obsessed with sense enjoyment and wealth cannot have the resolute determination needed for spiritual absorption.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जो लोग भोग-विलास और धन-संपत्ति में बहुत अधिक आसक्त हैं, उनमें आध्यात्मिक समाधि के लिए आवश्यक दृढ़ निश्चय नहीं होता।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે જે લોકો ભોગ-વિલાસ અને ધન-સંપત્તિમાં ખૂબ જ આસક્ત છે, તેમનામાં આધ્યાત્મિક સમાધિ માટે જરૂરી દ્રઢ નિશ્ચય હોતો નથી.
tweetEnglish: Those too attached to sense enjoyment and power cannot find the resolute determination for spiritual absorption.
threadsEnglish: In the minds of those too attached to sense enjoyment and material opulence, the resolute determination for spiritual absorption does not take place.
englishTransliteration:
bhogaiśvarya-prasaktānāṁ tayāpahṛta-cetasām
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
englishWBW: bhoga (material enjoyment) — aiśvarya (opulence) — prasaktānām (of those who are attached) — tayā (by such things) — apahṛta-cetasām (bewildered in mind) — vyavasāya-ātmikā (resolute) — buddhiḥ (intelligence) — samādhau (in the controlled mind) — na (never) — vidhīyate (takes place)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa delivers a hard truth about spiritual focus. For those who are too attached to material enjoyment and power, and whose minds are bewildered by such things, resolute determination for spiritual realization never takes place. Their minds are too cluttered with worldly plans.

‘Samādhi’ refers to a state of total absorption in the Divine. This state is impossible to reach if the mind is constantly chasing the next promotion, the next purchase, or the next sensory thrill. You cannot look toward the sun and the shadows at the same time.

Arjuna’s indecision was partly due to his concern for his future status and comfort. Kṛṣṇa is telling him that he must let go of these attachments if he wants to achieve the clarity of a yogī. A heart divided between God and gold can never find peace or steady wisdom.

sanskrit:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्।।
translationEnglish:
The Vedas deal mainly with the subject of the three modes of material nature.
O Arjuna, become transcendental to these three modes. Be free from all dualities and from all anxieties for gain and safety,
and be established in the self.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! वेद तीनों गुणों के कार्य रूप भोगों और उनके साधनों का प्रतिपादन करने वाले हैं; तू उन भोगों और उनके साधनों में आसक्तिहीन, हर्ष-शोकादि द्वन्द्वों से रहित, नित्यवस्तु परमात्मा में स्थित, योग-क्षेम को न चाहने वाला और आत्मपरायण हो।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! વેદ ત્રણેય ગુણોના કાર્ય રૂપ ભોગો અને તેના સાધનોનું પ્રતિપાદન કરનારા છે; તું તે ભોગો અને તેના સાધનોમાં આસક્તિરહિત, હર્ષ-શોક વગેરે દ્વંદ્વોથી મુક્ત, નિત્યવસ્તુ પરમાત્મામાં સ્થિત, યોગ-ક્ષેમને ન ઈચ્છનારો અને આત્મપરાયણ થા.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa advises Arjuna to rise above the three modes of material nature described in the Vedas, to be free from dualities and anxiety for gain, and to be established in the self.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को वेदों में वर्णित प्रकृति के तीन गुणों से ऊपर उठने, द्वंद्वों और लाभ की चिंता से मुक्त होने और आत्म-तत्व में स्थित होने की सलाह देते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને વેદોમાં વર્ણવેલા પ્રકૃતિના ત્રણ ગુણોથી ઉપર ઉઠવા, દ્વંદ્વો અને લાભની ચિંતાથી મુક્ત થવા અને આત્મ-તત્વમાં સ્થિત થવાની સલાહ આપે છે.
tweetEnglish: Rise above the modes of nature. Be free from duality and anxiety, and be established in the Self.
threadsEnglish: The Vedas deal mainly with the three modes of nature. O Arjuna, become transcendental to these modes. Be free from dualities and anxieties for gain.
englishTransliteration:
traiguṇya-viṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna
nirdvandvo nitya-Sattva-stho niryoga-kṣema ātmavān
englishWBW: trai-guṇya (the three modes of material nature) — viṣayāḥ (dealing with) — vedāḥ (the Vedic literatures) — nistraiguṇyaḥ (transcendental to the three modes) — bhava (be) — Arjuna (O Arjuna) — nirdvandvaḥ (free from dualities) — nitya-Sattva-sthaḥ (fixed in pure goodness) — niryoga-kṣemaḥ (free from ideas of gain and protection) — ātmavān (established in the self)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa advises Arjuna to transcend the Vedas. He explained that the Vedic scriptures deal mainly with the three modes of material nature—goodness, passion, and ignorance. They teach how to live successfully within these modes. But Kṛṣṇa wants Arjuna to go beyond them.

He tells him to be free from all dualities, like honor and dishonor, and to be ‘niryoga-kṣema’, or free from the anxiety of acquiring what he lacks and protecting what he has. This constant worry about security and profit kills the spirit.

By being established in pure existence (‘nitya-Sattva-sthaḥ’), Arjuna can become ‘ātmavān’, or truly self-possessed. Kṛṣṇa is asking him to stop being a player in the material game and to become an observer situated in the spiritual reality. This is the only way to find true freedom from the pressures of the world.

sanskrit:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः।।
translationEnglish:
All purposes served by a small well can at once be served by a great reservoir of water.
Similarly, all the purposes of the Vedas can be served to one who knows the purpose behind them.
translationHindi: सब ओर से परिपूर्ण जलाशय के प्राप्त हो जाने पर छोटे जलाशय में मनुष्य का जितना प्रयोजन रहता है, ब्रह्म को तत्त्व से जानने वाले ब्राह्मण का समस्त वेदों में उतना ही प्रयोजन रह जाता है।
translationGujarati: ચારે બાજુથી ભરેલા જળાશય પ્રાપ્ત થઈ જવા પર નાના જળાશયમાં મનુષ્યનું જેટલું પ્રયોજન રહે છે, બ્રહ્મને તત્વથી જાણનારા બ્રાહ્મણનું તમામ વેદોમાં તેટલું જ પ્રયોજન રહી જાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that just as a large reservoir fulfills all the needs served by a small well, one who knows the Absolute Truth fulfills the purpose of all the Vedas.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि जैसे एक विशाल जलाशय छोटे कुएं की सभी जरूरतों को पूरा कर देता है, वैसे ही जो परम सत्य को जानता है, वह वेदों के सभी उद्देश्यों को पूरा कर लेता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે જેમ એક વિશાળ જળાશય નાના કૂવાની બધી જરૂરિયાતો પૂરી કરી દે છે, તેમ જે પરમ સત્યને જાણે છે, તે વેદોના બધા ઉદ્દેશ્યો પૂરા કરી લે છે.
tweetEnglish: As a large reservoir fulfills all uses of a well, one who knows the Truth fulfills the purpose of all Vedas.
threadsEnglish: All purposes served by a small well can be served by a great reservoir. Similarly, all purposes of the Vedas are served to one who knows the Truth.
englishTransliteration:
yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake
tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
englishWBW: yāvān (all that) — arthaḥ (purpose) — uda-pāne (in a well) — sarvataḥ (everywhere) — sampluta-udake (in a large reservoir of water) — tāvān (similarly) — sarveṣu (in all) — vedeṣu (Vedic literatures) — brāhmaṇasya (of the man who knows Brahman) — vijānataḥ (who is in knowledge)
englishExplain:
