translationHindi: न तो कर्मों का आरम्भ किए बिना मनुष्य निष्कर्मता को प्राप्त होता है और न कर्मों के केवल त्यागमात्र से सिद्धि (योगनिष्ठा) को ही प्राप्त होता है।
translationGujarati: ન તો કર્મોનો આરંભ કર્યા વિના મનુષ્ય નિષ્કર્મતાને પામે છે અને ન તો કર્મોના કેવળ ત્યાગ માત્રથી સિદ્ધિ (યોગનિષ્ઠા) ને પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa clarifies that one does not attain freedom from reaction simply by abstaining from work, nor does one attain perfection by mere renunciation.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण स्पष्ट करते हैं कि केवल काम न करने से कोई कर्म-बंधन से मुक्त नहीं होता, और न ही केवल संन्यास लेने से सिद्धि प्राप्त होती है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સ્પષ્ટ કરે છે કે માત્ર કામ ન કરવાથી કોઈ કર્મ-બંધનમાંથી મુક્ત થતું નથી, અને માત્ર સંન્યાસ લેવાથી સિદ્ધિ પ્રાપ્ત થતી નથી.
tweetEnglish: Not by abstaining from work can one achieve freedom, nor by renunciation alone can one attain perfection.
threadsEnglish: One cannot achieve freedom from karmic reactions by merely abstaining from work, nor can one attain perfection through renunciation alone.
englishTransliteration:
na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṁ puruṣo ’śnute
na ca sannyasanād eva siddhiṁ samadhigacchati
englishWBW: na (not) — karmaṇām (of prescribed duties) — anārambhāt (by non-performance) — naiṣkarmyam (freedom from reaction) — puruṣaḥ (a man) — aśnute (achieves) — na (not) — ca (also) — sannyasanāt (by renunciation) — eva (simply) — siddhim (perfection) — samadhigacchati (attains)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa debunks the myth that spirituality means doing nothing. He states that one cannot achieve freedom from karmic reaction simply by abstaining from work. Nor can one attain perfection merely by taking the formal vow of renunciation, or sannyāsa.

Many people think that if they stop acting, they will stop creating karma. But Kṛṣṇa says that ‘Naiṣkarmyam’ (actionlessness) is a state of consciousness, not a physical state. You can be physically still but mentally full of desire, which is still a form of action.

True renunciation is internal. It is the giving up of the desire for the result, not the work itself. Simply changing one’s dress or moving to a cave doesn’t bring perfection if the heart is still attached to the world. Perfection is found through the purification that comes from doing one’s duty without ego.

sanskrit:
न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः।।
translationEnglish:
Everyone is forced to act helplessly according to the qualities he has acquired from the modes of material nature;
therefore no one can refrain from doing something, not even for a moment.
translationHindi: निस्संदेह कोई भी मनुष्य किसी भी काल में क्षणमात्र भी बिना कर्म किये नहीं रहता; क्योंकि सारा मनुष्य समुदाय प्रकृति से उत्पन्न गुणों द्वारा परवश हुआ कर्म करने के लिए बाध्य किया जाता है।
translationGujarati: નિઃશંક કોઈ પણ મનુષ્ય કોઈ પણ કાળમાં ક્ષણ માત્ર પણ કર્મ કર્યા વિના રહેતો નથી; કારણ કે સમસ્ત મનુષ્ય સમુદાય પ્રકૃતિથી ઉત્પન્ન થયેલા ગુણો દ્વારા પરવશ થઈને કર્મ કરવા માટે બાધ્ય થાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa points out that no one can remain without acting even for a moment, because everyone is helplessly forced to act by the qualities born of material nature.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि कोई भी व्यक्ति एक क्षण के लिए भी बिना कर्म किए नहीं रह सकता, क्योंकि हर कोई प्रकृति के गुणों द्वारा विवश होकर कर्म करने के लिए बाध्य है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ જણાવે છે કે કોઈ પણ વ્યક્તિ એક ક્ષણ માટે પણ કર્મ કર્યા વિના રહી શકતી નથી, કારણ કે દરેક જણ પ્રકૃતિના ગુણો દ્વારા વિવશ થઈને કર્મ કરવા માટે બાધ્ય છે.
tweetEnglish: Everyone is forced to act helplessly according to nature; no one can refrain from doing something.
threadsEnglish: No one can remain without performing action even for a moment. Everyone is driven to act by the impulses born of the modes of nature.
englishTransliteration:
na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhaty akarma-kṛt
kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛti-jair guṇaiḥ
englishWBW: na (never) — hi (certainly) — kaścit (anyone) — kṣaṇam (a moment) — api (even) — jātu (at any time) — tiṣṭhati (remains) — akarma-kṛt (without doing something) — kāryate (is forced to do) — hi (certainly) — avaśaḥ (helplessly) — karma (work) — sarvaḥ (everyone) — prakṛti-jaiḥ (born of material nature) — guṇaiḥ (by the modes)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains the reality of our biological and psychological existence. No one can remain without performing some kind of action, even for a single moment. Even when you are sleeping or sitting still, your heart is beating, your lungs are breathing, and your mind is processing.

Everyone is forced to act helplessly by the ‘guṇas’, or the modes of material nature (goodness, passion, and ignorance). These forces are like invisible strings that move the body and mind. We are not independent; we are part of a giant mechanical system that is always in motion.

Since activity is unavoidable, the goal of yoga is not to stop it, but to master it. Trying to be ‘inactive’ is a fight against nature that you cannot win. Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that since he *must* act, he should learn how to act in a way that leads to freedom rather than further bondage.

sanskrit:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्।
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते।।
translationEnglish:
One who restrains the senses of action but whose mind dwells on sense objects
certainly deludes himself and is called a pretender.
translationHindi: जो मूढ़बुद्धि मनुष्य समस्त इन्द्रियों को हठपूर्वक ऊपर से रोककर मन से उन इन्द्रियों के विषयों का चिन्तन करता रहता है, वह मिथ्याचारी (दम्भी) कहा जाता है।
translationGujarati: જે મૂઢબુદ્ધિ મનુષ્ય તમામ ઇન્દ્રિયોને હઠપૂર્વક ઉપરથી રોકીને મનથી તે ઇન્દ્રિયોના વિષયોનું ચિંતન કરતો રહે છે, તે મિથ્યાચારી (દંભી) કહેવાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa warns that one who restrains the senses of action but mentally dwells on sense objects is a pretender and deludes himself.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण चेतावनी देते हैं कि जो व्यक्ति अपनी कर्मेंद्रियों को तो रोक लेता है लेकिन मन ही मन विषयों का चिंतन करता रहता है, वह पाखंडी है और स्वयं को धोखा देता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ચેતવણી આપે છે કે જે વ્યક્તિ પોતાની કર્મેન્દ્રિયોને તો રોકી લે છે પરંતુ મનોમન વિષયોનું ચિંતન કરતો રહે છે, તે પાખંડી છે અને પોતાને છેતરે છે.
tweetEnglish: One who restrains the senses of action but whose mind dwells on sense objects is a pretender.
threadsEnglish: One who restrains the senses but dwells on sense objects in the mind is a hypocrite and is self-deluded.
englishTransliteration:
karmendriyāṇi saṁyamya ya āste manasā smaran
indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate
englishWBW: karmendriyāṇi (the five working senses) — saṁyamya (restraining) — yaḥ (anyone who) — āste (remains) — manasā (by the mind) — smaran (remembering) — indriya-arthān (sense objects) — vimūḍha-ātmā (foolish soul) — mithyā-ācāraḥ (a pretender) — saḥ (he) — ucyate (is called)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa condemns spiritual hypocrisy. He says that a person who restrains their outward senses (like sitting in a meditation pose) but continues to dwell on sense objects in their mind is a ‘mithyācāraḥ’, or a pretender. They are merely deluding themselves.

It is better to be an honest worker than a dishonest meditator. If your mind is full of desires for sex, money, or fame, putting on the robes of a monk is a form of cheating. This verse is a warning against premature renunciation. One should not try to imitate a sage if they haven’t yet purified their heart.

Real discipline starts with the mind, not just the body. Kṛṣṇa is pushing Arjuna toward an honest appraisal of his own state. He wants Arjuna to see that running away from the battlefield won’t make him a yogī if his mind is still preoccupied with his social standing and family attachments.

sanskrit:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन।
कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते।।
translationEnglish:
On the other hand, if a sincere person tries to control the active senses by the mind
and begins karma-yoga [in Kṛṣṇa consciousness] without attachment, he is far superior.
translationHindi: किन्तु हे अर्जुन! जो पुरुष मन से इन्द्रियों को वश में करके अनासक्त हुआ समस्त इन्द्रियों द्वारा कर्मयोग का आचरण करता है, वही श्रेष्ठ है।
translationGujarati: પરંતુ હે અર્જુન! જે પુરુષ મનથી ઇન્દ્રિયોને વશમાં કરીને અનાસક્ત થઈને તમામ ઇન્દ્રિયો દ્વારા કર્મયોગનું આચરણ કરે છે, તે જ શ્રેષ્ઠ છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa praises the person who sincerely controls the senses by the mind and engages his active senses in karma-yoga without attachment.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण उस व्यक्ति की प्रशंसा करते हैं जो मन से अपनी इंद्रियों को नियंत्रित करता है और बिना आसक्ति के कर्मयोग में लगा रहता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ તે વ્યક્તિની પ્રશંસા કરે છે જે મનથી પોતાની ઇન્દ્રિયોને નિયંત્રિત કરે છે અને આસક્તિ વિના કર્મયોગમાં લાગ્યો રહે છે.
tweetEnglish: But he who controls the senses by the mind and engages in karma-yoga without attachment is superior.
threadsEnglish: But one who controls the senses with the mind and engages them in selfless action, O Arjuna, is far superior.
englishTransliteration:
yas tv indriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate ’rjuna
karmendriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate
englishWBW: yaḥ (whoever) — tu (but) — indriyāṇi (the senses) — manasā (by the mind) — niyamya (regulating) — arabhate (begins) — Arjuna (O Arjuna) — karma-indriyaiḥ (by the active senses) — karma-yogam (devotion) — asaktaḥ (without attachment) — saḥ (he) — viśiṣyate (is far superior)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa defines the superior path. On the other hand, a person who tries to regulate their senses with their mind and engages their active senses in ‘Karma-yoga’ without attachment is far superior. This is the path of the sincere practitioner who stays in the world.

The superior person doesn’t run away from the ‘noise’ of life. Instead, they use their hands, legs, and speech to serve a higher purpose. They work as an offering to the Divine while remaining ‘asaktaḥ’, or unattached to the result. They are like a lotus leaf that lives in the water but stays dry.

This is the path Kṛṣṇa recommends for Arjuna. He wants Arjuna to use his warrior skills to re-establish Dharma, not for personal glory, but as a spiritual sacrifice. This active engagement with detachment is much harder and more glorious than the passive avoidance of the pretender.

sanskrit:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।
शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः।।
translationEnglish:
Perform your prescribed duty, for doing so is better than not working.
One cannot even maintain one’s physical body without work.
translationHindi: तू शास्त्रविहित कर्तव्यकर्म कर; क्योंकि कर्म न करने की अपेक्षा कर्म करना श्रेष्ठ है। तथा कर्म न करने से तेरा शरीर-निर्वाह भी नहीं सिद्ध होगा।
translationGujarati: તું શાસ્ત્રવિહિત કર્તવ્યકર્મ કર; કારણ કે કર્મ ન કરવા કરતા કર્મ કરવું શ્રેષ્ઠ છે. તથા કર્મ ન કરવાથી તારો શરીર-નિર્વાહ પણ સિદ્ધ નહીં થાય.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa advises Arjuna to perform his prescribed duties, as working is better than inaction, and without work, one cannot even maintain one’s physical body.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को अपना नियत कर्तव्य करने की सलाह देते हैं, क्योंकि कर्म न करने से कर्म करना बेहतर है, और कर्म के बिना तो शरीर का निर्वाह भी संभव नहीं है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને પોતાનું નિયત કર્તવ્ય કરવાની સલાહ આપે છે, કારણ કે કર્મ ન કરવા કરતા કર્મ કરવું શ્રેષ્ઠ છે, અને કર્મ વિના તો શરીરનો નિર્વાહ પણ શક્ય નથી.
tweetEnglish: Perform your prescribed duty, for it is better than inaction. Without work, you cannot maintain your body.
threadsEnglish: Perform your prescribed duty, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would be impossible without work.
englishTransliteration:
niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hy akarmaṇaḥ
śarīra-yātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ
englishWBW: niyatam (prescribed) — kuru (do) — karma (duty) — tvam (you) — karma (work) — jyāyaḥ (better) — hi (certainly) — akarmaṇaḥ (than no work) — śarīra (of the body) — yātrā (maintenance) — api (also) — ca (and) — te (your) — na (never) — prasiddhyet (would be achieved) — akarmaṇaḥ (without work)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa gives a direct command: “Perform your prescribed duty.” He explains that action is always better than inaction. Even the basic maintenance of the physical body—getting food, keeping clean, finding shelter—is impossible without some form of work.

If you don’t work, you can’t eat. If you don’t eat, your body dies. Since you cannot even be a healthy human being without work, how can you expect to be a yogī? Spirituality requires a functional body and mind as a base. Therefore, practical duty is not an obstacle to spiritual life; it is the foundation of it.

Arjuna is a prince and a warrior; those are his ‘prescribed’ duties. By fulfilling them, he maintains the social order and his own existence. Kṛṣṇa is telling him that quitting is not an option for anyone who still lives in a physical body. Action is the law of life.

sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर।।
translationEnglish:
Work done as a sacrifice for Viṣṇu has to be performed; otherwise work causes bondage in this material world.
Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform your prescribed duties for His satisfaction,
and in that way you will always remain free from bondage.
translationHindi: यज्ञ के लिए किये जाने वाले कर्मों से अतिरिक्त दूसरे कर्मों में लगा हुआ ही यह मनुष्य समुदाय कर्मों से बँधता है। इसलिए हे अर्जुन! तू आसक्ति से रहित होकर उस यज्ञ के लिए ही कर्तव्यकर्म का भली-भांति आचरण कर।
translationGujarati: યજ્ઞ માટે કરવામાં આવતા કર્મો સિવાયના બીજા કર્મોમાં લાગેલો આ મનુષ્ય સમુદાય કર્મોથી બંધાય છે. તેથી હે અર્જુન! તું આસક્તિ રહિત થઈને તે યજ્ઞ માટે જ કર્તવ્યકર્મનું સારી રીતે આચરણ કર.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa instructs Arjuna to perform work as a sacrifice to God, otherwise work causes bondage; therefore, he should perform his duties for His satisfaction without attachment.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को निर्देश देते हैं कि वे ईश्वर के लिए यज्ञ के रूप में कर्म करें, अन्यथा कर्म बंधन का कारण बनते हैं; इसलिए उन्हें बिना आसक्ति के भगवान की प्रसन्नता के लिए अपना कर्तव्य करना चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને નિર્દેશ આપે છે કે તેઓ ઈશ્વર માટે યજ્ઞના રૂપમાં કર્મ કરે, નહિતર કર્મ બંધનનું કારણ બને છે; તેથી તેમણે આસક્તિ વિના ભગવાનની પ્રસન્નતા માટે પોતાનું કર્તવ્ય કરવું જોઈએ.
tweetEnglish: Work done as a sacrifice to Viṣṇu is free from bondage. Therefore, perform your duties for His satisfaction.
threadsEnglish: Work must be done as a sacrifice to the Divine, otherwise it causes bondage in this material world. Therefore, perform your duties for His sake.
englishTransliteration:
yajñārthāt karmaṇo ’nyatra loko ’yaṁ karma-bandhanaḥ
tad-arthaṁ karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samācara
englishWBW: yajña-arthāt (done only for the sake of sacrifice) — karmaṇaḥ (than work) — anyatra (otherwise) — lokaḥ (world) — ayam (this) — karma-bandhanaḥ (bondage by work) — tat-artham (for that sake) — karma (work) — kaunteya (O son of Kuntī) — mukta-saṅgaḥ (liberated from attachment) — samācara (do perfectly)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa reveals the secret to working without creating karma. He says that work done as a sacrifice, or ‘Yajña’, for the Supreme Lord must be performed; otherwise, work causes bondage in this material world. Every action produces a reaction, unless it is an offering.

If you cook for yourself, you are binding yourself to the results. If you cook for God (and eat the remnants), the act becomes a form of worship and you stay free. Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna to perform his duties for the satisfaction of the Divine. This is the only way to be ‘mukta-saṅgaḥ’, or free from attachment.

This turns the entire world into a temple. The battlefield is not just a place of violence; it is a place of sacrifice if Arjuna fights for the right cause. By dedicating his actions to the Supreme, he escapes the cycle of cause and effect and transforms his work into a tool for liberation.

sanskrit:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः।
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक्।।
translationEnglish:
In the beginning of creation, the Lord of all creatures sent forth generations of men and demigods, along with sacrifices for Viṣṇu, and blessed them by saying,
“Be thou happy by this yajña [sacrifice] because its performance will bestow upon you everything desirable for living happily and achieving liberation.”
translationHindi: प्रजापति ब्रह्मा ने कल्प के आदि में यज्ञसहित प्रजा को रचकर कहा कि तुम लोग इस यज्ञ द्वारा वृद्धि को प्राप्त होओ और यह यज्ञ तुम लोगों को इच्छित भोग प्रदान करने वाला हो।
translationGujarati: પ્રજાપતિ બ્રહ્માએ કલ્પના આરંભમાં યજ્ઞ સહિત પ્રજાને રચીને કહ્યું કે તમે લોકો આ યજ્ઞ દ્વારા વૃદ્ધિ પામો અને આ યજ્ઞ તમને ઇચ્છિત ભોગ પ્રદાન કરનારો થાય.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that at the beginning of creation, the Lord of creatures sent forth generations of men and demigods along with sacrifices, blessing them to prosper through yajña.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि सृष्टि के प्रारंभ में प्रजापति ने यज्ञ के साथ मनुष्यों और देवताओं की रचना की और उन्हें आशीर्वाद दिया कि वे यज्ञ के माध्यम से समृद्ध हों।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે સૃષ્ટિના આરંભમાં પ્રજાપતિએ યજ્ઞની સાથે મનુષ્યો અને દેવતાઓની રચના કરી અને તેમને આશીર્વાદ આપ્યા કે તેઓ યજ્ઞના માધ્યમથી સમૃદ્ધ થાય.
tweetEnglish: In the beginning, the Lord sent forth men and demigods with sacrifices, saying: Be happy by this yajña.
threadsEnglish: In the beginning, the Creator sent forth generations of men and demigods, along with sacrifices, and said: Be prosperous by this sacrifice.
englishTransliteration:
saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ
anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣa vo ’stv iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk
englishWBW: saha (along with) — yajñāḥ (sacrifices) — prajāḥ (generations) — sṛṣṭvā (creating) — purā (anciently) — uvāca (said) — prajā-patiḥ (the Lord of creatures) — anena (by this) — prasaviṣyadhvam (be more and more prosperous) — eṣaḥ (this) — vaḥ (your) — astu (let it be) — iṣṭa (desired) — kāma-dhuk (bestower of all things)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa refers to the dawn of creation. He says that the Lord of all creatures sent forth generations of men along with the system of sacrifice (‘Yajña’). He blessed them, saying that through this sacrifice, they would become prosperous and happy.

The universe is designed as a cooperative system. Sacrifice is the currency of this cooperation. The Creator gave humans the ability to work and offer the results back to the source, and in return, the system would fulfill all their needs. It is like a ‘Circle of Life’ that includes the Divine.

We are not independent exploiters of nature; we are interdependent participants in a cosmic order. Kṛṣṇa is reminding Arjuna that duty and sacrifice are woven into the very fabric of existence. To stop performing one’s role is to go against the design of the universe itself.

sanskrit:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ।।
translationEnglish:
The demigods, being pleased by sacrifices, will also please you,
and thus, by cooperation between men and demigods, prosperity will reign for all.
translationHindi: तुम लोग इस यज्ञ द्वारा देवताओं को उन्नत करो और वे देवता तुम लोगों को उन्नत करें। इस प्रकार नि:स्वार्थ भाव से एक-दूसरे को उन्नत करते हुए तुम लोग परम कल्याण को प्राप्त हो जाओगे।
translationGujarati: તમે લોકો આ યજ્ઞ દ્વારા દેવતાઓને ઉન્નત કરો અને તે દેવતાઓ તમને ઉન્નત કરે. આ રીતે નિઃસ્વાર્થ ભાવે એકબીજાને ઉન્નત કરતા તમે લોકો પરમ કલ્યાણને પામશો.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa says that by pleasing the demigods through sacrifices, the demigods will please humans, and through this mutual cooperation, all will attain prosperity.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि यज्ञों के द्वारा देवताओं को प्रसन्न करने से देवता मनुष्यों को प्रसन्न करेंगे, और इस आपसी सहयोग से सभी परम कल्याण को प्राप्त करेंगे।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે યજ્ઞો દ્વારા દેવતાઓને પ્રસન્ન કરવાથી દેવતાઓ મનુષ્યોને પ્રસન્ન કરશે, અને આ પરસ્પર સહયોગથી બધા પરમ કલ્યાણને પામશે.
tweetEnglish: The demigods, being pleased by sacrifices, will also please you, and by this cooperation, prosperity will reign.
threadsEnglish: By sacrifice, please the demigods, and they will please you. By such mutual cooperation, all shall attain prosperity.
englishTransliteration:
devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ
parasparaṁ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha
englishWBW: devān (demigods) — bhāvayatā (having pleased) — anena (by this sacrifice) — te (those) — devāḥ (demigods) — bhāvayantu (will please) — vaḥ (you) — parasparam (mutually) — bhāvayantaḥ (pleasing one another) — śreyaḥ (all-good) — param (the supreme) — avāpsyatha (you will achieve)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains the symbiosis between humans and the higher powers, or demigods, who administer the natural world. By sacrifice, humans please the gods, and the gods, in turn, provide the rain, light, and resources needed for human life. This is the cosmic ‘Give and Take’.

Through this mutual cooperation (‘parasparaṁ bhāvayantaḥ’), everyone achieves prosperity and the ultimate good. The demigods are like departmental heads of the universe; they provide the supplies, but they expect the citizens to follow the laws of the King (God). Sacrifice is the act of recognizing this connection.

When we live in harmony with these natural and divine laws, society thrives. Kṛṣṇa is showing that Arjuna’s duty is part of this larger maintenance of the world. By refusing to fight, Arjuna is breaking the link of cooperation that keeps the universe stable and prosperous.

sanskrit:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः।।
translationEnglish:
In charge of the various necessities of life, the demigods, being satisfied by the performance of yajña [sacrifice], will supply all necessities to you.
But he who enjoys such gifts without offering them to the demigods in return is certainly a thief.
translationHindi: यज्ञ द्वारा बढ़ाये हुए देवता तुम लोगों को बिना मांगे ही इच्छित भोग निश्चय ही देते रहेंगे। इस प्रकार उन देवताओं द्वारा दिए हुए भोगों को जो पुरुष उनको बिना दिए ही भोगता है, वह चोर ही है।
translationGujarati: યજ્ઞ દ્વારા સંતુષ્ટ થયેલા દેવતાઓ તમને માગ્યા વિના જ ઇચ્છિત ભોગો નિશ્ચય આપતા રહેશે. આ રીતે તે દેવતાઓ દ્વારા અપાયેલા ભોગોને જે પુરુષ તેમને આપ્યા વિના જ ભોગવે છે, તે ચોર જ છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa warns that the demigods supply life’s necessities when satisfied by sacrifice, but he who enjoys these gifts without offering them in return is certainly a thief.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण चेतावनी देते हैं कि देवता यज्ञ से प्रसन्न होकर जीवन की आवश्यकताएं प्रदान करते हैं, लेकिन जो व्यक्ति इन उपहारों को उन्हें अर्पित किए बिना भोगता है, वह निश्चित रूप से चोर है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ચેતવણી આપે છે કે દેવતાઓ યજ્ઞથી પ્રસન્ન થઈને જીવનની જરૂરિયાતો પૂરી પાડે છે, પરંતુ જે વ્યક્તિ આ ભેટોને તેમને અર્પણ કર્યા વિના ભોગવે છે, તે નિશ્ચિતપણે ચોર છે.
tweetEnglish: He who enjoys gifts from the demigods without offering them in return is certainly a thief.
threadsEnglish: The demigods, pleased by sacrifice, will grant you the necessities of life. But he who enjoys these gifts without offering them in return is a thief.
englishTransliteration:
iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ
tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
englishWBW: iṣṭān (desired) — bhogān (necessities of life) — hi (certainly) — vaḥ (unto you) — devāḥ (the demigods) — dāsyante (will award) — yajña-bhāvitāḥ (being satisfied by sacrifice) — taiḥ (by them) — dattān (things given) — apradāya (without offering) — ebhyaḥ (to them) — yaḥ (he who) — bhuṅkte (enjoys) — stenaḥ (thief) — eva (certainly) — saḥ (he)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa warns against the mentality of a parasite. He says that the higher powers supply all the necessities of life when they are satisfied by our work and sacrifice. But anyone who enjoys these gifts without offering them back in return is certainly a thief.

We take air, water, and food from nature every day. If we never say ‘Thank You’ and never perform our prescribed duties toward the whole, we are stealing from the system. A thief may enjoy for a short while, but he is always under the shadow of punishment and guilt.

Modern society is largely a civilization of takers, which is why there is so much anxiety and ecological crisis. Kṛṣṇa is teaching Arjuna that the act of work must be an act of gratitude. Fighting for Dharma is Arjuna’s way of ‘paying back’ his debt to the universe and the Lord who maintains it.

sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्।।
translationEnglish:
The devotees of the Lord are released from all kinds of sins because they eat food which is offered first for sacrifice.
Others, who prepare food for personal sense enjoyment, verily eat only sin.
translationHindi: यज्ञ से बचे हुए अन्न को खाने वाले श्रेष्ठ पुरुष सब पापों से छूट जाते हैं; और जो पापी लोग अपने शरीर-पोषण के लिए ही अन्न पकाते हैं, वे तो पाप को ही खाते हैं।
translationGujarati: યજ્ઞમાંથી બચેલું અન્ન ખાનારા શ્રેષ્ઠ પુરુષો બધા પાપોમાંથી મુક્ત થઈ જાય છે; અને જે પાપી લોકો પોતાના શરીરના પોષણ માટે જ અન્ન રાંધે છે, તેઓ તો પાપ જ ખાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa states that devotees are freed from all sins by eating food offered in sacrifice, while those who cook only for their own sense enjoyment verily eat sin.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि यज्ञ में अर्पित भोजन (प्रसाद) खाने से भक्त सभी पापों से मुक्त हो जाते हैं, जबकि जो लोग केवल अपने इंद्रिय सुख के लिए भोजन पकाते हैं, वे पाप ही खाते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે યજ્ઞમાં અર્પણ કરેલું ભોજન (પ્રસાદ) ખાવાથી ભક્તો બધા પાપોમાંથી મુક્ત થઈ જાય છે, જ્યારે જે લોકો માત્ર પોતાના ઇન્દ્રિય સુખ માટે ભોજન રાંધે છે, તેઓ પાપ જ ખાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Devotees are released from sin by eating offered food. Others, who cook for themselves, eat only sin.
threadsEnglish: The devotees of the Lord are released from all sins because they eat food offered first in sacrifice. Others, who cook for themselves, eat only sin.
englishTransliteration:
yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ
bhuñjate te tv aghaṁ pāpā ye pacanty ātma-kāraṇāt
englishWBW: yajña-śiṣṭa-āśinaḥ (those who eat the remnants of sacrifice) — santaḥ (the devotees) — mucyante (are released) — sarva (all kinds of) — kilbiṣaiḥ (from sins) — bhuñjate (enjoy) — te (they) — tu (but) — agham (sin) — pāpāḥ (sinners) — ye (who) — pacanti (cook) — ātma-kāraṇāt (for their own sake)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains the spiritual ethics of eating. He says that those who eat food that has first been offered in sacrifice are released from all kinds of sins. But those who cook only for their own pleasure are effectively eating sin.

Every act of survival involves some level of violence—even plants are living beings. If we take from life solely for our own ego, we incur the karma of that taking. But if we offer the results of our labor back to the Divine, the act is sanctified and becomes ‘Prasādam’, or mercy.

This principle applies to all areas of life, not just food. If Arjuna fights for his own kingdom, he is a sinner. If he fights for Kṛṣṇa’s purpose, he is a saint. The difference lies in the destination of the results. Offering the fruit of one’s work is the ultimate cleanser of the heart.

sanskrit:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः।।
translationEnglish:
All living bodies subsist on food grains, which are produced from rains.
Rains are produced by performance of yajña [sacrifice], and yajña is born of prescribed duties.
translationHindi: सम्पूर्ण प्राणी अन्न से उत्पन्न होते हैं, अन्न की उत्पत्ति वृष्टि से होती है, वृष्टि यज्ञ से होती है और यज्ञ विहित कर्मों से उत्पन्न होता है।
translationGujarati: તમામ પ્રાણીઓ અન્નથી ઉત્પન્ન થાય છે, અન્નની ઉત્પત્તિ વરસાદથી થાય છે, વરસાદ યજ્ઞથી થાય છે અને યજ્ઞ વિહિત કર્મોથી ઉત્પન્ન થાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains the cycle of life: living beings subsist on food, food comes from rains, rains are produced by yajña (sacrifice), and yajña is born of prescribed duties.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण जीवन चक्र समझाते हैं: प्राणी अन्न पर निर्भर हैं, अन्न वर्षा से होता है, वर्षा यज्ञ से होती है, और यज्ञ निर्धारित कर्मों से उत्पन्न होता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ જીવન ચક્ર સમજાવે છે: પ્રાણીઓ અન્ન પર નિર્ભર છે, અન્ન વરસાદથી થાય છે, વરસાદ યજ્ઞથી થાય છે, અને યજ્ઞ નિર્ધારિત કર્મોથી ઉત્પન્ન થાય છે.
tweetEnglish: All living bodies subsist on food grains, which are produced from rains. Rains are produced by yajña.
threadsEnglish: All living bodies subsist on food grains, which are produced from rains. Rains are produced by performance of sacrifice, and sacrifice is born of duty.
englishTransliteration:
annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād anna-sambhavaḥ
yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ
englishWBW: annāt (from food grains) — bhavanti (grow) — bhūtāni (living entities) — parjanyāt (from rains) — anna (food grains) — sambhavaḥ (production) — yajñāt (from sacrifice) — bhavati (becomes possible) — parjanyaḥ (rain) — yajñaḥ (sacrifice) — karma (prescribed duties) — samudbhavaḥ (born of)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the ecological and spiritual cycle that sustains life. Living beings depend on food, food depends on rain, rain depends on sacrifice, and sacrifice depends on the performance of prescribed duties. This is the cosmic chain of command.

This verse links the economy (food) to ecology (rain) to spirituality (sacrifice) and sociology (duty). If any one link in this chain is broken, the entire system collapses. If people stop doing their honest work, the ‘Yajña’ stops. When sacrifice stops, the natural order is disturbed, and life suffers.

Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that his individual work is essential for the harmony of the whole universe. He cannot view his decision to fight as a private matter. He is a key link in the chain that keeps the world running. To quit is to sabotaging the very life-support system of the planet.

sanskrit:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्।।
translationEnglish:
Regulated activities are prescribed in the Vedas, and the Vedas are directly manifested from the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
Consequently the all-pervading Transcendence is eternally situated in acts of sacrifice.
translationHindi: कर्म समुदाय को वेद से उत्पन्न और वेद को अविनाशी परमात्मा से उत्पन्न हुआ जान। इससे सिद्ध होता है कि सर्वव्यापी परम अक्षर परमात्मा सदा ही यज्ञ में प्रतिष्ठित है।
translationGujarati: કર્મ સમુદાયને વેદથી ઉત્પન્ન થયેલો અને વેદને અવિનાશી પરમાત્માથી ઉત્પન્ન થયેલો જાણ. તેથી સિદ્ધ થાય છે કે સર્વવ્યાપી પરમ અક્ષર પરમાત્મા સદાય યજ્ઞમાં પ્રતિષ્ઠિત છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa reveals that regulated activities are prescribed in the Vedas, which come from the Supreme, and thus the all-pervading Transcendence is eternally situated in acts of sacrifice.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि नियत कर्म वेदों से उत्पन्न होते हैं और वेद परमात्मा से प्रकट हुए हैं, इसलिए सर्वव्यापी परमात्मा सदैव यज्ञ में प्रतिष्ठित रहते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ જણાવે છે કે નિયત કર્મો વેદોમાંથી ઉત્પન્ન થાય છે અને વેદ પરમાત્માથી પ્રગટ થયા છે, તેથી સર્વવ્યાપી પરમાત્મા સદાય યજ્ઞમાં પ્રતિષ્ઠિત રહે છે.
tweetEnglish: Regulated activities are prescribed in the Vedas, and the Vedas are manifested from the Supreme.
threadsEnglish: Prescribed duties are given in the Vedas, and the Vedas are directly manifested from the Imperishable. Therefore the all-pervading Divine is ever present in sacrifice.
englishTransliteration:
karma brahmodbhavaṁ viddhi brahmākṣara-samudbhavam
tasmāt sarva-gataṁ brahma nityaṁ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
englishWBW: karma (duty) — brahma (the Vedas) — udbhavam (produced from) — viddhi (know) — brahma (the Vedas) — akṣara (the Supreme/Imperishable) — samudbhavam (produced from) — tasmāt (therefore) — sarva-gatam (all-pervading) — brahma (transcendence) — nityam (eternally) — yajñe (in sacrifice) — pratiṣṭhitam (situated)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa traces the origin of duty. Prescribed activities are given in the Vedas, and the Vedas are directly manifested from the Supreme Lord. Therefore, the all-pervading Divine is eternally present in every act of sacrifice.

This means that your work is not mundane; it is a direct connection to God if done correctly. When you do your duty as an offering, you are tapping into the primary energy of the universe. The workplace is as holy as the temple when the consciousness is one of sacrifice.

Arjuna’s role as a warrior is not a secular job; it is a Vedic injunction. By performing it, he is participating in the divine energy. Kṛṣṇa is showing him that God is not found by avoiding work, but by performing work with the realization that the activity itself is a manifestation of the Divine.

sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति।।
translationEnglish:
My dear Arjuna, one who does not follow in human life the cycle of sacrifice thus established by the Vedas certainly leads a life full of sin.
Living only for the satisfaction of the senses, such a person lives in vain.
translationHindi: हे पार्थ! जो पुरुष इस लोक में इस प्रकार परम्परा से प्रचलित सृष्टिचक्र के अनुकूल नहीं चलता (अर्थात अपने कर्तव्य का पालन नहीं करता), वह इन्द्रियों द्वारा भोगों में रमने वाला पापायु पुरुष व्यर्थ ही जीता है।
translationGujarati: હે પાર્થ! જે પુરુષ આ લોકમાં આ રીતે પરંપરાથી ચાલતા સૃષ્ટિચક્રને અનુકૂળ નથી ચાલતો (અર્થાત પોતાના કર્તવ્યનું પાલન નથી કરતો), તે ઇન્દ્રિયો દ્વારા ભોગોમાં રમમાણ રહેનારો પાપાયુ પુરુષ વ્યર્થ જ જીવે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa condemns one who does not follow this cycle of sacrifice established by the Vedas, saying that such a sinful person living only for the senses lives in vain.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जो व्यक्ति वेदों द्वारा स्थापित इस यज्ञ-चक्र का पालन नहीं करता, वह इंद्रियों के सुख में जीने वाला पापी व्यर्थ ही जीवन जीता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે જે વ્યક્તિ વેદો દ્વારા સ્થાપિત આ યજ્ઞ-ચક્રનું પાલન નથી કરતો, તે ઇન્દ્રિયોના સુખમાં જીવનારો પાપી વ્યર્થ જ જીવન જીવે છે.
tweetEnglish: One who does not follow the cycle of sacrifice leads a sinful life, living only for the senses.
threadsEnglish: My dear Arjuna, one who does not follow this cycle of sacrifice leads a sinful life. Living only for the senses, such a person lives in vain.
englishTransliteration:
evaṁ pravartitaṁ cakraṁ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ
aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati
englishWBW: evam (thus) — pravartitam (established) — cakram (cycle) — na (not) — anuvartayati (follows) — iha (in this life) — yaḥ (who) — agha-āyuḥ (whose life is full of sin) — indriya-ārāmaḥ (satisfied in the senses) — mogham (uselessly) — pārtha (O Arjuna) — saḥ (he) — jīvati (lives)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa warns about the danger of being a parasite in the universe. He describes the ‘cakraṁ’, or the wheel of sacrifice, which He just outlined. Anyone who does not follow this cycle of duty and offering in their life is living in a state of sin.

Such a person is described as ‘indriya-ārāmaḥ’, meaning they find satisfaction only in their own senses. They take the resources of the world (food, water, light) but give nothing back to the Source. Kṛṣṇa says that such a person lives in vain; their life is ‘mogham’, or useless.

Arjuna is being warned that his desire to retire to a life of quiet contemplation might actually be a form of selfishness. If he doesn’t fulfill his role in the cosmic wheel, he is just an enjoyer taking from a system he refuses to support. Real life requires participation in the sacrifice that sustains all beings.

sanskrit:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते।।
translationEnglish:
But for one who takes pleasure in the self, whose human life is one of self-realization,
and who is satisfied in the self only, fully satiated—for him there is no duty.
translationHindi: परन्तु जो मनुष्य आत्मा में ही रमने वाला है और आत्मा में ही तृप्त तथा आत्मा में ही सन्तुष्ट हो, उसके लिए कोई कर्तव्य नहीं है।
translationGujarati: પરંતુ જે મનુષ્ય આત્મામાં જ રમમાણ રહેનારો છે અને આત્મામાં જ તૃપ્ત તથા આત્મામાં જ સંતુષ્ટ છે, તેના માટે કોઈ કર્તવ્ય નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa clarifies that for a person who takes pleasure in the self, is satisfied in the self, and is fully satiated, there is no prescribed duty.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण स्पष्ट करते हैं कि जो व्यक्ति अपनी आत्मा में ही आनंद लेता है और आत्मा में ही पूर्ण रूप से संतुष्ट रहता है, उसके लिए कोई कर्तव्य शेष नहीं रहता।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સ્પષ્ટ કરે છે કે જે વ્યક્તિ પોતાના આત્મામાં જ આનંદ લે છે અને આત્મામાં જ પૂર્ણ રીતે સંતુષ્ટ રહે છે, તેના માટે કોઈ કર્તવ્ય બાકી રહેતું નથી.
tweetEnglish: But for one who takes pleasure in the self and is satisfied in the self alone, there is no duty.
threadsEnglish: But for one who takes pleasure in the Self, whose life is enlightened in the Self, and who is satisfied in the Self only, there is no duty to perform.
englishTransliteration:
yas tv ātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛptaś ca mānavaḥ
ātmany eva ca santuṣṭas tasya kāryaṁ na vidyate
englishWBW: yaḥ (whoever) — tu (but) — ātma-ratiḥ (taking pleasure in the self) — eva (certainly) — syāt (is) — ātma-tṛptaḥ (self-illuminated) — ca (and) — mānavaḥ (a man) — ātmani (in himself) — eva (only) — ca (and) — santuṣṭaḥ (satisfied) — tasya (his) — kāryam (duty) — na (not) — vidyate (exists)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa gives an exception to the rule of work. He says that for a person who finds all their pleasure and satisfaction within their own soul, and who is fully self-realized, there is no prescribed duty left to perform. They have reached the goal.

The purpose of work and social duty is to purify the mind and detach it from matter. Once a person is ‘ātmany eva ca santuṣṭas’, or fully satisfied in the self, the ‘medicine’ of prescribed duty is no longer needed because the ‘disease’ of material desire is cured.

However, this is a very high stage of perfection. Until one is completely free from even the slightest material desire, they must continue to work. Kṛṣṇa is defining the finish line, but He is also subtly reminding Arjuna that he hasn’t crossed it yet. As long as Arjuna is feeling grief and attachment, he still needs the path of work for his purification.

sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः।।
translationEnglish:
A self-realized man has no purpose to fulfill in the discharge of his prescribed duties,
nor has he any reason not to perform such work.
Nor has he any need to depend on any other living being.
translationHindi: उस महापुरुष का इस विश्व में न तो कर्म करने से कोई प्रयोजन रहता है और न कर्मों के न करने से ही कोई प्रयोजन रहता है। तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियों में भी इसका किंचित्मात्र भी स्वार्थ का सम्बन्ध नहीं रहता।
translationGujarati: તે મહાપુરુષનું આ વિશ્વમાં ન તો કર્મ કરવાથી કોઈ પ્રયોજન રહે છે અને ન તો કર્મ ન કરવાથી જ કોઈ પ્રયોજન રહે છે. તથા તમામ પ્રાણીઓમાં પણ તેમનો કિંચિત્માત્ર પણ સ્વાર્થનો સંબંધ નથી રહેતો.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa says that a self-realized person has no purpose to gain by discharging duties nor any reason to cease work, and does not depend on any other being.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि एक आत्म-ज्ञानी पुरुष का न तो कर्म करने में कोई स्वार्थ होता है और न ही कर्म छोड़ने में, और वह किसी अन्य प्राणी पर निर्भर नहीं रहता।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે એક આત્મ-જ્ઞાની પુરુષનો ન તો કર્મ કરવામાં કોઈ સ્વાર્થ હોય છે અને ન તો કર્મ છોડવામાં, અને તે કોઈ અન્ય પ્રાણી પર નિર્ભર રહેતો નથી.
tweetEnglish: A self-realized man has no purpose to gain by discharging duties, nor any reason to cease work.
threadsEnglish: A self-realized person has no purpose to fulfill in the discharge of his duties, nor has he any reason not to perform them.
englishTransliteration:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana
na cāsya sarva-bhūteṣu kaścid artha-vyapāśrayaḥ
englishWBW: na (never) — eva (certainly) — tasya (his) — kṛtena (by discharge of duty) — arthaḥ (purpose) — na (not) — akṛtena (by not performing duty) — iha (in this world) — kaścana (whatever) — na (never) — ca (and) — asya (his) — sarva-bhūteṣu (among all beings) — kaścit (any) — artha (purpose) — vyapāśrayaḥ (taking shelter of)
englishExplain:
Elaborating on the self-realized soul, Kṛṣṇa says that such a person has nothing to gain by performing their duty and nothing to lose by skipping it. They are completely independent of all other living beings for their happiness or survival.

A liberated soul is like a person who has already arrived at their destination; they don’t need the map or the vehicle anymore. They don’t follow rules out of fear of punishment or hope for reward. They are truly free. They don’t rely on anyone else for their internal sense of peace.

Kṛṣṇa mentions this state to show Arjuna the ultimate result of Yoga. But the implication remains that Arjuna is currently dependent on his relatives and his status for his happiness. Since he is not yet at this stage of total independence, he must stay on the path of regulated duty to reach it. True freedom is earned through disciplined action.

sanskrit:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः।।
translationEnglish:
Therefore, without being attached to the fruits of activities, one should act as a matter of duty,
for by working without attachment one attains the Supreme.
translationHindi: इसलिए तू निरन्तर आसक्ति से रहित होकर कर्तव्यकर्म का भली-भांति आचरण कर; क्योंकि आसक्ति से रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परमात्मा को प्राप्त हो जाता है।
translationGujarati: તેથી તું નિરંતર આસક્તિ રહિત થઈને કર્તવ્યકર્મનું સારી રીતે આચરણ કર; કારણ કે આસક્તિ રહિત થઈને કર્મ કરતો મનુષ્ય પરમાત્માને પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa advises Arjuna to constantly perform his duty without attachment, for by working without attachment one attains the Supreme.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को सलाह देते हैं कि वे आसक्ति के बिना अपना कर्तव्य करते रहें, क्योंकि अनासक्त भाव से कर्म करने से मनुष्य परमात्मा को प्राप्त होता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને સલાહ આપે છે કે તેઓ આસક્તિ વિના પોતાનું કર્તવ્ય કરતા રહે, કારણ કે અનાસક્ત ભાવે કર્મ કરવાથી મનુષ્ય પરમાત્માને પામે છે.
tweetEnglish: Therefore, without being attached to the fruits of activities, one should act as a matter of duty.
threadsEnglish: Therefore, without being attached to the fruits of activities, one should act as a matter of duty, for by working without attachment one attains the Supreme.
englishTransliteration:
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samācara
asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ
englishWBW: tasmāt (therefore) — asaktaḥ (without attachment) — satatam (always) — kāryam (obligatory) — karma (work) — samācara (perform) — asaktaḥ (unattached) — hi (certainly) — ācaran (performing) — karma (work) — param (the Supreme) — āpnoti (achieves) — pūruṣaḥ (a man)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa applies the logic to Arjuna’s current situation: “Therefore, without attachment, always perform the work that is your duty.” Since Arjuna is still in the stage where he needs purification, he must work. The secret is to do it ‘asaktaḥ’, or without any personal stake in the result.

By working without attachment, a person gradually attains the Supreme. This answers Arjuna’s doubt about whether work binds the soul to the material world. It is not the work that binds, but the greed and ego we bring to the work. If you work for the Divine, the work itself becomes a form of meditation.

Kṛṣṇa is teaching the art of being a ‘Spiritual Warrior’. Arjuna must fight the war with total intensity, but with zero selfish interest. This balance of external action and internal detachment is the essence of Karma-yoga and the fastest path to the highest perfection.

sanskrit:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि।।
translationEnglish:
Kings such as Janak attained perfection solely by performance of prescribed duties.
Therefore, just for the sake of educating the people in general, you should perform your work.
translationHindi: जनकादि ज्ञानीजन भी आसक्तिरहित कर्म द्वारा ही परम सिद्धि को प्राप्त हुए थे। इसलिए तथा लोकसंग्रह को देखते हुए भी तू कर्म करने के ही योग्य है।
translationGujarati: જનક વગેરે જ્ઞાનીજનો પણ આસક્તિરહિત કર્મ દ્વારા જ પરમ સિદ્ધિને પામ્યા હતા. તેથી તથા લોકસંગ્રહને જોતા પણ તું કર્મ કરવાને જ યોગ્ય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa cites King Janak as an example of attaining perfection by performing duties, and urges Arjuna to perform his work to set an example for the people.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण राजा जनक का उदाहरण देते हैं जिन्होंने कर्म करते हुए ही सिद्धि प्राप्त की, और अर्जुन को लोक-संग्रह (लोगों को सही मार्ग दिखाने) के लिए अपना कर्म करने को कहते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ રાજા જનકનું ઉદાહરણ આપે છે જેમણે કર્મ કરતા કરતા જ સિદ્ધિ પ્રાપ્ત કરી, અને અર્જુનને લોક-સંગ્રહ (લોકોને સાચો માર્ગ બતાવવા) માટે પોતાનું કર્મ કરવા કહે છે.
tweetEnglish: Kings like Janak attained perfection solely by performance of prescribed duties. Set an example for the people.
threadsEnglish: Even kings like Janaka attained perfection by performing their prescribed duties. Therefore, you should also perform your work for the sake of educating the people.
englishTransliteration:
karmaṇaiva hi saṁsiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ
loka-saṅgraham evāpi sampaśyan kartum arhasi
englishWBW: karmaṇā (by work) — eva (even) — hi (certainly) — saṁsiddhim (perfection) — āsthitāḥ (attained) — janaka-ādayaḥ (Janaka and other kings) — loka-saṅgraham (education of the people) — eva api (only) — sampaśyan (considering) — kartum (to do) — arhasi (you deserve)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa uses historical examples to prove His point. He mentions King Janaka, who reached the highest stage of perfection solely by performing his prescribed duties as a ruler. Janaka didn’t need to leave his palace to find God; he found God through his work.

Even if Arjuna feels he is already wise and doesn’t need work for his own purification, Kṛṣṇa argues that he should still act for the sake of ‘loka-saṅgraham’—setting an example for the general public. Leaders have a responsibility to show others the right way to live.

If the righteous and wise people withdraw from society, the world will be led by the ignorant and the greedy. A great soul stays in the world to maintain social order and to teach others through their actions. Arjuna must fight not just for his own soul, but for the moral health of the entire nation.

sanskrit:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते।।
translationEnglish:
Whatever action a great man performs, common men follow.
And whatever standards he sets by exemplary acts, all the world pursues.
translationHindi: श्रेष्ठ पुरुष जो-जो आचरण करता है, अन्य पुरुष भी वैसा-वैसा ही आचरण करते हैं। वह जो कुछ प्रमाण कर देता है, समस्त मनुष्य-समुदाय उसी के अनुसार बरतने लग जाता है।
translationGujarati: શ્રેષ્ઠ પુરુષ જે જે આચરણ કરે છે, અન્ય પુરુષો પણ તેવું જ આચરણ કરે છે. તે જે કઈ પ્રમાણ કરી આપે છે, સમસ્ત મનુષ્ય સમુદાય તે અનુસાર વર્તવા લાગે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that whatever action a great man performs, common people follow, and whatever standard he sets, the whole world pursues.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि श्रेष्ठ पुरुष जैसा आचरण करते हैं, सामान्य लोग भी वैसा ही करते हैं, और वे जो प्रमाण स्थापित करते हैं, सारी दुनिया उसका अनुसरण करती है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે શ્રેષ્ઠ પુરુષ જેવું આચરણ કરે છે, સામાન્ય લોકો પણ તેવું જ કરે છે, અને તેઓ જે પ્રમાણ સ્થાપિત કરે છે, આખી દુનિયા તેનું અનુસરણ કરે છે.
tweetEnglish: Whatever action a great man performs, common men follow. Whatever standard he sets, the world pursues.
threadsEnglish: Whatever action a great man performs, common men follow. And whatever standards he sets by exemplary acts, all the world pursues.
englishTransliteration:
yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate
englishWBW: yat yat (whatever) — ācarati (does) — śreṣṭhaḥ (a respected leader) — tat tat (that and that only) — eva (certainly) — itaraḥ (common) — janaḥ (people) — saḥ (he) — yat (whatever) — pramāṇam (standard) — kurute (does) — lokaḥ (the world) — tat (that) — anuvartate (follows in the footsteps).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains the heavy responsibility of leadership. He states that whatever a great person (‘śreṣṭhaḥ’) does, the common people will naturally follow. Leaders set the standards for society not through their speeches, but through their ‘ācāra’, or behavior. If a leader is ethical, the public leans toward ethics; if a leader is corrupt, the culture degrades.

This is a call for Arjuna to consider his social impact. As a prince and a hero, his actions carry immense weight. If he abandons the battlefield out of personal sentiment, he will set a precedent of cowardice and irresponsibility for generations to come. He must fight not just for the kingdom, but to uphold the standard of duty for all of humanity.

This principle applies to everyone in a position of influence—parents, teachers, and executives. Our lives are being watched and mirrored by those who look up to us. To create a better world, we must first become the ‘pramāṇam’ or the living standard of the values we wish to see in others.

sanskrit:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन।
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि।।
translationEnglish:
O son of Prith, there is no work prescribed for Me within all the three planetary systems.
Nor am I in want of anything, nor have I a need to obtain anything—and yet I am engaged in prescribed duties.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! मुझे इन तीनों लोकों में न तो कुछ कर्तव्य है और न कोई भी प्राप्त करने योग्य वस्तु अप्राप्त है, तो भी मैं कर्म में ही बरतता हूँ।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! મારે આ ત્રણેય લોકમાં ન તો કંઈ કર્તવ્ય છે અને ન તો કંઈ પણ પ્રાપ્ત કરવા યોગ્ય વસ્તુ અપ્રાપ્ત છે, તો પણ હું કર્મમાં જ વર્તું છું.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa states that although He has no need for anything in the three worlds and no duty to perform, He still engages in prescribed duties.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि यद्यपि तीनों लोकों में उनके लिए कोई कर्तव्य नहीं है और उन्हें किसी चीज की आवश्यकता नहीं है, फिर भी वे कर्मों में लगे रहते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે જોકે ત્રણેય લોકમાં તેમના માટે કોઈ કર્તવ્ય નથી અને તેમને કોઈ વસ્તુની જરૂર નથી, તો પણ તેઓ કર્મોમાં લાગેલા રહે છે.
tweetEnglish: O Pritha, there is no work prescribed for Me within the three worlds, yet I am engaged in prescribed duties.
threadsEnglish: O son of Pritha, there is no work prescribed for Me within all the three worlds. Nor am I in want of anything, yet I am engaged in duty.
englishTransliteration:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṁ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana
nānavāptam avāptavyaṁ varta eva ca karmaṇi
englishWBW: na (not) — me (My) — pārtha (O Arjuna) — asti (there is) — kartavyam (prescribed duty) — triṣu (in the three) — lokeṣu (planetary systems) — kiñcana (any) — na (not) — anavāptam (wanted) — avāptavyam (to be gained) — varte (I am engaged) — eva (certainly) — ca (also) — karmaṇi (in prescribed duty)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa cites His own life as an example. He says that in all the three worlds, there is nothing He is required to do. As the Supreme Lord, He has no unfulfilled desires and nothing to gain from any activity. He is completely full and satisfied in Himself.

Yet, He is constantly engaged in work. During His appearance on earth, Kṛṣṇa acted as a prince, a student, a diplomat, and now a charioteer. He followed the rules of society and the duties of His position with total care. He worked even though He didn’t have to.

This reveals the altruistic nature of the Divine. Kṛṣṇa works not for Himself, but for the benefit of all living beings. He is showing Arjuna that if God Himself takes the trouble to perform duties for the sake of the world, then a human being should certainly do the same. Service is the highest expression of life, even at the highest level.

sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।
translationEnglish:
For if I ever failed to engage in carefully performing prescribed duties, O Pārtha,
certainly all men would follow My path.
translationHindi: क्योंकि हे पार्थ! यदि मैं सावधान होकर कर्तव्यकर्मों में न बरतूँ, तो बड़ी हानि हो जाए; क्योंकि मनुष्य सब प्रकार से मेरे ही मार्ग का अनुसरण करते हैं।
translationGujarati: કારણ કે હે પાર્થ! જો હું સાવધાન થઈને કર્તવ્યકર્મોમાં ન વર્તું, તો મોટું નુકસાન થાય; કારણ કે મનુષ્યો સર્વ પ્રકારે મારા જ માર્ગનું અનુસરણ કરે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that if He failed to perform duties carefully, all men would follow His path, leading to chaos.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि यदि वे सावधानीपूर्वक कर्तव्य नहीं करेंगे, तो सभी मनुष्य उनके मार्ग का अनुसरण करेंगे, जिससे अव्यवस्था फैल जाएगी।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ જણાવે છે કે જો તેઓ સાવધાનીપૂર્વક કર્તવ્ય નહીં કરે, તો બધા મનુષ્યો તેમના માર્ગનું અનુસરણ કરશે, જેનાથી અવ્યવસ્થા ફેલાઈ જશે.
tweetEnglish: For if I failed to perform duties, certainly all men would follow My path and be ruined.
threadsEnglish: For if I ever failed to engage in carefully performing duties, O Pārtha, certainly all men would follow My path.
englishTransliteration:
yadi hy ahaṁ na varteyaṁ jātu karmaṇy atandritaḥ
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
englishWBW: yadi (if) — hi (certainly) — aham (I) — na (not) — varteyam (thus engage) — jātu (ever) — karmaṇi (in performance of duty) — atandritaḥ (with great care) — mama (My) — vartma (path) — anuvartante (would follow) — manuṣyāḥ (all men) — pārtha (O Arjuna) — sarvaśaḥ (in all respects)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains the dangerous consequences of His own potential inaction. If He ever failed to perform His duties with great care, all people would follow His path. Being the ultimate role model, His behavior would become the global standard.

If God appeared to be lazy or irresponsible, people would use His example to justify their own neglect of duty. They would say, “Even Kṛṣṇa didn’t work, so why should I?” They would imitate His external freedom without having His internal divinity. This would lead to a complete breakdown of human civilization.

To prevent this ‘cheap imitation’ and the chaos it would bring, Kṛṣṇa acts with extreme precision and adherence to social laws. He is teaching Arjuna that the higher one’s position, the more careful one must be with their actions. Leadership is a sacrifice of personal whim for the sake of the collective good.

sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्।
सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः।।
translationEnglish:
If I did not perform prescribed duties, all these worlds would be put to ruination.
I would be the cause of creating unwanted population, and I would thereby destroy the peace of all living beings.
translationHindi: यदि मैं कर्म न करूँ तो ये सब लोक भ्रष्ट हो जाएं और मैं वर्णशंकर का करने वाला होऊँ तथा इस सारी प्रजा को नष्ट करने वाला बनूँ।
translationGujarati: જો હું કર્મ ન કરું તો આ બધા લોક ભ્રષ્ટ થઈ જાય અને હું વર્ણસંકરનો કરનારો થાઉં તથા આ બધી પ્રજાનો નાશ કરનારો બનું.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa warns that if He did not perform duties, all these worlds would be ruined, and He would be the cause of unwanted population and destruction of peace.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण चेतावनी देते हैं कि यदि वे कर्म नहीं करेंगे, तो ये सारे लोक नष्ट हो जाएंगे, और वे वर्णसंकर और शांति के विनाश का कारण बनेंगे।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ચેતવણી આપે છે કે જો તેઓ કર્મ નહીં કરે, તો આ બધા લોક નાશ પામશે, અને તેઓ વર્ણસંકર અને શાંતિના વિનાશનું કારણ બનશે.
tweetEnglish: If I did not perform duties, these worlds would be ruined. I would be the cause of unwanted population.
threadsEnglish: If I did not perform prescribed duties, all these worlds would be put to ruin. I would be the cause of creating unwanted population and would destroy the peace.
englishTransliteration:
utsīdeyu r ime lokā na kuryāṁ karma ced aham
saṅkarasya ca kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ
englishWBW: utsīdeyuḥ (would be put to ruin) — ime (all these) — lokāḥ (worlds) — na (not) — kuryām (I perform) — karma (work) — cet (if) — aham (I) — saṅkarasya (of unwanted population) — ca (and) — kartā (creator) — syām (would be) — upahanyām (would destroy) — imāḥ (all these) — prajāḥ (living entities)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the literal collapse of the world if He were to stop working. He says all these worlds would fall into ruin. Furthermore, He would be the cause of creating ‘saṅkara’, or a chaotic and unwanted population, and He would be the destroyer of all living beings.

If the Supreme Controller stopped maintaining the laws of nature—gravity, the movement of the sun, the growth of food—the physical universe would dissolve. Similarly, if He stopped maintaining the moral laws by setting a bad example, the social universe would dissolve into anarchy and irreligion.

Arjuna must see that his decision to quit is not just a personal choice; it is a vote for chaos. By neglecting his duty as a leader, he is contributing to the ruin of the very people he claims to care about. Kṛṣṇa fights to maintain the structure of reality, and He expects Arjuna to do the same in his own sphere.

sanskrit:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत।
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्िचकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम्।।
translationEnglish:
As the ignorant perform their duties with attachment to results, the learned may similarly act,
but without attachment, for the sake of leading people on the right path.
translationHindi: हे भारत! कर्म में आसक्त हुए अज्ञानीजन जिस प्रकार कर्म करते हैं, आसक्तिरहित विद्वान भी लोकसंग्रह करना चाहता हुआ उसी प्रकार कर्म करे।
translationGujarati: હે ભારત! કર્મમાં આસક્ત થયેલા અજ્ઞાનીજનો જેમ કર્મ કરે છે, આસક્તિરહિત વિદ્વાન પણ લોકસંગ્રહ કરવા ઈચ્છતો હોય તેમ જ કર્મ કરે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa advises that just as the ignorant perform duties with attachment, the wise should perform their duties without attachment to lead people on the right path.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण सलाह देते हैं कि जैसे अज्ञानी लोग आसक्ति के साथ कर्म करते हैं, वैसे ही विद्वानों को लोक-संग्रह के लिए अनासक्त होकर कर्म करना चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સલાહ આપે છે કે જેમ અજ્ઞાની લોકો આસક્તિ સાથે કર્મ કરે છે, તેમ જ વિદ્વાનોએ લોક-સંગ્રહ માટે અનાસક્ત થઈને કર્મ કરવું જોઈએ.
tweetEnglish: As the ignorant perform their duties with attachment, the learned may act similarly, but without attachment.
threadsEnglish: As the ignorant perform their duties with attachment to results, the learned may similarly act, but without attachment, for the sake of leading people.
englishTransliteration:
saktāḥ karmaṇy avidvāṁso yathā kurvanti bhārata
kuryād vidvāṁs tathāsaktaś cikīrṣur loka-saṅgraham
englishWBW: saktāḥ (attached) — karmaṇi (in prescribed duties) — avidvāṁsaḥ (the ignorant) — yathā (as) — kurvanti (they do) — bhārata (O descendant of Bharata) — kuryāt (must do) — vidvān (the learned) — tathā (similarly) — asaktaḥ (without attachment) — cikīrṣuḥ (desiring) — loka-saṅgraham (to lead the people in general)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa contrasts the ignorant worker with the wise worker. The outward action might look identical: both go to work, both take care of their responsibilities, and both might even fight in a war. The entire difference lies in the internal motive.

The ignorant work with ‘saktāḥ’, or intense attachment to the fruits—they work because they want money, fame, or power. The wise person should work with the same intensity, but ‘asaktaḥ’, or without any personal attachment. Their motive is simply to lead others on the right path.

Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna: “Don’t stop fighting. Just change your *Why*. Don’t fight for the crown; fight to set the standard of courage and sacrifice.” The world needs active, high-performing leaders who are internally detached. This is the perfect balance of material efficiency and spiritual depth.

sanskrit:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन्।।
translationEnglish:
So as not to disrupt the minds of ignorant men attached to the fruitive results of prescribed duties,
a learned person should not induce them to stop work.
Rather, by working in the spirit of devotion, he should engage them in all sorts of activities.
translationHindi: परमात्मा के स्वरूप में अटल स्थित हुए ज्ञानी पुरुष को चाहिए कि वह शास्त्रविहित कर्मों में आसक्ति वाले अज्ञानियों की बुद्धि में भ्रम (कर्मों में अश्रद्धा) उत्पन्न न करे, किन्तु स्वयं शास्त्रविहित समस्त कर्म भली-भांति करता हुआ उनसे भी वैसे ही करवाए।
translationGujarati: પરમાત્માના સ્વરૂપમાં અટલ સ્થિત થયેલા જ્ઞાની પુરુષે જોઈએ કે તે શાસ્ત્રવિહિત કર્મોમાં આસક્તિવાળા અજ્ઞાનીઓની બુદ્ધિમાં ભ્રમ (કર્મોમાં અશ્રદ્ધા) ઉત્પન્ન ન કરે, પરંતુ સ્વયં શાસ્ત્રવિહિત તમામ કર્મો સારી રીતે કરતો રહીને તેમની પાસે પણ તેમજ કરાવે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa instructs the wise not to disrupt the minds of ignorant people attached to fruitive work, but rather to engage them in all activities by working in a spirit of devotion.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण निर्देश देते हैं कि ज्ञानी पुरुष को सकाम कर्म में लगे अज्ञानी लोगों की बुद्धि को भ्रमित नहीं करना चाहिए, बल्कि भक्ति भाव से कर्म करके उन्हें भी काम में लगाना चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ નિર્દેશ આપે છે કે જ્ઞાની પુરુષે સકામ કર્મમાં લાગેલા અજ્ઞાની લોકોની બુદ્ધિને ભ્રમિત ન કરવી જોઈએ, પરંતુ ભક્તિ ભાવથી કર્મ કરીને તેમને પણ કામમાં લગાડવા જોઈએ.
tweetEnglish: Let not the wise disrupt the minds of the ignorant attached to fruitive action. Engage them in devotion.
threadsEnglish: The wise should not bewilder the minds of the ignorant who are attached to fruits. They should encourage them to act in the spirit of devotion.
englishTransliteration:
na buddhi-bhedaṁ janayed ajñānāṁ karma-saṅginām
joṣayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran
englishWBW: na (not) — buddhi-bhedam (disruption of intelligence) — janayet (should cause) — ajñānām (of the ignorant) — karma-saṅginām (who are attached to work) — joṣayet (should engage) — sarva (all) — karmāṇi (work) — vidvān (a learned person) — yuktaḥ (engaged) — samācaran (performing)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa gives a crucial lesson in spiritual leadership. He says that a wise person should not disrupt the minds of ignorant people who are attached to their work. You shouldn’t go to a hard-working person and tell them, “Work is an illusion, give it up.” This will only make them confused and irresponsible.

Instead, the wise person should encourage them by performing their own duties with devotion and showing them how to offer their work to the Divine. You teach people by meeting them where they are and showing them the next step, not by demanding they jump to the finish line.

Arjuna’s idea of becoming a monk would ‘bewilder’ the common people who look up to him as a hero. They wouldn’t understand his high philosophy; they would only see a coward running away. Kṛṣṇa wants Arjuna to stay in his role and spiritualize it, thus lifting everyone up with him through his example.

sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः।
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते।।
translationEnglish:
The spirit soul bewildered by the influence of false ego thinks himself the doer of activities
that are in actuality carried out by the three modes of material nature.
translationHindi: वास्तव में सम्पूर्ण कर्म सब प्रकार से प्रकृति के गुणों द्वारा किये जाते हैं, तो भी जिसका अन्तःकरण अहंकार से मोहित हो रहा है, ऐसा अज्ञानी ‘मैं कर्ता हूँ’ ऐसा मानता है।
translationGujarati: વાસ્તવમાં તમામ કર્મો સર્વ પ્રકારે પ્રકૃતિના ગુણો દ્વારા કરવામાં આવે છે, તો પણ જેનું અંતઃકરણ અહંકારથી મોહિત થઈ રહ્યું છે, એવો અજ્ઞાની ‘હું કર્તા છું’ એમ માને છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that while all activities are carried out by the modes of material nature, the soul bewildered by false ego thinks “I am the doer”.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि वास्तव में सभी कार्य प्रकृति के गुणों द्वारा किए जाते हैं, लेकिन अहंकार से भ्रमित व्यक्ति सोचता है कि “मैं कर्ता हूँ”।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે વાસ્તવમાં બધા કાર્યો પ્રકૃતિના ગુણો દ્વારા કરવામાં આવે છે, પરંતુ અહંકારથી ભ્રમિત વ્યક્તિ વિચારે છે કે “હું કર્તા છું”.
tweetEnglish: The spirit soul bewildered by the false ego thinks himself the doer of activities carried out by nature.
threadsEnglish: The spirit soul bewildered by the influence of false ego thinks himself the doer of activities that are in actuality carried out by nature.
englishTransliteration:
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ
ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate
englishWBW: prakṛteḥ (of material nature) — kriyamāṇāni (being done) — guṇaiḥ (by the modes) — karmāṇi (activities) — sarvaśaḥ (all kinds of) — ahaṅkāra-vimūḍha (bewildered by false ego) — ātmā (the spirit soul) — kartā (doer) — aham (I) — iti (thus) — manyate (thinks)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains the mechanical nature of the body. All activities are actually being carried out by the three modes of material nature (goodness, passion, and ignorance). The body is a machine made of nature’s elements, and it reacts to its environment according to its programming.

However, the spirit soul, when bewildered by the ‘ahaṅkāra’, or false ego, thinks, “I am the doer.” We take credit for the body’s movements and the mind’s thoughts. When the body gets hungry, we say, “I am hungry.” When the mind gets angry, we say, “I am angry.” This is a case of mistaken identity.

The wise man realizes that he is the observer of the machine, not the machine itself. This detachment from doership is the key to escaping the burden of karma. By realizing that nature is doing the work, the soul stays aloof and free from the pride of success and the shame of failure.

sanskrit:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः।
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते।।
translationEnglish:
One who is in knowledge of the Absolute Truth, O mighty-armed, does not engage himself in the senses and sense gratification,
knowing well the differences between work in devotion and work for fruitive results.
translationHindi: परन्तु हे महाबाहो! गुण विभाग और कर्म विभाग के तत्त्व को जानने वाला ज्ञानी ‘सम्पूर्ण गुण ही गुणों में बरत रहे हैं’ ऐसा समझकर उनमें आसक्त नहीं होता।
translationGujarati: પરંતુ હે મહાબાહુ! ગુણ વિભાગ અને કર્મ વિભાગના તત્વને જાણનારો જ્ઞાની ‘તમામ ગુણો જ ગુણોમાં વર્તી રહ્યા છે’ એમ સમજીને તેમાં આસક્ત થતો નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa says that one who knows the truth about the modes of nature and action does not get attached, knowing that it is just the modes interacting with each other.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जो गुण और कर्म के सत्य को जानता है, वह यह जानकर आसक्त नहीं होता कि यह केवल गुण ही गुणों में बरत रहे हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે જે ગુણ અને કર્મના સત્યને જાણે છે, તે એ જાણીને આસક્ત થતો નથી કે આ માત્ર ગુણો જ ગુણોમાં વર્તી રહ્યા છે.
tweetEnglish: One who knows the truth about the modes of nature does not engage himself in the senses and sense gratification.
threadsEnglish: One who is in knowledge of the Absolute Truth, O mighty-armed, does not engage himself in the senses and sense gratification.
englishTransliteration:
tattva-vit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ
guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
englishWBW: tattva-vit (the knower of the Absolute Truth) — tu (but) — mahā-bāho (O mighty-armed one) — guṇa-karma (of the modes and work) — vibhāgayoḥ (of the differences) — guṇāḥ (the senses/modes) — guṇeṣu (among the sense objects/modes) — vartante (are acting) — iti (thus) — matvā (thinking) — na (never) — sajjate (becomes attached)
englishExplain:
Who is the ‘tattva-vit’, the person who knows the truth? It is someone who understands the difference between the soul, the modes of nature, and the work being performed. They realize that ‘guṇā guṇeṣu vartante’—that the modes of nature are simply interacting with other modes of nature.

When the eyes (matter/modes) see a form (matter/modes), the wise person knows that this is just a physical event. They don’t get internally swept away by it. They stay in the position of the witness. This understanding prevents them from getting ‘sajjate’, or ‘stuck’/attached to the experience.

They see life as a movie playing on a screen. The soul is the audience member. While the character on the screen (the body) might be in a fight, the audience member remains safe in their seat. This ‘witness consciousness’ is the secret to staying calm and liberated in the middle of life’s most intense battles.

sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु।
तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत्।।
translationEnglish:
Bewildered by the modes of material nature, the ignorant fully engage themselves in material activities and become attached.
But the wise should not unsettle them, although these duties are inferior due to the performers’ lack of knowledge.
translationHindi: प्रकृति के गुणों से अत्यन्त मोहित हुए मनुष्य गुणों में और कर्मों में आसक्त रहते हैं, उन पूर्णतया न समझने वाले मन्दबुद्धि अज्ञानियों को पूर्णतया जानने वाला ज्ञानी विचलित न करे।
translationGujarati: પ્રકૃતિના ગુણોથી અત્યંત મોહિત થયેલા મનુષ્યો ગુણોમાં અને કર્મોમાં આસક્ત રહે છે, તે પૂરેપૂરું ન સમજનારા મંદબુદ્ધિ અજ્ઞાનીઓને પૂરેપૂરું જાણનારો જ્ઞાની વિચલિત ન કરે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa advises that the wise should not unsettle the ignorant who are bewildered by the modes of nature and attached to material activities.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण सलाह देते हैं कि ज्ञानी पुरुषों को उन अज्ञानी लोगों को विचलित नहीं करना चाहिए जो प्रकृति के गुणों से मोहित होकर सांसारिक कार्यों में आसक्त हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સલાહ આપે છે કે જ્ઞાની પુરુષોએ તે અજ્ઞાની લોકોને વિચલિત ન કરવા જોઈએ જે પ્રકૃતિના ગુણોથી મોહિત થઈને સાંસારિક કાર્યોમાં આસક્ત છે.
tweetEnglish: Bewildered by the modes, the ignorant engage in material activities. The wise should not unsettle them.
threadsEnglish: Bewildered by the modes of material nature, the ignorant fully engage themselves in material activities. The wise should not disturb them.
englishTransliteration:
prakṛter guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu
tān akṛtsna-vido mandān kṛtsna-vin na vicālayet
englishWBW: prakṛteḥ (of material nature) — guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ (bewildered by the modes) — sajjante (they become engaged) — guṇa-karmasu (in material activities) — tān (those) — akṛtsna-vidaḥ (persons with poor knowledge) — mandān (lazy/foolish) — kṛtsna-vit (one who knows the whole truth) — na (not) — vicālayet (should disturb)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa repeats the need for patience with those who are not yet spiritually awake. People who are bewildered by the modes of nature are naturally attached to material work and enjoyment. They think that this world is all there is.

A person who knows the whole truth (‘kṛtsna-vit’) should not disturb these ‘mandān’, or less intelligent people. If you forcibly take away their toys before they have a better interest, they will only become miserable and confused. You shouldn’t shatter their worldview without giving them a replacement.

The wise person acts as a gentle guide. They stay in society, perform their work perfectly, and slowly demonstrate through their character that there is something higher than material gain. Spiritual education is a gradual process of waking up, not a violent disruption of one’s current life.

sanskrit:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः।।
translationEnglish:
Therefore, O Arjuna, surrendering all your works unto Me, with full knowledge of Me,
without desires for profit, with no claims to proprietorship, and free from lethargy, fight.
translationHindi: इसलिए हे अर्जुन! तू अध्यात्मचित्त से समस्त कर्मों को मुझमें अर्पण करके, आशारहित, ममतारहित और संताप रहित होकर युद्ध कर।
translationGujarati: તેથી હે અર્જુન! તું અધ્યાત્મચિત્તથી તમામ કર્મોને મારામાં અર્પણ કરીને, આશારહિત, મમતારહિત અને સંતાપ રહિત થઈને યુદ્ધ કર.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa commands Arjuna to surrender all his works to Him, and with full knowledge and without desire for profit or ownership, to fight without lethargy.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को आदेश देते हैं कि वे अपने सभी कर्म उन्हें समर्पित करें, और पूर्ण ज्ञान के साथ, बिना किसी लाभ या स्वामित्व की इच्छा के, आलस्य छोड़कर युद्ध करें।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને આદેશ આપે છે કે તેઓ પોતાના બધા કર્મો તેમને સમર્પિત કરે, અને પૂર્ણ જ્ઞાન સાથે, કોઈપણ લાભ કે માલિકીની ઈચ્છા વિના, આળસ છોડીને યુદ્ધ કરે.
tweetEnglish: Therefore, O Arjuna, surrendering all your works unto Me, with no desire for gain, fight without lethargy.
threadsEnglish: Therefore, O Arjuna, surrendering all your works unto Me, with full knowledge of Me, without desires for profit and free from selfishness, fight!
englishTransliteration:
mayi sarvāṇi kर्माṇi sannyasyādhyātma-cetasā
nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ
englishWBW: mayi (unto Me) — sarvāṇi (all) — karmāṇi (work) — sannyasya (renouncing) — adhyātma (spiritual) — cetasā (with the mind) — nirāśīḥ (without desire for profit) — nirmamaḥ (without ownership) — bhūtvā (becoming) — yudhyasva (fight) — vigata-jvaraḥ (without lethargy/fever)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa gives the final, clear strategy for Arjuna: “Renounce all your activities unto Me, with your mind fixed on the spiritual self. Without desire for profit, without a sense of ownership, and free from the fever of the soul, fight.”

This is the complete formula for Karma-yoga. 1) ‘Mayi sannyasya’—hand the results to Kṛṣṇa. 2) ‘Nirāśīḥ’—don’t work for personal gain. 3) ‘Nirmamaḥ’—don’t claim ownership of the action. 4) ‘Vigata-jvaraḥ’—be calm and energetic, not lazy or frantic. The ‘fever’ of the soul is the anxiety of ‘I must win’ or ‘What will happen to me?’

Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna to be a professional soldier of the Divine. He should do the job with 100% focus and skill, but with 0% ego. This state of ‘spiritual detachment’ is the only way to perform a violent duty like war without losing his own soul in the process.

sanskrit:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः।
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः।।
translationEnglish:
Those persons who execute their duties according to My injunctions and who follow this teaching faithfully,
without envy, become free from the bondage of fruitive actions.
translationHindi: जो कोई मनुष्य दोष-दृष्टि से रहित और श्रद्धा से युक्त होकर मेरे इस मत का सदा अनुसरण करते हैं, वे भी सम्पूर्ण कर्मों (के बन्धन) से छूट जाते हैं।
translationGujarati: જે કોઈ મનુષ્ય દોષ-દ્રષ્ટિ રહિત અને શ્રદ્ધાથી યુક્ત થઈને મારા આ મતનું સદાય અનુસરણ કરે છે, તેઓ પણ તમામ કર્મો (ના બંધન) થી મુક્ત થઈ જાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa declares that those who follow His teachings with faith and without envy become free from the bondage of actions.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण घोषणा करते हैं कि जो लोग श्रद्धा और बिना ईर्ष्या के उनके उपदेशों का पालन करते हैं, वे कर्मों के बंधन से मुक्त हो जाते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ઘોષણા કરે છે કે જે લોકો શ્રદ્ધા અને ઈર્ષ્યા વિના તેમના ઉપદેશોનું પાલન કરે છે, તેઓ કર્મોના બંધનમાંથી મુક્ત થઈ જાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Those who follow My injunctions faithfully and without envy become free from the bondage of fruitive actions.
threadsEnglish: Those persons who execute their duties according to My injunctions and who follow this teaching faithfully, without envy, become free from the bondage of karma.
englishTransliteration:
ye me matam idaṁ nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ
śraddhāvanto ’nasūyanto mucyante te ’pi karmabhiḥ
englishWBW: ye (those who) — me (My) — matam (teachings) — idam (this) — nitya (regularly) — anutiṣṭhanti (follow) — mānavāḥ (human beings) — śraddhāvantaḥ (with faith) — anasūyantaḥ (without envy) — mucyante (become free) — te (they) — api (also) — karmabhiḥ (from the bondage of work)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa outlines the result of following His advice. Any human being who executes their duties according to these instructions and follows this teaching faithfully, without envy, becomes free from the bondage of karma. This is a universal promise.

Two qualities are needed: ‘śraddha’ (faith) and ‘anasūya’ (non-envy). Faith means trusting that the Creator knows the best way for the creature to live. Non-envy means not resenting God’s authority or the complexity of His laws. It is a humble acceptance of the spiritual path.

Even if one is not a great philosopher, simple, sincere adherence to these principles is enough to break the chains of material reaction. Kṛṣṇa is making liberation accessible to everyone. You don’t have to be a genius; you just have to be a faithful and non-envious servant of the truth.

sanskrit:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम्।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः।।
translationEnglish:
But those who, out of envy, disregard these teachings and do not follow them
are to be considered bereft of all knowledge, befooled, and ruined in their endeavors for perfection.
translationHindi: परन्तु जो मनुष्य मुझमें दोषारोपण करते हुए मेरे इस मत के अनुसार नहीं चलते हैं, उन मूर्खों को तू सम्पूर्ण ज्ञानों में मोहित और नष्ट हुए ही समझ।
translationGujarati: પરંતુ જે મનુષ્યો મારામાં દોષારોપણ કરતા મારા આ મત અનુસાર નથી ચાલતા, તે મૂર્ખોને તું તમામ જ્ઞાનોમાં મોહિત અને નષ્ટ થયેલા જ સમજ.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa warns that those who, out of envy, disregard His teachings are devoid of knowledge, bereft of consciousness, and doomed to ruin.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण चेतावनी देते हैं कि जो ईर्ष्यावश उनके उपदेशों की अवहेलना करते हैं, वे ज्ञानहीन और चेतना-शून्य हैं और उनका विनाश निश्चित है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ચેતવણી આપે છે કે જે ઈર્ષ્યાવશ તેમના ઉપદેશોની અવગણના કરે છે, તેઓ જ્ઞાનહીન અને ચેતના-શૂન્ય છે અને તેમનો વિનાશ નિશ્ચિત છે.
tweetEnglish: But those who, out of envy, do not follow these teachings are bereft of all knowledge and are ruined.
threadsEnglish: But those who, out of envy, do not follow these teachings and ignore them are to be considered bereft of all knowledge, befooled and ruined.
englishTransliteration:
ye tv etad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam
sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāṁs tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ
englishWBW: ye (those who) — tu (but) — etat (this) — abhyasūyantaḥ (out of envy) — na (not) — anutiṣṭhanti (do follow) — me (My) — matam (teachings) — sarva-jñāna (in all knowledge) — vimūḍhān (perfectly deluded) — tān (them) — viddhi (know) — naṣṭān (ruined) — acetasaḥ (without consciousness)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa warns those who reject His path. Those who, out of envy, disregard these teachings and do not follow them are to be considered completely deluded and bereft of all real knowledge. They are ‘naṣṭān’, or ruined in their endeavors for human perfection.

Envy of the Divine is the root of material bondage. It is the ego saying, “I don’t need a Higher Power, I am my own master.” This attitude closes the door to spiritual help. Without a connection to the Source, the intellect becomes ‘acetasaḥ’, or senseless, and life becomes a futile struggle.

Kṛṣṇa is not being angry; He is being realistic. If you ignore the laws of gravity, you will fall. if you ignore the spiritual laws of the universe, you will remain trapped in the cycle of suffering. Rejection of truth is the ultimate self-sabotage.

sanskrit:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि।
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति।।
translationEnglish:
Even a man of knowledge acts according to his own nature, for everyone follows the nature he has acquired from the three modes.
What can repression accomplish?
translationHindi: सभी प्राणी अपनी प्रकृति को प्राप्त होते हैं (अर्थात अपने स्वभाव के परवश हुए कर्म करते हैं); ज्ञानवान भी अपनी प्रकृति के अनुसार चेष्टा करता है। फिर इसमें हठ क्या करेगा?
translationGujarati: બધા પ્રાણીઓ પોતાની પ્રકૃતિને પામે છે (અર્થાત પોતાના સ્વભાવને પરવશ થઈને કર્મ કરે છે); જ્ઞાનવાન પણ પોતાની પ્રકૃતિ અનુસાર ચેષ્ટા કરે છે. તો પછી આમાં હઠ શું કરશે?
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa says that even a wise man acts according to his own nature, for all beings follow their nature; repression alone can accomplish nothing.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि ज्ञानी पुरुष भी अपने स्वभाव के अनुसार कार्य करता है, क्योंकि सभी प्राणी अपनी प्रकृति का अनुसरण करते हैं; केवल दमन से कुछ नहीं होगा।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે જ્ઞાની પુરુષ પણ પોતાના સ્વભાવ અનુસાર કાર્ય કરે છે, કારણ કે બધા પ્રાણીઓ પોતાની પ્રકૃતિનું અનુસરણ કરે છે; માત્ર દમનથી કશું થશે નહીં.
tweetEnglish: Even a man of knowledge acts according to his own nature, for everyone follows the nature he has acquired.
threadsEnglish: Even a man of knowledge acts according to his own nature, for everyone follows the nature he has acquired. What can repression accomplish?
englishTransliteration:
sadṛśaṁ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛter jñānavān api
prakṛtiṁ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṁ kariṣyati
englishWBW: sadṛśam (accordingly) — ceṣṭate (tries) — svasyāḥ (one’s own) — prakṛteḥ (modes of nature) — jñānavān (learned) — api (even) — prakṛtim (nature) — yānti (undergo) — bhūtāni (all living entities) — nigrahaḥ (repression) — kim (what) — kariṣyati (can do)
englishExplain:
