The practitioner then pushes their life air (‘prāṇa’) to the very top of the head. This is the process of ‘sensory withdrawal’ and ‘internalization’. The yogī is effectively shutting down the body’s connection to the outside world to focus all energy on the spiritual exit point.

This describes a state of total concentration. It is the physical and mental equivalent of preparing for a launch. Kṛṣṇa is showing that reaching the Supreme requires a deliberate withdrawal of interest from the temporary world. It is a total mobilization of the self toward the one point that matters.

sanskrit:
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन्।
यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम्।।
translationEnglish: After being situated in this yoga practice and vibrating the sacred syllable Oṁ, the supreme combination of letters, if one thinks of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and quits his body, he will certainly reach the spiritual planets.
translationHindi: ...जो पुरुष ‘ॐ’ इस एक अक्षर रूप ब्रह्म का उच्चारण करता हुआ और मेरा स्मरण करता हुआ शरीर को त्यागकर जाता है, वह परम गति को प्राप्त होता है।
translationGujarati: ...જે પુરુષ ‘ૐ’ આ એક અક્ષર રૂપ બ્રહ્મનું ઉચ્ચારણ કરતો અને મારું સ્મરણ કરતો શરીર છોડીને જાય છે, તે પરમ ગતિને પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa says that one who leaves the body while chanting the sacred syllable ‘Oṁ’ and remembering Him attains the supreme destination.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जो व्यक्ति ‘ओम’ का उच्चारण करते हुए और उनका स्मरण करते हुए शरीर त्यागता है, वह परम गति (मोक्ष) प्राप्त करता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે જે વ્યક્તિ ‘ઓમ’ નું ઉચ્ચારણ કરતા અને તેમનું સ્મરણ કરતા શરીર છોડે છે, તે પરમ ગતિ (મોક્ષ) પ્રાપ્ત કરે છે.
tweetEnglish: Vibrating ’oṁ’ and thinking of the Supreme Personality of Godhead at death, one reaches spiritual planets.
englishTransliteration:
oṁ ity ekākṣaraṁ brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran
yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṁ sa yāti parāṁ gatim
englishWBW: om (the sacred syllable om) — iti (thus) — eka-akṣaram (the one syllable) — brahma (Absolute) — vyāharan (vibrating) — mām (Me) — anusmaran (remembering) — yaḥ (whoever) — prayāti (leaves) — tyajan (quitting) — deham (the body) — saḥ (he) — yāti (attains) — parām (the supreme) — gatim (destination)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa gives the final instruction for the path of meditation. The yogī should vibrate the sacred syllable Oṁ, the sound representation of the Absolute, while constantly remembering the Supreme Lord. If a person leaves their body in this state of consciousness, they reach the supreme destination.

Oṁ is the primal sound from which the universe emerged. It is the ‘bridge’ between the material and the spiritual. But Kṛṣṇa adds a vital condition: ‘mām anusmaran’—remembering Me. Even while chanting the sacred sound, the heart must be fixed on the Person behind the sound.

This verse provides the mantra and the motive for liberation. It emphasizes that death is not the end of a soul, but a departure toward a ‘parāṁ gatim’, a higher destination. For those who can master their breath and their sound, the moment of death becomes the moment of absolute freedom. The goal is clear: leave the material frame behind while vibrating the name of the Divine.

sanskrit:
अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः।
तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः।।
translationEnglish: For one who always remembers Me without deviation, I am easy to obtain, O son of Prith, because of his constant engagement in devotional service.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! जो अनन्यचित्त वाला योगी मुझे नित्य-निरन्तर स्मरण करता है, उस नित्य-निरन्तर मुझमें युक्त हुए योगी के लिए मैं सुलभ हूँ अर्थात उसे मैं सहज ही प्राप्त हो जाता हूँ।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! જે અનન્યચિત્તવાળો યોગી મને નિત્ય-નિરંતર સ્મરણ કરે છે, તે નિત્ય-નિરંતર મારામાં જોડાયેલા યોગી માટે હું સુલભ છું અર્થાત તેને હું સહેજે જ પ્રાપ્ત થઈ જાઉં છું.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa assures Arjuna that He is easily attainable for the devotee who constantly remembers Him with undivided attention.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन को आश्वस्त करते हैं कि जो भक्त एकाग्र मन से निरंतर उनका स्मरण करता है, उसके लिए वे बहुत आसानी से उपलब्ध हो जाते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને આશ્વસ્ત કરે છે કે જે ભક્ત એકાગ્ર મનથી નિરંતર તેમનું સ્મરણ કરે છે, તેના માટે તેઓ બહુ સરળતાથી ઉપલબ્ધ થઈ જાય છે.
tweetEnglish: For one who remembers Me without deviation, I am easy to obtain because of his constant engagement.
englishTransliteration:
ananya-cetāḥ satataṁ yo māṁ smarati nityaśaḥ
tasyāhaṁ sulabhaḥ pārtha nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ
englishWBW: ananya-cetāḥ (without deviation of the mind) — satatam (always) — yaḥ (whoever) — mām (Me) — smarati (remembers) — nityaśaḥ (regularly) — tasya (for him) — aham (I am) — su-labhaḥ (very easy to achieve) — pārtha (O son of Pṛthā) — nitya (constantly) — yuktasya (engaged) — yoginaḥ (for the devotee)
englishExplain:
After describing the difficult paths of breath control and sensory withdrawal, Kṛṣṇa offers a ‘shortcut’ for His devotees. He says that for the person who always remembers Him without any deviation, He is ‘su-labhaḥ’—very easy to achieve. This is the path of Bhakti.

The only requirement is ‘ananya-cetāḥ’ (undivided focus) and ‘nityaśaḥ’ (regularity). A devotee doesn’t have to master complex physical postures or stop their breath. They simply need to make Kṛṣṇa their constant companion in their thoughts. Whether working, eating, or resting, their mind stays ‘yukta’, or connected, to Him.

Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that love is more powerful than technique. While the mystics struggle with their internal mechanics, the devotee simply turns their affection toward God. For such a loving soul, Kṛṣṇa removes all obstacles and makes Himself easily available. This is the most practical and accessible path for anyone living in the modern world.

sanskrit:
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम्।
नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः।।
translationEnglish: After attaining Me, the great souls, who are yogis in devotion, never return to this temporary world, which is full of miseries, because they have attained the highest perfection.
translationHindi: परम सिद्धि को प्राप्त महात्माजन मुझको प्राप्त होकर दुःखों के घर रूप क्षणभंगुर पुनर्जन्म को नहीं प्राप्त होते।
translationGujarati: પરમ સિદ્ધિને પ્રાપ્ત મહાત્માજનો મને પામીને દુઃખોના ઘર રૂપ ક્ષણભંગુર પુનર્જન્મને નથી પામતા.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that great souls who attain Him are not reborn into this temporary, miserable world, having achieved the highest perfection.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि उन्हें प्राप्त करने वाले महात्मा इस दुखों से भरे अस्थायी संसार में दोबारा जन्म नहीं लेते, क्योंकि उन्होंने परम सिद्धि प्राप्त कर ली होती है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે તેમને પામનારા મહાત્મા આ દુઃખોથી ભરેલા અસ્થાયી સંસારમાં ફરી જન્મ નથી લેતા, કારણ કે તેમણે પરમ સિદ્ધિ પ્રાપ્ત કરી લીધી હોય છે.
tweetEnglish: After attaining Me, the great souls never return to this temporary world of miseries.
englishTransliteration:
mām upetya punar janma duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam
nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṁsiddhiṁ paramāṁ gatāḥ
englishWBW: mām (Me) — upetya (achieving) — punaḥ janma (rebirth) — duḥkha-ālayam (place of miseries) — aśāśvatam (temporary) — na (never) — āpnuvanti (attain) — mahā-ātmānaḥ (the great souls) — saṁsiddhim (perfection) — paramām (the ultimate) — gatāḥ (having achieved)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the state of the souls who reach Him. These ‘mahātmānaḥ’, or great souls, have attained the ultimate perfection. Having reached the Lord, they never return to this temporary world, which He calls ‘duḥkhālayam’—a house of miseries.

This is a powerful reality check. Kṛṣṇa defines the material world as fundamentally miserable and temporary (‘aśāśvatam’). Even the best material life is shadowed by disease, aging, and death. Trying to find permanent happiness here is like trying to stay dry in the middle of the ocean. It is simply not the nature of the place.

By reaching Kṛṣṇa, the soul exits this ‘house of pain’ forever. This is not a negative escape, but a positive promotion to our original, blissful environment. Arjuna is encouraged to see the war and his earthly kingdom as small compared to the ‘paramāṁ saṁsiddhim’, the supreme perfection of never having to suffer material birth again.

sanskrit:
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन।
मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते।।
translationEnglish:
From the highest planet in the material world down to the lowest, all are places of misery wherein repeated birth and death take place.
But one who attains to My abode, O son of Kunti, never takes birth again.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! ब्रह्मलोकपर्यन्त सब लोक पुनरावर्ती हैं (अर्थात जहाँ से पुनः लौटना पड़ता है); परन्तु हे कुन्तीपुत्र! मुझको प्राप्त होकर पुनर्जन्म नहीं होता।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! બ્રહ્મલોક સુધીના બધા લોક પુનરાવર્તી છે (અર્થાત જ્યાંથી ફરી પાછા ફરવું પડે છે); પરંતુ હે કુંતીપુત્ર! મને પામીને પુનર્જન્મ નથી થતો.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa states that all worlds, even the highest realm of Brahmā, are subject to rebirth, but one who attains Kṛṣṇa never takes birth again.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि ब्रह्मा के लोक तक सभी लोकों से वापस लौटना पड़ता है (पुनर्जन्म होता है), लेकिन उन्हें प्राप्त करने के बाद पुनर्जन्म नहीं होता।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે બ્રહ્માના લોક સુધી બધા લોકમાંથી પાછા ફરવું પડે છે (પુનર્જન્મ થાય છે), પરંતુ તેમને પ્રાપ્ત કર્યા પછી પુનર્જન્મ નથી થતો.
tweetEnglish: From the highest planet down to the lowest, all are places of misery where birth and death repeat.
englishTransliteration:
ā-brahma-bhuvanāl lokāḥ punar āvartino ’rjuna
mām upetya tu kaunteya punar janma na vidyate
englishWBW: ā-brahma-bhuvanāt (up to the Brahmaloka planet) — lokāḥ (planetary systems) — punaḥ (again) — āvartinaḥ (returning) — Arjuna (O Arjuna) — mām (unto Me) — upetya (arriving) — tu (but) — kaunteya (O son of Kuntī) — punar janma (rebirth) — na (never) — vidyate (takes place)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa provides a map of the material universe. He says that from the highest planet (Brahmaloka) down to the lowest, every place is subject to ‘punaḥ āvartinaḥ’—repeated birth and death. No matter how high you climb in the material hierarchy, you are still inside the prison of time.

Even if one attains the status of a god or lives for millions of years on a celestial planet, they must eventually fall back and be reborn when their pious karma is exhausted. It is like moving from a basement apartment to a penthouse in a building that is scheduled for demolition. You are still in a temporary structure.

But reaching Kṛṣṇa is different. “Upon reaching Me, O son of Kuntī, there is no more birth.” Kṛṣṇa’s abode is outside the jurisdiction of material time and decay. This verse emphasizes that our true ambition should not be for a better material life, but for an eternal spiritual life. Kṛṣṇa is the only destination that offers permanent safety.

sanskrit:
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः।
रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः।।
translationEnglish: By human calculation, a thousand ages taken together form the duration of Brahmā’s one day. And such also is the duration of his night.
translationHindi: जो एक हजार चतुर्युगी तक की अवधि वाला ब्रह्मा का एक दिन जानते हैं और एक हजार चतुर्युगी तक की अवधि वाली ही रात्रि जानते हैं, वे पुरुष काल के तत्त्व को जानने वाले हैं।
translationGujarati: જે એક હજાર ચતુર્યુગી સુધીની અવધિવાળો બ્રહ્માનો એક દિવસ જાણે છે અને એક હજાર ચતુર્યુગી સુધીની અવધિવાળી જ રાત્રિ જાણે છે, તે પુરુષો કાળના તત્વને જાણનારા છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa describes the vastness of cosmic time: Brahmā’s one day lasts for a thousand cycles of ages, and his night is of equal length.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण ब्रह्मांडीय समय की विशालता का वर्णन करते हैं: ब्रह्मा का एक दिन एक हजार युगों (चतुर्युगी) के बराबर होता है, और उनकी रात भी इतनी ही लंबी होती है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ બ્રહ્માંડીય સમયની વિશાળતાનું વર્ણન કરે છે: બ્રહ્માનો એક દિવસ એક હજાર યુગો (ચતુર્યુગી) બરાબર હોય છે, અને તેમની રાત પણ એટલી જ લાંબી હોય છે.
tweetEnglish: By human calculation, a thousand ages form Brahmā’s one day. And such also is his night.
englishTransliteration:
sahasra-yuga-paryantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ
rātriṁ yuga-sahasrāntāṁ te ’ho-rātra-vido janāḥ
englishWBW: sahasra (one thousand) — yuga (ages) — paryantam (including) — ahaḥ (day) — yat (which) — brahmaṇaḥ (of Brahmā) — viduḥ (they know) — rātrim (night) — yuga (ages) — sahasra-antām (ending after a thousand) — te (they) — aho-rātra (day and night) — vidaḥ (who know) — janāḥ (people)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the staggering scale of cosmic time. He says that one day of Brahmā (the creator of the universe) lasts for a thousand cycles of the four ‘yugas’. His night is of the same immense duration. By human calculation, this is billions of years.

Those who understand this vast timeline are called ‘aho-rātra-vidaḥ’, those who know the nature of day and night. This scale is intended to shrink our human ego. We worry about our 80-year lives as if they were eternity, but in the eyes of cosmic time, even the lifespan of a universe is just a passing moment.

By revealing this, Kṛṣṇa helps Arjuna realize that material success and failure are tiny and fleeting. If even the life of Brahmā is just a day in the grand scheme, why get so attached to our small struggles? The wise person looks beyond these massive material cycles and seeks the Eternal Truth that remains unchanged even when billions of years have passed.

sanskrit:
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वा प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे।
रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके।।
translationEnglish: At the beginning of Brahmā’s day, all living entities become manifest from the unmanifest state, and thereafter, when the night falls, they are merged into the unmanifest again.
translationHindi: ब्रह्मा के दिन के आरम्भ में अव्यक्त (ब्रह्मा के सूक्ष्म शरीर) से सम्पूर्ण चराचर प्राणी पैदा होते हैं और ब्रह्मा की रात्रि के आरम्भ में उसी अव्यक्त नामक ब्रह्मा के सूक्ष्म शरीर में लीन हो जाते हैं।
translationGujarati: બ્રહ્માના દિવસના આરંભમાં અવ્યક્ત (બ્રહ્માના સૂક્ષ્મ શરીર) માંથી સંપૂર્ણ ચરાચર પ્રાણી પેદા થાય છે અને બ્રહ્માની રાત્રિના આરંભમાં તે જ અવ્યક્ત નામના બ્રહ્માના સૂક્ષ્મ શરીરમાં લીન થઈ જાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains the cycle of creation: at the start of Brahmā’s day, all beings manifest from the unmanifest, and at nightfall, they merge back into the unmanifest.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण सृष्टि चक्र समझाते हैं: ब्रह्मा के दिन की शुरुआत में सभी प्राणी अव्यक्त से प्रकट होते हैं, और रात होने पर वापस उसी अव्यक्त में विलीन हो जाते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સૃષ્ટિ ચક્ર સમજાવે છે: બ્રહ્માના દિવસની શરૂઆતમાં બધા પ્રાણીઓ અવ્યક્તમાંથી પ્રગટ થાય છે, અને રાત થવા પર પાછા તે જ અવ્યક્તમાં વિલીન થઈ જાય છે.
tweetEnglish: At the start of Brahmā’s day, all beings manifest. When night falls, they merge into the unmanifest again.
englishTransliteration:
avyaktād vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavanty ahar-āgame
rātry-āgame pralīyante tatraivāvyakta-saṁjñake
englishWBW: avyaktāt (from the unmanifest) — vyaktayaḥ (the living entities) — sarvāḥ (all) — prabhavanti (become manifest) — ahaḥ-āgame (at the beginning of the day) — rātri-āgame (at the fall of night) — pralīyante (are annihilated) — tatra (there) — eva (certainly) — avyakta (the unmanifest) — saṁjñake (called)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains the ‘breathing’ of the universe. When Brahmā’s day begins, all living entities become manifest from an unmanifest state. When his night falls, they are all merged back into that unmanifest condition. The universe is like a giant machine that is switched on and off in cycles.

This means that our current bodies and our current world are just one ‘waking’ phase of the cosmos. When the ‘night’ comes, everything we see will dissolve into a dormant state, like seeds waiting for the next spring. We have been through this cycle of appearing and disappearing countless times before.

This cycle is automatic and mechanical. It shows that material existence is a series of temporary flashes. Kṛṣṇa is teaching Arjuna that what he sees as ‘life’ and ‘death’ on the battlefield is just a micro-version of this cosmic pulse. Real life is found only when we break free from this rhythmic inhalation and exhalation of material energy.

sanskrit:
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते।
रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे।।
translationEnglish: Again and again, when Brahmā’s day arrives, all living entities come into being, and with the arrival of Brahmā’s night they are helplessly annihilated.
translationHindi: हे पार्थ! वही यह प्राणी-समुदाय उत्पन्न हो-होकर प्रकृति के वश में हुआ रात्रि के आने पर लीन होता है और दिन के आने पर फिर उत्पन्न होता है।
translationGujarati: હે પાર્થ! તે જ આ પ્રાણી-સમુદાય ઉત્પન્ન થઈ-થઈને પ્રકૃતિને વશ થઈને રાત્રિ આવવા પર લીન થાય છે અને દિવસ આવવા પર ફરી ઉત્પન્ન થાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa says that the multitude of beings is helplessly born again and again at the arrival of Brahmā’s day and annihilated at the arrival of his night.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि प्राणियों का समूह प्रकृति के वश में होकर बार-बार ब्रह्मा के दिन में पैदा होता है और रात में नष्ट हो जाता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે પ્રાણીઓનો સમૂહ પ્રકૃતિને વશ થઈને વારંવાર બ્રહ્માના દિવસમાં પેદા થાય છે અને રાતમાં નાશ પામે છે.
tweetEnglish: Again and again, when Brahmā’s day arrives, beings come into being, and at night they are annihilated.
englishTransliteration:
bhūta-grāmaḥ sa evāyaṁ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate
rātry-āgame ’vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavaty ahar-āgame
englishWBW: bhūta-grāmaḥ (the aggregate of all living entities) — saḥ (that) — eva (certainly) — ayam (this) — bhūtvā bhūtvā (repeatedly taking birth) — pralīyate (is annihilated) — rātri-āgame (at the arrival of night) — avaśaḥ (helplessly) — pārtha (O son of Pṛthā) — prabhavati (is manifest) — ahaḥ-āgame (at the arrival of day)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa emphasizes the helplessness of the conditioned soul. He says that this same multitude of living beings is born again and again, and then ‘helplessly’ annihilated at the arrival of the cosmic night. We have no choice in this matter as long as we remain in the material system.

‘Avaśaḥ’—helplessly—is the key word. We are like passengers on a train that keeps looping back to the start. We didn’t choose when the universe began, and we can’t stop it when it ends. This lack of control is a fundamental feature of material life. We are being moved by forces much larger than ourselves.

Arjuna’s struggle to control the outcome of the war is revealed to be a small part of this larger helplessness. Kṛṣṇa is showing him that the only way to gain true agency and freedom is to stop trying to control the material machine and instead connect with the Person who created it. The only choice we truly have is whether to stay in the loop or step out of it.

sanskrit:
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः।
यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति।।
translationEnglish:
Yet there is another unmanifest nature, which is eternal and is transcendental to this manifested and unmanifested matter.
It is supreme and is never annihilated. When all in this world is annihilated, that part remains as it is.
translationHindi: परन्तु उस अव्यक्त से भी परे जो दूसरा सनातन अव्यक्त भाव है, वह सम्पूर्ण भूतों के नष्ट होने पर भी नष्ट नहीं होता।
translationGujarati: પરંતુ તે અવ્યક્તથી પણ પર જે બીજો સનાતન અવ્યક્ત ભાવ છે, તે તમામ ભૂતોના નાશ થવા પર પણ નાશ પામતો નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa reveals a superior eternal unmanifest nature beyond this material world, which is not destroyed even when all beings are annihilated.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण इस भौतिक जगत से परे एक अन्य सनातन अव्यक्त प्रकृति के बारे में बताते हैं, जो सृष्टि के नष्ट होने पर भी नष्ट नहीं होती।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ આ ભૌતિક જગતથી પર એક અન્ય સનાતન અવ્યક્ત પ્રકૃતિ વિશે જણાવે છે, જે સૃષ્ટિના નાશ થવા પર પણ નાશ પામતી નથી.
tweetEnglish: Yet there is another unmanifest nature, eternal and transcendental. It is supreme and never annihilated.
englishTransliteration:
paras tasmāt tu bhāvo ’nyo ’vyakto ’vyaktāt sanātanaḥ
yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
englishWBW: paraḥ (transcendental) — tasmāt (to that) — tu (but) — bhāvaḥ (nature) — anyaḥ (another) — avyaktaḥ (unmanifest) — avyaktāt (to the unmanifest) — sanātanaḥ (eternal) — yaḥ (which) — saḥ (that) — sarveṣu (all) — bhūteṣu (living entities) — naśyatsu (being annihilated) — na (never) — vinaśyati (is annihilated)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa reveals the existence of a second, superior dimension. He says that beyond the manifest world and the dormant unmanifest energy, there is another unmanifest nature which is ‘sanātanaḥ’—eternal. This part of reality is never annihilated, even when the rest of the universe is destroyed.

This is the spiritual sky, or the kingdom of God. It is ‘anti-material’ in the sense that it doesn’t follow the laws of decay and time. While our world is like a shadow that appears and disappears, this higher realm is the solid reality that casts the shadow. It is our original home.

This verse provides the ultimate hope. We are not just particles in a recycling machine; we belong to an eternal family in an eternal world. Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that the goal of his life is to migrate to this ‘Sanātana’ nature. The war is temporary, the body is temporary, but the soul and the spiritual world are forever.

sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम्।
यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम।।
translationEnglish: That which the Vedantists describe as unmanifest and infallible, that which is known as the supreme destination, that place from which, having attained it, one never returns—that is My supreme abode.
translationHindi: उसी अव्यक्त को ‘अक्षर’ कहा गया है; उसी को परम गति कहते हैं; जिसको प्राप्त होकर (मनुष्य) वापस नहीं आते, वह मेरा परम धाम है।
translationGujarati: તે જ અવ્યક્તને ‘અક્ષર’ કહેવામાં આવ્યું છે; તેને જ પરમ ગતિ કહે છે; જેને પામીને (મનુષ્ય) પાછા નથી આવતા, તે મારું પરમ ધામ છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa describes His supreme abode as the unmanifest and imperishable destination; having reached it, one never returns to this material world.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अपने परम धाम का वर्णन करते हैं जिसे अव्यक्त और अक्षर कहा जाता है; जहाँ पहुँचने के बाद कोई इस संसार में वापस नहीं आता।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ પોતાના પરમ ધામનું વર્ણન કરે છે જેને અવ્યક્ત અને અક્ષર કહેવાય છે; જ્યાં પહોંચ્યા પછી કોઈ આ સંસારમાં પાછું નથી આવતું.
tweetEnglish: That unmanifest place from which one never returns is My supreme abode.
englishTransliteration:
avyakto ’kṣara ity uktas tam āhuḥ paramāṁ gatim
yaṁ prāpya na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama
englishWBW: avyaktāḥ (unmanifested) — akṣaraḥ (indestructible) — iti (thus) — uktaḥ (is called) — tam (that) — āhuḥ (is known) — paramām (the ultimate) — gatim (destination) — yam (which) — prāpya (achieving) — na (never) — nivartante (they come back) — tat (that) — dhāma (abode) — paramam (supreme) — mama (My)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes His supreme abode. This eternal realm is called ‘Akṣara’, meaning indestructible. It is known as the ‘paramāṁ gatim’, the ultimate destination of human life. Kṛṣṇa declares that once a person reaches this place, they never return to the world of suffering.

“Tad dhāma paramaṁ mama”—that is My supreme home. This is not a void or a state of non-existence; it is a ‘Dhāma’, a living environment where the soul interacts with God in its original, pure form. It is the place of absolute safety and permanent joy. It is the end of the long journey of rebirth.

Arjuna is being shown the ‘finish line’. Kṛṣṇa is motivating him by revealing the magnificent prize that awaits the successful seeker. By focusing on this supreme destination, the temporary terrors of the battlefield lose their power to disturb Arjuna’s heart. He is aiming for eternity.

sanskrit:
पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया।
यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।।
translationEnglish:
The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is greater than all, is attainable by unalloyed devotion.
Although He is present in His abode, He is all-pervading, and everything is situated within Him.
translationHindi: हे पार्थ! जिसके अन्तर्गत सम्पूर्ण भूत हैं और जिससे यह सम्पूर्ण जगत व्याप्त है, वह परम पुरुष तो अनन्य भक्ति से ही प्राप्त होने योग्य है।
translationGujarati: હે પાર્થ! જેની અંતર્ગત તમામ ભૂત છે અને જેનાથી આ સંપૂર્ણ જગત વ્યાપ્ત છે, તે પરમ પુરુષ તો અનન્ય ભક્તિથી જ પ્રાપ્ત થવા યોગ્ય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa states that the Supreme Person, in whom all beings reside and who pervades everything, can be attained only by unalloyed (pure) devotion.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि वह परम पुरुष, जिसके भीतर सभी प्राणी हैं और जो सब जगह व्याप्त है, केवल अनन्य भक्ति द्वारा ही प्राप्त किया जा सकता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે તે પરમ પુરુષ, જેની ભીતર બધા પ્રાણીઓ છે અને જે બધે વ્યાપ્ત છે, માત્ર અનન્ય ભક્તિ દ્વારા જ પ્રાપ્ત કરી શકાય છે.
tweetEnglish: The Supreme Personality of Godhead is attainable by unalloyed devotion. He is present everywhere.
englishTransliteration:
puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyas tv ananyayā
yasyāntaḥ-sthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idaṁ tatam
englishWBW: puruṣaḥ (the Personality) — saḥ (He) — paraḥ (the Supreme) — pārtha (O son of Pṛthā) — bhaktyā (by devotional service) — labhyaḥ (can be attained) — tu (but) — ananyayā (unalloyed) — yasya (whom) — antaḥ-sthāni (within) — bhūtāni (all of them) — yena (by whom) — sarvam (all) — idam (this) — tatam (is pervaded)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains how to reach the Supreme Person. He says that the Lord, who contains all beings and who pervades everything, is attainable only by ‘ananyayā bhaktyā’—unalloyed, pure devotion. No amount of wealth, knowledge, or physical discipline can buy entrance into His abode.

You cannot reach God through a ‘business transaction’ or a logical argument. You reach Him through a relationship of love. ‘Ananya’ means there is no second motive; the devotee wants God for God’s sake, not for a reward. This pure affection is the only force that can attract the Supreme.

This verse personifies the Absolute. Kṛṣṇa is not just an energy; He is the ‘Puruṣa’, the Person. Just as you can only enter a friend’s house if you have a relationship with them, you can only enter the spiritual world if you have developed a relationship with Kṛṣṇa. Arjuna is being encouraged to cultivate this singular focus of the heart.

sanskrit:
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः।
प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ।।
translationEnglish: O best of the Bharatas, I shall now explain to you the different times at which, passing away from this world, the yogī does or does not come back.
translationHindi: हे भरतश्रेष्ठ! जिस काल में शरीर त्यागकर गये हुए योगी वापस न लौटने वाली गति को और जिस काल में गये हुए वापस लौटने वाली गति को ही प्राप्त होते हैं, उस काल को मैं कहूँगा।
translationGujarati: હે ભરતશ્રેષ્ઠ! જે કાળમાં શરીર છોડીને ગયેલા યોગી પાછા ન ફરવાની ગતિને અને જે કાળમાં ગયેલા પાછા ફરવાની ગતિને જ પામે છે, તે કાળને હું કહીશ.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna that He will now explain the specific times of death which determine whether a yogī returns to this world or not.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि अब वे उन समयों के बारे में बताएंगे जब शरीर त्यागने पर योगी वापस आता है या नहीं आता।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને કહે છે કે હવે તેઓ તે સમય વિશે જણાવશે જ્યારે શરીર છોડવા પર યોગી પાછો આવે છે કે નથી આવતો.
tweetEnglish: O best of Bharatas, I shall explain the times at which the yogī passing away does or does not come back.
englishTransliteration:
yatra kāle tv anāvṛttim āvṛttiṁ caiva yoginaḥ
prayātā yānti taṁ kālaṁ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha
englishWBW: yatra (at which) — kāle (time) — tu (but) — anāvṛttim (no return) — āvṛttim (return) — ca (and) — eva (certainly) — yoginaḥ (the mystics) — prayātāḥ (having departed) — yānti (attain) — tam (that) — kālam (time) — vakṣyāmi (I shall describe) — bharata-ṛṣabha (O best of the Bharatas)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa begins to explain the different conditions under which a yogī departs from the world. He promises to tell Arjuna about the specific times of passing that lead either to ‘anāvṛttim’ (no return/liberation) or to ‘āvṛttim’ (return/rebirth).

In ancient Vedic mysticism, the circumstances of one’s death were considered very important. The time of day, the phase of the moon, and the path of the sun were thought to act as markers for the soul’s destination. Kṛṣṇa is addressing the technical traditions of the ‘Dhyāna-yogīs’ who relied on these cosmic timings.

This section shows that Kṛṣṇa is aware of all the mystical sciences. He is providing a complete education to Arjuna, covering both the technicalities of the mystics and the simplicity of the devotees. He is about to describe the ‘Path of Light’ and the ‘Path of Smoke’ as they were understood by the seekers of that time.

sanskrit:
अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम्।
तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः।।
translationEnglish: Those who know the Supreme Brahman attain that Supreme by passing away from the world during the influence of the fiery god, in the light, at an auspicious moment of the day, during the fortnight of the waxing moon, or during the six months when the sun travels in the north.
translationHindi: जिस मार्ग में अग्नि (प्रकाश) है, दिन का प्रकाश है, शुक्लपक्ष है और उत्तरायण के छः महीने हैं - उस मार्ग में शरीर त्यागकर गये हुए ब्रह्मवेत्ता पुरुष ब्रह्म को प्राप्त होते हैं।
translationGujarati: જે માર્ગમાં અગ્નિ (પ્રકાશ) છે, દિવસનો પ્રકાશ છે, શુક્લપક્ષ છે અને ઉત્તરાયણના છ મહિના છે - તે માર્ગમાં શરીર છોડીને ગયેલા બ્રહ્મવેત્તા પુરુષો બ્રહ્મને પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa describes the path of light (fire, day, waxing moon, northern sun) by taking which the knowers of Brahman attain Brahman.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण प्रकाश के मार्ग (अग्नि, दिन, शुक्ल पक्ष, उत्तरायण) का वर्णन करते हैं, जिससे जाने वाले ब्रह्मज्ञानी ब्रह्म को प्राप्त करते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ પ્રકાશના માર્ગ (અગ્નિ, દિવસ, શુક્લ પક્ષ, ઉત્તરાયણ) નું વર્ણન કરે છે, જેનાથી જનારા બ્રહ્મજ્ઞાની બ્રહ્મને પામે છે.
tweetEnglish: Those who know Brahman attain the Supreme by passing away in light, at an auspicious moment.
englishTransliteration:
agnir jyotir ahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇ-māsā uttarāyaṇam
tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahma-vido janāḥ
englishWBW: agniḥ (fire) — jyotiḥ (light) — ahaḥ (day) — śuklaḥ (the white fortnight of the moon) — ṣaṭ-māsāḥ (six months) — uttara-ayaṇam (when the sun passes on the northern side) — tatra (there) — prayātāḥ (those who pass away) — gacchanti (go) — brahma (to the Absolute) — brahma-vidaḥ (persons who know the Absolute) — janāḥ (people)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the ‘Path of Light’ (Devayāna). Those who know the Absolute and pass away during the influence of the fire-god, in the light of day, during the waxing moon, and during the six months when the sun travels in the north, reach the Supreme Brahman.

These elements—Fire, Light, Day, the Waxing Moon, and the Northern Sun—are symbolic of clarity, growth, and enlightenment. They are presided over by celestial deities who guide the soul upward. This is the auspicious exit for the person who has lived in knowledge and died in a state of wakefulness.

This path is for the ‘Brahma-vido’, the knowers of the Spirit. It emphasizes that dying in a state of brightness and consciousness is the goal of the mystical path. Kṛṣṇa is showing the traditional way that sages used to time their departure to ensure they moved toward the Light and away from the cycle of rebirth.

sanskrit:
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम्।
तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते।।
translationEnglish: The mystic who passes away from this world during the smoke, the night, the fortnight of the waning moon, or the six months when the sun passes to the south reaches the moon planet but again comes back.
translationHindi: तथा जिस मार्ग में धूम है, रात्रि है, कृष्णपक्ष है और दक्षिणायन के छः महीने हैं - उस मार्ग में शरीर त्यागकर गया हुआ योगी चन्द्रमा की ज्योति को प्राप्त होकर (स्वर्ग में अपने शुभ कर्मों का फल भोगकर) वापस लौट आता है।
translationGujarati: તથા જે માર્ગમાં ધુમાડો છે, રાત્રિ છે, કૃષ્ણપક્ષ છે અને દક્ષિણાયનના છ મહિના છે - તે માર્ગમાં શરીર છોડીને ગયેલો યોગી ચંદ્રમાની જ્યોતિને પામીને (સ્વર્ગમાં પોતાના શુભ કર્મોનું ફળ ભોગવીને) પાછો ફરે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa describes the path of darkness (smoke, night, waning moon, southern sun) by taking which the yogī reaches the lunar sphere but eventually returns to this world.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अंधकार के मार्ग (धुआं, रात, कृष्ण पक्ष, दक्षिणायन) का वर्णन करते हैं, जिससे जाने वाला योगी चंद्रलोक तक पहुँचता है लेकिन फिर वापस लौट आता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ અંધકારના માર્ગ (ધુમાડો, રાત, કૃષ્ણ પક્ષ, દક્ષિણાયન) નું વર્ણન કરે છે, જેનાથી જનારો યોગી ચંદ્રલોક સુધી પહોંચે છે પરંતુ પછી પાછો ફરે છે.
tweetEnglish: The mystic who passes away in smoke or darkness reaches the moon planet but returns.
englishTransliteration:
dhūmo rātris tathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇ-māsā dakṣiṇāyanam
tatra cāndramasaṁ jyotir yogī prāpya nivartate
englishWBW: dhūmaḥ (smoke) — rātriḥ (night) — tathā (also) — kṛṣṇaḥ (the dark fortnight of the moon) — ṣaṭ-māsāḥ (six months) — dakṣiṇa-ayaṇam (when the sun passes on the southern side) — tatra (there) — cāndramasam (the moon) — jyotiḥ (light) — yogī (the mystic) — prāpya (achieving) — nivartate (comes back)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the ‘Path of Darkness’ (Pitṛyāna). If a person passes away during smoke, at night, during the waning moon, or during the six months when the sun travels in the south, they reach the moon planet but eventually must return to earth.

These elements—Smoke, Night, the Waning Moon, and the Southern Sun—represent a lack of clarity and a lingering attachment to material results. This path leads to ‘Swarga’, or the temporary heavenly regions, where the soul enjoys the fruits of its pious deeds. Once the ‘credits’ are used up, the soul falls back into the world of birth and death.

This is the destination of the ‘good person’ who is not yet a ‘liberated person’. They are still caught in the system of reward and punishment. Kṛṣṇa is warning Arjuna that even the most glorious material success or a trip to heaven is still a temporary state that ends in ‘nivartate’—returning to the struggle.

sanskrit:
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते।
एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययावर्तते पुनः।।
translationEnglish:
According to Vedic opinion, there are two ways of passing from this world—one in light and one in darkness.
When one passes in light, he does not come back; but when one passes in darkness, he returns.
translationHindi: क्योंकि जगत के ये दो प्रकार के - शुक्ल और कृष्ण - मार्ग सनातन माने गये हैं। इनमें एक द्वारा गया हुआ वापस न लौटने वाली गति को प्राप्त होता है और दूसरे द्वारा गया हुआ फिर वापस आता है।
translationGujarati: કારણ કે જગતના આ બે પ્રકારના - શુક્લ અને કૃષ્ણ - માર્ગ સનાતન માનવામાં આવ્યા છે. આમાં એક દ્વારા ગયેલો પાછા ન ફરવાની ગતિને પામે છે અને બીજા દ્વારા ગયેલો ફરી પાછો આવે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa summarizes that there are two eternal paths: the path of light leading to liberation and the path of darkness leading to rebirth.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण सारांश में कहते हैं कि दो सनातन मार्ग हैं: प्रकाश का मार्ग जो मोक्ष की ओर ले जाता है और अंधकार का मार्ग जो पुनर्जन्म की ओर ले जाता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સારાંશમાં કહે છે કે બે સનાતન માર્ગ છે: પ્રકાશનો માર્ગ જે મોક્ષ તરફ લઈ જાય છે અને અંધકારનો માર્ગ જે પુનર્જન્મ તરફ લઈ જાય છે.
tweetEnglish: One passing in light does not come back; one passing in darkness returns. These are the two Vedic ways.
englishTransliteration:
śukla-kṛṣṇe gatī hy ete jagataḥ śāśvate mate
ekayā yāty anāvṛttim anyayāvartate punaḥ
englishWBW: śukla (light) — kṛṣṇe (and darkness) — gatī (ways of passing) — hi (certainly) — ete (these two) — jagataḥ (of the world) — śāśvate (eternal) — mate (in the opinion) — ekayā (by one) — yāti (goes) — anāvṛttim (to no return) — anyayā (by the other) — āvartate (comes back) — punaḥ (again)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa summarizes the two eternal paths of departure: the way of light and the way of darkness. One leads to the state of no return (liberation), and the other leads back to the world of repeated birth and death.

These two paths have existed since the beginning of the material world. They represent the two choices every human being faces: Do I seek the permanent Reality, or do I stay focused on the temporary world? The ‘light’ path is the path of wisdom and surrender; the ‘dark’ path is the path of ignorance and attachment.

By laying out these two options, Kṛṣṇa is making the stakes of Arjuna’s life very clear. The entire universe is a system of movement. We are all ‘going’ somewhere. Arjuna must decide if he wants to board the elevator to eternity or the treadmill of rebirth. This knowledge is intended to inspire a firm decision for the higher path.

sanskrit:
नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन।
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन।।
translationEnglish:
Although the devotees know these two paths, O Arjuna, they are never bewildered.
Therefore be always fixed in devotion.
translationHindi: हे पार्थ! इन दोनों मार्गों को तत्त्व से जानकर कोई भी योगी मोहित नहीं होता। इसलिए हे अर्जुन! तू सब समय में समबुद्धिरूप योग से युक्त हो।
translationGujarati: હે પાર્થ! આ બંને માર્ગોને તત્વથી જાણીને કોઈ પણ યોગી મોહિત નથી થતો. તેથી હે અર્જુન! તું હર સમયે સમબુદ્ધિરૂપ યોગથી યુક્ત થા.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa advises that knowing these two paths, a yogī is never bewildered; therefore, Arjuna should always remain fixed in yoga.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण सलाह देते हैं कि इन दोनों मार्गों को जानने वाला योगी कभी भ्रमित नहीं होता; इसलिए अर्जुन को हमेशा योग में स्थित रहना चाहिए।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સલાહ આપે છે કે આ બંને માર્ગોને જાણનાર યોગી ક્યારેય ભ્રમિત નથી થતો; તેથી અર્જુને હંમેશા યોગમાં સ્થિત રહેવું જોઈએ.
tweetEnglish: Devotees know these two paths but are never bewildered. Therefore be always fixed in devotion.
englishTransliteration:
naite sṛtī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaścana
tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yoga-yukto bhavārjuna
englishWBW: na (never) — ete (these two) — sṛtī (paths) — pārtha (O son of Pṛthā) — jānan (knowing) — yogī (the devotee) — muhyati (is bewildered) — kaścana (anyone) — tasmāt (therefore) — sarveṣu kāleṣu (at all times) — yoga-yuktaḥ (engaged in yoga) — bhava (be) — Arjuna (O Arjuna)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa gives a beautiful reassurance. He says that a yogī who knows these two paths—the light and the dark—is never bewildered by them. They don’t have to worry about the time of their death or the calendar of the universe.

Why? Because a true devotee is always ‘yoga-yuktaḥ’, or connected to the Lord. If you are always with Kṛṣṇa, then no matter when you die, Kṛṣṇa is there to guide you. The devotee transcends the technicalities of the mystics. They don’t need to wait for the ‘correct’ moon phase; their connection with God is their permanent light.

“Therefore, be always fixed in devotion.” Kṛṣṇa is simplifyng everything for Arjuna. Instead of worrying about astronomical timings, Arjuna should just keep his mind on Kṛṣṇa. This internal focus is the only insurance policy anyone needs. If the heart is right, the destination is guaranteed, regardless of the outward circumstances of death.

sanskrit:
वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव
दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम्।
अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा
योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम्।।
translationEnglish:
A person who accepts the path of devotional service is not bereft of the results derived from studying the Vedas, performing austere sacrifices, giving charity or pursuing philosophical and fruitive activities.
Simply by performing devotional service, he attains all these, and at the end he reaches the supreme eternal abode.
translationHindi: योगी इस रहस्य को जानकर, वेदों के पढ़ने में, यज्ञों में, तपों में और दानों में जो पुण्यफल कहा है, उन सबको निस्संदेह उल्लंघन कर जाता है और सनातन परम पद को प्राप्त होता है।
translationGujarati: યોગી આ રહસ્યને જાણીને, વેદોના વાંચવામાં, યજ્ઞોમાં, તપોમાં અને દાનોમાં જે પુણ્યફળ કહ્યું છે, તે બધાને નિઃશંક ઓળંગી જાય છે અને સનાતન પરમ પદને પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa concludes that a yogī who knows this surpasses the results of Vedic study, sacrifices, penance, and charity, and attains the supreme eternal abode.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण निष्कर्ष निकालते हैं कि इसे जानने वाला योगी वेदों, यज्ञों, तप और दान के फलों से भी ऊपर उठ जाता है और सनातन परम पद को प्राप्त करता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ નિષ્કર્ષ કાઢે છે કે આને જાણનાર યોગી વેદો, યજ્ઞો, તપ અને દાનના ફળોથી પણ ઉપર ઉઠી જાય છે અને સનાતન પરમ પદને પ્રાપ્ત કરે છે.
tweetEnglish: A person who accepts devotional service surpasses the results of all Vedic rituals and attains the supreme goal.
englishTransliteration:
vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva
dāneṣu yat puṇya-phalaṁ pradiṣṭam
atyeti tat sarvam idaṁ viditvā
yogī paraṁ sthānam upaiti cādyam
englishWBW: vedeṣu (in the study of the Vedas) — yajñeṣu (in sacrifices) — tapaḥsu (in austerities) — ca (also) — eva (certainly) — dāneṣu (in giving charity) — yat (that which) — puṇya-phalam (result of pious work) — pradiṣṭam (indicated) — atyeti (surpasses) — tat (that) — sarvam (all) — idam (this) — viditvā (knowing) — yogī (the devotee) — param (supreme) — sthānam (abode) — upaiti (reaches) — ca (and) — ādyam (original)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa concludes the eighth chapter by showing that the path of devotion is the ‘all-inclusive’ path. A person who takes to Bhakti is not deprived of the benefits of other spiritual activities. Simply by following this path, one automatically achieves all the results derived from studying the Vedas, performing sacrifices, doing penance, or giving charity.

The yogī ‘surpasses’ all these pious rewards and reaches the ‘param ādyam sthānam’—the supreme, original abode of the Lord. It is like getting a PhD that includes the credit for all previous grades. You don’t have to do the lower-level work if you have mastered the highest level.

This is a powerful closing statement. Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that by dedicating his life and his battle to the Lord, he is doing something much greater than any scholar or ascetic. He is on the ‘express lane’ to the original source. This realization empowers Arjuna to act with total confidence, knowing that he is fulfilling the purpose of all religion through his simple surrender.

sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्।।
translationEnglish:
The Supreme Personality of Godhead said:
My dear Arjuna, because you are never envious of Me, I shall impart to you this most confidential knowledge and realization,
knowing which you shall be relieved of the miseries of material existence.
translationHindi: श्री भगवान बोले: तुझ दोषदृष्टिरहित भक्त के लिए इस परम गोपनीय विज्ञान सहित ज्ञान को पुनः भली-भांति कहूँगा, जिसको जानकर तू दुःखरूप संसार से मुक्त हो जाएगा।
translationGujarati: શ્રી ભગવાન બોલ્યા: તારા જેવા દોષદ્રષ્ટિરહિત ભક્ત માટે હું આ પરમ ગોપનીય વિજ્ઞાન સહિત જ્ઞાનને ફરી સારી રીતે કહીશ, જેને જાણીને તું દુઃખરૂપ સંસારમાંથી મુક્ત થઈ જઈશ.
simpleEnglish: Lord Kṛṣṇa promises to reveal the most confidential knowledge and realization to Arjuna because he is free from envy, and this knowledge will liberate him from the miseries of material existence.
simpleHindi: भगवान कृष्ण अर्जुन को सबसे गोपनीय ज्ञान और विज्ञान देने का वादा करते हैं क्योंकि वह ईर्ष्या से मुक्त है, और यह ज्ञान उसे संसार के दुखों से मुक्त कर देगा।
simpleGujarati: ભગવાન કૃષ્ણ અર્જુનને સૌથી ગોપનીય જ્ઞાન અને વિજ્ઞાન આપવાનું વચન આપે છે કારણ કે તે ઈર્ષ્યાથી મુક્ત છે, અને આ જ્ઞાન તેને સંસારના દુઃખોમાંથી મુક્ત કરી દેશે.
tweetEnglish: Because you are never envious, I shall impart to you this most confidential knowledge and realization.
threadsEnglish: The Lord said: My dear Arjuna, because you are never envious of Me, I shall impart to you this most confidential knowledge and understanding, knowing which you shall be relieved of the miseries of material existence.
englishTransliteration:
śrī-bhagavān uvāca
idaṁ tu te guhyatamaṁ pravakṣyāmy anasūyave
jñānaṁ vijñāna-sahitaṁ yaj jñātvā mokṣyase ’śubhāt
englishWBW: śrī-bhagavān (the Supreme Personality of Godhead) — uvāca (said) — idam (this) — tu (but) — te (unto you) — guhya-tamam (most confidential) — pravakṣyāmi (I shall speak) — anasūyave (to the non-envious) — jñānam (knowledge) — vijñāna (realization) — sahitam (with) — yat (which) — jñātvā (knowing) — mokṣyase (you will be released) — aśubhāt (from miseries)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa begins the ninth chapter by introducing the ‘King of Knowledge’. He calls it ‘guhya-tamam’, the most secret and confidential of all wisdom. He is choosing to speak this to Arjuna for one specific reason: “because you are not envious of Me.”

‘Anasūya’, or non-enviousness, is the key to spiritual progress. If a person resents God’s supremacy, they will never understand the deep truths of the Gītā. They will see Kṛṣṇa’s instructions as arrogant. But Arjuna is a friend and a lover of the Lord, so he is qualified to receive the heart of the message.

Kṛṣṇa promises that this knowledge, combined with realization (‘vijñāna’), will free Arjuna from all the miseries of material life. It is the ultimate antidote to suffering. Kṛṣṇa is about to reveal how He personally interacts with the world and how a simple act of love can break the chains of karma forever.

sanskrit:
राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम्।
प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम्।।
translationEnglish:
This knowledge is the king of education, the most secret of all secrets.
It is the purest knowledge, and because it gives direct perception of the self by realization, it is the perfection of religion.
It is everlasting, and it is joyfully performed.
translationHindi: यह ज्ञान सब विद्याओं का राजा, सब गोपनीयों का राजा, अति पवित्र, अति उत्तम, प्रत्यक्ष फल वाला, धर्मयुक्त, साधन करने में बड़ा सुगम और अविनाशी है।
translationGujarati: આ જ્ઞાન બધી વિદ્યાઓનો રાજા, બધા રહસ્યોનો રાજા, અતિ પવિત્ર, અતિ ઉત્તમ, પ્રત્યક્ષ ફળવાળું, ધર્મયુક્ત, સાધવામાં અત્યંત સરળ અને અવિનાશી છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa describes this knowledge as the king of all education and secrets, pure and everlasting, which gives direct perception of the self and is joyfully performed.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण इस ज्ञान को सभी विद्याओं और रहस्यों का राजा बताते हैं, जो अति पवित्र और अविनाशी है, और जिसका पालन करना बहुत सुखद और धर्मसम्मत है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ આ જ્ઞાનને બધી વિદ્યાઓ અને રહસ્યોનો રાજા ગણાવે છે, જે અતિ પવિત્ર અને અવિનાશી છે, અને જેનું પાલન કરવું બહુ સુખદ અને ધર્મસંમત છે.
tweetEnglish: This knowledge is the king of education, the most secret, the purest, and gives direct perception of the self.
threadsEnglish: This knowledge is the king of education, the most secret of all secrets. It is the purest knowledge, and because it gives direct perception of the self by realization, it is the perfection of religion.
englishTransliteration:
rāja-vidyā rāja-guhyaṁ pavitram idam uttamam
pratyakṣāvagamaṁ dharmyaṁ su-sukhaṁ kartum avyayam
englishWBW: rāja-vidyā (the king of education) — rāja-guhyam (the king of secrets) — pavitram (the purest) — idam (this) — uttamam (transcendental) — pratyakṣa (by direct experience) — avagamam (understood) — dharmyam (the perfection of religion) — su-sukham (very happy) — kartum (to perform) — avyayam (everlasting)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa glorifies the knowledge He is about to share. He calls it the ‘rāja-vidyā’, the King of Education, and the ‘rāja-guhyaṁ’, the King of Secrets. It is the highest possible learning because it deals with the source of life itself. It is also ‘pavitram’, the purest knowledge, capable of washing away all material contamination.

One of its most beautiful features is that it is ‘su-sukhaṁ kartum’—it is joyfully performed. Unlike difficult penances or dry philosophical logic, the path of devotion (Bhakti) is full of happiness. It involves singing, dancing, and tasting divine food. It is not a struggle of the ego; it is a celebration of the heart.

Furthermore, this knowledge gives ‘pratyakṣāvagamaṁ’, or direct perception of the soul. It is not just a theory you have to believe in; it is something you can actually feel and experience in your own life. And because it is ‘avyayam’, the progress you make on this path is eternal. Kṛṣṇa is inviting Arjuna to a spiritual practice that is both effective and profoundly pleasant.

sanskrit:
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप।
अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि।।
translationEnglish:
Those who are not faithful in this devotional service cannot attain Me, O conqueror of enemies.
Therefore they return to the path of birth and death in this material world.
translationHindi: हे परन्तप! इस उपर्युक्त धर्म में श्रद्धारहित पुरुष मुझको न प्राप्त होकर मृत्युरूप संसार-चक्र में भ्रमण करते रहते हैं।
translationGujarati: હે પરંતપ! આ ઉપર્યુક્ત ધર્મમાં શ્રદ્ધારહિત પુરુષો મને પામ્યા વિના મૃત્યુરૂપ સંસાર-ચક્રમાં ભટકતા રહે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa warns that those who lack faith in this path of devotional service cannot attain Him and are forced to return to the cycle of birth and death in this world.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण चेतावनी देते हैं कि जिन लोगों को इस भक्ति मार्ग पर श्रद्धा नहीं है, वे उन्हें प्राप्त नहीं कर पाते और इस मृत्युलोक के चक्र में बार-बार लौटते रहते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ચેતવણી આપે છે કે જે લોકોને આ ભક્તિ માર્ગ પર શ્રદ્ધા નથી, તેઓ તેમને પામી શકતા નથી અને આ મૃત્યુલોકના ચક્રમાં વારંવાર પાછા ફરતા રહે છે.
tweetEnglish: Those not faithful in this service cannot attain Me and return to the path of birth and death.
threadsEnglish: Those who are not faithful in this devotional service cannot attain Me, O conqueror of enemies. Therefore they return to the path of birth and death in this material world.
englishTransliteration:
aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa
aprāpya māṁ nivartante mṛtyu-saṁsāra-vartmani
englishWBW: aśraddadhānāḥ (those who are faithless) — puruṣāḥ (persons) — dharmasya (of the religion) — asya (of this) — parantapa (O killer of the enemies) — aprāpya (without achieving) — mām (Me) — nivartante (come back) — mṛtyu (death) — saṁsāra (material existence) — vartmani (on the path)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa warns about the consequence of lacking faith. He says that those who have no faith in this path of devotional service can never reach Him. Instead, they are forced to return to the ‘mṛtyu-saṁsāra-vartmani’, the path of repeated birth and death in the material world.

Faith (‘śraddhā’) is the currency of the spiritual realm. Without faith in the personhood and kindness of God, a person remains trapped in their own limited logic. They may be good people or great scholars, but they cannot cross the boundary into the spiritual world because they don’t believe it exists or that they belong there.

This return to the world of death is not a punishment, but a natural result of choosing to stay disconnected from the Source. Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that the ‘exit door’ is wide open, but only for those who have the courage to trust in Him. Faith is the anchor that prevents the soul from being washed back into the ocean of suffering.

sanskrit:
मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना।
मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः।।
translationEnglish:
By Me, in My unmanifested form, this entire universe is pervaded.
All beings are in Me, but I am not in them.
translationHindi: मुझ अव्यक्तमूर्ति से यह सम्पूर्ण जगत व्याप्त है। सब भूत मेरे अन्तर्गत संकल्प के आधार स्थित हैं, किन्तु मैं उनमें स्थित नहीं हूँ।
translationGujarati: મારા અવ્યક્ત સ્વરૂપથી આ સંપૂર્ણ જગત વ્યાપ્ત છે. બધા પ્રાણીઓ મારામાં સંકલ્પના આધારે રહેલા છે, પરંતુ હું તેમનામાં સ્થિત નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that His unmanifested form pervades the entire universe; all beings rest in Him, yet He is not contained within them.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि उनका अव्यक्त स्वरूप पूरे ब्रह्मांड में व्याप्त है; सभी प्राणी उनमें स्थित हैं, लेकिन वे उन प्राणियों के भीतर सीमित नहीं हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે તેમનું અવ્યક્ત સ્વરૂપ આખા બ્રહ્માંડમાં વ્યાપ્ત છે; બધા પ્રાણીઓ તેમનામાં સ્થિત છે, પરંતુ તેઓ તે પ્રાણીઓની ભીતર સીમિત નથી.
tweetEnglish: By Me, in My unmanifested form, this entire universe is pervaded. All beings are in Me, but I am not in them.
threadsEnglish: By Me, in My unmanifested form, this entire universe is pervaded. All beings are in Me, but I am not in them.
englishTransliteration:
mayā tatam idaṁ sarvaṁ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā
mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na cāhaṁ teṣv avasthitaḥ
englishWBW: mayā (by Me) — tatam (pervaded) — idam (this) — sarvam (all) — jagat (universe) — avyakta-mūrtinā (by the unmanifested form) — mat-sthāni (in Me) — sarva-bhūtāni (all living entities) — na (not) — ca (and) — aham (I) — teṣu (in them) — avasthitaḥ (situated)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains His relationship with the universe. He says that the entire world is pervaded by Him in His ‘avyakta-mūrtinā’, His unmanifested form. All living beings rest in Him, yet He is not contained within them. This is the mystery of God’s simultaneous presence and absence.

God is like the space in a room; everything is ‘in’ the space, but the space is not the objects. He supports the universe like the screen supports a movie, but He is not a character in the movie. He provides the energy and the platform for all existence, yet He remains independent and transcendental.

This verse corrects the idea that God is ‘only’ the universe (pantheism) or that He is ‘only’ far away in heaven. Kṛṣṇa is saying, “I am everywhere as energy, but I am also distinct as a Person.” By understanding that everything rests in Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna can see that his relatives and his life are all within God’s careful and absolute jurisdiction.

sanskrit:
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्।
भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः।।
translationEnglish:
And yet everything that is created does not rest in Me.
Behold My mystic opulence!
Although I am the maintainer of all living entities and although I am everywhere, I am not a part of this cosmic manifestation, for My Self is the very source of creation.
translationHindi: वे सब भूत मुझमें स्थित नहीं हैं; किन्तु मेरी ईश्वरीय योगशक्ति को देख कि भूतों का धारण-पोषण करने वाला और भूतों को उत्पन्न करने वाला भी मेरा आत्मा वास्तव में भूतों में स्थित नहीं है।
translationGujarati: તે બધા પ્રાણીઓ મારામાં સ્થિત નથી; પરંતુ મારી ઈશ્વરીય યોગશક્તિને જો કે પ્રાણીઓનું ધારણ-પોષણ કરનારો અને પ્રાણીઓને ઉત્પન્ન કરનારો પણ મારો આત્મા વાસ્તવમાં પ્રાણીઓમાં સ્થિત નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa reveals His mystic opulence: although He is the creator and maintainer of all beings, He is not physically a part of this cosmic manifestation.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अपनी योगशक्ति प्रकट करते हैं: यद्यपि वे सभी प्राणियों के रचयिता और पालनहार हैं, फिर भी वे इस भौतिक जगत का हिस्सा नहीं हैं और उससे अलग हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ પોતાની યોગશક્તિ પ્રગટ કરે છે: જોકે તેઓ બધા પ્રાણીઓના રચયિતા અને પાલનહાર છે, છતાં તેઓ આ ભૌતિક જગતનો હિસ્સો નથી અને તેનાથી અલગ છે.
tweetEnglish: Behold My mystic opulence! Although I am the maintainer of all, I am not a part of this cosmic manifestation.
threadsEnglish: And yet everything that is created does not rest in Me. Behold My mystic opulence! Although I am the maintainer of all living entities and although I am everywhere, I am not a part of this cosmic manifestation, for My Self is the very source of creation.
englishTransliteration:
na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram
bhūta-bhṛn na ca bhūta-stho mamātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ
englishWBW: na (never) — ca (also) — mat-sthāni (situated in Me) — bhūtāni (all creation) — paśya (behold) — me (My) — yogam aiśvaram (inconceivable mystic power) — bhūta-bhṛt (the maintainer of all living entities) — na (never) — ca (also) — bhūta-sthaḥ (in the cosmic manifestation) — mama (My) — ātmā (Self) — bhūta-bhāvanaḥ (the source of all living entities)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa adds a second layer to the paradox. After saying that everything rests in Him, He now says, “And yet, everything that is created does not rest in Me.” He tells Arjuna to behold His ‘yogam aiśvaram’, His inconceivable mystic power. He is the maintainer of all beings, yet He is not a part of the material world.

This sounds like a contradiction, but it is the description of absolute freedom. A king is the source of the law and the maintainer of the kingdom, yet he is not personally involved in every small court case. His power is there, but he is at home in his palace. Kṛṣṇa supports every atom, but His ‘Self’ remains pristine and separate.

He is the ‘bhūta-bhāvanaḥ’, the very source of existence. He doesn’t ‘need’ the universe, and the universe doesn’t ‘burden’ Him. By showing this mystic opulence, Kṛṣṇa is teaching Arjuna that God is both intimately involved in our lives and perfectly free from our material limitations. We rest in His power, while He remains in His blissful independence.

sanskrit:
यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान्।
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय।।
translationEnglish:
Understand that as the mighty wind, blowing everywhere, rests always in the sky,
all created beings rest in Me.
translationHindi: जैसे आकाश से उत्पन्न सर्वत्र विचरने वाला महान वायु सदा आकाश में ही स्थित रहता है, वैसे ही मेरे संकल्प द्वारा उत्पन्न होने से सम्पूर्ण भूत मुझमें स्थित हैं, ऐसा जान।
translationGujarati: જેમ આકાશથી ઉત્પન્ન થયેલો સર્વત્ર વિચરનારો મહાન વાયુ સદાય આકાશમાં જ રહેલો છે, તેમ જ મારા સંકલ્પ દ્વારા ઉત્પન્ન થવાથી તમામ પ્રાણીઓ મારામાં રહેલા છે, એમ જાણ.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa uses the analogy of the mighty wind resting in the sky to explain how all created beings rest within Him without affecting Him.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण आकाश में स्थित वायु का उदाहरण देते हुए समझाते हैं कि कैसे सभी प्राणी उनमें स्थित रहते हैं, फिर भी वे उनसे प्रभावित नहीं होते।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ આકાશમાં સ્થિત વાયુનું ઉદાહરણ આપીને સમજાવે છે કે કેવી રીતે બધા પ્રાણીઓ તેમનામાં સ્થિત રહે છે, છતાં તેઓ તેમનાથી પ્રભાવિત થતા નથી.
tweetEnglish: Understand that as the mighty wind, blowing everywhere, rests always in the sky, all created beings rest in Me.
threadsEnglish: Understand that as the mighty wind, blowing everywhere, rests always in the sky, all created beings rest in Me.
englishTransliteration:
yathākāśa-sthito nityaṁ vāyuḥ sarvatra-go mahān
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni mat-sthānīty upadhāraya
englishWBW: yathā (just as) — ākāśa-sthitaḥ (situated in the sky) — nityam (always) — vāyuḥ (the wind) — sarvatra-gaḥ (blowing everywhere) — mahān (mighty) — tathā (similarly) — sarvāṇi (all) — bhūtāni (living entities) — mat-sthāni (situated in Me) — iti (thus) — upadhāraya (try to understand)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa provides a brilliant physical analogy to explain the previous paradox. He compares the living beings to the mighty wind that blows everywhere but always rests within the vastness of the sky. The wind is active and powerful, yet it can never leave the sky.

Similarly, all created beings are ‘in’ Kṛṣṇa, but they do not affect His nature. The sky is not moved by the wind, nor is it soiled by the dust the wind carries. The sky remains neutral and all-containing. In the same way, all the chaotic movements, births, and deaths of the material world happen within Kṛṣṇa, but He remains the pure and steady background of all reality.

This analogy helps Arjuna understand that even though he is in the middle of a war, he is still ‘in’ God. There is no place he can go where he is outside of Kṛṣṇa’s presence. This realization turns the terrifying battlefield into a safe space within the infinite ‘sky’ of the Divine. We are always contained within His care.

sanskrit:
सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम्।
कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम्।।
translationEnglish:
O son of Kunti, at the end of the millennium all material manifestations enter into My nature,
and at the beginning of another millennium, by My potency, I create them again.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! कल्पों के अन्त में सब भूत मेरी प्रकृति को प्राप्त होते हैं (अर्थात प्रकृति में लीन होते हैं) और कल्पों के आदि में उनको मैं फिर रचता हूँ।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! કલ્પોના અંતે બધા પ્રાણીઓ મારી પ્રકૃતિને પામે છે (અર્થાત પ્રકૃતિમાં લીન થાય છે) અને કલ્પોના આરંભમાં હું તેમને ફરી રચું છું.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains the cycle of creation and dissolution: at the end of an age, all beings merge into His nature, and at the beginning of the next, He creates them again.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण सृष्टि और प्रलय के चक्र को समझाते हैं: कल्प के अंत में सभी प्राणी उनकी प्रकृति में लीन हो जाते हैं, और नए कल्प की शुरुआत में वे उन्हें फिर से रचते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સૃષ્ટિ અને પ્રલયના ચક્રને સમજાવે છે: કલ્પના અંતે બધા પ્રાણીઓ તેમની પ્રકૃતિમાં લીન થઈ જાય છે, અને નવા કલ્પની શરૂઆતમાં તેઓ તેમને ફરીથી રચે છે.
tweetEnglish: At the end of the millennium all manifestations enter My nature, and I create them again.
threadsEnglish: O son of Kunti, at the end of the millennium all material manifestations enter into My nature, and at the beginning of another millennium, by My potency, I create them again.
englishTransliteration:
sarva-bhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṁ yānti māmikām
kalpa-kṣaye punas tāni kalpādau viśṛjāmy aham
englishWBW: sarva-bhūtāni (all created beings) — kaunteya (O son of Kuntī) — prakṛtim (nature) — yānti (enter) — māmikām (My) — kalpa-kṣaye (at the end of the millennium) — punaḥ (again) — tāni (all those) — kalpa-ādau (at the beginning of the millennium) — viśṛjāmi (I create) — aham (I)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the massive cycles of time. He says that at the end of a ‘kalpa’ (a day of Brahmā), all material manifestations dissolve back into His own nature. They go into a dormant, unmanifest state. Then, at the beginning of another ‘kalpa’, He creates them all again.

The universe ‘breathes’—manifestation is the exhalation, and dissolution is the inhalation. This reinforces the idea that the world is Kṛṣṇa’s energy in motion. We are part of a grand cosmic rhythm that has been repeating for eternity. Our current identity is just one ‘wave’ in this ocean.

By revealing this, Kṛṣṇa is de-escalating Arjuna’s anxiety about the war. He is showing that birth and death are part of a massive, automated system that He directs. The ‘end’ of the warriors on the battlefield is just a tiny part of the ‘kalpa-kṣaye’, the eventual dissolution of everything material. Understanding this scale takes the personal pressure off Arjuna’s shoulders.

sanskrit:
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः।
भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात्।।
translationEnglish:
The whole cosmic order is under Me.
Under My will it is automatically manifested again and again, and under My will it is annihilated at the end.
translationHindi: अपनी प्रकृति को अंगीकार करके स्वभाव के बल से परतंत्र हुए इस सम्पूर्ण भूत-समुदाय को बार-बार उनके कर्मों के अनुसार रचता हूँ।
translationGujarati: પોતાની પ્રકૃતિનો સ્વીકાર કરીને સ્વભાવના બળથી પરવશ થયેલા આ સમગ્ર પ્રાણી-સમુદાયને હું વારંવાર તેમના કર્મો અનુસાર રચું છું.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa controls the material nature and creates the multitude of beings again and again, who are helpless under the force of their own nature.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अपनी प्रकृति को वश में करके बार-बार प्राणियों के इस समुदाय की रचना करते हैं, जो अपने स्वभाव और कर्मों के अधीन होकर विवश हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ પોતાની પ્રકૃતિને વશમાં કરીને વારંવાર પ્રાણીઓના આ સમુદાયની રચના કરે છે, જે પોતાના સ્વભાવ અને કર્મોને અધીન થઈને વિવશ છે.
tweetEnglish: The whole cosmic order is under Me. Under My will it is manifested again and again, and annihilated at the end.
threadsEnglish: The whole cosmic order is under Me. Under My will it is automatically manifested again and again, and under My will it is annihilated at the end.
englishTransliteration:
prakṛtiṁ svām avaṣṭabhya viśṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ
bhūta-grāmam imaṁ kṛtsnam avaśaḥ prakṛter vaśāt
englishWBW: prakṛtim (material nature) — svām (My own) — avaṣṭabhya (entering into) — viśṛjāmi (I create) — punaḥ punaḥ (again and again) — bhūta-grāmam (the multitude of living entities) — imam (this) — kṛtsnam (entire) — avaśaḥ (helplessly) — prakṛteḥ (of nature) — vaśāt (under the obligation)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains how the creation happens. He enters into His own material energy and, through His will, manifests the multitude of beings again and again. Crucially, He says that these beings are ‘avaśaḥ’—helpless—under the control of their own material nature.

We don’t choose when to be born or how our bodies function; we are driven by the ‘guṇas’ (modes) and our past karma. We are like passengers on a ride we cannot stop. Our material desires force nature to give us matching bodies. We think we are free, but we are actually ‘under obligation’ to the laws of Prakṛti.

This verse highlights the difference between Kṛṣṇa’s power and our helplessness. He is the one who ‘switches on’ the system, and we are the ones caught in its gears. The only way to stop being ‘helpless’ is to align our will with the one who controls the machine. Arjuna is being shown that his only true freedom lies in surrender to the Divine Director.

sanskrit:
न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय।
उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु।।
translationEnglish:
O Dhanañjaya, all this work cannot bind Me.
I am ever detached from all these material activities, seated as though neutral.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! उन कर्मों में आसक्तिरहित और उदासीन के सदृश स्थित मुझ परमात्मा को वे कर्म नहीं बाँधते।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! તે કર્મોમાં આસક્તિરહિત અને ઉદાસીનની જેમ રહેલા મને પરમાત્માને તે કર્મો બાંધતા નથી.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa clarifies that these acts of creation and dissolution do not bind Him, as He remains neutral and detached from all material activities.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण स्पष्ट करते हैं कि सृष्टि और प्रलय के ये कर्म उन्हें नहीं बांधते, क्योंकि वे इन कार्यों में आसक्तिरहित और उदासीन रहते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સ્પષ્ટ કરે છે કે સૃષ્ટિ અને પ્રલયના આ કર્મો તેમને બાંધતા નથી, કારણ કે તેઓ આ કાર્યોમાં આસક્તિરહિત અને ઉદાસીન રહે છે.
tweetEnglish: O Dhanañjaya, all this work cannot bind Me. I am ever detached, seated as though neutral.
threadsEnglish: O Dhanañjaya, all this work cannot bind Me. I am ever detached from all these material activities, seated as though neutral.
englishTransliteration:
na ca māṁ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya
udāsīna-vad āsīnam asaktaṁ teṣu karmasu
englishWBW: na (never) — ca (also) — mām (Me) — tāni (all those) — karmāṇi (work) — nibadhnanti (bind) — dhanañjaya (O conqueror of wealth) — udāsīna-vat (as if neutral) — āsīnam (situated) — asaktam (unattached) — teṣu (in those) — karmasu (actions)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains why He is not responsible for the suffering in the world. He says that although He is the creator and maintainer, all this work does not bind Him. He remains ‘udāsīna-vad’, as if neutral, and perfectly unattached to the actions He performs.

God is like a judge in a courtroom. The judge may sentence a criminal to prison, but the judge is not the ‘cause’ of the crime or the suffering; the criminal’s own actions are the cause. The judge is just the neutral administrator of the law. Similarly, Kṛṣṇa sets the laws of nature in motion and lets them play out based on our karma.

He remains the blissful witness. This is a lesson for Arjuna in detachment. If even the Creator of the universe stays neutral and unattached to His massive work, then Arjuna should also perform his duty without becoming emotionally entangled. Neutrality is the shield that protects the soul from the stress of action.

sanskrit:
मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम्।
हेतुनाऽनेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते।।
translationEnglish:
This material nature, which is one of My energies, is working under My direction, O son of Kunti,
producing all moving and nonmoving beings.
Under its rule this manifestation is created and annihilated again and again.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! मुझ अधिष्ठाता के सकाश से प्रकृति चराचर जगत को रचती है और इस हेतु से ही यह संसार आवागमन के चक्र में घूमता रहता है।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! મારી અધ્યક્ષતામાં પ્રકૃતિ ચરાચર જગતને રચે છે અને આ કારણથી જ આ સંસાર આવાગમન (જન્મ-મરણ) ના ચક્રમાં ફરતો રહે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa states that material nature works under His direction to produce all beings, and this is why the universe is repeatedly created and destroyed.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि प्रकृति उनकी अध्यक्षता में ही चराचर जगत की रचना करती है, और इसी कारण से संसार का चक्र चलता रहता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે પ્રકૃતિ તેમની અધ્યક્ષતામાં જ ચરાચર જગતની રચના કરે છે, અને આ જ કારણથી સંસારનું ચક્ર ચાલતું રહે છે.
tweetEnglish: Material nature is working under My direction, producing all moving and nonmoving beings.
threadsEnglish: This material nature, which is one of My energies, is working under My direction, O son of Kunti, producing all moving and nonmoving beings. Under its rule this manifestation is created and annihilated again and again.
englishTransliteration:
mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sa-carācaram
hetunānena kaunteya jagad viparivartate
englishWBW: mayā (by Me) — adhyakṣeṇa (by the supervisor) — prakṛtiḥ (material nature) — sūyate (manifests) — sa (with) — cara-acaram (the moving and the nonmoving) — hetunā (by the cause) — anena (this) — kaunteya (O son of Kuntī) — jagat (the universe) — viparivartate (is working)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa summarizes His role as the ‘Supervisor’ of existence. He says that under His direction (‘mayādhyakṣeṇa’), material nature produces all moving and non-moving beings. Because of His presence and His will, the universe continues to revolve and function.

Nature is not a blind, accidental force. It is an intelligent system working under a Divine Superintendent. Every law of physics and every biological process is a manifestation of Kṛṣṇa’s management. He provides the ‘intent’, and Prakṛti (Nature) provides the ‘execution’.

This gives Arjuna a sense of cosmic order. The war he is facing is not a random disaster; it is a moment of recalibration within a system that Kṛṣṇa is supervising. By trusting the Supervisor, Arjuna can let go of his personal anxiety about the future. Everything is ‘working’ exactly as it should according to the divine plan. Our job is simply to play our part faithfully.

sanskrit:
अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम्।
परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम्।।
translationEnglish:
Fools deride Me when I descend in the human form.
They do not know My transcendental nature as the Supreme Lord of all that be.
translationHindi: मेरे परम भाव को न जानने वाले मूढ़ लोग मनुष्य का शरीर धारण करने वाले मुझ सम्पूर्ण भूतों के महान ईश्वर को तुच्छ समझते हैं (अर्थात अपनी योगमाया से संसार के उद्धार के लिए मनुष्य रूप में विचरते हुए मुझ परमेश्वर को साधारण मनुष्य मानते हैं)।
translationGujarati: મારા પરમ ભાવને ન જાણનારા મૂઢ લોકો મનુષ્યનું શરીર ધારણ કરનારા મને સર્વ પ્રાણીઓના મહાન ઈશ્વરને તુચ્છ માને છે (અર્થાત પોતાની યોગમાયાથી સંસારના ઉદ્ધાર માટે મનુષ્ય રૂપે વિચરતા મને પરમેશ્વરને સાધારણ મનુષ્ય માને છે).
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa points out that fools mock Him when He descends in human form, failing to recognize His higher nature as the Supreme Lord of all beings.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि मूर्ख लोग उनके मानव रूप का अपमान करते हैं, क्योंकि वे उनके परम स्वरूप को नहीं जानते जो सभी प्राणियों का ईश्वर है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે મૂર્ખ લોકો તેમના માનવ રૂપનું અપમાન કરે છે, કારણ કે તેઓ તેમના પરમ સ્વરૂપને નથી જાણતા જે બધા પ્રાણીઓનો ઈશ્વર છે.
tweetEnglish: Fools deride Me when I descend in human form. They do not know My transcendental nature.
threadsEnglish: Fools deride Me when I descend in the human form. They do not know My transcendental nature as the Supreme Lord of all that be.
englishTransliteration:
avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā mānuṣīṁ tanum āśritam
paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto mama bhūta-maheśvaram
englishWBW: avajānanti (deride) — mām (Me) — mūḍhāḥ (foolish men) — mānuṣīm (in a human form) — tanum (a body) — āśritam (assuming) — param (transcendental) — bhāvam (nature) — ajānantaḥ (not knowing) — mama (My) — bhūta (of everything that be) — mahā-īśvaram (the Supreme Lord)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa speaks about the tragedy of those who cannot recognize Him. He says that ‘mūḍhāḥ’, or foolish people, mock Him when He appears in a human-like form. They see His physical presence—eating, talking, and driving a chariot—and they assume He is just an ordinary mortal.

They are ignorant of His ‘paraṁ bhāvam’, His transcendental nature as the Supreme Lord of all that exists. They mistake the ‘role’ He is playing for His actual identity. It is like a citizen who sees the King dressed in simple clothes and forgets that he has the power of the entire state behind him.

This verse is a warning against judging by appearances. Kṛṣṇa’s human-like form is a manifestation of His kindness, allowing us to relate to Him. But those who lack spiritual vision use this very kindness as an excuse to disrespect Him. Kṛṣṇa wants Arjuna to keep his focus on the Divine Person behind the human face.

sanskrit:
मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः।
राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः।।
translationEnglish:
Those who are thus bewildered are attracted by demonic and atheistic views.
In that deluded condition, their hopes for liberation, their fruitive activities, and their culture of knowledge are all defeated.
translationHindi: जो व्यर्थ आशा, व्यर्थ कर्म और व्यर्थ ज्ञान वाले विक्षिप्तचित्त अज्ञानीजन हैं, वे मोहिनी प्रकृति को ही (अर्थात राक्षसी, आसुरी और मोहिनी प्रकृति को) धारण किये रहते हैं।
translationGujarati: જે વ્યર્થ આશા, વ્યર્થ કર્મ અને વ્યર્થ જ્ઞાનવાળા વિક્ષિપ્ત ચિત્તવાળા અજ્ઞાનીજનો છે, તેઓ મોહિની પ્રકૃતિને જ (અર્થાત રાક્ષસી, આસુરી અને મોહિની પ્રકૃતિને) ધારણ કરી રાખે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa describes those deluded people who embrace demonic and atheistic nature; their hopes, actions, and knowledge are all in vain.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण उन भ्रमित लोगों का वर्णन करते हैं जो राक्षसी और आसुरी स्वभाव को अपनाते हैं; उनकी सारी आशाएं, कर्म और ज्ञान व्यर्थ हो जाते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ તે ભ્રમિત લોકોનું વર્ણન કરે છે જે રાક્ષસી અને આસુરી સ્વભાવને અપનાવે છે; તેમની બધી આશાઓ, કર્મો અને જ્ઞાન વ્યર્થ થઈ જાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Bewildered, they are attracted by demonic views. Their hopes and activities are all defeated.
threadsEnglish: Those who are thus bewildered are attracted by demonic and atheistic views. In that deluded condition, their hopes for liberation, their fruitive activities, and their culture of knowledge are all defeated.
englishTransliteration:
moghāśā mogha-karmāṇo mogha-jñānā vicetasaḥ
rākṣasīm āsurīṁ caiva prakṛtiṁ mohinīm śritāḥ
englishWBW: mogha-āśāḥ (baffled in hope) — mogha-karmāṇāḥ (baffled in fruitive activities) — mogha-jñānāḥ (baffled in knowledge) — vicetasaḥ (bewildered) — rākṣasīm (demoniac) — āsurīm (atheistic) — ca (and) — eva (certainly) — prakṛtim (nature) — mohinīm (bewildering) — śritāḥ (taking shelter of)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the fate of those who deride Him. Because they ignore the Source, their hopes for happiness are ‘mogha’—useless and baffled. Their hard work yields no lasting result, and their knowledge is shallow and fruitless. They are fundamentally ‘vicetasaḥ’, or bewildered in heart.

Such people take shelter in a ‘rākṣasī’ and ‘āsurī’ nature—demoniac and atheistic views. They believe that they are the center of the universe and that there is no higher authority. This worldview is ‘mohinīm’, meaning it is a seductive illusion that leads only to further entanglement and frustration.

If you build a house on a foundation of sand, it will eventually collapse. Similarly, a life built on the denial of the Divine is destined for disappointment. Kṛṣṇa is showing that without God-consciousness, all human endeavors—no matter how impressive they look—are ultimately ‘mogha’, empty of eternal value. He is inviting Arjuna to build his life on the rock of Truth instead.

sanskrit:
महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः।
भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम्।।
translationEnglish:
O son of Prith, those who are not deluded, the great souls, are under the protection of the divine nature.
They are fully engaged in devotional service because they know Me as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, original and inexhaustible.
translationHindi: परन्तु हे कुन्तीपुत्र! दैवी प्रकृति के आश्रित महात्माजन मुझको सब भूतों का आदि और अविनाशी समझकर अनन्य मन से भजते हैं।
translationGujarati: પરંતુ હે કુંતીપુત્ર! દૈવી પ્રકૃતિના આશ્રિત મહાત્માઓ મને સર્વ ભૂતોના આદિ અને અવિનાશી સમજીને અનન્ય મનથી ભજે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa contrasts the deluded with the great souls (Mahatmas) who, taking shelter of the divine nature, worship Him with single-minded devotion, knowing Him as the imperishable origin.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि महान आत्माएं (महात्मा) दैवीय प्रकृति का आश्रय लेती हैं और उन्हें सबका आदि और अविनाशी जानकर अनन्य भाव से भजती हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ જણાવે છે કે મહાન આત્માઓ (મહાત્મા) દૈવી પ્રકૃતિનો આશ્રય લે છે અને તેમને સૌના આદિ અને અવિનાશી જાણીને અનન્ય ભાવથી ભજે છે.
tweetEnglish: Great souls are under divine protection. They engage in devotion knowing Me as the Supreme Personality.
threadsEnglish: O son of Pritha, those who are not deluded, the great souls, are under the protection of the divine nature. They are fully engaged in devotional service because they know Me as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, original and inexhaustible.
englishTransliteration:
mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha daivīṁ prakṛtim āśritāḥ
bhajanty ananya-manaso jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam
englishWBW: mahā-ātmānaḥ (the great souls) — tu (but) — mām (Me) — pārtha (O son of Pṛthā) — daivīm (divine) — prakṛtim (nature) — āśritāḥ (having taken shelter of) — bhajanti (render service) — ananya-manasaḥ (without deviation of the mind) — jñātvā (knowing) — bhūta (of creation) — ādim (the origin) — avyayam (inexhaustible)
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa contrasts the foolish with the ‘mahātmānas’, the great souls. These souls are not deluded because they have taken shelter in the ‘daivīṁ prakṛtim’, the divine nature or internal energy of the Lord. They are under the protection of God’s own kindness.

They worship Kṛṣṇa with ‘ananya-manaso’, an undivided and unwavering mind. Why? Because they know for certain that He is the ‘bhūtādim avyayam’—the inexhaustible origin of all creation. They don’t waste their time on shadows because they have found the Sun.

A ‘Mahātmā’ is not just a title; it is a state of being. It refers to someone whose heart has expanded enough to include the Divine. Such a person is always peaceful and focused, because they are anchored in the eternal Source. Kṛṣṇa is telling Arjuna that this is the path of true greatness: recognizing our smallness in relation to His vastness and taking shelter there.

sanskrit:
सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः।
नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।।
translationEnglish:
Always chanting My glories, endeavoring with great determination,
bowing down before Me, these great souls perpetually worship Me with devotion.
translationHindi: वे दृढ़निश्चयी भक्त निरन्तर मेरे नाम और गुणों का कीर्तन करते हुए तथा मेरी प्राप्ति के लिए यत्न करते हुए और मुझको बार-बार प्रणाम करते हुए सदा मेरे ध्यान में युक्त होकर अनन्य प्रेम से मेरी उपासना करते हैं।
translationGujarati: તે દ્રઢ નિશ્ચયી ભક્તો નિરંતર મારા નામ અને ગુણોનું કીર્તન કરતા તથા મારી પ્રાપ્તિ માટે પ્રયત્ન કરતા અને મને વારંવાર પ્રણામ કરતા સદાય મારા ધ્યાનમાં જોડાઈને અનન્ય પ્રેમથી મારી ઉપાસના કરે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains how these great souls worship Him: constantly chanting His glories, striving with determination, bowing down, and always engaging in devotion.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि ये महात्मा निरंतर उनका कीर्तन करते हैं, दृढ़ निश्चय के साथ प्रयास करते हैं, उन्हें नमन करते हैं और हमेशा भक्ति में लीन रहते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ જણાવે છે કે આ મહાત્માઓ નિરંતર તેમનું કીર્તન કરે છે, દ્રઢ નિશ્ચય સાથે પ્રયાસ કરે છે, તેમને નમન કરે છે અને હંમેશા ભક્તિમાં લીન રહે છે.
tweetEnglish: Always chanting My glories, endeavoring with determination, bowing down, they worship Me.
threadsEnglish: Always chanting My glories, endeavoring with great determination, bowing down before Me, these great souls perpetually worship Me with devotion.
englishTransliteration:
satataṁ kīrtayanto māṁ yatantaś ca dṛḍha-vratāḥ
namasyantaś ca māṁ bhaktyā nitya-yuktā upāsate
englishWBW: satatam (always) — kīrtayantaḥ (chanting) — mām (about Me) — yatantaḥ (fully endeavoring) — ca (also) — dṛḍha-vratāḥ (with determination) — namasyantaḥ (offering obeisances) — ca (and) — mām (Me) — bhaktyā (in devotion) — nitya-yuktāḥ (perpetually engaged) — upāsate (worship)
englishExplain:
