This verse emphasizes the analytical approach to spirituality. Kṛṣṇa doesn’t want blind faith; He wants Arjuna to logically understand the distinction between the observer and the observed. This clarity is the foundation of mental peace and spiritual stability.

sanskrit:
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक्।
ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः।।
translationEnglish:
That knowledge of the field of activities and of the knower of activities is described by various sages in various Vedic writings.
It is especially presented in the Vedanta-sutra with all reasoning as to cause and effect.
translationHindi: यह क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ का तत्त्व ऋषियों द्वारा बहुत प्रकार से कहा गया है और विविध वेदमन्त्रों द्वारा भी विभागपूर्वक कहा गया है तथा भली-भांति निश्चय किये हुए युक्तियुक्त ब्रह्मसूत्र के पदों द्वारा भी कहा गया है।
translationGujarati: આ ક્ષેત્ર અને ક્ષેત્રજ્ઞનું તત્વ ઋષિઓ દ્વારા અનેક પ્રકારે કહેવાયું છે અને વિવિધ વેદમંત્રો દ્વારા પણ વિભાગપૂર્વક કહેવાયું છે તથા સારી રીતે નિશ્ચય કરેલા યુક્તિયુક્ત બ્રહ્મસૂત્રના પદો દ્વારા પણ કહેવાયું છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa mentions that this truth about the field and its knower has been sung by sages in various Vedic hymns and logically presented in the Vedanta-sutra.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ के इस सत्य को ऋषियों ने वेदों में और ब्रह्मसूत्र में तर्कों के साथ विस्तार से समझाया है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ જણાવે છે કે ક્ષેત્ર અને ક્ષેત્રજ્ઞના આ સત્યને ઋષિઓએ વેદોમાં અને બ્રહ્મસૂત્રમાં તર્કો સાથે વિસ્તારથી સમજાવ્યું છે.
tweetEnglish: That knowledge of the field and knower is described by sages in various Vedic writings.
threadsEnglish: That knowledge of the field of activities and of the knower of activities is described by various sages in various Vedic writings. It is especially presented in Vedanta-sutra with all reasoning as to cause and effect.
englishTransliteration:
ṛṣibhir bahudhā gītaṁ chandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛthak
brahma-sūtra-padaiś caiva hetumadbhir viniścitaiḥ
englishWBW: ṛṣibhiḥ (by the sages) — bahudhā (in many ways) — gītam (sung) — chandobhiḥ (by Vedic hymns) — vividhaiḥ (various) — pṛthak (differently) — brahma-sūtra (the Vedānta-sūtra) — padaiḥ (by the aphorisms) — ca (and) — eva (certainly) — hetu-madbhiḥ (with logic) — viniścitaiḥ (conclusive).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa cites historical and scriptural authorities to validate His teachings. He mentions that the truths about the field and the knower have been sung by many sages in the Vedic hymns and presented with rigorous logic in the Vedānta-sūtra. He is not teaching a new theory, but the timeless truth.

By pointing to the ‘Brahma-sūtra’, Kṛṣṇa highlights the importance of logic (‘Hetu’) in spiritual life. True knowledge is not based on emotion alone; it is ‘Viniścitaiḥ’ or conclusively proven through reasoning. The Gītā is the essence of all these ancient analytical texts.

This verse encourages us to study the foundational texts of spiritual science. It reminds us that we belong to a long lineage of thinkers who have explored the nature of reality. When our personal realizations are aligned with the words of the sages and the logic of the scriptures, our path becomes certain and steady.

sanskrit:
महाभूतान्यहंकारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च।
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः।।
translationEnglish: The five great elements, false ego, intelligence, the unmanifested, the ten senses and the mind, the five sense objects...
translationHindi: पाँच महाभूत, अहंकार, बुद्धि और मूल प्रकृति भी तथा दस इन्द्रियाँ, एक मन और पाँच इन्द्रियों के विषय (शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस, गन्ध)...
translationGujarati: પાંચ મહાભૂત, અહંકાર, બુદ્ધિ અને મૂળ પ્રકૃતિ પણ તથા દસ ઇન્દ્રિયો, એક મન અને પાંચ ઇન્દ્રિયોના વિષય (શબ્દ, સ્પર્શ, રૂપ, રસ, ગંધ)...
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa lists the components of the ‘field’: the five great elements, ego, intellect, the unmanifested nature, the ten senses, the mind, and the five sense objects.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण ‘क्षेत्र’ (शरीर) के घटकों को गिनाते हैं: पाँच महाभूत, अहंकार, बुद्धि, अव्यक्त प्रकृति, दस इंद्रियां, मन और पाँच विषय।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ‘ક્ષેત્ર’ (શરીર) ના ઘટકો ગણાવે છે: પાંચ મહાભૂત, અહંકાર, બુદ્ધિ, અવ્યક્ત પ્રકૃતિ, દસ ઇન્દ્રિયો, મન અને પાંચ વિષયો.
tweetEnglish: The five elements, ego, intelligence, unmanifested, ten senses, mind, and five sense objects...
threadsEnglish: The five great elements, false ego, intelligence, the unmanifested, the ten senses and the mind, the five sense objects, desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the aggregate, the life symptoms, and convictions—all these are considered, in summary, to be the field of activities and its interactions.
englishTransliteration:
mahā-bhūtāny ahaṅkāro buddhir avyaktam eva ca
indriyāṇi daśaikaṁ ca pañca cendriya-gocarāḥ
englishWBW: mahā-bhūtāni (the great elements) — ahaṅkāraḥ (false ego) — buddhiḥ (intelligence) — avyaktam (the unmanifested) — eva (certainly) — ca (and) — indriyāṇi (the senses) — daśa-ekam (eleven) — ca (and) — pañca (five) — ca (and) — indriya-gocarāḥ (the objects of the senses).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa lists the 24 material elements that constitute the ‘Field’ or the body. This list includes the five gross elements (Earth, Water, Fire, Air, Ether), the three subtle elements (Ego, Intellect, Unmanifest nature), the ten senses, the mind, and the five sense objects like sound and touch.

This is a complete breakdown of the human machinery. It shows that even our mind, ego, and intelligence are material products, not the soul itself. We are often confused because we think our thoughts are ‘us’, but Kṛṣṇa categorizes them as part of the field being observed.

By analyzing our body as a set of 24 components, we can achieve a healthy distance from our physical and mental states. We realize that the soul is the 25th element—the conscious observer sitting inside this complex biological robot. This realization is the first step toward true self-realization.

sanskrit:
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं संघातश्चेतना धृतिः।
एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम्।।
translationEnglish: ...desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the aggregate, the life symptoms, and convictions—all these are considered, in summary, to be the field of activities and its interactions.
translationHindi: ...तथा इच्छा, द्वेष, सुख, दुःख, स्थूल देह का पिण्ड, चेतना और धृति - इस प्रकार विकारों सहित यह क्षेत्र संक्षेप में कहा गया है।
translationGujarati: ...તથા ઈચ્છા, દ્વેષ, સુખ, દુઃખ, સ્થૂળ દેહનો પિંડ, ચેતના અને ધૃતિ - આ પ્રકારે વિકારો સહિત આ ક્ષેત્ર સંક્ષેપમાં કહેવાયું છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa concludes the description of the field by adding desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the body, consciousness, and determination as its modifications.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण क्षेत्र के वर्णन को पूरा करते हुए कहते हैं कि इच्छा, द्वेष, सुख-दुख, शरीर, चेतना और धैर्य - ये सब विकारों सहित क्षेत्र ही कहलाते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ ક્ષેત્રના વર્ણનને પૂરું કરતા કહે છે કે ઈચ્છા, દ્વેષ, સુખ-દુઃખ, શરીર, ચેતના અને ધૈર્ય - આ બધા વિકારો સહિત ક્ષેત્ર જ કહેવાય છે.
tweetEnglish: ...desire, hatred, happiness, distress, and convictions—all these are the field and its interactions.
threadsEnglish: The five great elements, false ego, intelligence, the unmanifested, the ten senses and the mind, the five sense objects, desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the aggregate, the life symptoms, and convictions—all these are considered, in summary, to be the field of activities and its interactions.
englishTransliteration:
icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ saṅghātaś cetanā dhṛtiḥ
etat kṣetraṁ samāsena sa-vikāram udāhṛtam
englishWBW: icchā (desire) — dveṣaḥ (hatred) — sukham (happiness) — duḥkham (distress) — saṅghātaḥ (the aggregate/body) — cetanā (consciousness/life symptom) — dhṛtiḥ (determination) — etat (all this) — kṣetram (the field) — samāsena (in summary) — sa-vikāram (with its changes) — udāhṛtam (is described).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa concludes His description of the field by adding our psychological interactions. He includes desire, hatred, pleasure, and pain as part of the material field. Even the determination to stick to a goal is categorized here as a change occurring within the field of matter.

This is a revolutionary psychological insight. Kṛṣṇa is saying that our emotions are not the soul; they are the ‘Vikāras’ or modifications of the material body and mind. The soul is merely the witness of these passing storms of emotion. When you feel sad, it is your mind that is sad, not ‘You’.

Understanding this helps us remain equanimous. We stop being victims of our mood swings once we realize they are just movements in the field. This summary helps us identify exactly where the body ends and where the conscious soul begins, allowing us to find stability in our true identity.

sanskrit:
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम्।
आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः।।
translationEnglish: Humility; pridelessness; nonviolence; tolerance; simplicity; approaching a bona fide spiritual master; cleanliness; steadiness; self-control...
translationHindi: श्रेष्ठता के अभिमान का अभाव, दम्भाचरण का अभाव, किसी भी प्राणी को सताना नहीं, क्षभाव, मन-वाणी आदि की सरलता, श्रद्धा-भक्तिसहित गुरु की सेवा, बाहर-भीतर की शुद्धि, अन्तःकरण की स्थिरता और मन-इन्द्रियों सहित शरीर का निग्रह...
translationGujarati: શ્રેષ્ઠતાના અભિમાનનો અભાવ, દંભી આચરણનો અભાવ, અહિંસા, ક્ષમાભાવ, મન-વાણી વગેરેની સરળતા, શ્રદ્ધા-ભક્તિ સહિત ગુરુની સેવા, બહાર-ભીતરની શુદ્ધિ, અંતઃકરણની સ્થિરતા અને મન-ઇન્દ્રિયો સહિત શરીરનો નિગ્રહ...
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa begins listing the qualities that constitute true knowledge: humility, lack of pride, nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity, service to the guru, cleanliness, steadiness, and self-control.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण सच्चे ज्ञान के लक्षण बताते हैं: विनम्रता, दंभहीनता, अहिंसा, क्षमा, सरलता, गुरु की सेवा, पवित्रता, स्थिरता और आत्म-संयम।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સાચા જ્ઞાનના લક્ષણો જણાવે છે: વિનમ્રતા, દંભહીનતા, અહિંસા, ક્ષમા, સરળતા, ગુરુની સેવા, પવિત્રતા, સ્થિરતા અને આત્મ-સંયમ.
tweetEnglish: Humility, nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity, cleanliness, steadiness, and self-control...
threadsEnglish: Humility; pridelessness; nonviolence; tolerance; simplicity; approaching a bona fide spiritual master; cleanliness; steadiness; self-control; renunciation of the objects of sense gratification; absence of false ego; the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease; detachment...
englishTransliteration:
amānitvam adambhitvam ahiṁsā kṣāntir ārjavam
ācāryopāsanaṁ śaucaṁ sthairyam ātma-vinigrahaḥ
englishWBW: amānitvam (humility) — adambhitvam (pridelessness) — ahiṁsā (nonviolence) — kṣāntiḥ (tolerance) — ārjavam (simplicity) — ācārya-upāsanam (service to the teacher) — śaucam (cleanliness) — sthairyam (steadiness) — ātma-vinigrahaḥ (self-control).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa begins to define true knowledge, but He doesn’t list books or facts. Instead, He lists character traits. Knowledge starts with ‘Amānitvam’ (humility) and ‘Adambhitvam’ (lack of pride). It includes nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity, and service to a bona fide spiritual master.

In the Vedic worldview, a person with a head full of data but a heart full of pride is considered ignorant. Real knowledge is a process of purification. To know the truth, the mirror of the heart must be clean. Traits like cleanliness and self-control are the tools that polish that mirror.

This verse teaches us that spirituality is built on a moral foundation. You cannot reach higher dimensions of consciousness if you are still violent or deceptive. By cultivating these virtues, we align our character with the Divine, making ourselves capable of perceiving the soul that lies beyond the material field.

sanskrit:
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहंकार एव च।
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्।।
translationEnglish: ...renunciation of the objects of sense gratification; absence of false ego; and the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease...
translationHindi: ...इस लोक और परलोक के सम्पूर्ण भोगों में आसक्ति का अभाव और अहंकार का भी अभाव, जन्म, मृत्यु, जरा और रोग आदि में दुःख और दोषों का बार-बार विचार करना...
translationGujarati: ...આ લોક અને પરલોકના તમામ ભોગોમાં આસક્તિનો અભાવ અને અહંકારનો પણ અભાવ, જન્મ, મૃત્યુ, જરા અને રોગ વગેરેમાં દુઃખ અને દોષોનો વારંવાર વિચાર કરવો...
simpleEnglish: ...detachment from sense objects, absence of ego, and understanding the misery inherent in birth, death, old age, and disease...
simpleHindi: ...इंद्रिय विषयों से वैराग्य, अहंकार का अभाव, और जन्म, मृत्यु, बुढ़ापे और बीमारी में छिपे दुखों को बार-बार देखना...
simpleGujarati: ...ઇન્દ્રિય વિષયોથી વૈરાગ્ય, અહંકારનો અભાવ, અને જન્મ, મૃત્યુ, ઘડપણ અને બીમારીમાં છુપાયેલા દુઃખોને વારંવાર જોવા...
tweetEnglish: ...renunciation of sense objects, absence of ego, and perception of the evil of birth and death...
englishTransliteration:
indriyārtheṣu vairāgyam anahaṅkāra eva ca
janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣānudarśanam
englishWBW: indriya-artheṣu (in sense objects) — vairāgyam (detachment) — anahaṅkāraḥ (lack of ego) — eva (certainly) — ca (and) — janma (birth) — mṛtyu (death) — jarā (old age) — vyādhi (disease) — duḥkha (misery) — doṣa (fault) — anudarśanam (observing repeatedly).
englishExplain:
Continuing His definition of knowledge, Kṛṣṇa mentions detachment from sense objects and the absence of false ego. He then introduces a crucial meditation: ‘Anudarśanam’—repeatedly observing the faults in birth, death, old age, and disease. This is spiritual realism.

Most people try to ignore the fact that the body is aging and will eventually die. Kṛṣṇa says that facing this truth is actual knowledge. If we realize the body is a dying machine, our attachment to material things naturally weakens. We stop wasting time on temporary pleasures and start seeking eternal solutions.

Pridelessness and detachment go hand-in-hand. When we lose the ‘False Ego’ that says ‘I am this body’, we no longer feel the need to chase objects for the body’s satisfaction. This clarity allows us to live with purpose, knowing that our true self is untouched by the decay of the physical field.

sanskrit:
असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु।
नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु।।
translationEnglish: ...detachment; freedom from entanglement with children, wife, home and the rest; even-mindedness amid pleasant and unpleasant events...
translationHindi: ...पुत्र, स्त्री, घर और धन आदि में आसक्ति का अभाव, ममता का न होना तथा प्रिय और अप्रिय की प्राप्ति में सदा ही चित्त का सम रहना...
translationGujarati: ...પુત્ર, સ્ત્રી, ઘર અને ધન વગેરેમાં આસક્તિનો અભાવ, મમતાનું ન હોવું તથા પ્રિય અને અપ્રિયની પ્રાપ્તિમાં સદાય ચિત્તનું સમાન રહેવું...
simpleEnglish: ...freedom from attachment to family and home, and maintaining a balanced mind in both desirable and undesirable circumstances...
simpleHindi: ...परिवार और घर में आसक्ति न रखना, और अच्छी या बुरी हर परिस्थिति में मन को समान रखना...
simpleGujarati: ...પરિવાર અને ઘરમાં આસક્તિ ન રાખવી, અને સારી કે ખરાબ દરેક પરિસ્થિતિમાં મનને સમાન રાખવું...
tweetEnglish: ...detachment, freedom from entanglement, and even-mindedness amid pleasant and unpleasant events...
englishTransliteration:
asaktir anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putra-dāra-gṛhādiṣu
nityaṁ ca sama-cittatvam iṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu
englishWBW: asaktiḥ (detachment) — anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ (lack of entanglement) — putra (children) — dāra (wife) — gṛha-ādiṣu (home and so on) — nityam (perpetually) — ca (and) — sama-cittatvam (equanimity) — iṣṭa (desirable) — aniṣṭa (undesirable) — upapattiṣu (upon having attained).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the social and emotional aspect of knowledge. He advises detachment and freedom from excessive entanglement with family and home. He also emphasizes ‘Sama-cittatvam’—maintaining an even mind whether something desirable or undesirable happens.

This doesn’t mean becoming cold or neglecting duties. It means realizing that these relationships are temporary connections between souls in different bodies. If we think our family members ‘belong’ to us, we suffer when they change or leave. If we see them as Kṛṣṇa’s property, we serve them with love but without the pain of attachment.

Being even-minded in success and failure is the hallmark of a wise person. A person in knowledge knows that ‘Good Luck’ and ‘Bad Luck’ are just passing seasons in the material world. By staying centered in the Self, they remain peaceful through the highs and lows of life.

sanskrit:
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी।
विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि।।
translationEnglish: ...constant and unalloyed devotion to Me; aspiring to live in a solitary place; detachment from the general mass of people...
translationHindi: ...मुझ परमेश्वर में अनन्य योग द्वारा अव्यभिचारिणी भक्ति तथा एकान्त और शुद्ध देश में रहने का स्वभाव और विषयी मनुष्यों के समुदाय में प्रेम का न होना...
translationGujarati: ...મારા પરમેશ્વરમાં અનન્ય યોગ દ્વારા અવ્યભિચારિણી ભક્તિ તથા એકાંત અને શુદ્ધ દેશમાં રહેવાનો સ્વભાવ અને વિષયી મનુષ્યોના સમુદાયમાં પ્રેમનું ન હોવું...
simpleEnglish: ...unwavering devotion to Me, living in solitary places, and disinterest in socializing with ordinary people...
simpleHindi: ...मुझमें अटूट भक्ति रखना, एकांत स्थानों में रहना पसंद करना, और सांसारिक लोगों की भीड़भाड़ से दूर रहना...
simpleGujarati: ...મારામાં અટૂટ ભક્તિ રાખવી, એકાંત સ્થાનોમાં રહેવાનું પસંદ કરવું, અને સાંસારિક લોકોની ભીડભાડથી દૂર રહેવું...
tweetEnglish: ...constant devotion to Me, aspiring for solitary places, and detachment from the masses...
englishTransliteration:
mayi cānanya-yogena bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī
vivikta-deśa-sevitvam aratir jana-saṁsadi
englishWBW: mayi (in Me) — ca (and) — ananya-yogena (with unalloyed devotion) — bhaktiḥ (devotional service) — avyabhicāriṇī (without deviation) — vivikta (secluded) — deśa (place) — sevitvam (aspiring for) — aratiḥ (detachment) — jana-saṁsadi (from the masses).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa reveals the most important item of knowledge: unalloyed, unwavering devotion to Him. He also suggests spending time in secluded places and avoiding the ‘Jana-saṁsadi’—the noisy crowds of materialistic people. Solitude and focus are necessary for deep realization.

Knowledge is not dry; it culminates in ‘Bhakti’ or love. Dry philosophy can only take you so far. To cross the finish line of self-realization, you need to connect your heart to the Supreme. ‘Avyabhicāriṇī’ means ‘chaste’ devotion—not mixing spiritual goals with material desires.

Avoiding the masses doesn’t mean hating people; it means protecting your vibration. Materialistic talk can pull your consciousness down into the field of matter. By spending time in ‘Vivikta’ or quiet spaces and focusing on the Divine, you maintain the mental clarity needed to see through the illusions of the world.

sanskrit:
अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम्।
एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा।।
translationEnglish: ...accepting the importance of self-realization; and philosophical search for the Absolute Truth—all this is declared to be knowledge, and besides this whatever there may be is ignorance.
translationHindi: ...अध्यात्मज्ञान में नित्य स्थिति और तत्त्वज्ञान के अर्थरूप परमात्मा को ही देखना - यह सब ‘ज्ञान’ है और जो इससे विपरीत है, वह ‘अज्ञान’ है - ऐसा कहा गया है।
translationGujarati: ...અધ્યાત્મજ્ઞાનમાં નિત્ય સ્થિતિ અને તત્વજ્ઞાનના અર્થરૂપ પરમાત્માને જ જોવા - આ બધું ‘જ્ઞાન’ છે અને જે આનાથી વિપરીત છે, તે ‘અજ્ઞાન’ છે - એવું કહેવાયું છે.
simpleEnglish: ...and constancy in spiritual knowledge and seeing the philosophical goal of truth—this is declared to be true knowledge, and everything else is ignorance.
simpleHindi: ...आध्यात्मिक ज्ञान में स्थित रहना और तत्वज्ञान के लक्ष्य (परमात्मा) को देखना—यही ज्ञान कहा गया है, और इसके अलावा जो कुछ भी है वह अज्ञान है।
simpleGujarati: ...આધ્યાત્મિક જ્ઞાનમાં સ્થિત રહેવું અને તત્વજ્ઞાનના લક્ષ્ય (પરમાત્મા) ને જોવા—આ જ જ્ઞાન કહેવાયું છે, અને આના સિવાય જે કંઈ પણ છે તે અજ્ઞાન છે.
tweetEnglish: ...accepting self-realization and searching for Truth—this I declare to be knowledge; the rest is ignorance.
threadsEnglish: Humility; pridelessness; nonviolence; tolerance; simplicity; approaching a bona fide spiritual master; cleanliness; steadiness; self-control; renunciation of the objects of sense gratification; absence of false ego; the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease; detachment...
englishTransliteration:
adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvaṁ tattva-jñānārtha-darśanam
etaj jñānam iti proktam ajñānaṁ yad ato ’nyathā
englishWBW: adhyātma (spiritual) — jñāna (knowledge) — nityatvam (constancy) — tattva-jñāna (of knowledge of the truth) — artha (object) — darśanam (philosophy) — etat (all this) — jñānam (knowledge) — iti (thus) — proktam (declared) — ajñānam (ignorance) — yat (what) — ataḥ (from this) — anyathā (other).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa concludes His 20-item list of knowledge. He highlights the importance of being constant in spiritual study and keeping the philosophical goal of the Absolute Truth in sight. He then gives a stunning ultimatum: Everything He just listed is knowledge, and anything else is ignorance.

You might have a PhD in science, economics, or politics, but if you lack these 20 qualities (like humility, non-violence, and devotion), Kṛṣṇa considers you ignorant. Material education only teaches you about the ‘Field’. Real education teaches you about the ‘Observer’ and the ‘Creator’.

This verse challenges our definition of success. A truly ‘educated’ person is one who has transformed their character and realized their eternal nature. By following this path, we move from the darkness of ‘A-jñāna’ (ignorance) to the light of truth. This is the only knowledge that can actually save us from the cycle of birth and death.

sanskrit:
ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते।
अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते।।
translationEnglish: I shall now explain the knowable, knowing which you will taste the eternal. Brahman, the spirit, beginningless and subordinate to Me, lies beyond the cause and effect of this material world.
translationHindi: जो जानने योग्य है तथा जिसको जानकर मनुष्य परमानन्द को प्राप्त होता है, उसको भली-भांति कहूँगा। वह अनादिवाला परमब्रह्म न सत् ही कहा जाता है, न असत् ही।
translationGujarati: જે જાણવા યોગ્ય છે તથા જેને જાણીને મનુષ્ય પરમાનંદને પામે છે, તેને સારી રીતે કહીશ. તે અનાદિવાળું પરમબ્રહ્મ ન સત્ જ કહેવાય છે, ન અસત્ જ.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa now describes the object of knowledge (Brahman), knowing which one attains immortality; it is beginningless and beyond both existence and non-existence.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण अब ‘ज्ञेय’ (जानने योग्य ब्रह्म) का वर्णन करते हैं, जिसे जानकर अमरता मिलती है; वह अनादि है और सत् (कार्य) और असत् (कारण) दोनों से परे है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ હવે ‘જ્ઞેય’ (જાણવા યોગ્ય બ્રહ્મ) નું વર્ણન કરે છે, જેને જાણીને અમરતા મળે છે; તે અનાદિ છે અને સત્ (કાર્ય) અને અસત્ (કારણ) બંનેથી પર છે.
tweetEnglish: I shall explain the knowable. Brahman, the spirit, beginningless and subordinate to Me, lies beyond cause.
threadsEnglish: I shall now explain the knowable, knowing which you will taste the eternal. Brahman, the spirit, beginningless and subordinate to Me, lies beyond the cause and effect of this material world.
englishTransliteration:
jñeyaṁ yat tat pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvāmṛtam aśnute
anādi mat-paraṁ brahma na sat tan nāsad ucyate
englishWBW: jñeyam (the knowable) — yat (which) — tat (that) — pravakṣyāmi (I shall now explain) — yat (which) — jñātvā (knowing) — amṛtam (nectar/immortality) — aśnute (one tastes) — anādi (beginningless) — mat-param (subordinate to Me) — brahma (spirit) — na (neither) — sat (cause) — tat (that) — na (nor) — asat (effect) — ucyate (is said to be).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa now moves from the ‘Process of Knowledge’ to the ‘Object of Knowledge’ (Jñeyam). He promises that by knowing this truth, one tastes ‘Amṛta’ or immortality. He introduces the Brahman—the eternal, beginningless spirit that is beyond the categories of cause (Sat) and effect (Asat).

He clarifies that this Brahman is ‘Mat-param’—it rests upon Him. While Brahman is the vast spiritual energy, Kṛṣṇa is the Person who owns that energy. Knowing our identity as Brahman (Spirit) is the first step toward freedom from the fear of death. We realize we are not the changing body but the unchanging light.

This knowledge is the cure for existential anxiety. Once you know that your core is ‘Anādi’ (without beginning), you realize it can also have no end. You move beyond the temporary world of things and enter the eternal world of being. This is the ‘Nectar’ that satiates the thirsty soul.

sanskrit:
सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्।
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति।।
translationEnglish: Everywhere are His hands and legs, His eyes, heads and faces, and He has ears everywhere. In this way the Supersoul exists, pervading everything.
translationHindi: वह सब ओर हाथ-पैर वाला, सब ओर नेत्र, सिर और मुख वाला तथा सब ओर कान वाला है; क्योंकि वह संसार में सबको व्याप्त करके स्थित है।
translationGujarati: તે ચારે બાજુ હાથ-પગવાળું, ચારે બાજુ નેત્ર, શિર અને મુખવાળું તથા ચારે બાજુ કાનવાળું છે; કારણ કે તે સંસારમાં બધાને વ્યાપ્ત કરીને સ્થિત છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that this Supreme Truth has hands, feet, eyes, heads, faces, and ears everywhere, pervading the entire universe.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि उस परमात्मा के हाथ, पैर, आँखें, सिर, मुख और कान हर जगह हैं, और वह पूरे संसार को व्याप्त करके स्थित है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ જણાવે છે કે તે પરમાત્માના હાથ, પગ, આંખો, માથા, મુખ અને કાન દરેક જગ્યાએ છે, અને તે પૂરા સંસારને વ્યાપ્ત કરીને સ્થિત છે.
tweetEnglish: Everywhere are His hands, legs, eyes, and heads. In this way the Supersoul pervades everything.
threadsEnglish: Everywhere are His hands and legs, His eyes, heads and faces, and He has ears everywhere. In this way the Supersoul exists, pervading everything.
englishTransliteration:
sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṁ tat sarvato ’kṣi-śiro-mukham
sarvataḥ śrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
englishWBW: sarvataḥ (everywhere) — pāṇi-pādam (hands and legs) — tat (that) — sarvataḥ (everywhere) — akṣi (eyes) — śiraḥ (heads) — mukham (faces) — sarvataḥ (everywhere) — śrutimat (ears) — loke (in the world) — sarvam (everything) — āvṛtya (pervading) — tiṣṭhati (exists).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the all-pervading nature of the Supersoul (Paramātmā). He says the Lord has hands, feet, eyes, and ears everywhere. This is a poetic way of saying that God is omnipresent and omniscient. There is no corner of the universe where He is not watching or acting.

This verse personifies the concept of presence. How does God hear our prayers? Because His ears are right there with us. How does He sustain the world? Because His hands are everywhere. He is not a distant, localized king; He is the living fabric of reality that ‘Āvṛtya’ (covers) and sustains everything.

For a seeker, this is deeply reassuring. It means we are never truly alone or unnoticed. Every thought we have and every act we perform is witnessed by the Supreme Friend. This realization helps us live more mindfully and with a sense of constant connection to the Divine.

sanskrit:
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम्।
असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च।।
translationEnglish: The Supersoul is the original source of all senses, yet He is without senses. He is unattached, although He is the maintainer of all living beings. He transcends the modes of nature, and at the same time He is the master of all the modes.
translationHindi: वह सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियों के विषयों को जानने वाला है, परन्तु वास्तव में सब इन्द्रियों से रहित है तथा आसक्तिरहित होने पर भी सबका धारण-पोषण करने वाला और निर्गुण होने पर भी गुणों को भोगने वाला है।
translationGujarati: તે સંપૂર્ણ ઇન્દ્રિયોના વિષયોને જાણનારું છે, પરંતુ વાસ્તવમાં બધી ઇન્દ્રિયોથી રહિત છે તથા આસક્તિરહિત હોવા છતાં સૌનું ધારણ-પોષણ કરનારું અને નિર્ગુણ હોવા છતાં ગુણોને ભોગવનારું છે.
simpleEnglish: Although He perceives all sense objects, He is without senses; He is unattached yet maintains all; He is beyond the modes of nature yet experiences them.
simpleHindi: यद्यपि वह सभी इंद्रियों के विषयों को जानता है, फिर भी वह इंद्रियों से रहित है; वह अनासक्त है फिर भी सबका पालनहार है; वह गुणों से परे है फिर भी उनका भोक्ता है।
simpleGujarati: જોકે તે બધી ઇન્દ્રિયોના વિષયોને જાણે છે, છતાં તે ઇન્દ્રિયોથી રહિત છે; તે અનાસક્ત છે છતાં સૌનો પાલનહાર છે; તે ગુણોથી પર છે છતાં તેમનો ભોક્તા છે.
tweetEnglish: The Supersoul is the source of senses yet without them. He is unattached but maintains all beings.
threadsEnglish: The Supersoul is the original source of all senses, yet He is without senses. He is unattached, although He is the maintainer of all living beings. He transcends the modes of nature, and at the same time He is the master of all the modes of material nature.
englishTransliteration:
sarvendriya-guṇābhāsaṁ sarvendriya-vivarjitam
asaktaṁ sarva-bhṛc caiva nirguṇaṁ guṇa-bhoktṛ ca
englishWBW: sarva (all) — indriya (senses) — guṇa (qualities) — ābhāsam (the original source) — sarva (all) — indriya (senses) — vivarjitam (without) — asaktam (unattached) — sarva-bhṛt (the maintainer of everyone) — ca (and) — eva (certainly) — nirguṇam (without material modes) — guṇa-bhoktṛ (the master of the modes) — ca (and).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa presents a series of divine paradoxes. The Supersoul is the source of all senses, yet He has no material senses. He is unattached, yet He maintains all beings. He is beyond the three modes of nature (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas), yet He is the ultimate ‘Bhoktṛ’ or enjoyer of those modes.

This explains the difference between God and the human soul. We are controlled by our senses and the modes of nature. Kṛṣṇa, however, is the Master of the senses. He can perceive everything without needing a physical retina or an eardrum. His perception is transcendental and immediate.

By calling Him ‘Sarva-bhṛt’ (the maintainer of all), Kṛṣṇa reminds us that our survival depends on His energy. He provides the air, the water, and the gravity that keeps us alive, yet He remains ‘Asaktam’ (unattached), never becoming entangled in the world He sustains. He is the independent source of all dependent beings.

sanskrit:
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च।
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत्।।
translationEnglish: The Supreme Truth exists outside and inside of all living beings, the moving and the nonmoving. Because He is subtle, He is beyond the power of the material senses to see or to know. Although far, far away, He is also near to all.
translationHindi: वह चराचर सब भूतों के बाहर-भीतर परिपूर्ण है और चर-अचर भी वही है। और वह सूक्ष्म होने से अविज्ञेय है तथा अति समीप में और दूर में भी वही स्थित है।
translationGujarati: તે ચરાચર બધા ભૂતોની બહાર-ભીતર પરિપૂર્ણ છે અને ચર-અચર પણ તે જ છે. અને તે સૂક્ષ્મ હોવાથી અવિજ્ઞેય છે તથા અતિ નજીકમાં અને દૂર પણ તે જ સ્થિત છે.
simpleEnglish: The Supreme is inside and outside all beings, moving and non-moving; being subtle, He is incomprehensible; He is both very far and very near.
simpleHindi: वह परमात्मा सभी प्राणियों के भीतर और बाहर है, चर और अचर भी वही है; सूक्ष्म होने के कारण उसे जाना नहीं जा सकता, और वह बहुत दूर होते हुए भी सबके पास है।
simpleGujarati: તે પરમાત્મા બધા પ્રાણીઓની ભીતર અને બહાર છે, ચર અને અચર પણ તે જ છે; સૂક્ષ્મ હોવાના કારણે તેને જાણી શકાતો નથી, અને તે બહુ દૂર હોવા છતાં બધાની પાસે છે.
tweetEnglish: The Supreme Truth exists outside and inside all beings. He is subtle and beyond material senses.
threadsEnglish: The Supreme Truth exists outside and inside of all living beings, the moving and the nonmoving. Because He is subtle, He is beyond the power of the material senses to see or to know. Although far, far away, He is also near to all.
englishTransliteration:
bahir antaś ca bhūtānām acaraṁ caram eva ca
sūkṣmatvāt tad avijñeyaṁ dūra-sthaṁ cāntike ca tat
englishWBW: bahiḥ (outside) — antaḥ (inside) — ca (and) — bhūtānām (of all living beings) — acaram (not moving) — caram (moving) — eva (certainly) — ca (and) — sūkṣmatvāt (due to being subtle) — tat (that) — avijñeyam (incomprehensible) — dūra-stham (far away) — ca (and) — antike (near) — ca (and) — tat (that).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains that the Supreme Truth is simultaneously inside and outside all beings. He is both the stationary and the moving. Because He is ‘Sūkṣma’ or incredibly subtle, He is incomprehensible to material senses. He is the furthest star and the nearest heartbeat.

This verse destroys the idea that God is ‘only’ in heaven or ‘only’ in the heart. He is both localized and infinite. To the materialist who relies only on logic, God is ‘Dūra-stham’—unreachably far. But to the devotee, He is ‘Antike’—closer than one’s own breath.

Understanding the ‘subtlety’ of God means realizing that He cannot be found through physical instruments like telescopes or microscopes. He is found through the refinement of consciousness. He is the silent space between atoms and the vast expanse of the cosmos, pervading every layer of existence.

sanskrit:
अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्।
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च।।
translationEnglish: Although the Supersoul appears to be divided among all beings, He is never divided. He is situated as one. Although He is the maintainer of every living entity, it is to be understood that He devours and develops all.
translationHindi: वह परमात्मा विभागरहित एक रूप से आकाश के सदृश परिपूर्ण होने पर भी चराचर सम्पूर्ण भूतों में विभक्त-सा स्थित प्रतीत होता है तथा वह जानने योग्य परमात्मा विष्णुरूप से भूतों को धारण-पोषण करने वाला और रुद्ररूप से संहार करने वाला तथा ब्रह्मारूप से सबको उत्पन्न करने वाला है।
translationGujarati: તે પરમાત્મા વિભાગરહિત એક રૂપથી આકાશની જેમ પરિપૂર્ણ હોવા છતાં ચરાચર સંપૂર્ણ ભૂતોમાં વિભક્ત જેવો સ્થિત પ્રતીત થાય છે તથા તે જાણવા યોગ્ય પરમાત્મા વિષ્ણુરૂપથી ભૂતોનું ધારણ-પોષણ કરનારો અને રુદ્રરૂપથી સંહાર કરનારો તથા બ્રહ્મારૂપથી સૌને ઉત્પન્ન કરનારો છે.
simpleEnglish: Although undivided, He appears divided among beings; He maintains, creates, and destroys all living entities.
simpleHindi: यद्यपि वह अखंड है, फिर भी वह प्राणियों में बंटा हुआ सा लगता है; वही सबका पालनहार, सृजनहार और संहारक है।
simpleGujarati: જોકે તે અખંડ છે, છતાં તે પ્રાણીઓમાં વહેંચાયેલો હોય તેવો લાગે છે; તે જ સૌનો પાલનહાર, સર્જનહાર અને સંહારક છે.
tweetEnglish: Although appearing divided, He is never divided. He maintains, devours, and develops all.
threadsEnglish: Although the Supersoul appears to be divided among all beings, He is never divided. He is situated as one. Although He is the maintainer of every living entity, it is to be understood that He devours and develops all.
englishTransliteration:
avibhaktaṁ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktam iva ca स्थितम्
bhūta-bhartṛ ca taj jñeyaṁ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca
englishWBW: avibhaktam (undivided) — ca (and) — bhūteṣu (in all beings) — vibhaktam (divided) — iva (as if) — ca (and) — sthitam (situated) — bhūta-bhartṛ (the maintainer of all beings) — ca (and) — tat (that) — jñeyam (to be known) — grasiṣṇu (devouring) — prabhaviṣṇu (developing) — ca (and).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the Unity of God. Although the Supersoul appears divided because He is present in millions of different bodies, He is actually ‘Avibhaktam’—undivided and one. He is the maintainer of all beings, the one who devours all at death, and the one who creates all at birth.

Imagine the sun reflecting in millions of different water pots. It looks like there are millions of suns, but there is only one. Similarly, the Lord is one, but He manifests in every heart. This verse identifies Him as the ‘Bhūta-bhartṛ’—the one who carries the burden of the entire creation.

He is the source (Prabhaviṣṇu) and the end (Grasiṣṇu). This cyclical nature of creation and destruction is all handled by the one Supreme Person. By knowing this, we stop being distracted by the ‘Many’ and start focusing on the ‘One’ who underlies all variety in the universe.

sanskrit:
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्।।
translationEnglish: He is the source of light in all luminous objects. He is beyond the darkness of matter and is unmanifested. He is knowledge, He is the object of knowledge, and He is the goal of knowledge. He is situated in everyone’s heart.
translationHindi: वह परब्रह्म ज्योतियों का भी ज्योति और माया से अत्यन्त परे कहा जाता है। वह परमात्मा बोधस्वरूप, जानने योग्य और तत्त्वज्ञान से प्राप्त करने योग्य है और सबके हृदय में विशेष रूप से स्थित है।
translationGujarati: તે પરબ્રહ્મ જ્યોતિઓનો પણ જ્યોતિ અને માયાથી અત્યંત પર કહેવાય છે. તે પરમાત્મા બોધસ્વરૂપ, જાણવા યોગ્ય અને તત્વજ્ઞાનથી પ્રાપ્ત કરવા યોગ્ય છે અને સૌના હૃદયમાં વિશેષ રૂપે સ્થિત છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa describes Him as the Light of lights, beyond darkness; He is knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the goal of knowledge, dwelling in every heart.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि वह ज्योतियों की भी ज्योति है और अंधकार से परे है; वह ज्ञान है, जानने योग्य है, और ज्ञान का लक्ष्य है, जो सबके हृदय में विराजमान है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે તે જ્યોતિઓનો પણ જ્યોતિ છે અને અંધકારથી પર છે; તે જ્ઞાન છે, જાણવા યોગ્ય છે, અને જ્ઞાનનું લક્ષ્ય છે, જે સૌના હૃદયમાં બિરાજમાન છે.
tweetEnglish: He is the source of light, beyond darkness. He is knowledge and the goal of knowledge.
threadsEnglish: He is the source of light in all luminous objects. He is beyond the darkness of matter and is unmanifested. He is knowledge, He is the object of knowledge, and He is the goal of knowledge. He is situated in everyone’s heart.
englishTransliteration:
jyotiṣām api taj jyotis tamasaḥ param ucyate
jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ jñāna-gamyaṁ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam
englishWBW: jyotiṣām (in all luminous objects) — api (also) — tat (that) — jyotiḥ (the light) — tamasaḥ (of darkness) — param (beyond) — ucyate (is said to be) — jñānam (knowledge) — jñeyam (the object of knowledge) — jñāna-gamyam (the goal of knowledge) — hṛdi (in the heart) — sarvasya (of everyone) — viṣṭhitam (situated).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa identifies the Supersoul as the ‘Light of all lights’. He is beyond all darkness (‘Tamasaḥ param’). He is simultaneously the Knowledge, the Object being studied, and the Goal of that study. And this magnificent being is localized right in your heart.

The sun, the stars, and even electricity get their power to illuminate from Him. But He is also the internal light that allows the intellect to function. He is the ultimate ‘Subject’ of our life’s journey. Everything we learn is ultimately an attempt to find this source.

This verse is incredibly intimate. The cosmic force that powers the galaxies is the same force sitting in your heart, waiting for you to turn toward Him. He is not just a concept to be analyzed; He is the very destination of all our searching. He is the light that makes seeing possible.

sanskrit:
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः।
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते।।
translationEnglish: Thus the field of activities [the body], knowledge and the knowable have been briefly described by Me. Only My devotees can understand this thoroughly and thus attain to My nature.
translationHindi: इस प्रकार क्षेत्र, ज्ञान और ज्ञेय का स्वरूप संक्षेप में कहा गया; मेरा भक्त इसको तत्त्व से जानकर मेरे स्वरूप को प्राप्त होता है।
translationGujarati: આ રીતે ક્ષેત્ર, જ્ઞાન અને જ્ઞેયનું સ્વરૂપ સંક્ષેપમાં કહેવાયું; મારો ભક્ત આને તત્વથી જાણીને મારા સ્વરૂપને પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa summarizes that He has briefly described the field, knowledge, and the object of knowledge; understanding this, His devotee attains His nature.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण सारांश में कहते हैं कि उन्होंने क्षेत्र, ज्ञान और ज्ञेय का वर्णन कर दिया है; इसे जानकर उनका भक्त उनके स्वरूप को प्राप्त कर लेता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સારાંશમાં કહે છે કે તેમણે ક્ષેત્ર, જ્ઞાન અને જ્ઞેયનું વર્ણન કરી દીધું છે; આ જાણીને તેમનો ભક્ત તેમના સ્વરૂપને પ્રાપ્ત કરી લે છે.
tweetEnglish: Thus the field, knowledge, and knowable have been described. My devotees understand this.
threadsEnglish: Thus the field of activities [the body], knowledge and the knowable have been summarily described by Me. Only My devotees can understand this thoroughly and thus attain to My nature.
englishTransliteration:
iti kṣetraṁ tathā jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ coktaṁ samāsataḥ
mad-bhakta etad vijñāya mad-bhāvāyopapadyate
englishWBW: iti (thus) — kṣetram (the field) — tathā (also) — jñānam (knowledge) — jñeyam (the knowable) — ca (and) — uktam (described) — samāsataḥ (in summary) — mat-bhaktaḥ (My devotee) — etat (all this) — vijñāya (understanding) — mat-bhāvāya (to My nature) — upapadyate (attains).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa summarizes this section of the chapter. He has described the body (Field), the process of character building (Knowledge), and the Supersoul (the Knowable). He now gives the qualification for mastering this: being a ‘Mad-bhakta’—His devotee.

Only a devotee can truly ‘Vijñāya’ or understand these truths. To others, they might seem like dry philosophy. But to one who loves God, these truths become a living experience. This understanding leads the soul to ‘Mad-bhāvāya’—attaining the same transcendental nature as the Lord.

This verse emphasizes that intellectual brilliance is not enough. To truly grasp the science of consciousness, one needs a heart full of devotion. The devotee realizes that the body is just a tool, the world is a stage, and the Lord is the ultimate goal, leading to an eternal life of bliss.

sanskrit:
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि।
विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान्।।
translationEnglish: Material nature and the living entities should be understood to be beginningless. Their transformations and the modes of matter are products of material nature.
translationHindi: प्रकृति और पुरुष - इन दोनों को ही तू अनादि जान और राग-द्वेषादि विकारों को तथा त्रिगुणात्मक सम्पूर्ण पदार्थों को भी प्रकृति से ही उत्पन्न हुए जान।
translationGujarati: પ્રકૃતિ અને પુરુષ - આ બંનેને જ તું અનાદિ જાણ અને રાગ-દ્વેષાદિ વિકારોને તથા ત્રિગુણાત્મક સંપૂર્ણ પદાર્થોને પણ પ્રકૃતિથી જ ઉત્પન્ન થયેલા જાણ.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa states that both material nature (Prakṛti) and the living entity (Puruṣa) are beginningless, and all changes and qualities arise from nature.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि प्रकृति और पुरुष दोनों ही अनादि हैं, और सभी विकार और गुण प्रकृति से ही उत्पन्न होते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે પ્રકૃતિ અને પુરુષ બંને જ અનાદિ છે, અને બધા વિકાર અને ગુણ પ્રકૃતિથી જ ઉત્પન્ન થાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Material nature and living entities are beginningless. Their transformations are products of nature.
threadsEnglish: Material nature and the living entities should be understood to be beginningless. Their transformations and the modes of matter are products of material nature.
englishTransliteration:
prakṛtiṁ puruṣaṁ caiva viddhy anādī ubhāv api
vikārāṁś ca guṇāṁś caiva viddhi prakṛti-sambhavān
englishWBW: prakṛtim (material nature) — puruṣam (the living entities) — ca (and) — eva (certainly) — viddhi (know) — anādī (beginningless) — ubhau (both) — api (also) — vikārān (transformations) — ca (and) — guṇān (the modes of nature) — ca (and) — eva (certainly) — viddhi (know) — prakṛti (material nature) — sambhavān (produced of).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa clarifies the origin of the two players in this world: Matter (Prakṛti) and the Soul (Puruṣa). He explains that both are beginningless (‘Anādī’) because they are eternal energies of God. However, the changes we see—like aging or changing emotions—are strictly products of Matter, not the Soul.

The soul is like a passenger in a car. The car may get dented, painted, or broken down (Vikāras), but the passenger remains the same. Our bodies and our moods are generated by the three modes of nature. We often mistakenly think we are changing, but it is only our material container that is in flux.

By understanding that both nature and the soul are eternal, we lose the fear of non-existence. We realize that our core self is an ancient traveler who has merely picked up a temporary set of habits and features from the material world. This knowledge helps us identify with our eternal essence rather than our temporary traits.

sanskrit:
कार्यकरणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते।
पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते।।
translationEnglish: Nature is said to be the cause of all material causes and effects, whereas the living entity is the cause of the various sufferings and enjoyments in this world.
translationHindi: कार्य (आकाश-वायु आदि) और करण (इन्द्रियादि) के पैदा करने में प्रकृति हेतु कही जाती है और जीवात्मा सुख-दुःखों के भोक्तापन में अर्थात भोगने में हेतु कहा जाता है।
translationGujarati: કાર્ય (આકાશ-વાયુ વગેરે) અને કરણ (ઇન્દ્રિયો વગેરે) ને પેદા કરવામાં પ્રકૃતિ કારણ કહેવાય છે અને જીવાત્મા સુખ-દુઃખોના ભોક્તાપણામાં અર્થાત ભોગવવામાં કારણ કહેવાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Nature is the cause of the body and senses, while the living entity (Puruṣa) is the cause of experiencing happiness and distress.
simpleHindi: प्रकृति शरीर और इंद्रियों के निर्माण का कारण है, जबकि पुरुष (जीवात्मा) सुख और दुख के भोग का कारण है।
simpleGujarati: પ્રકૃતિ શરીર અને ઇન્દ્રિયોના નિર્માણનું કારણ છે, જ્યારે પુરુષ (જીવાત્મા) સુખ અને દુઃખના ભોગનું કારણ છે.
tweetEnglish: Nature is the cause of material effects; the living entity is the cause of sufferings and enjoyments.
threadsEnglish: Nature is said to be the cause of all material causes and effects, whereas the living entity is the cause of the various sufferings and enjoyments in this world.
englishTransliteration:
kārya-kāraṇa-kartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtir ucyate
puruṣaḥ sukha-duḥkhānāṁ bhoktṛtve hetur ucyate
englishWBW: kārya (effect) — kāraṇa (cause) — kartṛtve (in the matter of creation) — hetuḥ (the cause) — prakṛtiḥ (material nature) — ucyate (is said to be) — puruṣaḥ (the living entity) — sukha (of happiness) — duḥkhānām (and distress) — bhoktṛtve (in the matter of enjoyment/suffering) — hetuḥ (the cause) — ucyate (is said to be).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa defines the roles of matter and spirit. Nature (Prakṛti) is the cause of all physical activities, causes, and effects. It provides the machinery. The living entity (Puruṣa) is the cause of the experience—the feeling of happiness and distress. Nature builds the roller coaster; the soul feels the thrill or the fear.

This verse explains why we feel responsible for our lives. While our bodies act according to the laws of physics and biology, our experience of those actions belongs to us. We are the ‘Bhoktṛ’ or the enjoyers and sufferers of our situation. We provide the desire, and nature provides the facility.

Understanding this distinction helps us stop blaming God or others for our suffering. We realize that while the body follows material laws, our internal state is our own responsibility. By changing our consciousness, we can change our experience of the world, even if the material ‘machinery’ remains the same.

sanskrit:
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान्।
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु।।
translationEnglish: The living entity in material nature thus follows the ways of life, enjoying the three modes of nature. This is due to his association with that material nature. Thus he meets with good and evil among various species.
translationHindi: प्रकृति में स्थित हुआ ही पुरुष प्रकृति से उत्पन्न त्रिगुणात्मक पदार्थों को भोगता है और इन गुणों का संग ही इस जीवात्मा के अच्छी-बुरी योनियों में जन्म लेने का कारण है।
translationGujarati: પ્રકૃતિમાં સ્થિત થયેલો જ પુરુષ પ્રકૃતિથી ઉત્પન્ન ત્રિગુણાત્મક પદાર્થોને ભોગવે છે અને આ ગુણોનો સંગ જ આ જીવાત્માના સારી-ખરાબ યોનિઓમાં જન્મ લેવાનું કારણ છે.
simpleEnglish: The living entity dwelling in nature enjoys the modes of nature; attachment to these modes is the cause of its birth in good or bad wombs.
simpleHindi: प्रकृति में स्थित जीवात्मा प्रकृति के गुणों को भोगता है; इन गुणों के साथ उसका लगाव ही उसके अच्छे या बुरे जन्म का कारण बनता है।
simpleGujarati: પ્રકૃતિમાં સ્થિત જીવાત્મા પ્રકૃતિના ગુણોને ભોગવે છે; આ ગુણો સાથે તેનો લગાવ જ તેના સારા કે ખરાબ જન્મનું કારણ બને છે.
tweetEnglish: The living entity follows the ways of life, enjoying the three modes. Thus he meets good and evil.
threadsEnglish: The living entity in material nature thus follows the ways of life, enjoying the three modes of nature. This is due to his association with that material nature. Thus he meets with good and evil among various species.
englishTransliteration:
puruṣaḥ prakṛti-stho hi bhuṅkte prakṛti-jān guṇān
kāraṇaṁ guṇa-saṅgo ’sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu
englishWBW: puruṣaḥ (the living entity) — prakṛti-sthaḥ (situated in the material energy) — hi (certainly) — bhuṅkte (enjoys) — prakṛti-jān (produced by material nature) — guṇān (the modes of nature) — kāraṇam (the cause) — guṇa-saṅgaḥ (the association with the modes) — asya (of his) — sat-asat (good and bad) — yoni (wombs) — janmasu (in births).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains the mechanism of rebirth. He says the soul, situated in material nature, tries to enjoy the modes (Goodness, Passion, Ignorance). It is this ‘Guṇa-saṅga’ or association with these modes that determines whether the soul will take its next birth in a ‘good’ or ‘bad’ species.

Our attachments act like a magnetic force. If we associate with ignorance (drugs, laziness), we develop the consciousness of a lower animal and nature provides a matching body. If we associate with goodness (knowledge, kindness), we rise to higher forms. We are the architects of our own future bodies through our current attachments.

This verse is a call to mindfulness. It reminds us that our daily choices—what we watch, what we eat, how we think—are not just passing moments. they are building the ‘vibe’ that will pull us into our next life. To break the cycle, we must stop trying to ‘enjoy’ the material modes and instead seek the spirit.

sanskrit:
उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः।
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः।।
translationEnglish: Yet in this body there is another, a transcendental enjoyer, who is the Lord, the supreme proprietor, who exists as the overseer and permitter, and who is known as the Supersoul.
translationHindi: इस देह में स्थित यह आत्मा वास्तव में परमात्मा ही है। वह साक्षी होने से उपद्रष्टा और यथार्थ सम्मति देने वाला होने से अनुमन्ता, सबका धारण-पोषण करने वाला होने से भर्ता, जीवरूप से भोक्ता, ब्रह्मादि का भी स्वामी होने से महेश्वर और शुद्ध सच्चिदानन्दघन होने से परमात्मा - ऐसा कहा गया है।
translationGujarati: આ દેહમાં સ્થિત આ આત્મા વાસ્તવમાં પરમાત્મા જ છે. તે સાક્ષી હોવાથી ઉપદ્રષ્ટા અને યથાર્થ સંમતિ આપનારો હોવાથી અનુમંતા, સૌનું ધારણ-પોષણ કરનારો હોવાથી ભર્તા, જીવરૂપથી ભોક્તા, બ્રહ્માદિનો પણ સ્વામી હોવાથી મહેશ્વર અને શુદ્ધ સચ્ચિદાનંદઘન હોવાથી પરમાત્મા - એમ કહેવાયો છે.
simpleEnglish: Within the body, there is also the Supreme Puruṣa (Supersoul), who acts as the overseer, permitter, supporter, enjoyer, and the Supreme Lord.
simpleHindi: इस शरीर में एक परम पुरुष भी है, जिसे परमात्मा कहा जाता है; वह साक्षी, अनुमति देने वाला, पालनहार, भोक्ता और महान ईश्वर है।
simpleGujarati: આ શરીરમાં એક પરમ પુરુષ પણ છે, જેને પરમાત્મા કહેવાય છે; તે સાક્ષી, અનુમતિ આપનારો, પાલનહાર, ભોક્તા અને મહાન ઈશ્વર છે.
tweetEnglish: Yet in this body there is a transcendental enjoyer, the Lord, the supreme proprietor and overseer.
threadsEnglish: Yet in this body there is another, a transcendental enjoyer, who is the Lord, the supreme proprietor, who exists as the overseer and permitter, and who is known as the Supersoul.
englishTransliteration:
upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ
paramātmeti cāpy ukto dehe ’smin puruṣaḥ paraḥ
englishWBW: upadraṣṭā (overseer) — anumantā (permitter) — ca (and) — bhartā (supporter) — bhoktā (enjoyer) — mahā-īśvaraḥ (the supreme lord) — parama-ātmā (the Supersoul) — iti (thus) — ca (also) — api (also) — uktaḥ (is said) — dehe (in the body) — asmin (this) — puruṣaḥ (personality) — paraḥ (transcendental).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa defines the Supersoul (Paramātmā) residing within us. He is the ‘Upadraṣṭā’—the Overseer who witnesses everything we do. He is the ‘Anumantā’—the Permitter who sanctions our desires. Without His silent approval, we cannot even move a finger. He is the ultimate Master within the body.

While the individual soul tries to be the enjoyer, the Supersoul is the true ‘Bhoktā’ and ‘Maheśvara’. He supports our existence from within, providing the intelligence and memory we need to function. He is our closest friend, waiting for us to stop trying to play ‘God’ and start recognizing His presence.

This realization brings great humility. We see that we are not the masters of our own bodies. We are guests in a house owned by the Lord. By aligning our will with the ‘Permitter’ in our heart, we stop struggling against destiny and find a flow of grace in our lives.

sanskrit:
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह।
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते।।
translationEnglish: One who understands this philosophy concerning the material nature, the living entity and the interaction of the modes of nature is sure to attain liberation. He will not take birth here again, regardless of his present position.
translationHindi: इस प्रकार पुरुष को और गुणों के सहित प्रकृति को जो मनुष्य तत्त्व से जानता है, वह सब प्रकार से कर्तव्यकर्म करता हुआ भी फिर नहीं जन्मता।
translationGujarati: આ રીતે પુરુષને અને ગુણો સહિત પ્રકૃતિને જે મનુષ્ય તત્વથી જાણે છે, તે સર્વ પ્રકારે કર્તવ્યકર્મ કરતો હોવા છતાં ફરી નથી જન્મતો.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa guarantees that one who truly understands the difference between the soul (Puruṣa) and nature (Prakṛti) with its modes will not be reborn, no matter their lifestyle.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जो व्यक्ति पुरुष (आत्मा) और प्रकृति (गुणों सहित) को इस प्रकार जान लेता है, उसका पुनर्जन्म नहीं होता, चाहे वह किसी भी स्थिति में क्यों न हो।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે જે વ્યક્તિ પુરુષ (આત્મા) અને પ્રકૃતિ (ગુણો સહિત) ને આ રીતે જાણી લે છે, તેનો પુનર્જન્મ નથી થતો, ભલે તે કોઈપણ સ્થિતિમાં કેમ ન હોય.
tweetEnglish: One who understands nature, the living entity, and the modes will not take birth again.
threadsEnglish: One who understands this philosophy concerning material nature, the living entity and the interaction of the modes of nature is sure to attain liberation. He will not take birth here again, regardless of his present position.
englishTransliteration:
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecid ātmānam ātmanā
anye sāṅkhyena yogena karma-yogena cāpare
englishWBW: dhyānena (by meditation) — ātmani (in the self) — paśyanti (see) — kecit (some) — ātmānam (the Supersoul) — ātmanā (by the mind) — anye (others) — sāṅkhyena (by analytical study) — yogena (by the yoga) — karma-yogena (by the yoga of work) — ca (and) — apare (others).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa acknowledges that different people have different temperaments, so He offers three paths to realize the Supersoul within. Some find the Divine through ‘Dhyāna’ or silent meditation, turning the mind inward. Others use ‘Sāṅkhya’—the analytical study of matter and spirit—to logically deduce the presence of God. Still others find Him through ‘Karma-yoga’—selfless service.

This shows the incredible inclusivity of the Bhagavad Gītā. God is not restricted to one method of discovery. If you are an introvert, you may prefer meditation. If you are an intellectual, you may prefer philosophy. If you are an active person, you may prefer service. All these paths converge at the same point: the vision of the Self.

By saying ‘Paśyanti’ (they see), Kṛṣṇa confirms that these are practical techniques that produce a result. Realization is not a matter of luck; it is a matter of choosing a method that fits your ‘Svabhāva’ (nature) and practicing it with sincerity. The Lord is waiting to be discovered at the end of every legitimate spiritual road.

sanskrit:
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना।
अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे।।
translationEnglish: Some perceive the Supersoul within themselves through meditation, others through the cultivation of knowledge, and still others through working without fruitive desires.
translationHindi: उस परमात्मा को कितने ही मनुष्य तो शुद्ध हुई सूक्ष्म बुद्धि से ध्यान द्वारा हृदय में देखते हैं; अन्य कितने ही ज्ञानयोग द्वारा और दूसरे कितने ही कर्मयोग द्वारा देखते हैं।
translationGujarati: તે પરમાત્માને કેટલાય મનુષ્યો તો શુદ્ધ થયેલી સૂક્ષ્મ બુદ્ધિથી ધ્યાન દ્વારા હૃદયમાં જુએ છે; અન્ય કેટલાય જ્ઞાનયોગ દ્વારા અને બીજા કેટલાય કર્મયોગ દ્વારા જુએ છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that some realize the Self within through meditation, others through the path of knowledge, and others through the path of selfless action.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि कुछ लोग ध्यान के माध्यम से, कुछ ज्ञान योग के माध्यम से और कुछ कर्म योग के माध्यम से परमात्मा को अपने भीतर देखते हैं।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ જણાવે છે કે કેટલાક લોકો ધ્યાનના માધ્યમથી, કેટલાક જ્ઞાન યોગના માધ્યમથી અને કેટલાક કર્મ યોગના માધ્યમથી પરમાત્માને પોતાની ભીતર જુએ છે.
tweetEnglish: Some perceive the Supersoul by meditation, others by knowledge, and others by working without fruit.
threadsEnglish: Some perceive the Supersoul within themselves through meditation, others through the cultivation of knowledge, and still others through working without fruitive desires.
englishTransliteration:
anye tv evam ajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhya upāsate
te ’pi cātitaranty eva mṛtyuṁ śruti-parāyaṇāḥ
englishWBW: anye (others) — tu (but) — evam (this) — ajānantaḥ (not knowing) — śrutvā (by hearing) — anyebhyaḥ (from others) — upāsate (begin to worship) — te (they) — api (also) — ca (and) — atitaranti (cross over) — eva (certainly) — mṛtyum (the path of death) — śruti-parāyaṇāḥ (inclined to the process of hearing).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa offers hope to the common person who may not be a great philosopher or a master of meditation. He says that even those who do not possess deep spiritual knowledge themselves, but simply begin to worship after hearing from authorities, can also transcend the path of death. They are ‘Śruti-parāyaṇāḥ’—dedicated to the process of hearing.

This highlights the power of ‘Śravaṇam’ or hearing. You don’t need to be a scholar to be saved. If you find a realized soul and listen to their instructions with faith, that hearing acts as a boat to carry you across the ocean of material existence. Simple sincerity is more important than intellectual brilliance. The sound vibration of truth is enough to purify the soul.

It teaches us that spiritual life is accessible to everyone. Whether you are a laborer, a housewife, or a child, if you just lend your ear to the words of the Gītā from a proper source, your journey toward liberation has begun. God doesn’t require us to be geniuses; He only requires us to be attentive and receptive to His message.

sanskrit:
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते।
तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः।।
translationEnglish: Again there are those who, although not conversant in spiritual knowledge, begin to worship the Supreme Person upon hearing about Him from others. Because of their tendency to hear from authorities, they also transcend the path of birth and death.
translationHindi: परन्तु इनसे दूसरे अर्थात जो मन्दबुद्धि पुरुष हैं, वे इस प्रकार न जानते हुए दूसरों से अर्थात तत्त्व के जानने वाले पुरुषों से सुनकर ही तदनुसार उपासना करते हैं और वे सुनने के परायण हुए पुरुष भी मृत्युरूप संसार-सागर को निःसंदेह तर जाते हैं।
translationGujarati: પરંતુ આનાથી બીજા અર્થાત જે મંદબુદ્ધિ પુરુષો છે, તેઓ આ રીતે ન જાણતા હોવાથી બીજાઓ પાસેથી અર્થાત તત્વને જાણનારા પુરુષો પાસેથી સાંભળીને જ તે અનુસાર ઉપાસના કરે છે અને તે સાંભળવામાં પરાયણ થયેલા પુરુષો પણ મૃત્યુરૂપ સંસાર-સાગરને નિઃશંક તરી જાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Even those who do not know these paths but worship based on hearing from authorities also transcend death through their dedication to hearing.
simpleHindi: जो लोग स्वयं नहीं जानते लेकिन दूसरों से सुनकर उपासना करते हैं, वे भी केवल सुनकर पालन करने की निष्ठा से मृत्यु को पार कर जाते हैं।
simpleGujarati: જે લોકો સ્વયં નથી જાણતા પરંતુ બીજાઓ પાસેથી સાંભળીને ઉપાસના કરે છે, તેઓ પણ માત્ર સાંભળીને પાલન કરવાની નિષ્ઠાથી મૃત્યુને પાર કરી જાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Others worship the Supreme Person upon hearing from others. They also transcend death.
threadsEnglish: Again there are those who, although not conversant in spiritual knowledge, begin to worship the Supreme Person upon hearing about Him from others. Because of their tendency to hear from authorities, they also transcend the path of birth and death.
englishTransliteration:
yāvat sañjāyate kiñcit sattvaṁ sthāvara-jaṅgamam
kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṁyogāt tad viddhi bharatarṣabha
englishWBW: yāvat (whatever) — sañjāyate (comes into being) — kiñcit (anything) — sattvam (existence) — sthāvara (stationary) — jaṅgamam (moving) — kṣetra (of the field) — kṣetra-jña (of the knower of the field) — saṁyogāt (by the union) — tat (that) — viddhi (know) — bharata-ṛṣabha (O chief of the Bharatas).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa summarizes the mechanics of the material world. He tells Arjuna that every single thing in existence—whether it is a stationary rock or a moving insect—is produced solely by the union of the ‘Field’ (Matter) and the ‘Knower’ (Spirit). Nothing in this world exists without this combination of biological machinery and conscious energy.

This is the secret of life. Matter by itself is dull and inert, like a car without a driver. Spirit by itself is transcendental and free, like a driver without a car. But when they are joined, the drama of ‘Samsāra’ begins. A human being is a conscious soul driving a material body; even an atom is matter animated by the presence of the Supersoul. Kṛṣṇa is the one who orchestrates this meeting.

By seeing the world this way, we stop being distracted by the surface appearances of things. We realize that the same spiritual spark is present in a tree, a mountain, and a person. This unified vision is the beginning of universal compassion. We are all ‘half-spirit’ and ‘half-matter’, navigating this world together under the Lord’s direction.

sanskrit:
यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम्।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ।।
translationEnglish: O chief of the Bharatas, know that whatever you see in existence, both the moving and the nonmoving, is only a combination of the field of activities and the knower of the field.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! यावन्मात्र जितने भी स्थावर-जंगम प्राणी उत्पन्न होते हैं, उन सबको तू क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ के संयोग से ही उत्पन्न हुए जान।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! માત્ર જેટલા પણ સ્થાવર-જંગમ પ્રાણીઓ ઉત્પન્ન થાય છે, તે બધાને તું ક્ષેત્ર અને ક્ષેત્રજ્ઞના સંયોગથી જ ઉત્પન્ન થયેલા જાણ.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that whatever exists, moving or non-moving, is born from the union of the field (matter) and the knower of the field (spirit).
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि जो कुछ भी मौजूद है, चाहे वह चर हो या अचर, वह क्षेत्र (प्रकृति) और क्षेत्रज्ञ (आत्मा) के संयोग से ही पैदा होता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે જે કંઈ પણ અસ્તિત્વમાં છે, ભલે તે ચર હોય કે અચર, તે ક્ષેત્ર (પ્રકૃતિ) અને ક્ષેત્રજ્ઞ (આત્મા) ના સંયોગથી જ પેદા થાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Whatever you see in existence is only a combination of the field of activities and the knower.
threadsEnglish: O chief of the Bharatas, know that whatever you see in existence, both the moving and the nonmoving, is only a combination of the field of activities and the knower of the field.
englishTransliteration:
yāvat sañjāyate kiñcit sattvaṁ sthāvara-jaṅgamam
kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṁyogāt tad viddhi bharatarṣabha
englishWBW: yāvat (whatever) — sañjāyate (comes into being) — kiñcit (anything) — sattvam (existence) — sthāvara (stationary) — jaṅgamam (moving) — kṣetra (of the field) — kṣetra-jña (of the knower of the field) — saṁyogāt (by the union) — tat (that) — viddhi (know) — bharata-ṛṣabha (O chief of the Bharatas).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa summarizes the nature of all existence. He tells Arjuna that every single thing he sees—whether it is a stationary rock or a moving insect—is born from the union of the ‘Field’ (Matter) and the ‘Knower’ (Spirit). Nothing in the material world exists without this combination.

This is the secret of life. Matter by itself is dull and inert; Spirit by itself is transcendental and free. But when they are joined by the Lord’s energy, the drama of the universe begins. A human being is a conscious soul driving a material body; even an atom is matter animated by the presence of the Supersoul.

By seeing the world this way, we stop being distracted by the surface appearances of things. We realize that the same spiritual spark is present in a tree, a mountain, and a person. This unified vision is the beginning of universal compassion and a deep understanding of the ‘Samsāra’ or the cycle of life.

sanskrit:
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम्।
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति।।
translationEnglish: One who sees the Supersoul accompanying the individual soul in all bodies, and who understands that neither the soul nor the Supersoul within the destructible body is ever destroyed, actually sees.
translationHindi: जो पुरुष नष्ट होते हुए सब चराचर भूतों में परमेश्वर को नाशरहित और समभाव से स्थित देखता है, वही यथार्थ देखता है।
translationGujarati: જે પુરુષ નાશ પામતા બધા ચરાચર ભૂતોમાં પરમેશ્વરને નાશરહિત અને સમભાવે સ્થિત જુએ છે, તે જ યથાર્થ જુએ છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa states that he truly sees who sees the imperishable Supreme Lord dwelling equally within all perishable beings.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि वही वास्तव में देखता है जो सभी नश्वर प्राणियों के भीतर अविनाशी परमात्मा को समान रूप से स्थित देखता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે તે જ વાસ્તવમાં જુએ છે જે બધા નશ્વર પ્રાણીઓની ભીતર અવિનાશી પરમાત્માને સમાન રીતે સ્થિત જુએ છે.
tweetEnglish: One who sees the Supersoul accompanying the soul in all bodies actually sees.
threadsEnglish: One who sees the Supersoul accompanying the individual soul in all bodies, and who understands that neither the soul nor the Supersoul within the destructible body is ever destroyed, actually sees.
englishTransliteration:
samaṁ paśyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśvaram
na hinasty ātmanātmānaṁ tato yāti parāṁ gatim
englishWBW: samam (equally) — paśyan (seeing) — hi (certainly) — sarvatra (everywhere) — samavasthitam (situated) — īśvaram (the Lord) — na (does not) — hinasti (degrade/kill) — ātmanā (by the mind) — ātmānam (the self) — tataḥ (then) — yāti (attains) — parām (the supreme) — gatim (destination).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains the benefit of ‘Equal Vision’. He says that one who sees the Supersoul (‘Īśvaram’) situated equally in every living being does not degrade his own soul through the whims of his mind. Because he respects the Divine presence in others, he naturally approaches the ‘Parāṁ gatim’—the supreme destination. His vision of unity prevents him from acting selfishly.

When we see only the ‘Field’ (the body), we see differences: ‘He is my enemy,’ or ‘She is a stranger.’ This leads to exploitation and sin, which degrades the self. But if we see the ‘Knower’ (God) in everyone, we cannot hate or hurt anyone. Our mind becomes a friend rather than an enemy. We treat every encounter as a meeting with a sacred temple.

It teaches us that morality is based on spiritual perception. If you want to be a good person, you must first be a ‘Seer’ of the spirit. By acknowledging the Lord’s presence in all hearts, we automatically become kind, fair, and peaceful. This mindset is the fastest elevator to the highest spiritual goal.

sanskrit:
समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम्।
न हिनस्त्यात्मनात्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम्।।
translationEnglish: One who sees the Supersoul equally present everywhere, in every living being, does not degrade himself by his mind. Thus he approaches the transcendental destination.
translationHindi: क्योंकि जो पुरुष सबमें समभाव से स्थित परमेश्वर को समान देखता हुआ अपने द्वारा अपने को नष्ट नहीं करता, इससे वह परम गति को प्राप्त होता है।
translationGujarati: કારણ કે જે પુરુષ બધામાં સમભાવે સ્થિત પરમેશ્વરને સમાન જોતો પોતાના દ્વારા પોતાનો નાશ નથી કરતો, તેથી તે પરમ ગતિને પામે છે.
simpleEnglish: By seeing the Lord equally present everywhere, one does not degrade the self by the self and thus attains the supreme destination.
simpleHindi: जो व्यक्ति हर जगह ईश्वर को समान रूप से देखता है, वह अपने मन से अपना पतन नहीं करता और इस प्रकार परम गति को प्राप्त करता है।
simpleGujarati: જે વ્યક્તિ દરેક જગ્યાએ ઈશ્વરને સમાન રીતે જુએ છે, તે પોતાના મનથી પોતાનું પતન નથી કરતો અને આ રીતે પરમ ગતિને પ્રાપ્ત કરે છે.
tweetEnglish: One who sees the Supersoul equally present everywhere does not degrade himself.
threadsEnglish: One who sees the Supersoul equally present everywhere, in every living being, does not degrade himself by his mind. Thus he approaches the transcendental destination.
englishTransliteration:
prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ
yaḥ paśyati tathātmānam akartāraṁ sa paśyati
englishWBW: prakṛtyā (by material nature) — eva (certainly) — ca (also) — karmāṇi (activities) — kriyamāṇāni (being performed) — sarvaśaḥ (in all respects) — yaḥ (anyone who) — paśyati (sees) — tathā (similarly) — ātmānam (himself) — akartāram (the non-doer) — saḥ (he) — paśyati (actually sees).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa introduces the concept of the ‘Non-Doer’. He says that one who sees that all activities are being performed by the body and senses (which are products of material nature), and that he, the soul, actually does nothing, is the one who ‘actually sees’. This is the vision of detachment. The soul is the passenger; nature is the car’s engine.

Most of our stress comes from the illusion of ‘doership’. We think, “I am running,” or “I am accomplishing this.” But the Gītā clarifies that the soul only ‘desires’, and then the body (nature) executes the action using its elements. The soul is the observer of the process. When we realize this, we stop being so anxious about our material performance.

This doesn’t mean we become lazy. It means we act with a sense of ‘witness-consciousness’. We do our duty with excellence, but we realize that the physical results are being handled by the laws of nature. This detachment allows us to work without being crushed by the weight of responsibility. We become the silent, peaceful presence inside the active machine.

sanskrit:
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः।
यः पश्यति तथात्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति।।
translationEnglish: One who can see that all activities are performed by the body, which is created of material nature, and that he himself does nothing, actually sees.
translationHindi: और जो पुरुष सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को सब प्रकार से प्रकृति द्वारा ही किये जाते हुए देखता है और आत्मा को अकर्ता देखता है, वही यथार्थ देखता है।
translationGujarati: અને જે પુરુષ સંપૂર્ણ કર્મોને સર્વ પ્રકારે પ્રકૃતિ દ્વારા જ કરવામાં આવતા જુએ છે અને આત્માને અકર્તા જુએ છે, તે જ યથાર્થ જુએ છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa says that he truly sees who sees that all actions are performed by nature alone and that the self is actionless.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि सच्चा ज्ञानी वह है जो यह देखता है कि सारे काम प्रकृति द्वारा किए जा रहे हैं और आत्मा वास्तव में कुछ नहीं करती।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ કહે છે કે સાચો જ્ઞાની તે છે જે એ જુએ છે કે બધા કામ પ્રકૃતિ દ્વારા કરવામાં આવી રહ્યા છે અને આત્મા વાસ્તવમાં કશું નથી કરતી.
tweetEnglish: One who sees that all activities are performed by the body and that he does nothing, actually sees.
threadsEnglish: One who can see that all activities are performed by the body, which is created of material nature, and sees that the self does nothing, actually sees.
englishTransliteration:
yadā bhūta-pṛthag-bhāvam eka-stham anupaśyati
tata eva ca vistāraṁ brahma sampadyate tadā
englishWBW: yadā (when) — bhūta (living beings) — pṛthak-bhāvam (different identities) — eka-stham (situated in one) — anupaśyati (one tries to see) — tataḥ (thereafter) — eva (certainly) — ca (and) — vistāram (expansion) — brahma (the Absolute) — sampadyate (he attains) — tadā (at that time).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa describes the moment of Brahman-realization. He says that when a person ceases to see different identities based on material bodies and instead sees how all beings are expanded from and situated in the One Supreme, they attain the spiritual conception of reality. They move from the vision of ‘Variety’ to the vision of ‘Unity’.

This is like seeing that all the different ornaments (rings, necklaces, bangles) are actually just gold. On the surface, they look different, but the substance is one. Similarly, a dog, a cat, and a human look different, but they are all expansions of the same Divine energy. The wise person focuses on the ‘Expansion’ (Vistāram) from the Source rather than the surface labels.

It teaches us to look for the common thread in life. When we realize that everyone and everything is connected to the same Kṛṣṇa, our prejudices and fears disappear. We start to feel at home in the universe because we see the same ‘family’ everywhere. This unified vision is the doorway to the eternal, spiritual sky.

sanskrit:
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा।।
translationEnglish: When a sensible man ceases to see different identities due to different material bodies and he sees how beings are expanded everywhere, he attains to the Brahman conception.
translationHindi: जिस क्षण यह पुरुष भूतों के पृथक्-पृथक् भाव को एक परमात्मा में ही स्थित तथा उस परमात्मा से ही सम्पूर्ण भूतों का विस्तार देखता है, उसी क्षण वह सच्चिदानन्दघन ब्रह्म को प्राप्त हो जाता है।
translationGujarati: જે ક્ષણે આ પુરુષ ભૂતોના અલગ અલગ ભાવને એક પરમાત્મામાં જ સ્થિત તથા તે પરમાત્માથી જ સંપૂર્ણ ભૂતોનો વિસ્તાર જુએ છે, તે જ ક્ષણે તે સચ્ચિદાનંદઘન બ્રહ્મને પામી જાય છે.
simpleEnglish: When one sees the variety of beings resting in the One and spreading forth from That alone, one attains Brahman.
simpleHindi: जब कोई व्यक्ति अलग-अलग प्राणियों को एक ही परमात्मा में स्थित देखता है और यह समझता है कि सब उसी से विस्तारित हुए हैं, तब वह ब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
simpleGujarati: જ્યારે કોઈ વ્યક્તિ અલગ-અલગ પ્રાણીઓને એક જ પરમાત્મામાં સ્થિત જુએ છે અને એ સમજે છે કે બધું તેનાથી જ વિસ્તરિત થયું છે, ત્યારે તે બ્રહ્મને પ્રાપ્ત કરે છે.
tweetEnglish: When one ceases to see different identities due to bodies, he attains the Brahman conception.
threadsEnglish: When a sensible man ceases to see different identities due to different material bodies and he sees how beings are expanded everywhere, he attains to the Brahman conception.
englishTransliteration:
anāditvān nirguṇatvāt paramātmāyam avyayaḥ
śarīra-stho ’pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate
englishWBW: anāditvāt (due to being beginningless) — nirguṇatvāt (due to being transcendental to material modes) — parama-ātmā (the Supreme Soul) — ayam (this) — avyayaḥ (imperishable) — śarīra-sthaḥ (dwelling in the body) — api (even though) — kaunteya (O son of Kuntī) — na (never) — karoti (acts) — na (never) — lipyate (is entangled).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa explains why the soul remains pure despite being in a material body. He says that because the soul is ‘Anādi’ (beginningless) and ‘Nirguṇa’ (beyond the three modes), it is ‘Avyaya’ or imperishable. Even though it is situated in the body, it neither performs the body’s actions nor is it entangled by them. It is like oil in water—always present but never mixed.

This is a great comfort for the seeker. It means that our true self is never actually ‘dirty’ or ‘broken’. No matter how many mistakes the body has made or how much trauma it has endured, the soul remains pristine and spiritual. We are like a diamond that has fallen into the mud; the mud covers us, but it doesn’t change our nature. Our job is simply to wash the mud away.

It teaches us to identify with our immunity rather than our vulnerability. The body ages, gets sick, and dies, but ‘You’ remain untouched. By realizing that we are ‘Na lipyate’—never entangled—we can live with a sense of dignity and freedom, knowing that our eternal spiritual identity is always intact.

sanskrit:
अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः।
शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते।।
translationEnglish: Those with the vision of eternity can see that the imperishable soul is transcendental, eternal, and beyond the modes of nature. Despite contact with the material body, O Arjuna, the soul neither does anything nor is entangled.
translationHindi: हे अर्जुन! अनादि होने से और निर्गुण होने से यह अविनाशी परमात्मा शरीर में स्थित होने पर भी वास्तव में न तो कुछ करता है और न लिप्त ही होता है।
translationGujarati: હે અર્જુન! અનાદિ હોવાથી અને નિર્ગુણ હોવાથી આ અવિનાશી પરમાત્મા શરીરમાં સ્થિત હોવા છતાં વાસ્તવમાં ન તો કંઈ કરે છે અને ન તો લિપ્ત થાય છે.
simpleEnglish: Kṛṣṇa explains that because the Supreme Soul is beginningless and without material qualities, it neither acts nor gets tainted, even while dwelling in the body.
simpleHindi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि अनादि और निर्गुण होने के कारण, परमात्मा शरीर में रहते हुए भी न तो कुछ करता है और न ही किसी कर्म से बंधता है।
simpleGujarati: કૃષ્ણ સમજાવે છે કે અનાદિ અને નિર્ગુણ હોવાના કારણે, પરમાત્મા શરીરમાં રહેવા છતાં ન તો કંઈ કરે છે અને ન તો કોઈ કર્મથી બંધાય છે.
tweetEnglish: Those with vision see the soul is transcendental. Despite contact with the body, it is not entangled.
threadsEnglish: Those with the vision of eternity can see that the imperishable soul is transcendental, eternal and beyond the modes of nature. Despite contact with the material body, O Arjuna, the soul neither does anything nor is entangled.
englishTransliteration:
yathā sarva-gataṁ saukṣmyād ākāśaṁ nopalipyate
sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate
englishWBW: yathā (as) — sarva-gatam (all-pervading) — saukṣmyāt (due to being subtle) — ākāśam (the sky) — na (never) — upalipyate (mixes) — sarvatra (everywhere) — avasthitaḥ (situated) — dehe (in the body) — tathā (similarly) — ātmā (the soul) — na (never) — upalipyate (is entangled).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa uses a beautiful analogy from nature to explain the soul’s purity. He compares the soul to the sky (‘Ākāśa’). The sky is everywhere—it is inside a house and inside a sewer—but because it is subtle, it never mixes with the things it contains. You can throw mud into the air, but the sky doesn’t get muddy; the mud just falls back down.

Similarly, the soul is situated throughout the body, but it is never tainted by the body’s activities. The soul provides the consciousness for the body to function, but it remains aloof from the chemical reactions and the physical decay. It is the silent, pure space within which the body’s drama takes place. This ‘subtlety’ is the hallmark of spirit.

This verse helps us practice ‘detachment by analogy’. When you feel overwhelmed by physical pain or mental stress, imagine yourself as the sky. The clouds of pain may pass through you, but they cannot stain you. You are the vast, eternal space of awareness that remains clear and untouched by the weather of the material world.

sanskrit:
यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते।
सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथात्मा नोपलिप्यते।।
translationEnglish: The sky, due to its subtle nature, does not mix with anything, although it is all-pervading. Similarly, the soul situated in Brahman vision does not mix with the body, though situated in that body.
translationHindi: जिस प्रकार सर्वत्र व्याप्त आकाश सूक्ष्म होने के कारण लिप्त नहीं होता, वैसे ही देह में सर्वत्र स्थित आत्मा निर्गुण होने के कारण देह के गुणों से लिप्त नहीं होता।
translationGujarati: જેમ સર્વત્ર વ્યાપ્ત આકાશ સૂક્ષ્મ હોવાના કારણે લિપ્ત થતું નથી, તેમ જ દેહમાં સર્વત્ર સ્થિત આત્મા નિર્ગુણ હોવાના કારણે દેહના ગુણોથી લિપ્ત થતો નથી.
simpleEnglish: Just as the all-pervading sky does not mix with anything due to its subtlety, the soul positioned in the body does not mix with it.
simpleHindi: जैसे सर्वव्यापी आकाश सूक्ष्म होने के कारण किसी चीज से नहीं चिपकता, वैसे ही शरीर में स्थित आत्मा शरीर के गुणों से प्रभावित नहीं होती।
simpleGujarati: જેમ સર્વવ્યાપી આકાશ સૂક્ષ્મ હોવાના કારણે કોઈ વસ્તુ સાથે ચોંટતું નથી, તેમ જ શરીરમાં સ્થિત આત્મા શરીરના ગુણોથી પ્રભાવિત થતો નથી.
tweetEnglish: The sky does not mix with anything. Similarly, the soul does not mix with the body.
threadsEnglish: The sky, due to its subtle nature, does not mix with anything, although it is all-pervading. Similarly, the soul situated in Brahman vision does not mix with the body, though situated in that body.
englishTransliteration:
yathā prakāśayaty ekaḥ kṛtsnaṁ lokam imaṁ raviḥ
kṣetraṁ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṁ prakāśayati bhārata
englishWBW: yathā (as) — prakāśayati (illuminates) — ekaḥ (one) — kṛtsnam (entire) — lokam (world) — imam (this) — raviḥ (the sun) — kṣetram (the field/body) — kṣetrī (the owner of the field/soul) — tathā (similarly) — kṛtsnam (entire) — prakāśayati (illuminates) — bhārata (O son of Bharata).
englishExplain:
Kṛṣṇa gives the definitive analogy for consciousness.
